Heading: For staff’s fitness, PMC gets Baba Ramdev on Oct 18 - Indian Express
Content:
After developing the road from Airport to Balewadi, the Pune Municipal Corporation is all set to introduce Bus Rapid Transit System (BRTS) on the route.

"We are resolving all issues related to introducing the BRTS on the 30-km Airport-Balewadi stretch. The decision on the date to start the work will be taken in a month," Pardeshi told reporters.

He said the pilot BRTS route from Katraj to Hadapsar will be completed by year-end after removing the bottlenecks.

The work on BRTS on various routes on Nagar road, old Mumbai-Pune highway, Alandi Road and Karve Road will be speeded up to complete it by January next year. The work on Sinhagad Road will take time, he said.

Meanwhile, the civic administration will install 15 new signals on the Airport to Balewadi stretch for better flow of traffic, Pardeshi said.

He said that deadlines will be set for the completion of various roads being developed under Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission so that there is effective execution of the project.

Heading: 6 yrs later, consumer court’s justice to 7, asks builder to give flats - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to increase their employees' efficiency, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has invited Baba Ramdev to give wellness tips and pranayam to its staff, including conservancy workers.

The special two and a half hour session to be held at the Jawaharlal Nehru stadium on October 18 has been made compulsory for the entire PMC staff.

"Our employees work in stressful conditions and their mental as well as physical fitness plays a major role in their efficiency. Thus, we have organised a yoga session of Baba Ramdev for the employees," Municipal Commissioner Pravinsinh Pardeshi.

The special session will be attended by the employees and their family members, he said. The session will also be attended by Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar and state Minister for Marketing Harshwardhan Patil.

The Patanjali Yog Samiti, in association with the PMC, will continue the yoga sessions throughout the city, he said. Gardens, parks and public places will be provided to the Samiti in the mornings to conduct yoga lessons for the PMC employees and common citizens.

Special efforts will be taken to provide pranayam lessons to conservancy staff, Pardeshi said.

Since the city police also works under stress, the civic chief said that he has urged the police commissioner to take advantage of the special pranayam session for the police staff.

Heading: CYG bus service catches up - Indian Express
Content:
250 Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe Magaswargiya Sanstha members booked flats in 2002, waited for flats till 2006, then 21 members appealed in court, get justice in 2008

After a six-year wait and over coming many obstacles, finally, the seven members of the Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe Magaswargiya Sanstha will get the flats they had booked in 2002.

Following a consumer court ruling, builder Prabhakar Bhosale of Sankalp Constructions, Dhanori, will hand over the flats to the members in the next four weeks.

In 2002, about 250 members of the Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe Magaswargiya Sanstha booked flats at the behest of the chairman of the society Shivaji More.

According to the agreement, Bhosale was to hand over the flats, measuring 500 sq.ft., by 2005. Bhosale had taken a booking amount of Rs 25,000 each from the members and asked them to take a loan of Rs 2 lakh for the completion of the houses. They immediately paid him Rs1.25 lakh. The cost of one flat was Rs 2.6 lakh, as mentioned in the agreement. Interestingly, the current market value of these flats is around Rs 12.5 to Rs 13 lakh each.

However, he did not hand over the flats to the members and instead said that he will require more money for the completion of the project citing rising prices. By 2006, most of the members had paid up to Rs 1.75 lakh each but yet had not obtained possession. It was then that, 21 members of the Sanstha filed an appeal in the consumer court.

Advocate Jayashree Kulkarni, who represented the members, said, "According to the ruling, he (the builder) will have to hand over the flats to the seven members within the next four weeks, and give the flat sale papers within six weeks from the date of possession. The results of the remaining 14 members will also be dispatched shortly."

One of the members Suresh Shelar said, "We are happy that the verdict is finally out and that we shall receive the flats soon. According to the judgment, we will pay the remaining amount within the next four weeks and he will have to hand over the flats."

When contacted, Bhosale said, "We have already filed an appeal in the higher court. We expect a stay order in the next two days." He said, "The members had defaulted in their payments and it was impossible for me to continue construction without money."

Heading: Cop held for taking bribe, gets bail - Indian Express
Content:
After the initial lull on the first two days, the number of commuters on the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited's buses to Balewadi has increased, said PMPML officials. On Thursday, PMPML officers said that nearly 25,000 people travelled by PMPML buses to the stadium.

"The free CNG bus service between the parking lot to the stadium has been a success and are running packed. On other routes as well, the crowd has increased since the opening day. On Thursday, our buses to Balewadi carried nearly 25,000 people to the stadium, many of them were students," said PMPML spokesperson Deepak Pardeshi.

One of the reasons for this turnout is droves of schoolchildren going to watch the Games. "We are issuing free passes to all schools, not just the 71 participating schools. We saw the maximum turnout on Thursday — nearly 40,000 people attended the Games — because of the athletics finals. The trend is expected to continue on Friday which is the final day for all other events," said Ashok Kapoor, additional director general, CYG committee. Kapoor said that threat of rain on the first two days was responsible for the poor turnout.

According to PMPML officials, nearly 50,000 people have commuted on PMPML buses to the CYG venue. This includes the sizable chunk that had used the CNG bus service from the parking lot to the stadium.

The company has reserved 200 buses for the Games. These buses were running on 16 different routes and had been diverted from the regular city routes.

Heading: Death of three: Viscera tests confirm death due to consumption of cyanide - Indian Express
Content:
Police sub inspector Bhujang alias Nana Dattatray Kadam, who was arrested by the Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Wednesday — for allegedly taking a bribe from Sheikh Rashid Chotumiyan, over a period of one year — was produced in the Shivajinagar District and Sessions court today. Kadam has been charged under the Prevention Of Corruption Act 1988.

Rashid, a resident of Chakan, is a scrap dealer. He was arrested some months ago with his tempo (MH-14 F 8383) full of scrap iron, by PSI Kadam and his assistant PSI Rahul Kale.

Despite having all the papers, they told him to pay up if he wanted his tempo back. They first took Rs 1.5 lakh and then Rs 30,000 twice from him. They also threatened him of dire consequences if he complained against them.

Two months ago, another businessman from Ahmednagar had come to Rashid's shop to buy some scrap iron. He loaded his tempo (MH-04 C-3419) and was going back when Kadam and Kale again stopped the tempo. Rashid went to the Alandi police station to get the tempo back. There, Kadam and Kale asked him for another Rs 90,000 if he wanted the tempo back. Rashid told them that he will pay them in two installments of Rs 50,000 and Rs 40,000.

Meanwhile, Rashid lodged an FIR with the ACB in Ahmednagar. On Wednesday, he went to pay Kadam and ACB officials nabbed Kadam red-handed.

Kadam has been remanded to magisterial custody till November 3. However, later he was granted a bail on a personal bond of Rs 15,000.

Heading: IT engineer arrested for manhandling traffic cop - Indian Express
Content:
Chemical analysis of viscera of three bodies found at Kishkinda Nagar in Kothrud two months ago has confirm the cause of death as consumption of potassium cyanide.

Vaishali Sanjay Tonde (30), her sister Nalini Dhondiba Gawade (23) and her 14-month-old daughter Samruddhi were found dead in her residence on August 9. The Kothrud police had then registered an accidental death case. Viscera of the deceased were preserved for chemical test.

The Kothrud police on Wednesday arrested Vaishali's husband Sanjay (35) for abetting suicide. Investigations are on to know from where the deceased got the potassium cyanide.

Sanjay operates a flour mill at Paud Road. He married Vaishali three years ago. According to the police, Vaishali was Sanjay's second wife. Sanjay used to abuse Vaishali claiming that she was not looking after his children. He also sought sexual favours from Vaishali's sister Nalini.

According to the police, the sisters consumed poison. And the 14-month-old baby consumed the froth that came out of their mouth. The police suspect that Nalini and Vaishali committed suicide because of the harassment caused by Sanjay.

Heading: And now, a Pune model for poverty eradication - Indian Express
Content:
A computer engineer thrashed a traffic police constable on duty at the Vetal Baba chowk on Senapati Bapat Road on Thursday morning.

However, this time constable, Amol Sadashiv Sarde, also hit back with his baton — specially provided by the traffic control branch in the wake of rising number of attacks on traffic police.

The police have arrested the engineer identified as Manas Raju Nalukishor Kher (27), following a complaint filed by Sarde with the Chatuhshrungi police station.

According to the police, Sarde is a new recruit. He was deployed at the Vetal Baba chowk as a part of the special drive against traffic violations. Kher was coming on a motorcycle on the same route.

As the signal turned red, Kher stopped at the chowk, but violated traffic rule by stopping his bike over the zebra crossing. Sarde asked Kher for his driving licence. When Kher failed to produce his license, Sarde asked him to pay fine. At this, Kher started arguing and beating Sarde.

Deputy Commissioner (Traffic) Manoj Patil said that Sarde hit back as he did not have an option. "I personally visited the crime scene. The engineer is at fault. He has been arrested for causing disturbance in government work and manhandling a policeman on duty," Patil said.

Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane said, "it is unfortunate that Kher, an employee with a prominent corporate company in Pune, broke the law. He was beating a police constable on the road and none of the citizens there stepped forward in support of the police.

Action against 17,000 offenders in 3 days
The traffic control branch of police conducted a major drive between October 14 and 16 and collected a fine of Rs 19.5 lakh from 17,000 offenders for violating various traffic norms. Traffic police teams were deployed at 25 spots across the city. DCP Manoj Patil said that traffic police personnel worked hard and managed to file so many cases without affecting their bandobast duties and routine work.

Heading: No staff: CoEP goes the tech way - Indian Express
Content:
Devised by Dr Vasant Pethe, it has city thinkers appealing for its feasibility study

He claims to have the answer to the most persistent problem of the country-poverty. What's more it's one that's apparently workable with the focus on the transformation of the individual leading to the transformation of the nation, as against all policies and plans till now that tend to focus on mega development with the hope that the benefits will trickle down to the poor. And that is precisely what makes Dr Vasant Pethe's model that he calls the "Indian model for poverty eradication and economic development" an innovative one.

This former professor with Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics, Pethe has a complete roadmap drawn out that also promises 100 per cent employment.

"The focus of my model is an individual's development which later helps in nation's development. This is exactly opposite to today's government policy that lays stress on mega-industrialisation and the resulting economic development and which, as everyone knows, this has not helped much," said Pethe.

By focusing on the individual, Pethe highlights empowerment of men and women by providing education, health facilities and ethical upbringing. "While education and health can be worked upon by the government, ethical upbringing can happen by value education and similar methods," he said. The model is aimed at developing an individual's potential and providing him with opportunities so that he can contribute to the nation's cause.

Appreciating the innovative approach of this model, a group of thinkers like senior economist Dr Sulabha Brahme, Dr Arun Nigavekar, former chairman of University Grants Commission, senior socialist leader G P Pradhan, dean of faculty of management of University of Pune Dr P C Shejwalkar, Dr Y B Damle former head of Pune University's Sociology department, among others, are now likely to appeal to the government to appoint a group to study the model and its feasibility.

Damle said, "It is a unique approach and if the suggested road map is followed, it shall definitely help in controlling poverty and population." Brahme said that when most economists are busy in deciding the poverty line, this is a welcome alternative presented by Pethe that has the potential of eradicating the need of having a poverty line.

The next step proposed by the model, after empowering the individual, speaks of developing villages by optimisation of its natural resources. "The optimisation process could start with a survey of natural resources in the village, economic planning of villages, implementation of the plan and evaluation. This will ensure that jobs will be generated locally and the required talent will also be available locally, thus reducing migration to cities," said Pethe who is in the process of coming up with a book also.

Heading: PCB mulls liberal policy for hiring conservancy staff - Indian Express
Content:
IIT-B faculty teach students via video conferencing

Faced with 40 per cent shortage of staff, the College of Engineering, Pune (CoEP) is banking on technology to minimise the problem. The IIT-B faculty is teaching the CoEP students through video conferencing, thus reducing the extra burden on the present staff.

"We are facing the staff crunch in every stream and presently we are short of 85 teachers," said Anil Sahasrabuddhe, director of CoEP. "The main reason behind the staff crunch is non-availability of qualified teachers," he added. The CoEP has an approved quota of 230 posts of lecturers and readers of which 145 are occupied.

"The facility started in July 2007 and so far, the students have been taught 19 courses through video conferencing," said Sahasrabuddhe. "Students can interact with the faculty during the video conferencing. We also have industry experts as visiting faculties," he said.

Sahasrabuddhe also said that the CoEP now plans to extend the same facility to the colleges in small towns where the problem of staff crunch is even severe. "We will telecast our lectures live in these colleges," he said.

However, the shortage of staff for engineering faculty is not new. According to Pandit Vidyasagr, director of Board of College and University Development, University of Pune, "it is actually a global phenomenon. The qualified teachers for engineering faculty are hard to get and Pune is no exception."

Agreeing with Vidyasagar, founder of Flucon Equipments Sanjay Inamdar said that the number of engineering students going for PhD or masters are less. "According to an estimate, every year five lakh engineers graduate. Of these, at least 50,000 are expected to turn to masters degree or PhD and finally land up in teaching. But it is not happening," he said.

CoEP alumni meet, graduation ceremony on October 19,20
The CoEP will conduct its graduation ceremony for two batches on October 20 coinciding with its alumni meet on October 19 and 20, Sahasrabuddhe told media persons on Wednesday.

The graduation ceremony will be for the first two batches after the college got autonomous status. "We could not hold graduation ceremony last year. This year we will present gold medals and certificates of merit to the students who have graduated this year and last year," he said.

Sahasrabuddhe said that though the college was autonomous, the ceremony could not be termed as convocation ceremony. "According to the norms, we can offer gold medals and prizes on our own as we conduct the examinations. But we cannot offer degree, as the degree is offered by the University of Pune," he said.

Sahasrabuddhe said that the college is expecting an announcement from the alumni for the campus makeover plan. "The makeover will cost around Rs 350 crore. Christopher Benninger, the architect appointed for the infrastructure development, will make a presentation before the alumni," he said.

"We have already asked the state government to help us with a fund of Rs 25 crore for a girls' hostel and academic complex, which are on the top of our priority list," said Sahasrabuddhe.

Heading: Over the moon - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Cantonment Board (PCB) may soon adopt a more moderate policy in hiring conservancy staff and is planning to forward a proposal in this regard to the Southern Command Headquarters.

According to PCB chief executive officer S K Sardana, "Several applications for conservancy staff vacancies, submitted in the past two years or so, are pending with the PCB office in the category of compassionate grounds. At present, 21 vacancies are available but as per the central government's directive, only five per cent of the pending vacancies should be filled. Thus, only one person can be appointed and the remaining vacancies stay unfilled."

The PCB would soon submit a proposal to the Southern Command Headquarters requesting relaxation of the current norms so that deserving candidates who have applied on compassionate grounds can be taken as full-time employees, Sardana said on Thursday.

Earlier, the annual review meeting of conservancy staff workers was held. The major unions — Akhil Bhartiya Safai Mazdoor Sangha, All India Safai Mazdoor Congress, and Pune Cantonment Kamgar Sangha — which comprise around 700 persons in all, attended it. The demands made by the unions include implementation of a standard dress code for all personnel and scaling up the number of daily-wage workers, apart from masks to be used at the workplace and regular health check-ups.

Heading: Between the lines - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood and parties may have added that dash of glamour to the festival, but the thought of eternal companionship that signifies Karva Chauth remains unchanged

Entreating and invoking the Gods for a long and happy life of their beloved and vouching for an everlasting companionship, the fast of Karva Chauth has been an intrinsic part of North Indian traditions. Along with marking an important day for suhagans (married women), this day also brings along with it a carnival to celebrate and a reason to load the shopping bags.

On Wednesday, the pre-Karva Chauth party held at the Kwality Restaurant, on East Street by an event management group named Kity Kat girls, had women enjoying all the fanfare. Flaunting their best designer outfits in glittering shades of red, maroon and pink accompanied by dazzling gold and diamond jewellery, women were truly at their best. "Karva Chauth is not only about fasting and performing rituals, it's also about cheering and celebrating the occasion. This party is meant only for women and the main idea behind the gathering is to set the mood of celebration and also make the women aware of the idea of the festival," shares Gayatri Sehgal, a member of the organising team. With different competitions, group games, non-stop dancing and hit numbers from the DJ; this extravaganza let ladies loosen their party instincts. "The party is very colourful, I look forward to have a lot of fun here," said Reena Karulkar who was cheering her daughter Stutee who performed the traditional Bhavai dance.

With henna artistes and bangle stalls proving to be an added attraction, the venue was draped in the colour red. Jaya, a party reveler, said, "All of us are here to have a great time, it is just like a fest before fasting. The best part of these parties is that there are no men around. Women are on their own and can go wild" chukled Masserat Raina As the Saas-Bahu saga continues everywhere, the party had mothers-in-law shaking a leg with their daughters-in-law and the winner of Mrs Karva Chauth won couple tickets to Goa.

Others who celebrate at home also seem to make the day special for them. "With lot of emotions involved in it, Karva Chauth, is like a one-day carnival where our family gets together for celebrations. Well yes, this is a day when my husband pampers me the most," says Renu Arya, an entrepreneur. While otherwise, starving during a daylong fast, may seem exhausting and unattainable this day women abide by the austere rituals with a lot of interest. Although the tradition was initiated for married women, interestingly, these days unmarried girls also observe the fast. "We pray for the health and happiness of our future partners but unlike married women we break the fast at the glimpse of stars and not the moon, says Nidhi Jaidka, who is unmarried.

"Before sunrise, all women observing the fast, eat the Sargi, a meal prepared by their mother-in-law," says Ruchita Sahni while elaborating on the rituals. "The rest of the day is spent in celebration, applying mehndi, decorating karva (the clay pot), preparing the puja ki thali and exchanging gifts. Before sunset, women adorn bridal finery to worship Gauri Mata. Once the moon comes into sight, women worship the moon through a sieve and then they see their husbands through it, after which the husband offers water to his wife," describes Sahni, who is celebrating the third Karva Chauth after her marriage. Delving deeper into the motives behind these celebrations, and reasons for such customs to be observed, one realizes these gestures are not just rituals, but lessons that coil the emotions of love and devotion.

Heading: Books and Bookers - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune Book Fair takes booklovers on a diverse and linguistic experience

The best buys are the ones that you stumble upon-that is the experience which a stroll through the cool hushed ambience of the Pune Book Fair provides one with.

October 15 saw the inauguration of Pune's seventh book fair at Ganesh Kala Krida Manch. Though not on the grand lines of the New Delhi and Kolkatta book fairs, the Pune Book Fair provides an important meeting ground for publishers, booksellers, book distributors, librarians, professionals, academicians and booklovers. "We cater to people with more distinct taste and expectations in literature," says Mr. V.B.Joshi, Co convener of the fair. "The topics and themes on display are slightly offbeat, and many in vernacular languages. Our aim is to give smaller or individual publishers a chance to display their books," adds he.

In turn this also offers booklovers a truly diverse linguistic and quantitative experience, which was evident at the venue, where, books on Konkani literature, classic erotica and Falun Dafa, the banned and brutally persecuted practice in China, were all on offer, often at throwaway prices.

The exhibition hosts over a 100 stalls; few of which stand out more than the others. Ebrahim Aghajari, who is currently completing his Ph.D in engineering and instrumentation in Pune, manages the stall on Iranian culture. Aghajari guides you through the intricacies of Persian, Urdu and Arabic literature and the wonders of ancient cities of Tehran, and Kashan in Isfahan.

In complete contrast to this quiet corner is the Lokayat, a stall that bursts with revolutionary literature, slogans and posters. Be it a dissertation on Nandigram, writings of Noam Chomsky, documentaries on Godhra riots, Ayodhya issue or discussions on our post-modern world, it is sure to find a place here.

Magazines play a prominent part in this fair too. Rohan Book Centre which houses magazines from across the globe, is a place where one can pick up original copies of Vogue and National Geographic for a steal, apart from other lesser known but equally interesting foreign journals and publications.

Adjacent to it is the Heritage India stall, a Pune based publication. Each page contains a slice of India's rich and varied heritage from wildlife to art and history. The magazine is beautifully packaged with high quality photographs.

The Vivek Book Depot and Pragati Book Centre are also places where with patience one can unearth good second hand books. The former especially stocks classics by Henry James, Daniel Defoe and William Makepeace Thackeray. The fair abounds in vernacular literature, be it philosophy or mythology based comic books, all is on offer in Hindi and Marathi. World Health Organization (WHO) also makes its presence felt, disseminating health information and researched publications on health problem in Africa and South – East Asia. Libre Edition also presented The Shine, the first english translation of French writer Frederic Mari. On from the October 15 to 19 from 10 am to 8 pm, the Pune book fair is truly a hunting ground for bibliophiles. Check it out.

Heading: Cong to hold state-wide padyatras against UP govt - Indian Express
Content:
Pune bookstores run out of The White Tiger

When it comes to Indian literature in English, it has always been the West that leads the way for Indian booklovers. Never has this trend more keenly been seen than now. Aravind Adiga's book The White Tiger won the Man Booker Prize award on October 15 and since thenbookstores around town have been left bereft of this certain book. A quick trip to a few stores reveals that it was not till the Man Booker Prize Shortlist was announced in September that sales of The White Tiger started picking up."

"We had the book in stock since February 2006,' says Mary John at Crossword bookstore. " Initially the sales were slow, we recommended it to people looking for new arrivals, but today we are out of stock!" Manney's bookstore in Camp experienced the same trend. Waiting for a new batch to arrive tomorrow, the last of their stock was picked up last evening when Aravind Adiga was announced winner.

At Landmark too, although the book has been re ordered every week since its release, their largest order was just placed yesterday. "We have sold 80 books so far," says Balbir Singhof Landmark, but tomorrow we will get our largest order for 200 copies of the book. We have been getting messages from customers as early as six thirty this morning, pre ordering their copy." Adiga has already said that his second book 'is almost done'. Rest assured, he certainly will not have to wait long for the next one to be picked off the shelves almost as soon as it gets there!

Heading: Jet episode ruffles wings of aviation aspirants - Indian Express
Content:
The state unit of the Congress party has decided to organise padyatras in all Assembly constituencies of the state from October 19 to 24 to mobilise people against the "anti-development" state government. The padyatras will culminate in dharnas before all collectorate offices on October 24.

State party president Rita Bahuguna Joshi said the party's slogan during the campaign will be "Vikas laao, Pradesh bachao, Mayawati hosh mein aao."

"With this slogan, our party wokers will meet people at the grassroots level, organise street plays, write on walls and explain how the government of Uttar Pradesh is hampering the future of the youth," she said.

Joshi said party workers had been told to defy prohibitory orders wherever these were imposed.

The campaign will be Congress' reply to the government's decision to take back the allotted land meant for a rail coach factory at Rae Bareli on the eve of its bhumi pujan ceremony. The state government had also denied permission to Congress president Sonia Gandhi to hold public meetings.

A section of Congressmen, especially the young ones, are, however, not impressed with the plan. They believe that a more aggressive "jail bharo" agitation would create a better impact.

A senior party leader said they would decide their next course of action on October 24.

Joshi described Chief Minister Mayawati's remarks against Sonia Gandhi, as "shameful, undignified and condemnable."

Reacting to the chief minister's allegation that the Central government was obstructing the state government's development schemes, Joshi said,

"The sate government is sitting on large sums of development funds. They have shifted around Rs 12,000 crore to the public ledger account following their inability to use it last year."

Heading: BJP’s youth wing demands ouster of Bangla migrants - Indian Express
Content:
The hopes to fly for young men and women from the states' smaller towns survived a fright late on Thursday night after Jet Airways announced that it would take back the 1,900 employees they had sacked on Wednesday.

The training academies that groom personnel for airlines are brimming with youngsters from places like Barabanki, Lakhimpur-Kheri, Bahraich and Gorakhpur.

Since Wednesday, students of the academies had not stopped receiving anxious calls from their parents and friends.

Shilpa Singh from Lakhimpur-Kheri is undergoing airhostess training. She said: "My family and friends are worried about my career. I had a tough time convincing my father, a school teacher, to let me pursue the career of an airhostess and not a teacher. I hope all airlines will be be careful in future." s

Rajiv Gupta from Barabanki said: "My father, a farmer, took a loan against his land to pay my fees and stay in Lucknow. I hoped to pay it back after getting a good job. I do not know what would be the scenario of the aviation industry, when I begin to look for placement."

Meerut resident Devankur Prakash, a student of an aviation academy in Agra, said his family was against his decision to prepare for the aviation industry instead of the Civil Services. "They are worried now. My institute says it is just a passing phase," he said, adding, "it is, however, reassuring that given the nature of our training we have job options in the corporate sector and the hotel industry."

Ravi Kumar Yadav from Moradabad, Sheela Jaswani from Kanpur and Rajvir Mishra from Gorakhpur are clueless about the present situation and avoiding to speak or meet their parents.

The institutes' officials are trying hard to smooth the ruffled feathers. Gitika Mehta, branch manager of AHA Airhostess Academy Pvt Ltd Lucknow, said the students were not a worried lot. "We have been telling them that the slump would be over soon. There are reports that even management students are looking for a career in aviation industry. Besides, the hospitality industry is only growing."

Heading: Ammo stocks depleted, UP Police bite the bullet - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janta Party Yuva Morcha (BJPYM) on Thursday staged a protest outside the Vidhan Sabha demanding verification of the increasing number of the madarsas in Lucknow.

The workers of the morcha also protested against growing number of illegal Bangladeshis residing in the city. The protest was led by the

National President of BJPYM, Pankaj Singh. Later, the protestors gave a memorandum to the Governor through the Additional District Magistrate of the city.

Addressing the party activists, Singh said that the government needs to throw out all the Bangaldeshi migrants from the state as they are a threat to the country's security.

He said Pakistani and Bangladeshi migrants have played a big role in increasing terror activities. He added that even police probes have revealed the role of migrants in terrorism and fake currency related rackets.

Others who were present on the occasion included state president of the Yuva Morcha Dayashankar Singh and district president Ramniwas Yadav.

Heading: At a court in Meerut, witness judge turns hostile in a 26-year-old case - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Police have not had much shooting practice in recent years because their request for ammunition has been turned down by successive governments.

Police officers said that their department had submitted a Rs 18 crore-budget for buying ammunition in 2006-07, but the government did not sanction it. A year later, the police again submitted an increased budget of Rs 22 crore that also met the same fate.

This year, a budget of Rs 18 crore and a supplementary budget of Rs 20 crore submitted to the government in June for purchasing ammunition is gathering dust, sources said.

When asked about the lack of ammunition in police department, Additional Director General of Police (Law & Order) Brij Lal said that ADG (Police Headquarters) S P Srivastava is dealing with the matter. Srivastava admitted, "Our ammunition stocks are depleted but we are managing it somehow."

A senior police office said: "Usually, the department maintains ammunition stock that can last for a year but in the absence of funds for the last three years, we are left with little ammo."

The scarcity has hit both the policing and shooting practice sessions, which are compulsory for every junior-level policemen. 

A senior IPS officer said: "The state police have nearly 1.25 lakh personnel up to the rank of inspector. A one-month shooting session in a year is compulsory for each of them."

Senior superintendent of police of a district said: "Shooting practice in Kanpur, Allahabad, Varanasi, Agra and Lucknow is somehow being managed, but it has almost come to a halt in other 65 districts of the state."

Another senior police officer said: "Districts like Azamgarh, Balia, Mirzapur, Chitrakoot and Banda have not received ammunition even for policing for almost two years."

Srivastava, however, tried to shrug it off and said: "There is a crisis in many departments and the police is no exception. The force, nevertheless, has managed to perform better in the present regime."  He added, "The department recently received Rs 8 crore for buying ammunition under the head of modernisation of the police force."

Srivastava also said, "Arranging funds for ammunition is a joint responsibility of the Central and the state governments. While the Centre contributes 75 per cent of the fund, the state provides 25 per cent." He, however, could not explain why the police have not received funds for the last three years.

Heading: Maya learnt of Rae Bareli land transfer 4 days before Sonia visit - Indian Express
Content: The Reserve Bank has further relaxed banking norms by allowing holders of certain types of savings bonds to raise funds by pledging the government papers as collateral with cooperative banks.  Following the decision, the holders of savings bonds will be able to borrow money for their needs from the urban cooperative banks. The central bank in a communication to all cooperative banks said that 7 per cent saving bonds, 2002, 6.5 per cent saving bonds, 2003, and 8 per cent savings (taxable) bonds, 2003, can be pledged as collaterals for obtaining loans. "The holders of...bonds will be entitled to create, pledge or hypothecation or lien in favour of scheduled banks in accordance with the Government Securities Act," the RBI said. Earlier, savings bonds were not eligible as collateral for loans from banks, financial institutions and non-banking financial companies.

Heading: Lucknow Bypass to become operational in seven months - Indian Express
Content:
It now transpires that till the day she gave orders for the cancellation of land allotment for a rail coach factory in Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mayawati had no idea that the state land revenue department had gone ahead and transferred 261.25 hectares to the Railways for the project.

Documents with The Indian Express show that the land allotment — the cancellation of which has pitted Mayawati against Congress president and Rae Bareli MP Sonia Gandhi — was cleared this May by then Principal Secretary (Revenue) Balwinder Kumar without the consent of the state cabinet which had only given in-principle approval for it a year earlier.

Mayawati learnt of the allotment just four days before Sonia Gandhi was to land in Rae Bareli for the bhoomi pujan at the project site on October 14. Furious that it had been done without cabinet approval, the Chief Minister pulled up senior bureaucrats and instructed that the allotment be cancelled. Balwinder Kumar was removed from his post on October 13.

The Central request for a rail coach factory at the site came in February 2007. On July 11, 2007, the Mayawati government gave in-principle approval to allot land for the factory.

Since the factory would require an additional 72 hectares of gram sabha land in Rae Bareli, Balwinder Kumar recorded in April, 2008 that the land transfer needed the approval of the state cabinet. But the very next month, Kumar made another jotting on the file that he had "erroneously" written that the land transfer matter be referred to the state cabinet. He noted there was no need to take state cabinet approval since the administration was empowered to take this decision. This was the green signal for allotment of land to the Railways.

When contacted, Balwinder Kumar admitted he had "erroneously recommended the matter to be taken before the cabinet which was not needed as resumption cases are sorted out at the level of district magistrate and commissioners".

Heading: Export industry, especially leather, feels US recession chill - Indian Express
Content:
Work on the 23-km Lucknow Bypass, also called Amar Shaheed Path, which was stalled for the last eight months, will resume from November 15. A new contractor for the project is likely to be finalised soon.

National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) officials say 14-km stretch of road will be opened to traffic within six months and the rest in another one year.

The project aims to ease the traffic on Lucknow roads by providing a diversion to the long-distance vehicles. Once the bypass gets operational, the traffic from Kanpur to Rae Bareli, Sultanpur and Faizabad, or vice versa will not have to enter the city.  

Construction of the four-lane bypass was started in August 2001 to connect the Amausi Airport at NH-25 with Chinhat on NH-28, also known as Faizabad Road.

Initially, the project cost was estimated at Rs 159.8 crore. But after delay by the Lucknow Development Authority in acquiring the land and some changes in the project design, it was revised to Rs 220 crore.

Two contractors, Prakash and Atlanta, were given the contract to complete the work by August 2004.   

But they missed the deadline and it was extended to November 2006. Project Director M K Jain said, "Since they again failed to execute the project in time, NHAI terminated their contract in March 2008." 

Under the original plan, Shaheed Path was to have 10 underpasses, two bridges, three railway overbridges and a 1.2 km flyover. Two more underpasses were later included in the project.

"The additional construction and the delay pushed up the cost by Rs 113 crore," said Jain.

The new underpasses will be constructed in Gomti Nagar Extension and near Sultanpur Road, site of a proposed super-specialty hospital.

Project Manager C M Dwivedi said: "The 14-km stretch from Amausi to Sultanpur Road is almost complete, except an underpass. We are hiring a new contractor, who will have to ready this stretch for traffic in six months, while the remaining part will have to be completed in another one year."

Amar Shaheed Path will be connected with Faizabad Road near Chinhat where an under-construction flyover, a part of the East-West Corridor, had collapsed last month.

"If the work is completed on time, the project will be ready for traffic in the next 18 months." Dwivedi said.

Heading: To dent SP vote bank, Maya will hold OBC convention - Indian Express
Content:
The economic slowdown in US and Europe has hit the state's leather industry hard. In spite of a cheaper rupee, the demand is falling, leaving the exporters petrified.

So far, the leather industry, concentrated in Kanpur and Agra, had an annual revenue of Rs 4,500 crore and enjoyed an annual growth of 18 to 20 per cent. But this year, there is an altogether a different story with the industry sliding down.

Maqsood Alam, proprieter of Model Tanners India (P) Ltd, blamed the global recession behind it.

Kanpur has around 100 leather units of which 95 per cent are small and medium entrepreneurs and the rest are big leather industries. "But now the work in many factories are coming to a halt," said Alam. Many foreign buyers have asked the factories to stop the supply.

"We are facing 10 per cent losses on goods we have already shipped, as these were booked at the rate when the one dollar was equal to Rs 40 or 42. In many cases, goods are lying at ports and the buyers are not releasing the consignments," he added.

The sudden drop in demand has led to accumulation of stocks which can't be sold. The products are made according to standards and specifications in Europe and America, of which there is not much demand in India.

"I am waiting for Diwali when I will give my labourers bonus and request them to return to their homes and join work only when I would be able to call them," Alam said, underlining his desperation. Iftikhar-ul-Amin of UP Leather Industries Association said that appreciation of the dollar did not because the orders were drying up. "What has caused the situation is the uncertainty about the future in general," Amin said.

Another leather product exporter, Farooq Omar of Riding Home, said, "This is the worst period that the leather export industry has faced in the last 15 to 20 years."

Other export industries of Uttar Pradesh like silk, carpets and brassware are also facing a similar situation, said Rajiv Agarwal, president of the Eastern UP Exporters' Association. The carpet belt of Bhadohi and Khamaria, which has an annual turnover of Rs 4,000 to 5,000 crore, is going through severe crisis, Aggarwal said.

Hardly any buyer at Noida Expo Mart
Many exporters of the state, who are not taking part in India Expo Mart being held in Noida, are already getting the taste of market slump. "There used be over 1,500 big buyers from the US every time to this event, but this year the number has gone down to around 50," said Rikesh Kumar, president of the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts. This handicraft fair is held in the state twice a year to provide a platform to the manufacturers in the state to hold direct interaction with buyers. Incidentally, 65 per cent of the total handicraft export of India is from UP. In the last four days, the fair has attracted only one-fourth of buyers that it usually witnesses, said an industrialist. "The situation is especially bad for luxury items," said Kumar, adding, "The export industry is going through hibernation where everyone wants to maintain a status quo because of uncertainty".

Heading: Central agency slams chief minister for ignoring OBC Muslims - Indian Express
Content:
BSP feels Dalit-Brahmin combination not enough to win LS polls

After making efforts to woo the Muslims, Chief Minister Mayawati is now seeking to bring members of the Other Backward Classes into the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) fold. The party aims to make inroad into the OBC's votebank of its rival Samajwadi Party in the state.

On October 18, the BSP will organise a convention on "Problems of Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST) and Other Backward Castes (OBC): its causes and solution" in Lucknow. Sources said the party will also hold a convention to woo upper castes voters.

BSP insiders feel that the presence of SC, ST and OBC on one platform under the banner of the BSP would help Mayawati to examine the compatibility of OBCs with existing SC/ST members of the party.  

"This will be a new experiment in state politics. In several parts of the state, different constituents of the OBCs are engaged in a political war of supremacy with the SCs," said a BSP MLA, explaining the importance of the convention is to jointly discuss the problems of both the groups on one platform.

"The party will project Mines and Panchayat Raj Minister Babu Singh Kushwaha as its OBC face at the convention," said another MLA.

He added while SC/ST forms the base of BSP, OBCs have been accommodated in almost every political party. "The BSP wants to capture the votebank of SP, which has a good support of OBC in the state," he said.  

BSP sources said the party is not eying for the total support of all the OBC groups. Since the party had successfully experimented with the Dalit-Brahmin combination in the last Assembly elections, it is now planning to get associated with small groups, besides the Kushwahas and the Kurmi voters.

Party sources felt the Dalit-Brahmin combination is not enough to ensure considerable seats for the BSP in the state.

"Hence, the CM is exploring every possibility for the forthcoming parliamentary elections," said another BSP MLA.

Sources said the party has invited representatives of almost every OBC group from all the parliamentary constituencies of the state to the convention. Before the last Assembly elections, the BSP had formed bhaichara committees within the party on the basis of caste lines across the state.

"Party functionaries at all the levels- right from the booth to zonal level- were asked to identify the influential people within each caste in their areas. The party has invited such people of various OBC groups at the convention," said an MLA.

By holding the convention, the party is also trying to identify the basic problems of various caste groups.

"The CM will raise these issues during her campaign for the Lok Sabha Elections in the respective areas," party sources said.

India is not a jagir of Congress: BSP
A day after Congress leaders said their workers can stop Chief Minister Mayawati from travelling across the country, the ruling BSP hit back on Thursday. A statement released by the party said: "The country is not a jagir (property) of the Congress Party."

The state government had earlier enforced Section 144 in Rae Bareli during UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi's visit. Gandhi had dared Mayawati to put her in jail.

BSP's state unit president Swami Prasad Maurya today termed the last salvo from the Congress as "irresponsible and unconstitutional." Maurya said the threat that Mayawati would not be allowed to travel could provoke BSP workers. He added. developments of Rae Bareli and Amethi could not be described development of Uttar Pradesh. The release also said the previous government had provided land for setting up 20 factories in Rae Bareli, out of which only 9 factories are functional. According to Maurya, 192 acres of land is of no use due to the closure of the factories in Rae Bareli. In Amethi, seven factories have been closed and so 862 acres of land remains without use, the release said.— ENS

Heading: PU youth festival concludes, hosts steal the show - Indian Express
Content:
National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) said the Mayawati government has been indifferent towards the backwards among the Muslims, leading to the overall decline of the community in all the spheres of life.

Criticising the state government, NCBC member Abdul Azizi said: "The condition of backward Muslims in the state is poor and the present government has done nothing to uplift their social, economic and educational status."

He pointed out that within the UP Backward Classes Commission, there are 17 members but not a single belong to the Muslim community, while out of 22 members of UP Minority Commission, only six are Muslims.

"Of the total Muslim population in UP, 85 per cent come under the backward classes as per the Mandal commission report," he added.

"UP chief minister claims to be heading a sarvajan samaj sarkar but the backwards among Muslims have been denied representation in all the spheres of polity," Azizi said.

"Students belonging to backward Muslim castes have been denied even education loans and scholarships," Azizi added.

The NCBC member further said:

"A recent advertisement of the UP government claiming welfare measures for all sections of the society did not make any mention of the OBCs among Muslims."

He also criticised the commercial banks and said: "There are clear guidelines by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to provide 15 per cent of priority sector loans to minorities, but it is not being implemented in UP."

Azizi said against the norm of one hostel in each tehsil for students of backward classes, UP has only one hostel in a district.

Heading: Dengue cases touch 1729, officials see no early respite - Indian Express
Content:
The five-day Youth and Heritage Festival of Zone B of the Panjab University, which came to an end on Thursday, established the Government College for Women in a cut above the rest in literary events.

While they bagged most of the literary events, Ramgarhia Girls College performed well in the musical programmes.

On the other hand, Master Tara Singh Memorial College for Women won most of the events in the 'ladies traditional category'.

In dramatics, Guru Nanak Girls College bagged the first prizes in drama and histrionics out of the four events in the category.

On the concluding day, students of 11 colleges presented scintillating performances in various forms of dance, especially giddha, to enthral the audiences at Guru Nanak Girls College (GNGC), Model Town.

Giddha, the folk dance of the state, mesmerised the audiences who kept on clapping throughout the event. The competition was won by hosts GNGC, while the second position was taken by the Government College for Women.

Earlier in the festival, the host college had also won the first prize in the drama competition based on the theme of Mirza Sahiba.

The last day began with classical dance competition followed by group dance and giddha. Ramgarhia Girls College won in the classical dance and group dance categories.

Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang, was the chief guest on the concluding day. He was accompanied by wife Dr Neeta D Kang, the Head of Department of Research and Innovations, CMCH. The V-C praised the college authorities for making the festival a success.

Noted Punjabi singer Amarinder Gill also graced the occasion and regaled the audience with the rendering of one of his popular numbers.

Heading: LIC told to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation - Indian Express
Content:
With bed strength at several hospitals getting exhausted, the total number of dengue patients rose to a whopping 1,729 on Thursday. Health officials suspect that the disease may continue to spread till the end of this month.

The cases belonging to the district alone have reached 1,011, while 441 patients diagnosed in the district hospitals are from other districts and 277 cases are placed under the suspected category.

On Thursday, 103 fresh cases were added to yesterday's tally of 908 confirmed cases in the district. While the Dayanand Medical College Hospital (DMCH) registered 59 cases, Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) reported 26 new cases. Mohan Dai Oswal Cancer Hospital recorded 10 patients and SPS Apollo Hospitals reported five. Over 100 fresh dengue cases are being reported per day in the last few days in the district. Nearly 1,400 dengue patients have been admitted at the DMCH and the CMCH so far, with a major chunk undergoing treatment at the DMCH.

Health officials said the number was expected to subside once the temperature decreased. "Since the weather has been fluctuating, the vector mosquito received a prolonged period of optimum temperature for its growth," said an official. It is now predicted that the cases may increase further by the end of the month.

Heading: Toxicology meet starts at GADVASU - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum has directed Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) to pay Rs 50,000 along with interest at the rate of nine per cent, and Rs 10,000 as compensation to an aggrieved consumer for thrusting unnecessary litigation on her.

Sukhdeep Kaur, a resident of Mohanpur, in Khanna tehsil of Ludhiana district, had filed a complaint accusing the insurance company of refusing her claims after her husband Sukhdev Singh died in a road accident.

According to her, Sukhdev had taken a policy of Rs 50,000 from the LIC. Doctors from the insurance company had examined him before giving them the policy.

The policy was issued promising accidental benefits equal to the insurance amount. Sukhdev, who used to work as a linesman with the PSEB department, was posted at Khatra village. On June 16, 2006, he met with a road accident and passed away.

Sukhdeep then, asked LIC to pay her the claim amount. But, the insurance company refused the claim on flimsy grounds.

The president of the forum accepted the complaint and held that the consumer had successfully proved her case and the insurance company's denial of the claim was not justified.

Heading: Take steps to tackle cyber terrorism, Grewal urges President - Indian Express
Content:
The 28th annual conference of Society of Toxicology (STOX), India, and international symposium on "Monitoring and modulating global resources of environmental and food contaminants: Nature versus chemicals" kicked off at Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University here today. 200 delegates from all over India and abroad are teking part in the conference.

Toxicology is emerging as one of the most important discipline of bio-medical sciences. All of us know that today we are living in a sea of man-made chemicals. Many of these chemicals have improved our living standards by providing facilities which were not known earlier but they have also added to the diseases and miseries not earlier known to man-kind. We see finely tuned environment that we utterly depend upon fading away before our eyes due to large-scale contamination of air, water and food. There is a dire need to check it by creating awareness among public about the hazards of man-made chemicals and ultimately reducing their use.

Dr Hardyal Singh, Ex-director, Research and Medical Education, Punjab, was the chief guest of the day while Dr V. K. Taneja, Vice-Chancellor, GADVASU, presided over the function.

Dr Simrat Sagar Singh, Dean, College of Veterinary Science, welcomed the delegates, guests and participants. The report of the society was presented by Dr P. V. Mohanan, General Secretary, STOX. This was followed by award-presenting ceremony.

On this occasion, a compendium of abstracts to be presented during the conference, a compilation of summary of post-graduate research and current volume of the Toxicology International Journal were released by the chief guest, Dr Hardyal Singh. Four retired professors of the alumni of the Department of Pharmacology & Toxicology, College of Veterinary Science, GADVASU, were honoured for their dedication towards teaching and research and their significant contributions in the field of toxicology.

President, STOX, Dr K. S. Rao addressed the gathering and suggested means and ways for improvement of education in the field of toxicology. He focussed on the need of training for the students and research workers on Good Laboratory Practices.

Dr Hardyal Singh highlighted the importance of adverse effect of drugs. He stressed the optimisation of the therapeutic use of drugs for better clinical outcome and safety of human health, which is a primary concern for the present society.

Dr Singh informed that CFL, which is promoted as electricity saver, is also affecting our environment and it contains mercury which is quite toxic. Mobile phones have thermal effect on the users which can affect the nervous system of the users.

Dr Shiv Chopra, an eminent scientist, and fellow of WHO from Canada, stressed that everything people eat must be organically grown.

Dr. V. K. Taneja expressed concern on environmental pollution and its impact on human and animal health. He advocated rational use of pesticides and agro-chemicals for safeguarding the health of future generations. Dr H. S. Sandhu, organizing secretary, STOX-2008, proposed the vote-of-thanks.

Heading: Meet on genetically modified food held - Indian Express
Content:
Sukhminderpal Singh Grewal, state president of the Punjab BJP Investor Cell, has urged the President, Partibha Patil to ensure that remedial measures to tackle cyber terrorism.

In a letter sent to Patil, Grewal said that recent terrorist attacks in India spoke volumes of ignorance of the governments over misuse of information technology by the terrorists. "Terrorists are openly using websites to propagate hatred through inflammatory articles, pictures and videos among people motivating them to raise funds, organise advocacy and volunteer terror activities for these outfits. Social networking sites are helping these perpetrators to communicate, collaborate and network with the like-minded people. Search engines index these websites and inadvertently help these terror outfits by routing internet users to these websites," he added.

Grewal said that terrorists can now plan and execute terror activities without apprehending arrest as emerging technologies provide substantial information about vital demographic know-how and even real time GPS tracking. technologies such as voice-over IP and Chinese phones without any IMEI number or a forged IMEI number help them to communicate and collaborate with their peers without fearing any identity loss.

"Terrorists have been using advanced cryptographic techniques to encode their messages into photos and share these normal-looking photos with their bosses sitting in neighbouring countries through websites without fearing the message being decoded by intelligence agencies," he said.

Grewal demanded that governments should immediately take remedial measures to ensure that these terror outfits should not misuse internet and websites run by these terror outfits should immediately be blocked.

Heading: Ryan wins best school trophy - Indian Express
Content:
A seminar on "Safety and security of health and food in the era of genetically modified foods" organised by the Indian Medical Association, Ludhiana, in association with Environmental Health Action Group, an associate of Kheti Virasat Mission at IMA House, expressed concern at the health risk of the Genetically Modified Crops which are now being introduced in our country.

These products are potential risk to our health through their direct effect as well as through the effect on the eco-system around us. Dr Shiv Chopra, a renowned scientist and microbiologist, while speaking on the occasion, pointed out that only a few countries using Genetically Engineered Food - USA, Canada and Argentina account for 96% of World's Genetically Engineered crops.

He said several species in nature came up and got mutated through natural means. "But in genetically engineered crops, the basic genetic structure of the organism is changes by introducing genes from other species like viruses, bacteria and insects etc. This changes the basic protein structure of the organism. This causes allergies to the individual from products hitherto unknown to cause allergies to him. That is why the European Union and most of the South American countries have by and large banned the production and sale of these products in their countries. Even the British Medical Association called for moratorium on transgenic plantations in 1999."

The claims of the companies propagating the GMO products that nutritional value of the GM crops is higher is untrue as these may marginally supplement the proteins or vitamins. For example to meet the protein requirement from GM potatoes a child would need to consume 1.5 kg of potatoes per day. Likewise a person would have to consume 9 Kg of GM Golden Rice to meet the same requirement of Vitamin A as can be met with by consuming just 2 carrots a day.

Only the Monsanto company accounts for 93 per cent of GM Crops grown. In the fields the pollens from the GM Crops pollute the other crops by over crossing. This affects the indigenous varieties which are most suited to the area and changes their character. These crops develop unknown characters in the second and third generation.

Dr L S Chawla Patron IMA Ludhiana and National President IDPD said that the protagonists of GM Crops must prove the sustainability of these products as several animal trials have shown that the offspring of rats fed on GM Crops have stunted growth. Dr.Arun Mitra - President IMA Ludhiana said that there is need to spread awareness on the subject and mobilize people on the issue to resist the entry of Monsanto etc. in our country.

Heading: From stand-point of food, world is one civilisation: V-C - Indian Express
Content:
Ishpuneet Chug of Class VIII of Ryan International School won the second prize in a poster-making competition held at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital here today. Ryan International School also won the best school trophy.

The theme of the competition was "Organ donation — gift of life." Twelve students from Ryan International School participated in the contest.

According to Dr Augustine Pinto, chairman of Ryan Group of Institutions, "Various forms of art are the best medium to influence people and create awareness among them." The students made lovely and informative posters. Their work demonstrated they understood the motive of the competition. Gurpreet Kaur Sandhu, the school principal, encouraged the students to participate in such contests to hone their artistic skills.

Heading: ‘Innovation has become necessary tool for growth’ - Indian Express
Content:
Different aspects of food insecurity were discussed at a function held at the PAU to celebrate the World Food Day today. The event was organised by the PAU Science Club in association with different departments of PAU. PAU Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang was the chief guest.

In his remarks, Dr Kang said that World Food Day was observed throughout the world by about 150 countries adding that the event held a great significance as the number of hungry people was on the rise in the world. He said that developmental plans addressing the food insecurity problem faced by children, women and other vulnerable communities were needed to be put in place by the governments. Dr Kang said that the theme of World Food Day included food security and challenges of climate change and bio-diversity. He said that from the stand-point of food, world was one civilization.

On this occasion, post-graduate students of different departments of PAU including Jyoti Jha, Ruchika Joshi (Food Science and Technology), Rachna Srivastava, Navita Viveky (Foods and Nutrition), Saloni (Microbiology), Prem Kashyap (Plant Pathology), Lovepreet Singh Shergil (Agronomy), Inderpal Singh (Economics and Sociology), Raghupati (Plant Breeding and Genetics), Dhruv Juyal (Processing and Food Engineering) deliberated on the theme of "Food Security" highlighting the role of their respective departments.

The issues of cereal fortification, human nutrition, obesity, functional foods, food-borne illnesses, emerging food-borne pathogens, packaging of horticultural foods etc., were also discussed. It emerged that obesity was a multi-factorial problem linked with nutritional, environmental and behavioral factors.

The speakers highlighted that more than 30% fruits and vegetables were lost due to post-harvest problems, which could feed 232 million people. He said cost-effective technologies, increasing population, decreasing productivity and shrinking cultivated area were aggravating the food-insecurity problem. Bio-fortification of crops with micro-nutrients and vitamins could be useful for nutritional security, said a speaker, adding that golden rice had 23 times more beta-carotene than normal rice. Giving illustration of involvement of different countries in the development and popularization of wheat varieties leading to ushering in of green revolution of the country, concern over intellectual property right was also discussed.

The Dean, Post-graduate Studies, Dr S.K. Mann said that the event was celebrated at the PAU to create awareness about the problem of food insecurity. Dr Neelam Grewal, Dean, College of Home Science, in her remarks said that the tripod of food security involved food availability, accessibility and utilization adding that PAU was making endeavours to address the problem through sustainable agriculture. Need-based education programmes were also important for skill development and creating awareness among students, said she.

An inter-school quiz on nutrition was organised wherein teams of students from Govt High School, Ayali Khurd (team A), Govt Senior Secondary School, Haibowal Khurd (team B), Govt Senior Secondary School, PAU, Ludhiana (team C) and Govt Middle School, Haibowal Kalan (team D) participated.

The first, second and third positions were won by team B, team C and team D and A (bracketed), respectively. The winning team members and speakers while deliberating on food security were awarded certificates and prizes. An exhibition of posters prepared by students, relating to different aspects of World Food Day, was arranged on the occasion. The vote of thanks was proposed by Dr Neelam Setia.

Heading: Challenges facing agriculture discussed at farmers’ meet - Indian Express
Content:
"Innovation will be the necessity for social and economical growth of the nation in future. We live and die through relative innovation. The world has changed because of innovation only. Science is responsible for all the innovations we feel around," remarked Srinivasan K. Swamy, President, All India Management Association (AIMA), New Delhi, while delivering his lecture to the members of Ludhiana Management Association (LMA) at Hotel Park Plaza here on Wednesday evening.

Swamy was accompanied by Uma Oberoi, Director, AIMA. The topic of the lecture was "Innovation". Dr. K.N.S. Kang, General Secretary, LMA, welcomed all the guests, members and speakers on the occasion. V.K. Goyal, Senior Vice-President, LMA, explained the activities of the association to the president of AIMA and introduced the speaker to the audience.

While introducing the topic, Dr K.N.S. Kang, General Secretary, LMA, said, "Innovations can take place in all the business activities and there is a dire need at present to innovate products, processes and marketing in the field of business. Today's organisations have already innovated new methods of HR management as well. Innovation will be life-blood of the business in future"

Swamy said that inventions were indeed different from innovation, unless the invention was not offered to the public. If the invention improved some product, process or service for the public, then that invention transforms into an innovation. Science is mainly responsible for all inventions which are finally transformed into innovations. Swamy said that broadly saying there were four types of innovations, which lead the business world namely fundamental innovations, outstanding innovations, relative innovations and process innovations. Swamy said the business organisations should stress more on relative and process-based innovations which can enhance the business competitiveness.

Swamy said that telephone was a fundamental innovation and internet/fax/SMS facilities in mobile telephones were an evident example of outstanding innovation. Swamy quoted an example of Apple Computers which gave cut-throat competition to Sony, IBM, HP etc. by introducing relative innovation in computer manufacturing.

Swamy gave example of Tatas, Hindalco, Hero group for their excellence in process innovation. He said that these companies had innovated the business processes and as a result had become leaders of the market. At the end of the lecture, Swamy explained the objectives of AIMA and its activities.

While delivering his presidential remarks, Anil Kumar, president, LMA, thanked the speaker, guests and members. Kumar said the future of many businesses would depend on their ability to innovate. Kumar stressed that the process-based innovations should be encouraged more by the industry.

Heading: New technique gives hope to kidney patients - Indian Express
Content:
"We need to be self-sufficient in food," said Dr. N.S. Malhi, Director of Extension Education, while speaking to the gathering of farmers and farm women at Bharsingwala village in Jalandhar district, adding that there were many constraints in the face of our contemporary agriculture. He mentioned that soils were becoming deficient in nutrients and funds available for agricultural research were meagre.

Dr Malhi said that food processing and value addition to food stuffs needed to be encouraged so as to enable farmers to get more income. The event was organised jointly by PAU Directorate of Extension Education and KRIBHCO. Dr Malhi said that Punjab agriculture largely relied on rice-wheat and efforts were being made to address food and nutritional security. He mentioned that the PAU-201 variety of paddy was nutritionally rich but people were reluctant to appreciate it on account of its colour.

"Winners of various competitions such as food products prepared by women, noodles making and healthy baby competitions were given prizes," said Dr Neelam Mahajan, coordinator of the programme.

The importance of balanced diet and use of pulses were highlighted. Dr Pushpinder Singh Ranote, while demonstrating preparation of apple chutney and squash, provided tips on preservation of fruits and vegetables. Dr Aggarwal from IGMRI advised the gathering to protect grains against infestation of storage pests by following expert advice.

Dr Mittal from Verka milk plant spoke on hygienic handling of milk and milk products to prevent growth of harmful bacteria. Formation of self-help groups for collection and distribution of milk was suggested.

Dr Mahajan informed that an exhibition was organised on the occasion on scientific storage of grains, preservation of fruits and vegetables, effects of food adulteration, educational toys, candles, kitchen garden and balanced nutrition.

Heading: Investiture ceremony held at BCM - Indian Express
Content:
RG Stone and Super Speciality Hospital, part of the RG Stone Hospital Chain for Urology & Laparoscopy, announced the successful treatment of three patients suffering from kidney stones by Holmium Laser Flexible Ureteroscopy here today.

All three patients were unsuitable candidates for treatment by older techniques and had resigned themselves to their disease due to the unavailability of the Holmium Laser Flexible Ureteroscopy in the region till recently. Now, with the availability of the technology and expertise at RG Stone Hospital, the patients got a new lease on life when Dr. Anand Sehgal, M.Ch. (Urology) and Chief Endoscopic & Laparoscopic Urologist, RG Stone and Super Speciality Hospital, successfully operated upon them.

Holmium Laser Flexible Ureteroscopy is the latest Minimally Invasive technique for treating Kidney Stones utilizing the natural urinary passage. The Flexible Ureteroscope, an endoscope of very small caliber, is introduced through ureter into the kidney, said Dr Anand Sehgal of the hospital, adding that RG Stone and Super Speciality Hospital in the city is the only institute in Punjab to possess the Holmium Laser Flexible Ureteroscopy, which is widely recognized as the latest & most advanced treatment for Kidney Stones available today.

"This endoscope can visualize stones in any part of the kidney. Stones are fragmented using the Holmium Laser. The laser fragments the stones into sand like particles, which are then flushed out through the natural urinary passage. As Holmium Laser Flexible Ureteroscopy can fragment stones of all composition with very high precision, it is widely considered the most effective treatment for Kidney Stones. Before the advent of the Holmium Laser Flexible Ureteroscopy, there were a number of techniques used for the treatment of Kidney Stones."

Heading: Verka boss unearths ‘milk scam’ - Indian Express
Content:
BCM Arya Model Senior Secondary School, Shastri Nagar, organised an investitute ceremony on Thursday. B.D. Arora, a prominent advocate of the city, was the chief guest on this occasion. The programme started with a national song.

Paramjit Kaur, the school principal, urged the students to be enterprising, optimistic and enthusiastic as well as role models for juniors. She also blessed the prefects and proctors on this occasion. While introducing the new office-bearers, their achievements in various curricular and co-curricular fields were also highlighted.

After dispending over sashes and badges, flags of four houses along with the prestigious school flag were handed over to the respective captains. Formal avowal was asserted by the prefects with Surinder Kaur, Chief Proctor.

On this occasion, the chief guest congratulated the selected students and motivated them to scale new heights. Gaurav Jhamb and Ekta, were selected as head boy and head girl.

Heading: Simi claims 4th leg - Indian Express
Content:
The Chairman of Verka Milk Plant, Ludhiana, today claimed to have unearthed a "milk scam." According to Ajmer Singh, chairman of the milk plant, supplies from Ludhiana plant used to go to Delhi but on the way, the vehicles were stopped at Murthal where milk used to be stole .

Ajmer Singh said, "Daily 40,000 litres supply used to go via Sukhwinder Transport Company and last week, I caught red-handed people stealing milk from the tankers. Owner of Deepak Dhaba was also hand in glove."

Singh has got an FIR registered against the transport company, owner of Deepak Dhaba and one Bittu, the kingpin behind this scam. Ali Khan, driver of a tempo in which milk was being transferred was arrested on the spot. He said more than 15,000 litres of milk was being stolen daily and water used to be mixed to maintain quantity.

Heading: Servant drugs family, nabbed later with accomplices - Indian Express
Content:
Simi Mehra played another excellent round of 2 under 70 to win the 4th leg of the DLF Women's Professional Golf Tour with a three day total of 4 under 212, a clear 29 shots ahead of her nearest rival.

Simi's round consisted of birdies on the 2nd, 8th, 13th, 14th and 18th holes with bogeys on the 10th, 11th and 15th holes. Simi hit 13 greens in regulation and had 29 putts.

Finishing in second position is Kolkata's Vandana Agarwal, who is a rookie on the Tour with a three day total of 241 followed closely by Nalini Singh who finished third at 242 for the tournament. Playing in the leader group, Sharmila Nicollet maintained display of excellent golf as she returned a card of 1 over 73 to take her three day total to 4 over 220, beating Shweta Galande by 13 shots to win the Amateur Category.

Heading: Fateh Ali had made trips to China and Dubai: Police - Indian Express
Content:
Three members of a family were taken ill after their servant served them drug-laced food in order to steal cash and valuables from the house on Wednesday night.

The three, residents of Subhash Nagar, were admitted to the CMC Hospital after falling unconscious. However, the servant did not succeed in his attempt as he, along with two of his accomplices, was caught by the neighbours and handed over to the police.

The three victims were identified as Kapil Dawar, a local businessman, his wife Riya Dawar and their daughter Priyagya Dawar. Kapil is the nephew of former parliamentary secretary and Congress leader Surinder Dawar.

According to sources, the family had hired Rajesh as domestic servant nearly 15 days ago. Last night, after serving dinner to the family, Rajesh went out saying he had some urgent work.

After some time, Kapil also left for market, and soon he started vomiting. He immediately called up his elder brother Sanjeev Dawar, who also lives in the same house. Sanjeev, who was at work, rushed to the house to get a vehicle to pick up his brother. When he reached home, he found his sister-in-law Riya and niece Priyagya also vomiting.

He came out and saw Rajesh roaming around in the street. With the help of other residents, Sanjeev nabbed Rajesh. When question sternly, the servant confessed to have served drug-laced food for robbery purpose.

Rajesh also told them that he was part of a five-member gang which had committed similar thefts at Jaipur, Kolkata and Zira. Sanjeev asked him to call up his accomplices on their cellphones, and when two members came to the spot, the people nabbed them. The trio was later handed over to the Division 4 police.

In the mean time, Kapil, his wife and daughter were rushed to the hospital. Their condition has been declared out of danger.

Area DSP Gurdeep Singh said they are investigating the matter. However, the police had not announced the arrest of the servant and his accomplices till this report was filed.

Heading: Kolkata crew too joins hands with airport workers’ union against Jet’s ‘illegal’ termination - Indian Express
Content:
During his stay in Kolkata, dreaded Bangladeshi criminal Fateh Ali alias Subrata Bayen, who was arrested on Monday from his residence on Palm Avenue, had made five trips to China and Dubai.

Sources in the West Bengal Police said Ali was in the process of building a smuggling network, dealing mostly in electronic goods.

"Ali had been smuggling Chinese-made electronic goods into India via Nepal. It was to supervise these deals, as well as to make new contacts, that he had been to China. His visit to Dubai, too, was for the same purpose, as there is a ready market for illegal electronic goods in the region. We believe his first trip to China was funded by a Bangladeshi politician from the BNP," sources said.

Additional Commissioner of Police Rajiv Kumar, who heads the Kolkata Police's Special Task Force that tracked Ali to Palm Avenue, said Ali had recently been to China and had entered India through China and Nepal after escaping from Bangladesh.

Investigators say Ali left his home country in 2005 following the bomb blast at Awami League leader Sheikh Hasina's rally that killed 24 people. Ali is said to be linked to the blast.

Ali's bid to put together multiple business ventures also led him to invest in real estate, TV and film production.

Apart from the four-storeyed building that he constructed after coming to Kolkata, investigators said he had also purchased a flat in Thakurpukur.

Initial investigations have shown that he had invested in production of TV serials and had an affair with a starlet.

Already, his links with Bangla politicians are being investigated. Ali, who had formed the dreaded "Seven Star" gang in Bangladesh, was associated with Bangladeshi criminals Tokai Sagar, Kala Jahangir, Prokash, Kamrul Hasan alias Chhoto Hannan, Imam Hussain, Jabbar Munna, Manik, Mollah Masud and Aga Shamim.

Most are suspected to be staying in India and the police are on the look out for them.

Ali's residence on Palm Avenue, sources added, was reconstructed after demolishing an old building that had been originally constructed on the property.

The paperwork for purchasing the property had been facilitated by local contacts, they said.
