On Wednesday, 5.9 kilos of ivory was seized by the state forest department from Laldhang division in Uttarakhand, close to Rajaji National Park. One person, a middleman, has been arrested.

Officials from the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) point out that the poaching of elephant molars (back teeth) is a first time occurence and may signify a rise in the general trend of elephant poaching. "Taking out elephant molars is a very time consuming and laborious process. This means two things, firstly the elephant would certainly have been killed to remove molars, and secondly the poachers would have been very familiar with the routes taken by the elephants. This generally indicates a rise in poaching," says Ramesh Pandey of the WCCB. He also points out that the two seizures may be linked, with the source elephants coming from Corbett Tiger Reserve or Rajaji.

Heading: A day after CEC nod, Omar ‘evasive’ on poll timing - Indian Express
Content:
The Kerala Police which probed into the removal of two Muslim policemen from the security duty of BJP leader L K Advani during his Kozhikode visit on Tuesday, found little religious discrimination in it and gave a clean chit to the NSG. Muslim organisation had alleged religious discrimination when two Muslim police drivers had been removed from the motorcade of Advani.

Additional DGP K S Jang Pangi, who investigated into the incident, said that the removal of the policemen was only an administrative mistake that should not have happened. "The National Security Guard (NSG) should not be blamed for the removal. Kozhikode city Assistant Commissioner C M Pradeepkumar removed the two drivers after their performance was not found up to the mark. The incident has no substance to prove religious discrimination as alleged by certain quarters. The Assistant Commissioner should have been more careful," Jang Pangi said. Asked whether any action would be recommended against the police officer, the ADGP said it was up to the DGP to take action.

He said there had been many Muslim policemen on security duty at various points at Kasargode and Kozhikode, during Advani's visit. The propaganda of religious discrimination was totally false.

Meanwhile, distancing itself from the incident, the NSG on Thursday said it had no role in any such incident. "No such incident involving NSG personnel has taken place," NSG Director General Jyoti Krishan Dutt said on the sidelines of NSG's 24th Raising Day at its garrison at Manesar in Gurgaon.

Minister of State for Home Affairs Sripraksash Jayaswal, too, dismissed the incident saying that the Government did not have any information on such an incident.

Meanwhile, Advani has asserted that neither he nor his party had any role in the incident.

"A controversy is sought to be created with insinuations directed at my party. Neither I nor any one in my party had any knowledge whatsoever of the incident, which I have come to know only through the media. Neither my party nor I have ever given any instructions to this effect, since we do not believe in discrimination on the basis of religion in any matter," said Advani in a statement.

BJP spokesperson Prakash Javadekar, on the other hand, said that the Congress could be behind the incident.

War on terror complicated: Patil

Saying that the war against terror had become complicated, Home Ministry Shivraj Patil on Thursday said this kind of a battle couldn't be fought with a conventional approach. Speaking at the 24th Raising Day of NSG, Patil said that human body, collection of intelligence and smaller weapons were being used by the perpetrators of terror who were deciding the time and place of such acts. Patil underlined that no effort would be spared to improve and modernise NSG and better weapons and facilities will be made available.

Heading: Amarnath row on mind, ‘deal’ to lease out land to CRPF ‘cancelled’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Chief Election Commissioner N Gopala- swami welcomed the National Conference's (NC) change of stand to favouring early elections in Jammu and Kashmir, NC president Omar Abdullah seems to be having second thoughts.

A section of the J&K press today reported his comments that the situation in the state was not conducive for elections. Pressed on the matter by The Indian Express, Omar was evasive, saying "there's no guarantee it (the siutation) would be any better six months down the line".

Asked if his party favoured an early election, he again chose not to give a direct answer, instead saying that "it's already late for elections in the state".

"It's already late for the elections. But it's for the Election Commission to take a call. We have already said that we would go with their decision. The moot point is that this uncertainty in the state must end. We have recorded our view before the Election Commission," he said.

Asked again if he would be disappointed if the EC doesn't hold early elections in the state, Omar said: "I would rather not answer the question."

The NC's view is going to matter in any decision taken by the EC on the polls. Along with the People's Democratic Party, it is the other major state party, and the stands taken by them were one of the major talking points in the EC deliberations on the J&K elections early this week. The CEC, who is reportedly against early elections, is said to have based his decision on the feedback received from parties he has been meeting.

In one of its representations before the EC, the NC delegation, among other things, had said that "an early election could mean a referendum on the religious, regional divide in the state". Asked today if his party subscribed to the view, Omar said he didn't recall having said that, and added that "an election is about the performance of the functioning of the last government".

"A new initiative in the state needs to come from an elected government. The uncertainty is not good for the people or the state. But it's for the EC to take a call on the election dates," he said.

Meetings lined up at EC

The Election Commission is meeting top officials from seven Hindi-speaking states on Friday on the possibility of sending some 4,000 Urdu-speaking officials for poll-related duties to J&K, if the local staff decides to stay away. The CEC has also summoned J-K Chief Secretary S S Kapoor for talks on the ground situation in the state, while the state Chief Electoral Officer may be called next.

Heading: Post riots, a healing touch by police - Indian Express
Content:
With the apprehension of another Amarnath-like controversy weighing on government mind, a proposal to lease out 18.10 acres of land in Pampore, South Kashmir, to the Central Reserve Police Force may fall through.

The Hurriyat Conference yesterday threatened to oppose any such move and the issue has already seen protests locally.

Playing it safe, the state Government today said no such decision had been taken to lease out a mill and the land around it, located along the Srinagar-Jammu national highway and in the middle of Kashmir's largest saffron fields. "No land has been leased out to the CRPF at Pampore," an official spokesperson said. He admitted that a request by the CRPF is lying with Jammu and Kashmir Industries Limited (JKIL), which owns the land, but said no money had been received in this regard nor any allotment letter issued.

Compounding the confusion are the opposing statements by the CRPF and JKIL. While the paramilitary force insists the deal -- meant "as a financial favour" to bail out JKIL -- is still on, JKIL says it cancelled the deal as the CRPF had failed to meet a deadline to deposit the premium money.

A few months ago, JKIL had received an application from the CRPF Directorate General in Delhi for land in Pampore to set up a camp. The Hurriyat raked up the matter following reports that JKIL was planning to give the land amounting to 145 kanals (18.10 acres) for a 90-year lease. The CRPF was reportedly directed to deposit an amount of Rs 22 crore as premium by October 15.

Heading: Cong delegation to Sonia: Push UPA Govt to clear the air on encounter - Indian Express
Content:
Communal riots in the state over the past three weeks prompted the Maharashtra Police to convene on Thursday a state-level meeting with prominent members of the Muslim community and representatives from riot-affected minority pockets.

The meeting marks the beginning of a monthly review session of the police machinery, facing much criticism following the riots, to work out ways to check alienation of the community and prevent communal flare-ups in future.

Immediately after the Malegaon riots, areas like Dhule, Thane and Shirud and villages in their vicinity saw communal flare-ups in the past three weeks.

Representatives from various districts, including Aurangabad, Latur, Dhule, Nandurbar, were present in the meeting. Issues like "lack of immediate policing that could have otherwise prevented the riots", "inaction of the police machinery in registering FIRs", "inadvertent acts of omission and commission by the police officials" in the riot-affected areas were placed in the meeting by the members of the community.

President, Movement for Peace and Justice, Dr Azimuddin alleged that though the police were apprised of inflammatory pamphlets and CDs that were in circulation in Dhule a day before the riot broke out, no action was taken.

Representatives from Dhule and Malegaon said the rioters in their areas came from "outside".

Others who spoke at the meeting demanded to know from the state machinery as to why riot control machinery did not reach the areas in time. The "sensation hungry media" and "over-enthusiastic police" were also condemned for painting a picture of Muslim educated boys being terrorists even before the chargesheets were filed.

Another scholar, Farid Batatawala said, "An earnest appeal to prepare a list of all communally sensitive areas in the state was made to ensure that these areas were monitored stringently for any untoward incident that later assume the shape of a riot."

Dr Zaheer Kazi, secretary, Anjuman Islam Trust, applauding the initiative, said, such a meeting with the police was taking place after the 1993 riots though "it was for the first time that something on this scale and at the state-level was happening".

"I had called representatives of the minority community to understand their grievances and ensure that all channels of communication were open. They need to have the confidence and a platform where they can directly communicate with the top echelons of the police force. We heard them and assured them that action will be taken on their complaints and we have heard what they have to say.

"These people will go back to their districts now and inform that such a forum exists. They will also help the police in diffusing a sensitive situation if one arises. We will meet regularly every month," DGP A N Roy told The Indian Express.

Heading: Lanka battle gives new ammo to parties in TN - Indian Express
Content:
A delegation of senior Congress leaders on Thursday met party president Sonia Gandhi and urged her to press the UPA Government to clarify "doubts" about the Batla House encounter. The leaders have also sought an appointment with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in this regard on Friday.

The delegation, which called on the Congress president, included her political secretary Ahmed Patel, AICC general secretary Mohsina Kidwai, senior party leader Salman Khursheed, AICC minority department chairman Imran-ur-Rehman Kidwai and secretary Anees Durani.

Khursheed said the delegation discussed a host of issues, including Sachar committee recommendations, attacks on Christians, media image of minorities, and "policing of terrorism including what happened at Batla House".

"How to restore confidence (of minorities) and remove doubts prevailing in the area (Jamia Nagar) has to be decided. The way confidence can be restored and facts be given to the people has to be decided as well," Khursheed told The Indian Express.

The delegation is learnt to have conveyed to the Congress president the apprehensions of the community about the encounter, which could turn out to be damaging for the party in the ensuing elections. They urged her to ensure that the Government takes some action — by ordering a judicial probe or through some other means.

Heading: In poll season, foes turn friends - Indian Express
Content:
Kaliamma, a Lankan repatriate in Dhanushkodi, said she could hear the sound of heavy firing like rumbles in the sky from across the sea in Sri Lanka; its echoes have now grown louder in Chennai, and the national capital.

After a brief lull, the battle in Sri Lanka between the Government forces and the rebel tigers of the LTTE has taken centrestage in Tamil Nadu politics. Even as the Armed Forces there claimed strategic victories over the LTTE strongholds, the crisis faced by Tamil families, who were caught in the middle of the bloody war, reported to be suffering without food or medicines, increased the pitch of the calls from Tamil nationalist and human rights organisations here for an immediate ceasefire.

When it was reported that some Indian Army personnel were injured in an LTTE attack — which revealed Indian presence in the battlefield, and was duly denied by the military top brass — and that the Lankan Government was racially profiling the Tamilian families, most vocal supporters of the Eelam cause like MDMK and PMK took up the Tamil brethren cause again: the former using the opportunity to criticise the ruling DMK, while the latter organised statewide protest against the Army's atrocities.

Next to follow was the CPI, which convened a fast in support of the Tamils in Lanka on October 2. While the offensive was against the Lankan Government and its Armed Forces, the real target was said to be the DMK, from which the Left had just broken an alliance over the Indo-US nuclear deal. The sting, however, was off, thanks to the non-participation of Jayalalithaa's AIADMK. Her party later joined hands with alliance partner MDMK in a public protest and courted arrest on October 10.

Facing criticism for "not doing enough though in power", the DMK's counter came through a public rally in support of the Lankan Tamils, addressed by its president and Chief Minister M Karunanidhi on October 6. An "all-party" meeting was next, in which members of both the Houses of Parliament from Tamil Nadu decided to resign their posts if New Delhi failed to ensure ceasefire by October 29.

What started as a trickle of telegrams, as urged by Karunanidhi to be sent to the Prime Minister by the citizens of the state, has now assumed larger proportions, with protests being organised across the state by lawyers, students, Government staff, and the omnipresent Kollywood in the coming days. Lanka, lying at the other end of the Ram Sethu across Palk Straits, is again in the eye of a storm.

• The DMK, as Karunanidhi is at pains to point out whenever its pro-Tamil credentials are questioned or challenged, has always been a supporter of the Tamil cause: a general council of the party had passed a resolution to this effect as early as 1956. A vocal supporter of the LTTE, Karunanidhi did not receive the IPKF on their way back from the island. However, this was to change with the assassination of former PM Rajiv Gandhi near Chennai by the LTTE in 1991.

Political observers say that the party's growth from a regional outfit into national politics tempered the strong support that was extended to the proscribed Tigers. When S P Tamilselvan, a front-ranking leader of the LTTE was killed by the Lankan forces last November, all parties in the state — barring Congress and AIADMK — mourned the death; Karunanidhi went a step ahead and penned a poem in his memory, which was criticised by his ally, the Congress, for "eulogising terrorism".

Now, straddling power at both Centre and state, the DMK has taken a step to differentiate between "terrorism" and "human suffering" to continue its support to the Lankan Tamils, even while steering clear of the Tigers. In his more recent speeches, Karunanidhi criticised the rebel outfit for fratricidal killings. "War is another thing which needs a political solution. The issue right now is the suffering of thousands of Tamil families, without food or medicine," said a senior leader, while Kanimozhi, Karunanidhi's daughter and Rajya Sabha member, was quoted as saying that the party cannot stand as a mute witness.

• If the DMK was one of the loudest pro-LTTE voices, its bête noire AIADMK was exactly at the other extreme, considering the Tigers as a "banned terrorist organisation". However, things were different earlier, when party founder and matinee idol, M G Ramachandran was alive. He was an open supporter of the various Tamil organisations in Lanka and extended financial support to the cause, even to the LTTE. After his death, the AIADMK became the staunchest LTTE critic when Rajiv Gandhi was killed. Some years ago, Jayalalithaa introduced a resolution that said if the Lankan Army failed to capture LTTE leader Prabhakaran, the Indian Army should do so.

Quite like the DMK, the AIADMK also shifted its stance a little, to accommodate the "Tamils' fight for self-determination", while strongly opposing "Tamil militancy or terrorism". Jayalalithaa said on Wednesday that the country cannot interfere in the internal affairs of another sovereign country. But India could stop providing assistance to the Lankan Government in its war, she added.

• The Congress, caught between its deepest feelings against LTTE and regional interests, has decided to go with ally DMK in the present round of the Lankan crisis. During the all-party meeting, it supported the opinion that New Delhi should help resolve the crisis. With polls approaching and regional interests finding strong resonance with the electorate, it has little choice but to back "public sentiment".

• MDMK founder Vaiko's connection dates back to his time in the DMK, where he was considered an upcoming star, before being expelled from it. Over the years, Vaiko became something of an ambassador for the Tigers, even after the outfit was banned following Rajiv's assassination. Vaiko's speech in support of the Tigers was cited by the last regime under the then chief minister Jayalalithaa to imprison him under POTA. Though neither he nor his two Lok Sabha members took part in the October 14 meeting, Vaiko issued a statement on Wednesday that the MPs would resign for the sake of the Tamils in Lanka, but demanded that all Union ministers from the state should quit their posts if the Centre fails to stop the war or stop supply of weapons and other military assistance to the Lankan Army.

• The PMK, yet another pro-Tamil organisation in Tamil Nadu, openly supported the LTTE, much to the discomfort of its alliance partner, Congress. In organising protests against the "atrocities committed by the Lankan forces", its founder S Ramadoss found partners in MDMK, VCK and many Tamil chauvinist outfits. However, like the DMK, the PMK has also been tempered by its alliance with the Congress with whom it is trying to tailor an alliance in the state. From pro-LTTE to anti-Lankan Army, the rhetoric of the party has been toned down though the substance remains the same.

• The Left parties in the state have always been of the opinion that any solution to the conflict in Lanka should be a political one. Though this did not find much acceptance in earlier times, all parties in the state, keen not to be seen supportive of any "terrorist" outfit, have been demanding the same now.

• The latest entrants like the DMDK or actor-politician Vijayakanth and AISMK floated by yet another actor-politician Sarath Kumar are also demanding that relief materials should be provided to the families caught in the middle. "The Indian Government should not look at this crisis as an emotional issue concerning Tamilians. Apart from the civil war and the related humanitarian crisis there, the issue has indirect bearing on our own security situation," said Sarath Kumar.

Heading: ‘Imbalanced’ Indian diet leading to diabetes, hypertension: study - Indian Express
Content:
That the BJP has entered into an electoral alliance with the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) after much dilly-dallying shows that the poll climate is hotting up in the state. The results of the Lok Sabha polls, likely to be held early next

year, would also help see which way the wind will blow in the Assembly elections due in early 2010.

The ruling Congress, which won nine out of 10 seats in the last Lok Sabha elections, is keen to improve its tally. However, it is the main opposition party, the Indian National Lok Dal, for which the elections are very crucial. Undone by anti-incumbency votes and routed in both the Lok Sabha and Assembly polls last time, the INLD is desperate to make a comeback. That explains why it has decided to join hands with the BJP again, though their last alliance collapsed soon after the two grabbed power in the 2000 Assembly elections.

Realising its mistakes, the INLD, led by former chief minister Om Prakash Chautala, has since been trying to make amends with the electorate, attacking the Congress Government on all policies it feels are 'anti-people'. The party has been holding impressive rallies, and if the huge crowds are any indication, it clearly has an edge over others. The party put up a good show of strength on the occasion of the birth anniversary of late Devi Lal at Bhiwani this year and Ambala the year before. However, crowds do not always translate into votes.

As for the second player in the alliance, the BJP had to eat humble pie in the 2004 Lok Sabha and the 2005 Assembly polls after it broke away from the INLD. It won just one Lok Sabha seat and two Assembly seats, puncturing the party's claims of coming to power in the state on its own.

The BSP too is keen to make a mark in Haryana politics. It has already announced its intention not to have any poll pact for the Lok Sabha polls. The party has also declared names of candidates for five of the 10 Lok Sabha constituencies of the state.

As for the Congress, Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda has been announcing welfare schemes for the underprivileged at regular intervals. While he has struck a good rapport with Congress president Sonia Gandhi, he faces some rivalry from Haryana Finance Minister Birender Singh, who nurses ambitions of becoming the chief minister.

However, Hooda has succeeded in getting the better of his arch rival, former chief minister Bhajan Lal and his rebel son, Kuldeep Bishnoi, who went on to launch his own party — the Haryana Janhit Congress (HJC). The HJC had reportedly been trying to forge an alliance with the BJP for the Lok Sabha polls, but its attempts came to naught with the BJP-INLD tie up being finalised on Sunday. The party now plans to contest the elections alone.

Heading: The beginning of LTTE’s end? - Indian Express
Content:
In a severe criticism of the average Indian diet, a study in the coming edition of the prestigious British Journal of Nutrition says that the nutritional imbalance in it is one of the reasons for the increasing cases of diabetes and hypertension in the country. Hypertension is usually an accompanying condition in diabetes and is often present in Type 2 diabetes as part of the metabolic syndrome of insulin resistance.

The study, which reviews the influence of dietary nutrients on insulin resistance — also called the metabolic syndrome — in Asian Indians and South Asians, says that there are severe imbalances in the average Indian diet. Data pertaining to nutrient intake, insulin resistance and cardiovascular risk factors in Asian Indians and South Asians has been reviewed and dietary imbalances have been reported in the following areas: low intake of MUFA, n-3 PUFA and fibre, and high intake of fats, saturated fats, carbohydrates and transfatty acids (mostly related to the widespread use of vanaspati, a hydrogenated oil). Data suggests that these nutrient imbalances are associated with insulin resistance and a changed lipid profile.

"We have reviewed all kind of literature available and have seen that there is a great imbalance in Indian diet. What should be consumed in good amount is consumed less and what should be consumed less is in excess," said Dr Anoop Misra, HoD, Department of Diabetes and Metabolic Diseases, Fortis Hospital, New Delhi, who conducted the study in collaboration with Centre for Diabetes, Obesity, and Cholesterol Disorders (C-DOC), Diabetes Foundation and Department of Medicine, All India Institute of Medical Sciences.

The problem is particularly severe in children and young individuals — a high intake of n-6 PUFA (mostly in fats) is correlated with glucose intolerance — whereas in adults, a high-carbohydrate meal consumption was reported to cause insulin resistance. Dietary supplements with n-3 PUFA lead to an improved lipid profile but not insulin sensitivity. Inadequate maternal nutrition during pregnancy, low birth weight and childhood 'catch-up' obesity may be important for the development of the metabolic syndrome and diabetes.

Even among the rural population, which usually consumes a traditional frugal diet, there is an increasing prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors and the metabolic syndrome due to changes in diets and lifestyle.

Heading: Session to resume today, Houses brace for turmoil - Indian Express
Content:
In view of the ongoing military offensive led by the Sri Lankan military in Wanni and Colombo's assertion that they are within a few kilometers of Kilinochchi, the LTTE's administrative headquarters, PALLAVI SINGH explains the ramifications of the current offensive.

•Is there any significance behind the timing of the offensive?

It is the culmination of the Lankan military's efforts to systematically obliterate the LTTE and a peaking of the steady territorial gains since July 2006. The Tigers stand isolated and the Sri Lankan Government has made the most of the support of the international community. However, questions are being raised about the conduct of the operation and the human cost.

•How effective is the campaign?

The Lankan military claims to have killed at least 11,000 LTTE cadre since the current phase of hostilities began in July 2006 (after the LTTE abandoned the Norway-brokered Ceasefire Agreement) and, on the basis of intelligence reports, the Tigers' strength is down to less than 5,000.

•Has Kilinochchi ever been under Government control since the Tigers made it their administrative headquarters?

Yes. It was previously captured by the Lankan government in 1997. However, the Mahinda Rajapaksa government's claim is that this time around, the LTTE is "encircled" rather than the operation being confined to certain pockets in LTTE-controlled areas. It says this is the "beginning of the end of the LTTE".

•What are the main concerns of the international community?

There are at least 1,60,000 internally displaced persons in LTTE-controlled Mullaitivu and Kilinochchi districts according to a report by the Inter Agency Standing Commission, under the aegis of the UN. The overriding concern is about the plight of these civilians caught in the crossfire.

•What has been India's response?

India has followed a policy of non-intervention in the area since 1991. Concerns about the Tamil minority community have prompted the Government to ask Colombo to observe restraint in its military campaign. The DMK has taken the lead in condemning killing of Tamils in Lanka. India has put on the table its concerns regarding the civilians in the north and plight of the fisherfolk caught in the crossfire.

While India has strongly resisted the demand for providing offensive weapons to the Sri Lankan military, it has provided defensive weapons like anti-aircraft guns and low-flying detection radars to thwart aerial strikes by the LTTE. Even though a defence cooperation agreement hasn't made much headway, India extended a $100 million soft loan to the Lankan Government for arms purchases.

Heading: Paddy MSP hiked by Rs 50 per quintal - Indian Express
Content:
Parliament is set to meet from Friday with a host of issues competing for attention and debate. They range from the controversy triggered by the Mayawati Government's refusal to allow Sonia Gandhi to address a rally in her constituency Rae Bareli, terrorist attacks, police encounters and anti-Christian violence.

While the India-US nuclear deal issue has been overtaken by a number of contentious domestic issues, Minister for Foreign Affairs Pranab Mukherjee is expected to make a statement on the latest developments on the matter.

The Congress plans vis-à-vis the Rae Bareli rally controversy are not clear. The moot point is whether or not the UP Government action is violative of a privilege of an MP. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Vayalar Ravi failed to end this speculation as he briefed the media on the Government business lined up for the session. "It is for the party to decide," a non-committal Ravi said on Wednesday. However, he said Mayawati had set a bad precedent. "This tendency (of barring rivals from addressing public meetings) is not acceptable," he said.

The two Houses would tentatively remain in session till November 21, providing for 24 sittings spread over 36 days. When reporters wondered if the session, officially described as the second party of the 14th session, would be the last for the present Lok Sabha, Ravi said he could not make any forecast. However, he said, the Government was prepared for more sittings. Regarding the possibility of a curtailment of the session on account of Assembly polls, Ravi said the business advisory committees of the two Houses and political parties would take the call.

Regarding anti-Christian violence in Orissa and Karnataka, Ravi said the Government would not shy away from a discussion.

Heading: India will try its best for peace in Lanka: Pranab - Indian Express
Content:
In an important move to boost procurement of rice in the current kharif season, the Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs (CCEA) on Thursday announced a bonus of Rs 50 over and above the minimum support price of paddy. This will raise the price of common grade rice from Rs 850 to Rs 900 per quintal and that of grade A rice from Rs 880 to Rs 930 per quintal.

Announcing the decision at a press briefing, Union Minister for Science and Technology Kapil Sibal said the incentive was aimed at encouraging production and procurement of rice. The arrival of paddy in mandis has been slow this year as farmers have been waiting for announcement of bonus.

However, the Union Cabinet deferred a decision to raise the FDI cap in insurance. "The decision was not taken today as the Finance Minister was unable to attend the meeting. It will be taken up at the next meeting," said Sibal.

Among other decisions taken by the CCEA was approval of two infrastructure projects, one each in aviation and railways. It cleared the proposal to construct a greenfield airport at Pakyong, 35 km from Gangtok (Sikkim). The airport, which will have a 1,700-metre-long runway with two parking bays, will involve an investment of Rs 309 crore.

The CCEA also cleared the gauge conversion project of Bhuj-Naliya in Gujarat to facilitate the mushrooming cement manufacturing industry in the region. The project requires an investment of Rs 318.24 crore, of which Rs 238.24 crore will be funded through budgetary support and Rs 80 crore will be invested by cement industries in the area.

Other important decisions include extension of the ICDS scheme in the Twelfth Plan, with an allocation of Rs 44,400 crore.

Renuka in Cabinet face-off

The meeting also saw an "agitated" Women and Child Development Minister, Renuka Chaudhary, pressing for her department's proposal to supply ready-to-eat food under the Integrated Child Development Services in the face of stiff opposition from Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia and her own Cabinet colleagues. Sources said Chaudhary was "agitated" when a number of Cabinet members opposed the proposal and stressed that fortified food could not be a substitute for cooked meal. She underlined that there was no infrastructure available at Anganwadi centres to cook the meal. The Cabinet agreed to constitute a GoM to give its recommendations after consultations with state governments.

Heading: Distance education Bill goes to Group of Ministers - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing "grave concern" regarding the situation in Sri Lanka, India on Thursday said that the Government "will do all in its power to achieve a peacefully negotiated political settlement and ameliorate the humanitarian conditions in the island nation".

The Government's concern, voiced by External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee, came a day after Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's comments where he had expressed serious concerns on the situation in Sri Lanka and had also said that there is no military solution to the crisis, thereby giving a call for a negotiated political settlement that would respect the basic human rights of the ethnic Tamil minorities.

In an official statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs, Mukherjee said, "The situation in Sri Lanka remains a matter of grave concern to us in India. We are particularly worried about the humanitarian effect of the continuing conflict on civilians who have been caught up in circumstances not of their making. It is essential that their rights be respected, that they be immune from attacks, and that food and other essential supplies be allowed to reach them. We have consistently made it clear that a return to normalcy cannot be brought about by military means or battlefield victories. What is required in Sri Lanka is a peacefully negotiated political settlement which allows each community to realise its own potential within the framework of a united Sri Lanka." "(The) Government of India will do all in its power to achieve this goal, to ameliorate the humanitarian conditions in Sri Lanka and has been making representations to the Government of Sri Lanka at several levels," he added.

The other issue, Mukherjee said, which is engaging the Government's efforts is the "harassment and killing of Indian fishermen in neighbouring areas that must cease forthwith. The Government will be taking steps to ensure this."

Earlier in the day, the Sri Lankan High Commissioner to India, C R Jayasinghe, said that Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's observations will be regarded as "most important" by Colombo and that the Lankan Government will keep the best interests of the bilateral relationship while addressing these issues. He was responding to questions based on Prime Minister's comments at the IBSA summit on Wednesday, where Singh had expressed serious concerns on the situation in Sri Lanka.

Heading: An ‘all-clear’ education Bill set to get Cabinet nod - Indian Express
Content:
The HRD Ministry's proposed legislation to create an independent regulator for the distance learning sector — a Distance Education Council (DEC) — has run into trouble for now with the Cabinet on Thursday deciding to refer it to a Group of Ministers (GoM). While the HRD Minister is said to have agreed for a GoM referral, it is still not decided who will be part of this GoM to address outstanding issues on the Bill.

This is the second proposed legislation of the ministry to have gone the GoM way ahead of the Parliament session. Earlier, the Right

to Education (RTE) Bill was referred to a GoM in August this year.

The Bill seeks to establish an independent and statutory regulator in the form of a 19-member DEC to monitor and regulate standards of open learning in the country. It is learnt that the proposed legislation was strongly opposed by Commerce and Industry Minister Kamal Nath among others and HRD Minister Arjun Singh is finally said to have given in for a GoM referral even though his ministry is keen on pushing the Bill through this session. Sources said questions were raised on the constitution of this body.

The DEC will have on board the V-C, IGNOU; Secretary Higher Education, HRD Ministry; Secretary University Grants Commission; director National Assessment & Accreditation Council (NAAC); UGC member nominated by the UGC Chairman; two board members from IGNOU; and three persons nominated by the visitors to the universities.

Keeping in mind the immense growth and role of the private sector in the open learning sector, the DEC will also have on board two heads of institutions offering distance education programmes.

The new regulator will be a statutory body independent of the central university.

Heading: Goa Govt in crisis over rape case - Indian Express
Content:
In the works since 2002 when the 86th constitutional amendment was effected, the Right to Education (RTE) Bill is set to get the green signal from the Cabinet soon and is on the business agenda for Parliament.

All outstanding issues that have held back the Bill so far have now been addressed by a Group of Ministers (GoM) when it met last week and the legislation will now come with a decentralised district level grievance redressal system, a broad spectrum National Advisory Council of experts to help implement the legislation's provisions and a clearly spelt out role of the Finance Commission to ensure a controversy-free state and Centre fund-sharing formula. The Bill will also apply to all private schools stipulating 25 per cent reservations for needy children.

When the Bill was first taken to the Cabinet on August 8 this year, not only were questions raised about the funding formulae to bear the cost of the Bill that seeks to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 but also about the grievance redressal mode. While the legislation earlier called for all grievances to be addressed by the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), the Cabinet had raised questions on the issue saying this would centralise grievance redressal. The Law Ministry had also earlier raised doubts about the Bill's provisions inviting litigation. The GoM has accordingly decided that grievance redressal would be decentralised and authorities will be instituted at regional level.

That apart provision is also there in the Bill for constitution of a National Advisory Council comprising experts who will advice on the implementation of the Bill. The Council have representatives from academic, child welfare, administrative and management fields as well. The Bill also takes a more 'clear stand' on the funding issue saying that the Centre would prepare estimates and ask the states to share a proportion of the amount needed to implement the RTE Bill. The role of the Finance Commission in devolution of funds to states will also be explicitly mentioned drawing from Article 280 of the Constitution.

Heading: Gay laws: Patil’s stand finds support in Cabinet - Indian Express
Content:
The Digamber Kamat ministry in Goa appears to be heading for a crisis with a group of legislators threatening to submit a memorandum, seeking removal of the Chief Minister in the coastal state. The crisis is a fall out of the recent spat between Home Minister Ravi Naik and Education Minister Atanasio Monserratte.

Goa police recently booked Monserratte's 21-year-old son Rohit for allegedly raping a minor German girl. Monserratte had claimed that he and his family were being targeted by the Home Minister. The group of ruling legislators, including Churchill Alemao, Aleixo Reginaldo Lourenco, Agnelo Fernandes, Jose Philip D'Souza, Manohar Asgaonkar and Chandrakant Kavlekar, met on Wednesday night at Monserratte's residence to chalk out the revolt against Kamat.

"The group sympathetic towards Monserratte contended that the minister is being unnecessarily targeted by the Home Minister and Chief Minister is a silent spectator to it," a Congress minister, who participated in the meeting said. The group, which has launched an exercise to garner more support from the other legislators, has decided to submit the memorandum to the Congress High Command by afternoon, sources said.

Jose Philip D'Souza, the legislature wing leader of the ruling-alliance partner NCP, was also part of the group which met last night. However, the Maharashtrawadi Gomantak Party (MGP), another coalition partner, and both the independents have not spelt out their stand on the issue. Sensing trouble, the Congress High Command on Thursday commissioned its senior leader Rajiv Shukla to Goa to defuse the imbroglio. "Shukla will be arriving in Goa as there are some disturbances between an alliance partner and police," All India Congress Committee general secretary B Hariprasad said on Thursday.

Atanasio Monserratte is a United Goans Democratic Party (Unattached) legislator and has been instrumental in several government toppling in the recent past. Monserratte was inducted in the cabinet recently after Congress minister Dayanand Narvekar was forced to resign following charges of cricket ticket scam framed against him by a local court.

Meanwhile, Kamat said that he is not disturbed by the happenings and is ready to step down. "The government is bound to have ramifications whenever such incidents happen," he said referring to the case against Monserratte's son. Digamber Kamat-led coalition government enjoys support of 25 legislators including 17 Congress, 3 Nationalist Congress Party, one United Goans Democratic party, two Maharashtrawadi Gomantak party and two independents, while the opposition Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) has 14 legislators.

Heading: Abu Salem ‘hurt’ by Monica’s behaviour on Bigg Boss - Indian Express
Content:
It seems a majority of the Union Cabinet, like Union Minister for Home Affairs (MHA) Shivraj Patil, wants Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code to stay. Section 377 bans sexual relations among people of the same gender.

At the Cabinet meeting on Thursday, many ministers not only supported Patil but also took exception to Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss's "uncalled for utterances" on the issue, which, they said, showed the Government in bad light and were causing embarrassment to the MHA.

Ramadoss, who has already written to the Prime Minister on the issue, was not present in the meeting.

The Cabinet also decided to continue opposing the demand for its repeal in court.

For the record though, Science and Technology Minister Kapil Sibal, who briefed the media after the meeting, said the Cabinet had deferred taking a decision on the issue. "Whatever the court decides, we will agree," Sibal said. The ministers also said that only the MHA and the Law Ministry should decide what the government line on the issue should be.

The MHA and Ramadoss have been airing divergent views on Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code.

While the MHA has told the Delhi High Court, which is hearing a PIL challenging the legality of the anti-gay law, that it was not inclined to repeal the law, the Health Minister and the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) want homosexuality to be legalised as a ban on it was hampering the anti-AIDS drive in the country.

The MHA recently also asked the court not to consider Ramadoss's views on legalising gay sex among consenting adults. It said Section 377 was "the will of Parliament and the people".

Taking a strong view of the continuing stand-off, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh asked Ramadoss and Patil to sit together and sort out the issue amicably. "The Prime Minister has directed the two ministers to sit together and discuss the matter and sort out their differences," Sibal said.

Heading: Navy to patrol Gulf of Aden - Indian Express
Content:
After actor Monica Bedi got entry into the reality show, Big Boss, for the second time, extradited gangster Abu Salem said he was "perplexed with her liaison with other men in the show". Salem on Thursday sent a fresh notice to Bedi saying that he is "mentally tortured and deeply hurt" whenever she denies that she was ever married to him. Salem in the notice claimed that they got married in a Los Angeles mosque in November 2000. "If Monica wants to go ahead with her life, she's is free to demand talaq," he added.

Bedi, in several interviews to the media after her exit from the show had said that she had known Salem for many years, but never married him.

Salem in the notice claimed that his anguish had been "multiplied manifold" since he was unable to communicate with Bedi due to his imprisonment. Salem has been lodged at Arthur Road Jail ever since his deportation from Portugal in November 2005. There're several murder and terrorism cases pending against him.

Salem in his earlier notice had also made a mention of his displeasure with Bedi for her continuous statements to the media. In interviews to the media, she had said that she was "single" and not married to Salem.

On a romantic note, Salem in his initial notice had mentioned how he found "peace, solace and comfort while reading Bedi's letters and cards sent to him on (their) marriage anniversaries in prison".

But this time in his notice, Salem has "warned" Bedi that if she fails to publicly acknowledge that she's married to Salem, he will be forced to resort to legal action against her.

Heading: Pay panel: Central police forces against raising Lt Col rank above commandant - Indian Express
Content:
In a bold move, India on Thursday gave a go-ahead for an Indian Naval warship — carrying helicopters and marine commandos — to begin patrolling the Gulf of Aden even as the Japanese ship carrying 18 Indians was not released by Somalian pirates.

This comes almost a month after the Navy had sought to be authorised to take necessary steps, including right of hot pursuit and use of force against pirates. The government had then denied permission.

The pirates had issued an ultimatum of 48 hours on Tuesday to pay a ransom of $ 2.5 million to free the 18 Indian sailors onboard the Stolt Valor.

Though the "operational details" were kept under wraps, sources said naval warships - which are in the vicinity of the patrolling route between Salalah (Oman) and Aden (Yemen) - are being sent for patrolling."The warship will have carrier helicopters, boats and endurance to stay in water for a long period of time as it is being sent more than 500 nautical miles away," a Navy official said. The warship will coordinate the patrol with French and US warships, already present in the region.

The Defence ministry, in an official statement said, "This anti-piracy patrol will be carried out in coordination with Directorate General Shipping Shipping, who will keep Indian Flagship vessels informed in case they want to travel in Indian Ocean along with Indian Navy ship. The patrolling is commencing immediately."

Patrolling in the area will be significant as Gulf of Aden is a strategic point in the Indian Ocean and provides access to the Suez Canal through which a sizeable portion of India's trade flows.

Heading: Three sailors held hostage aboard Iranian ship return - Indian Express
Content:
Continuing their tug-of-war on recommendations of the Sixth Pay Commission report, central police organisations (CPOs) have strongly opposed some of the demands being made by the Armed Forces, including a proposal to elevate the rank of a Lieutenant Colonel above that of a commandant in central paramilitary forces (CPMFs).

In a memorandum submitted to Minister of External Affairs Pranab Mukherjee, who heads the committee to look into the grievances of the Armed Forces on the pay commission recommendations, the CPOs have argued that the demand of the Armed Forces was entirely unjustified and would result in operational difficulties if acceded to.

A delegation comprising officials from BSF, CRPF, ITBP and CISF met Mukherjee on Wednesday and explained why they were opposed to certain proposals, sources said. The delegation told the minister that the Armed Forces were using pressure tactics to get their demands met.

The Armed Forces have openly expressed their dissatisfaction with the pay commission recommendations and one of their demands has been to elevate the rank of a Lt Colonel above that of a commandant in a central police force. Both Lt Colonel and a commandant are placed as the commanding officer of a battalion but during times of joint operations, the Armed Forces commander takes precedence. The Armed Forces have used this to argue that a Lt Colonel should be treated as a higher rank.

However, the CPOs have pointed out a number of discrepancies in this argument. Sources said the delegation brought to the notice of the minister that while there were usually more than one Lt Colonel in a battalion — with the senior most being the commanding officer — only one commandant was present in a CPMF battalion.

The delegation argued that the work profile of a commandant was completely different and his promotion was based on his performance unlike that of a Lt Colonel who gets time-bound promotions. Sources said it was only after considering these that the Sixth Pay Panel had recommended a higher rank for the commandant but the Armed Forces want it reversed.

Heading: Ministry unsure if Kolkata judge should be impeached - Indian Express
Content:
Three sailors who spent seven weeks in captivity aboard a ship in Somalia returned home safely even as the fate of 18 Indians on board 'Stolt Valor' is uncertain. Akbar Rafiq Ahmed, Jeevan Kiran D'souza and Anthony Clyde Thimudo were on board Iranian vessel 'Deyanat' which was hijacked by pirates on August 21, while it was travelling from China to Netherlands carrying a cargo of industrial products.

"We were not told what their demands were and we were very scared since the pirates were carrying guns." Rafiq said. "There was a shortage of food,"he said, adding that "The pirates allowed us to call our families".

The ship was released on October 10 but there was no confirmation regarding whether any ransom was paid.

Heading: A-I floats leave-sans-pay scheme - Indian Express
Content:
Despite recommendation by the Chief Justice of India (CJI) to remove Calcutta High Court judge Soumitra Sen from service, the Union Ministry of Law and Justice is not sure if the case made out against Sen will stand scrutiny. The ministry has decided to seek legal opinion on whether there is adequate ground to form the basis of initiating impeachment proceedings against the judge, who has not been allotted any judicial work for the last one year.

Initially, Law Minister Hans Raj Bhardwaj had categorically said that since the judge's removal had been sought by the CJI himself, there was little that the Government could do except initiate impeachment proceedings. However, this line of thinking seems to have changed after it was pointed out that there was nothing in the case to suggest any act of commission or omission by Sen as a High Court judge.

"The impeachment process is almost like a court process. We will have to establish that he committed misconduct after his appointment as a judge. However, in this case, Justice Sen's alleged misconduct relates to his working as a lawyer. This is why we need to be certain that the action, because of which his removal from office has been sought, will stand scrutiny before Parliament," said a senior officer of the ministry.

Under the Judges Inquiry Act 1968, Parliament through the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of Rajya Sabha can set up a committee of three persons to inquire into the conduct of a judge. The report of this committee is binding on Parliament. "If this committee finds a judge innocent, then Parliament cannot proceed further," pointed out the officer.

On his part, despite suggestion by the CJI, Sen has refused to put in his papers. His lawyer has asserted that the judge would defend himself before Parliament if need be.

As first reported by The Indian Express, CJI K G Balakrishnan sometime back wrote to the Prime Minister seeking Sen's removal as he had been found to have indulged in financial misconduct prior to his elevation as High Court judge in December, 2003. Sen, working as court-appointed receiver in a lawsuit between Steel

Authority of India Ltd and Shipping Corporation of India, had deposited Rs 32 lakh received by him on behalf of SAIL in his personal account.

Heading: Citi posts loss of $2.8-bn for third quarter - Indian Express
Content:
Barely had the aviation industry recovered from the shock of Jet Airways laying off around 1,900 of its employees, the largest layoff in Indian aviation history, that National Aviation Company of India Ltd (NACIL) announced its plans of cutting the flab in the national carrier. A 'voluntary leave scheme' has been introduced in which around 15,000 'non-operational' employees of Air India will be eligible to apply.

Causing complete disarray in the morning's proceedings of the two-day India Aviation 2008 expo, NACIL chairman and managing director Raghu Menon let the cat out of the bag announcing his company's new voluntary leave scheme. Those 'non-operational' employees who take up the offer would be taken back into the company's fold, if they so desire, at the same level of seniority and last drawn pay, Menon said.

Allaying fears of retrenchment by the state carrier, the damage control exercise began with civil aviation minister Praful Patel clearing the air. "There will be no retrenchment of Air India staff. Certainly, the current crisis will affect growth plans...it will affect future employment opportunities which would have come Air India's way (if) the aviation industry was in better financial health," he said addressing reporters soon after the landing of the Airbus A320. A senior ministry official later admitted that NACIL's employee strength needed to be pruned, especially from the middle to higher staff levels.

Giving out sketchy details of the scheme, Air India spokesperson Jitendra Bhargva said the scheme was still at the proposal stage. It would come up before the company's board and that union leaders would be consulted before the scheme is launched. The entire process is likely to take 2-3 weeks.

"After the merger of two airlines (Air India and Indian Airlines), the base of employees has gone up. Even if 200 (employees) were to go on a voluntary basis, there will be savings for NACIL," he said. Under the scheme, NACIL employees can voluntarily apply for a leave of a minimum period of three years to a maximum of five years. During this period, they would not be eligible for their monthly salary. However, they still might be able to avail of some emoluments and benefits. The emoluments will depend on the position of the employee, said Bhargava.

NACIL has a combined staff strength of 33,000, with an aircraft to employee ratio of 1:1600. For the company, which had incurred losses of around Rs 2,100 crore last fiscal, the current wage bill stands at Rs 6,500 crore, informed Bhargava. It had introduced a similar scheme in 2002-03, which company sources said, didn't find many takers.

Trying again?

NACIL had introduced a similar scheme in 2002-03, which didn't find many takers. Out of 17,000 employees at that time only 300 applied

What happens?

A-I's 15,000 'non-operational' employees are eligible for the 'voluntary leave scheme'. Employees can apply for a leave for a period of three to five years. Though they would not be eligible for their monthly salary, they may be able to avail of some emoluments and benefits

What Next?

The scheme is still at the proposal stage. It will first come up before the company's board for approval. Union leaders would also be consulted. The entire process is likely to take 2-3 weeks

Heading: Producers demand reimposition of steel duty - Indian Express
Content:
Banking giant Citigroup today attributed its higher lending costs in the third quarter in Asia to deteriorating credit condition in India.

Citigroup, led by India-origin chief executive Vikram Pandit today posted a loss of $2.8 billion for the third quarter ended September, against a net profit of $2.2 billion in the same period a year ago.

In the Asia region, Citigroup saw credit costs rise of 51 per cent. "Credit costs more than doubled, driven by higher net credit losses, up 91 per cent or $83 million, and a $64 million incremental net charge to increase loan loss reserves.

"Higher credit costs were mainly driven by a continued deterioration in the credit environment in India, where the business is being actively repositioned to reduce costs and mitigate losses," Citi said in a statement.

The banking major pointed out that in Asia, credit costs increased 51 per cent, reflecting higher net credit losses, up 36 per cent or $42 million and a $65 million incremental net charge to increase loan loss reserves.

"Higher credit costs reflect continued deterioration, primarily in India. The net credit loss ratio increased 52 basis points to 3.63 per cent," it added.

Heading: Public-private projects: Get ready for audit, PM tells CAG - Indian Express
Content:
Stung by a surge in cheaper steel imports and a receding order book, domestic steel majors have demanded reimposition of import duty on steel of 10-15 per cent. The issue is likely to dominate tomorrow's meeting between producers and the steel ministry's top brass. Producers claim that in the absence of import duty, cheaper imports have flooded local markets leading to piling up of their inventories.

"Yes, we have received representations from various steel companies seeking reimposition of import duty in view of decreasing global steel prices. They say secondary producers and other users are resorting to large-scale imports taking advantage of nil duty despite exercising self-restraint on exports. We will talk to them on the matter," a senior ministry official said. In their SOS to the steel ministry, the producers said hot rolled coils imports have surged from nations like Ukraine, China and Thailand at $615 a tonne, which has not only eroded their already shrinking margins, but has also rendered their operations economically unviable.

"There is an express need to ensure safeguards against cheaper imports," Ispat Industries vice-chairman and managing director Vinod Mittal told The Indian Express. State-run steel giant Steel Authority of India chairman Sushil Kumar Roongta said, "When prices were high, government took special measures to ensure availability of steel at affordable prices. But since the situation has changed, the government must take measures to ensure safeguards against such imports." Essar Steel has demanded the same.

Steel majors in their representations to the ministry maintained that secondary producers as well as traders were importing cheaper steel despite huge price reductions. These producers have forgotten that they were provided HR coils for $900 a tonne when global prices were hovering around $1250 in May this year.

Heading: Excise collections dip 3.8% in Sept - Indian Express
Content:
Having flagged off public-private-partnership projects (PPP) in infrastructure in a big way during its term, the UPA government now seems to be pushing for a special audit for PPP projects.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh asked the comptroller and auditor general (CAG) of India to develop new skills and mechanism for auditing the huge investment being made in various sectors through the PPP model.

"Public-private-partnership projects are becoming increasingly common in key infrastructure sectors. Audit needs new skills to evaluate these complex arrangements," Singh said addressing the All-India Conference of Accountants General.

The PM also stressed on the need for bringing implementation agencies such as non-government organisations (NGOs) and societies under the ambit of public audit through the CAG.

Amounts released to these agencies are booked as revenue expenditure in the books of the Central government. The utilisation is known only through a utilisation certificate issued, which does not give a transparent view of the accounts.

Speaking at the conference, CAG of India Vinod Rai said that the CAG office had already engaged a few states towards adopting accrual based accounting in line with the recommendations of the twelfth finance commission.

This would cause below-the-line liabilities in the Union Budget such as oil bonds and fertiliser bonds to be reflected in the expenditure side of the Union Budget and not just as liabilities.

Heading: AviationMin to urge airlines to not charge for congestion - Indian Express
Content:
Excise duty collections recorded a dip of 3.8 per cent in September 2008-09 vis-à-vis the same period last fiscal. The government could shore up Rs 9,800 crore in September 2008 compared to revenue of Rs 10,186 crore collected through excise duty in September 2007. While the government targets a 7.75 per cent growth in excise duty for the current fiscal, excise duty collections have grown by only 2.3 per cent in the period between April to September 2008 compared to the same period the year before.

"The dip in collections is due to slow down in manufacturing/ demand. With industrial product prices on the retreat, collections have been affected," said E&Y partner Uday Pimprikar.

Heading: Sebi loosens investment norms to check FIIs’ Quit India movement - Indian Express
Content:
In its meeting with civil aviation companies' honchos scheduled in November, the civil aviation ministry will suggest the removal of air congestion surcharge levied by them.

Speaking to The Indian Express, a ministry official admitted that even as capacity building and airport modernisation efforts have reduced congestion at airports to near-zero, aviation companies have not yet fallen in line. Despite repeated warnings to the industry, some airlines are still charging the air congestion surcharge.

"There is no congestion at Delhi airport since the third runway has been launched. Hyderabad and Bangalore being new airports, there is hardly any congestion. Mumbai airport is the only one where congestion may be a problem,"said an official.

Heading: CRR effect: Call rates, bond yields plunge - Indian Express
Content:
Foreign investors will now have investment freedom in Indian markets. With foreign institutional investors (FIIs) engaged in a 'quit India' movement, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has decided to do away with the 70:30 ratio of FII investment in equity and debt respectively with immediate effect. This is expected to give the overseas investors more flexibility in taking investment decisions depending on the market situation. This move, along with the lifting of the curbs on participatory notes (PNs), is expected to result in more inflows in the long term.

The Sebi move has come after total FIIs' total investment in listed Indian companies fell by 16.72 per cent from a high of $66.32 billion on December 31, 2007 to $ 55.23 billion on October 16, 2008. FIIs have pulled out $11.09 billion in 2008 as Indian markets joined the global meltdown triggered by the subprime and credit crises. A major reason for the 50 per cent fall in the Sensex this year is FII withdrawals.

The investment flexibility for FIIs follows the announcement by the government and the Sebi on Wednesday to increase in ceiling in FII investments in corporate debt from $3 billion to $6 billion. "In order to accord flexibility to the FIIs to allocate the investments across equity and debt, it has been decided to do away with the conditions provided in regulation 15(2) of Sebi FII regulations pertaining to restrictions of 70:30 ratio of investment in equity and debt respectively, with immediate effect. Necessary amendments to the FII Regulations will be carried out in due course," Sebi said. The FIIs have already shown interest in the debt market and put $1.9 billion in 2008 while they pulled out $11 billion from equities. "In order to maintain the 70:30 ratio, FIIs are forced to sell debt whenever they sell equity. Now they will have flexibility and put their money wherever they want. Many FIIs had complained about this restriction earlier," said a market source.

According to the Sebi, the relaxation is aimed at according "greater flexibility to the FIIs to allocate investments across equity and debt". Henceforth, FIIs would not be required to follow the 70:30 equity-debt ratio.

Meanwhile, Sebi said the enhanced limit for investment in corporate debt will be allocated among the FIIs on a 'first-come-first-served' basis, subject to a ceiling of US $300 million per registered entity.

Heading: PSU banks rally on rate cut hopes - Indian Express
Content:
After the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) cut the CRR for the the second time this month and released Rs 40,000 crore to the banking system, the cash availability has improved, bringing down the inter-bank call money rates and yields on government bonds. On the other hand, even as the Reserve Bank today allowed banks to extend 0.50 per cent of their deposits to mutual funds as liquidity support, the Rs 20,000 crore special repo for mutual funds also received a better response with Rs 2,270 crore being taken up as against Rs 200 crore on Wednesday and Rs 3500 crore on Tuesday.

Indicating the improvement in the situation, call money rates ended at 7.00 per cent, sharply lower than 10.25 per cent on Wednesday and 23 per cent on last Friday. The 10-year government bond yield ended at 7.72 per cent, compared with Wednesday's close of 7.91 per cent. In early deals, it hit 7.65 per cent, just off a seven-month low of 7.64 per cent touched last week.

Meanwhile, after opening a special repo window for mutual funds which are facing redemption pressure, the RBI has permitted banks to provide additional liquidity support of up to 0.5 per cent of their total net deposits to aid these funds. "It has been decided, purely as a temporary measure, that banks may avail of additional liquidity support exclusively for the purpose of meeting the liquidity requirements of mutual funds to the extent of up to 0.5 per cent of their net demand and time liabilities (deposits)," RBI said.

Earlier this week, the RBI had allowed banks to take money from apex bank against the government securities, up to a total of Rs 20,000 crore, to provide it to mutual fund industry. The RBI is to conduct the special repo facility every day until Rs 20,000-crore limit is exhausted.

Said Indranil Sengupta, economist, DSP Merrill Lynch, "The pressure on MF (and reportedly, NBFCs) liquidity is, in a sense, 'systemic' reflecting "knock on" effects of global risk aversion. CRR cuts, however, hardly help since banks are not likely to lend to non-bank financial intermediaries in perceived distress." He said, "The RBI could also not reach out to MFs and NBFCs since it essentially deals with banks and PDs. It is for this reason we had preferred a directed lending facility of the type that is now being put in place."

(With agencies)

Heading: Think tanks think again on GDP growth - Indian Express
Content:
The cut in cash reserve ratio (CRR) and other steps to boost liquidity in the banking system failed to avert a slide on Dalal Street as stocks ended lower in a choppy session amidst global recession worries and the fall in some Asian markets. However, after European stocks pared initial steep losses and Wall Street futures showed gains, the Sensex — led by PSU bank stocks — cut the intra-day losses and closed down at 227.63 points or 2.11 per cent at 10,581.49.

Inching down to the 10,000 level in the opening session, the index had initially declined 791.32 points to the day's low of 10,017.80 in early afternoon trade, its lowest level since July 24, 2006.

Banking stocks bounced back as the fall in inflation and the hefty cut in CRR and other liquidity-boosting steps raised hopes for a reduction in interest rates. SBI, India's biggest commercial bank, was up 3 per cent to Rs 1,543.90 off day's low of Rs 1,420.55. A host of other state-run banks like PNB, Indian Bank, Corporation Bank, Dena Bank IDBI Bank, Canara Bank, Bank of India, Syndicate Bank, Bank of Baroda, Union Bank of India, Allahabad Bank and Indian Overseas Bank rose between 2.03 and 8.07 per cent.

"Lower inflation may trigger a cut in interest rate by the RBI which may spur lending. PNB has already reduced home and auto loan rates. Other banks are likely to follow suit," said an analyst. "Indian stocks will recover once Wall Street and Europe stabilise. They are triggering the fall here," said BSE dealer Pawan Dharnidharka.

Sebi had tightened margins in the derivatives segment to ward off defaults and curb volatility. The exposure margin for gross open positions in single stock futures and gross open positions in stock options will now be higher of 10 per cent or 1.5 times the standard deviation in the notional value of the positions. "This also prompted dealers to be cautious," said a market source.

A warning of tough times ahead by Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke sent Asian markets sharply lower, as investors brace for looming recession. Key benchmark indices in China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan were down by between 3.25 and 11.41 per cent. Shrugging off recent optimism about massive government efforts to prop up the global financial system, Wall Street on Wednesday suffered its worst one-day percentage decline since the stock market crash of 1987. Bernanke warned that credit market turmoil posed a significant threat to an already slowing American economy.

Heading: Hindalco issue falls prey to financial turmoil - Indian Express
Content:
Two of the country's leading economic think tanks — the National Council for Applied Economic Research (NCAER) and the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) — today lowered their respective forecasts of gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the current fiscal.

While NCAER revised its growth forecast to 7.6 per cent as against a forecast of 7.8 per cent in August and 8.5-8.8 per cent in May. CMIE, on the other hand, continued to remain more upbeat on the India growth story compared a lot of other similar organisations forecasted a healthy growth rate of 8.7 per cent, down from 9.4 per cent a couple of months ago.

"The GDP forecast has been changed keeping in mind the current global financial turmoil and how it has impacted investor confidence globally. We believe investment spending will be certainly hit this year, which will affect growth," Shashanka Bhide, senior fellow at NCAER told The Indian Express. "Primarily, capital intensive sectors are likely to take a hit."

NCAER predicted a growth of 2.3 per cent for agriculture, 8.2 per cent for industry and a little less than 10 per cent for services. According to Bhide, farm sector growth is likely to dip partly on account of a base effect over last year — when growth was exceptionally good at 4.5 per cent — and partly because there has been no significant across-the-board improvement in the harvest this year.

CMIE, however, said it didn't revise GDP growth forecast on account of the current financial crisis, but because of pressures in the real estate sector and slowdown in the implementation of investment projects.

"Growth in capital formation has thus been scaled down from 18 per cent to 14 per cent and growth in the construction sector has been reduced from 15 to 10 per cent. Industrial sector, that was expected to grow by 9.1 per cent is now expected to grow by a lower 8.3 per cent. The most significant correction is in the steel and copper sectors," CMIE said in a press statement.

CMIE added that apart from this, the Indian economy had endured all the major hardships witnessed over the past few months — from high inflation and higher cost of borrowings to repatriation of foreign institutional investors from the stock markets — and that the outlook is even brighter now with the Reserve Bank softening its liquidity stance.

Why the decline?
