With other complaints like long and unaccounted working hours, trade unions seem to have sensed opportunity.

And, for the first time, two major trade unions of the country, the Left-backed Indian National Trade Union Congress and Centre of Indian Trade Unions have decided to raise the issue together. They are being supported in their effort by UNI, a global union federation representing 900 unions in the service sector in over 140 countries.

G4S, the multinational company that has been entrusted with the responsibility of security during the Commonwealth Games, is in the eye of the storm, with trade unions and employees crying hoarse about exploitation of workers. Representatives of the company, however, could not be reached for comments.

Representatives of the major Indian company involved in the private security guard business, Premier Security Services, denies these allegations.

Senior vice-president of the company, SP Diwan says, "We provide salaries through cheques. All salaries are on record. How can anyone claim we give less than promised? There is no denying that sometimes salaries get delayed because we depend on our clients for payment. But, it's never more than a few days late."

Philip Bowyer, Deputy General Secretary, UNI says, "For India, the Commonwealth Games are not only an opportunity to showcase talent and organizational skills, but also the respect this nation has for human rights."

"We appeal to the Indian government to recognise security services as an industry so that these guards can come under the Industrial Disputes Act and their interests can be safeguarded," he adds.

Sudhir Kumar, CITU representative from Delhi says, "According to the law of the land, minimum wage for a guard is Rs 3,683 per month. But, these companies bifurcate even this into basic salary and perks, the guards end up losing a lot of money."

Sunil Kumar Singh, working for the Premier Security Services, for the last six years, says, "I earn Rs 3,600 per month. My family is in the village. I can hardly send them anything so they are all dependent on farming. Diwali is round the corner and I have not received my salary for the last two months."

Another employee of the same organization, Suchit Kumar, rues that his one day's pay was cut for the Bihar flood victims without even asking for his permission.

"Every time we are transferred, the charges for a new uniform are deducted from our salary. That means we lose around Rs 1,000 every six months for uniforms," he adds.

Says SP Diwan of Premier Security Services, "We have been in the market for the last 31 years. Our image has never been tarnished. Some people are jealous of our success. When some security guards are transferred because of indiscipline or sleeping during the working hours, they join such unions to get back at us. There is no truth in these allegations."

Heading: Gaming fever grips city at Cyber Games - Indian Express
Content:
KARZZZ
CAST: Urmila Matondkar, Himesh Reshammiya, Shweta Kumar, Gulshan Grover, Dino Morea;
DIRECTOR: Satish Kaushik
When Subhash Ghai's Karz came out in 1980, there were mutterings about how it had ripped off cheesy Hollywood drama The Reincarnation of Peter Proud. But they soon subsided, not only because Ghai cleverly admitted to copying, having out-cheesed the original effortlessly. It was also because Karz was a cracker of an entertainer: as the born-again hero, Rishi rocked, there's never been a crueller, classier vamp than Simi, and if ever there is a compilation of classic movie themes, the haunting Ek Hasina Thi is sure to top the list.
This Karzzz, despite the extra zees for luck, is a blot. Except for the names of the characters, which are exactly the same, nothing else is: the treatment is sloppy, even by Satish Kaushik's standards, and the acting is plain execrable.
For those who've come in twenty-eight years after the fact, this is how it goes. Pop star Monty (Himesh) starts having visions  of a man and a woman, a huge mansion in the hills, a "Kali ka mandir", and an airplane going up in flames. It's a case of "punarjanam", a psychiatrist declares sagely. And whoosh, we are launched into a series of flashbacks, unravelling how Monty is actually rich businessman Ravi Varma (Dino) re-incarnated, and has come into the world to wreak revenge on the murderous, greedy-for-his-millions wife Kamini (Urmila).
Himesh adds a hair transplant and a smile to his extremely-limited repertoire (in his last year's debut Aap Ka Suroor, he had appeared throughout in his till-then trademark baseball cap, and scowl). A badly-made up Urmila dons skin-tight gowns, large tracts of her chest gleaming with bronzer, gold trousers, and scarlet lipstick. She also sounds distressingly like Archana Puran Singh when she simpers: hard to think that she was once an A-list actress. There's also a new girl, Shweta (director Indra Kumar's daughter) getting a brief look-see: all she has to do is to gaze adoringly at Himesh. That must have been tough.
Even the climactic song-cum-whodunit denouement, which has been lifted completely, is mangled. In between, you can hear Rohini Hattangadi, who plays the "dukhiyari maa" utter lines like these: "mere kaleje ke tukda", she goes, "mere laal".
Moral: if you can't make, don't re-make.

SHOOT ON SIGHT
CAST: Naseeruddin Shah, Om Puri, Brian Cox, Greta Scacchi, Gulshan Grover;
DIRECTOR: Jagmohan Mundhra
JAG Mundhra's films have topical, relevant subjects. That's the good part. The bad part is that they do not possess a single subtle note: everything is heavily underscored, leaving no place for understatement or nuance.
And that's something one misses sorely, especially in a film like his latest. Shoot On Sight is based on the London bombings in 2005, which unleashed a whole spate of racial profiling. Is it a crime to be Muslim? Are all Muslims terrorists? These questions, asked by sundry characters in Shoot On Sight yield answers which, for all their truth, seem like they are stating the obvious.
It's not as if Naseer, as Commander Ali of Scotland Yard, doesn't know the pitfalls of playing a Muslim cop in a still-white country. In his scenes with 'gori' wife (Greta), defiant daughter, couple of openly racist colleagues, and sympathetic boss (Brian), he shows as much deftness as the script allows. But that's not much at all: Ali's childhood friend from Lahore, now a "mullah" advocating jehad (Om) is all surface¿ he strokes his beard, recites from the Koran, and colours impressionable minds.
More predictabilities abound. Rebellious Muslim teenager facing off da ¿ he won't let her date white boys who want to go all the way. Jolly meat-shop owner doling out gosht and good cheer. Good white wife trying to balance the tensions in her family, and his. We've seen all this before, with much more depth: there's more to multi-culturalism, and the problems of being brown, post 9/11, than these very broad, too familiar brush-strokes.
The Hindi dub flattens the film even more; catch the English version, if you have to.

CHEENTI CHEENTI BANG BANG (animation)
Voices by Ashish Vidyarthi, Mahesh Manjrekar, Asrani, Anjan Srivastava
DIRECTOR: R D Mallik
TWO colonies of ants live on either side of a river bank. Lal Cheentas and Kala Cheentas have presumably lived happily before the evil Ghun arrives in their midst to sow dissent and discord. This could have been a fun flick: ants, and other cute creepy-crawlies, lend themselves well to animation (Antz, A Bug's Life). Some money and effort has been spent on the production, but the characters are all cardboard, not being able to create the slightest interest in the proceedings.
What you get is endless, inane chatter peppered with creaky dialogue ( "nestanabood"; "yudhh ka danka baja diya", "yunki baat ki baat hai", "mere dil mein saadh hai"). And an old ant called Lal Boodha who's supposed to have leered at a comely young thing, who tells the ant queen: "woh mardood hamare badan pe toot pada".
Huh? This is supposed to be a film for little children?

SHUBHRA GUPTA shubhra.gupta@gmail.com

BODY OF LIES
CAST: Leonardo DiCaprio, Russell Crowe
DIRECTOR: Ridley Scott
"THERE'S nothing to like in the Middle East," mumbles Ed Hoffman, a CIA top-notch played by Crowe, trying to dissuade Roger Ferris (DiCaprio) from staying back in Amman. Of course, the shoe can be on the other foot. From that part of the world, there's little to like in America. And Body of Lies, written by the screenwriter of The Departed and Kingdom of Heaven and adapted from a book of the same name by The Washington Post's David Ignatius, is certainly not going to help the US cause.
Pitched as a terror/spy thriller  "Trust No One. Deceive Everyone." Body of Lies makes no bones about its politics. If the utter disgust for the war being waged in the name of jehad is supposed to be an inverse joke on how the Bush Administration is fighting it, or a view of the war on terror that is refreshingly politically incorrect, the message is lost. And that's despite the trite use of W H Auden in the beginning: "Those to whom evil is done, do evil in return."
As Hoffman and Ferris proceed to see it, though, there are absolutely no grounds for the evils being wrought in the name of God. A suicide bomber who has lost his nerve tells Ferris: "If they think you know too much, they say martyrdom." Looking for "low-level al-Qaeda operatives" for a counter-operation, Ferris seeks: "Basically someone between Osama and Oprah." Another faithful is dismissed as "so he touches his head to the ground four-five times a day". All it takes for Ferris to smoke out (to use the famous expression) the dreaded terror head is cooking up a fictitious terror group of his own over the net.
The story basically deals with the hunt for that terror head, Al-Saleem, of undefined al-Qaeda links who has threatened to target places in the US and UK. Ferris speaks Arabic, often dresses up like an Arab, wears a helpful goatee and is not averse to being hit by missiles or bitten by rabid dogs. Hoffman is his CIA handler, keeping a watch on him via an eerily clear satellite.
True to the film's theme, there is an underpinning of distrust in the relationship between Ferris and Hoffman. While Ferris is the one taking all the risks, from Iraq to Jordan, Turkey and Dubai to Syria, as a boorish Hoffman tries to instruct him 24/7 on earphon while chaperoning his kids to school or ballgames  Crowe gives Hoffman the sense of credibility that comes with age and experience. When Ferris urges that a local accomplice be protected or looked after, or strikes up instant likes and dislikes, you tend to agree with Hoffman that he could be naive.
However, the abilities of Crowe and DiCaprio or director Ridley Scott  who has enough Middle East under his belt but handles this one like The Gladiator  can't keep away the disquiet over how the highly wrought and complex issue of terror has been handled.
Even as tokenism, the film doesn't make a nod to the history that tinges and singes the region's geography. Instead, look at the tokenism it does employ: if DiCaprio is called Ferris, sounding closely like Faris (meaning a Knight in Arabic), his love interest is a woman of Iranian descent called Aisha (the Prophet's wife's name; she didn't exist in the book). Aisha's nephews don't like their mother's cooking; they would rather have pasta, spaghetti. Me too, chuckles Ferris.
The Jordanian intelligence chief is an enigmatic gentleman by the name of Hani (Mark Strong), who handles what's engulfing the region without having his dinner jacket cuffs soiled. In the heat of the Jordanian desert, he doffs his best suits for interrogation. In contrast, Hoffman is overweight, and underwashed. (Another message?) The role Hani ultimately plays is unclear, to say the least, but he at least knows what he is getting at. Al-Saleem, who stands in for Osama we presume, on the other hand, is shown smoking away into the phone at one time.
One year ago, The Kingdom came out of Hollywood, featuring government agents sent into Riyadh to investigate the bombing of an American facility. Whether tackling the question of terror, culture clash or religion, the fear and uncertainty on the ground, or the American dilemma in the Middle-East, it was a far superior effort.
Body of Lies, on the other hands, is full of half-truths. And that's worse.

SHALINI LANGER
shalini.langer@expressindia.com

Heading: Eight injured in bus pile-up - Indian Express
Content:
Rohan Kirry, 10, has been hooked to video games since he was five, after he saw his uncle playing a PC-based game at his cyber café.

Kirry is the youngest participant at the regional rounds of the World Cyber Games that were held in the Capital on Friday. Over 2,000 youngsters participated in the sixth edition of the regional rounds of the World Cyber Games—an annual feature. Contestants were tested on their gaming abilities through five games: Counter Strike 1.6, War Craft, NFS Pro-Street, FIFA Soccer 2008 and a mobile-based game Asphalt 4. The games were selected on the basis of their popularity.

This is the first time the mobile gaming platform has been introduced in the India round of the e-gaming championships. "World over, the mobile gaming concept has been taken over successfully. In India, however, this is the first time it has being implemented, as we fall in the Tier II list of countries," says Ajit Kashyap, head of the World Cyber Games, India.

The craze among contestants was palpable across the hall where the regional rounds were being conducted. Teams of gaming enthusiasts from Jaipur, Chandigarh, Bikaner came down to Delhi to enlist for the regional rounds. "We have been coming to participate in the regional rounds of the Games for the past four years and love this concept. This is a Mecca of video-gaming in the country," said Mayur Singh, 24, from the Jaipur team, XGI. The World Cyber Games will be taking place across 70 countries this year.

The finals of the Delhi regional rounds will be held on Saturday, while the national finals are scheduled for October 25 in Mumbai. The winners from Delhi and Mumbai will battle it out to get on a final team of 10, who will then head for the international level competition in Germany.

Heading: Unauthorised colonies as per 2002 survey to be regularised - Indian Express
Content:
Eight people were injured after a DTC bus crashed into a Blueline in IP Estate in Central Delhi on Friday evening. Police said a delivery van in front of the bus halted suddenly after one of its tyres got punctured. A Blueline bus crashed against it followed by a DTC bus. Police officials said the incident was reported around 5 pm near Rajghat red light and because it was peak hours, traffic was held up for about an hour.

Police officials said the eight injured in the Blueline bus, plying on route number 39 (Kamla Market to IGI Stadium), were discharged from a nearby hospital after first aid.

The driver of the Blueline bus, yet to be identified, fled after the incident. Police have registered a case of rash and negligent driving against him.

Heading: Big steps on the learning curve - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre on Friday said all unauthorised colonies found by an aerial survey in 2002 will be eligible for regularisation subject to the fulfilment of certain conditions set by the government.

In a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha, Minister of State for Urban Development Ajay Maken said existing regulations were modified on June 16 authorising the Delhi government to issue provisional regularisation certificates to the colonies following completion of prescribed formalities. All unauthorised colonies (except those inhabited by affluent sections of society) as existed as per aerial survey of 2002 will be eligible for regularisation subject to fulfilment of prescribed conditions, he said.

However, he said actual regularisation will be subject to the orders of Supreme Court and Delhi High Court.

Heading: Young Bengal club disqualified from league - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi golfer Himmat Rai has improved every step of the way in his first season as a professional

Digression is a ploy that doesn't work too well with Himmat Rai. The talk on golf is to the point; veer it away from his sport a little bit, and the answers get even briefer. Luckily, he brings the same attitude to the course.

In a year that took the learning curve higher than ever for the 21-year-old, just his first full season as a professional, he travelled from the many domestic tour crests to a few Asian Tour troughs, but it was at home that Rai found the perfect balance between the two. Rai's four patient rounds at last week's Asian Tour Indian Open, hidden among more famous names at the Delhi Golf Club but closely watched by family, gave him a 21st place finish.

More than that, though, it gave him extra confidence of having done it from among the best continental players.

"The experience was so much more meaningful because I put four solid rounds together in a big event," says Rai. "It gives me the feeling that my game is beginning to come around and working under pressure too."

But that is not credit to just a week's show. Rai started this domestic season with a fabulous run at the big Bilt Open, finishing in third place, and in the 12 months since then, he has found himself being in the weekend mix at each tournament he's played. With three more top-ten spots in the process to boot, the current 12th spot on the Order of Merit surprises no one.

Lesson in experience
The travels around Asia, on one of the country spots for India, had been without a spectacular week, but Rai chooses to concentrate on the sum of the parts. It's a sport, after all, where living out of the suitcase is a lesson in itself. "It's been a learning time there. For a first season on the road, I think I've done well to make the experience worth the while," he says.
To give a little spurt to his final aim of "regularly playing in Europe and USA," Rai has been having a go at the early stages of the European Tour qualifying school for the past two years. "It is just different sort of conditions and that means different challenges. This time it was constantly raining and it was extremely cold throughout the qualifying stage, so that was a big test in itself," Rai says.
But that's a little bit of digression, and so, the focus is back to the present at once. "At the moment, my short term goal is to just give my 100 per cent everyday, in practice and in competition, work on little niggles," Rai says. "This season has given me a lot of satisfaction and the hope to improve rapidly next year too."

Heading: Qualifier Bisht defeats top seed, enters final - Indian Express
Content:
Young Bengal Association were disqualified from this year's DSA 'B' division league after failing to satisfy an amended criterion. However, both DSA and the club owners have failed to clarify the circumstances under which the decision was being made. According to the DSA, Young Bengal Association appeared directly for their second match of the draw against Dwarka Club, skipping their opener against Hans FC, which resulted in their demotion.

"One of our amended rules this year says if a team fail to appear for their first match, they will be termed 'non-functional' which means they can't participate in the league for the current year. A report will be sent to the higher authorities too. The Young Bengal Association club didn't appear for the first match at all. They came for the second match when they were told that they won't be playing in the league anymore. Their officials weren't aware of the new rules; they thought it's a two-match affair like it used to be. Apart from that, I don't think they had a prepared team at all. A few of their players had come for the match in practice shoes," said NK Bhatia, secretary, DSA.

Late arrival
In reply, club co-owner Mohammad Rais said his team came late for their first match on October 8 against Hans FC, due to which they were not allowed to play. "Our team, on reaching the Ambedkar Stadium for the first match, were told that a walkover had been given. Earlier, the rule applied till the second match of the draw. It would be wrong to say we weren't aware of the new rules, but they have been changed to favour some of the teams playing in the league. I would also like to add that our boys were in proper kits on that day," said Rais.
Bhatia countered the argument saying, "Teams like Delhi Students and Gulabi Bagh are also owned by the same people. Then there's no question of being impartial." Joint co-owner and former India international Salauddin, however, took the blame on his head, adding that he didn't have any knowledge of his club's preparations. "There have been two deaths in my family recently. I couldn't look after their preparations at all. They must have gone for the second game on their own after reading some newspaper. I'm solely responsible for this. This is the first time this has happened to our club."

Heading: 3 cops, lawyer held in attempt to extort city trader - Indian Express
Content:
Ronit Bisht slammed a ball into the wall behind him, threw up his hands in frustration while looking at his father, and let out a few yells of exasperation during his Under-18 nationals semi-final match at the DLTA Complex. Strangely enough, these displays of petulance happened to be during his 6-3, 6-1 win over top seed Chandril Sood, a victory which puts him in line for his second consecutive title on Saturday. Perhaps he's simply become used to ending up on the winning side.

The youngster, who won the Under-14 national title a week ago, qualified into the main draw of this week's meet, and there has been no stopping him ever since. On Saturday, he will play second seed Abhijeet Tiwari, who battled past Maharashtra's Christopher Marquis 4-6, 6-4, 7-6 (1).

Missed chances
Ronit's unforced errors caused him to miss a few chances in the first set, but he remained largely untroubled. To counter the Delhi player's groundstrokes, Sood made his way to the net a few times, and enjoyed a fair bit of success with his drop shots before Ronit figured out his plan. In addition, a series of unforced errors from this week's top seed made his job easier. It was these careless shots that gave the qualifier a break in the eighth game, and Ronit employed his groundstrokes perfectly when he was closing out the opening set, a backhand winner bringing it to an end, 6-3.
A short break later, Sood looked far from refreshed. He opened the second set with a double fault, and a backhand wide on break point gave Ronit the first game. The errors from the UP player's racket showed no signs of slowing down, and soon he found himself facing a 3-0 deficit with a double-break disadvantage. Sood did manage to get a break back in the fourth, but could win no more games.
In the girls' semi-finals, Delhi's Sweta Solanki defeated Sonia Dayal 7-5, 6-2. She will play Karnataka's Nimisha Mohan for the title. Nimisha thrashed Rishika Sunkara 6-1, 6-3.

Heading: Soon, dial 108 for all emergency situations across India - Indian Express
Content:
Three Delhi policemen and an advocate were arrested by the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) of Delhi government for falsely implicating a businessman and attempts to extort his son in a murder that took place last September.

The ACB on Thursday arrested Crime Branch Inspector K G Tyagi, Sub-Inspector Mukesh and Assistant Sub-Inspector Rajvir and advocate Ravindra Chaddha.

Additional Commissioner of Police (anti-corruption) N Dilip Kumar said ACB gathered evidence against the accused after victim Gopal Krishna Aggarwal's son Abhinav Krishna filed a complaint some 10 months ago. A sting operation Abhinav did, with help from the Branch, proved foursome's involvement, Kumar said.

The four were produced before a city court on Friday. While the policemen were sent to police custody till Monday, Chaddha was sent to judicial custody. 

Kumar said the sting operations found advocate Ravinder Chaddha was acting as a conduit on behalf of Tyagi and was to get Rs 4 lakh of the total amount they were trying to coax out of Abhinav, who runs a printing and building business, to save his father.

Aggarwal senior, along with eight others, was arrested in the murder committed in Hauz Khas on September 29 last year.

The complainant, present at the Additional CP's office in Civil Lines, said the murder took place outside their shop in Hauz Qazi and his father was detained three months later — in December 2007. Abhinav claims to have paid Inspector Tyagi Rs 8 lakh — "he asked me to pay the amount if I wanted to save my father — but Aggarwal senior was detained the following day.

"He arrested my father saying there was immense pressure from higher-ups. Tyagi said my father would be freed in a few days."

According to the complainant, Tyagi then advised him to contact Chaddha, and the policemen allegedly used the advocate as middleman to extort him. Aggarwal said he has till date paid "nearly Rs 26 lakh, and he (Tyagi) was asking for another Rs 25 lakh."

With his father's condition deteriorated, a frustrated Abhinav approached the Anti-Corruption Branch and also began collecting evidence by secretly taping his conversations with Chaddha and the others.

Abhinav said the case would be heard next on October 25.

Kumar said, "We will ask Delhi Police to probe the matter. Further investigations are on."

A case under Prevention of Corruption Act and relevant section of Indian Penal Coden (IPC) has been registered against the four accused.

Who is Inspector Tyagi?
Inspector K G Tyagi played a major role in solving cases such as the Inderlok murder (seven of a family were murdered), the Gujarat merchant abduction, and the Hailey Road murder among others.
Recruited in Delhi Police as a Sub-Inspector in 1982, Tyagi has been deputed in the Crime Branch for the last more than three years. He was also the SHO of several police stations of northeast district and is said to have a good network. He spent sometime with New Delhi district special staff as well.

Inspector 'stung'?
The Anti-Corruption Branch says the 56-page transcript of the sting op is main evidence in the case.
Investigating Officer Tyagi is purportedly shown in the sting as telling Abhinav Aggarwal: "We have helped more than we should have. People don't do this much even after taking Rs 50 lakh. You have given a very nominal charge."

Heading: Now, Lok Adalats set to judge issues of marital discord, violence - Indian Express
Content:
It's official: 108 will soon be the national emergency helpline number. Like 911 in the United States, Delhiites and people across the country would have to dial 108 for all emergencies — from trauma care to rescuing a cat ¿ going by Health minister Dr Anbumani Ramadoss's plans.

While states such as Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Uttarakhand are already using 108 as their toll-free emergency number, the Capital is still dialling 102 for emergencies. "We will meet Chief Minister (Sheila Dikshit) to see whether Delhi can also switch to 108, to avoid confusion," Ramadoss said. Delhi will soon be floating a tender for EMRI emergency services."

The 108 programme will be integrated with EMRI, or Emergency Management and Research Institute, operations to provide comprehensive trauma care services. An NGO promoted by Satyam Computers, EMRI provides emergency response ambulance services under public-private partnership.

The service would soon come to the Capital, Delhi's Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta said. "The Delhi government will float tenders and soon sign an MoU with EMRI," Mehta said.

As part of the scheme, all national highways will have a telephone every five kilometres, a fully loaded ambulance with basic life support every 50 km, a trauma centre every 100 km, a super-specialty hospital every 300 km, and a tertiary care hospital every 500 km. "We are not going to build a single hospital," Ramadoss said, "the existing facilities are going to be developed and we will sanction the necessary amount for that.

"In case there are no government hospitals, we will give money to nearest private hospital to upgrade their facilities."

Once the national 108 programme kicks in, every call will be received by a 24-hour call centre, which will take down all important information. The call centre would then locate an ambulance, fire vehicle or police vehicle, depending on the type of emergency, through GPRS technology and dispatch it for further help.

"Since all states have different languages, we will have state specific call centres," the minister said.

Heading: The anti-life - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Legal Services Authority (DLSA) has spread out its sphere in an attempt to deliver justice at a faster clip as it organises the first Lok Adalat on Saturday for settlement of matrimonial disputes, and cases of custody, alimony and domestic violence.

The DLSA has constituted eight special courts in four district court complexes. The move is an attempt to clear the huge backlog of cases.

There will be three courts at Rohini, two courts each at Karkardooma and Tis Hazari, and one at Patiala House. Every court would comprise a retired additional district judge and a mediator to settle the dispute.

As per a circular issued by DLSA member-secretary Asha Menon, the Lok Adalat would adjudge various issues under the Hindu Marriage Act, Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, Prevention of Women from Domestic Violence Act, and petitions for custody of children and maintenance sought under Code of Criminal Procedure.

Around 250 such cases have been referred by different courts to the Lok Adalat.

"Considering the huge backlog of cases, the DLSA is trying to minimise litigation," DLSA project Officer Sanjay Sharma said. The idea, he said, is two-pronged: to reduce the burden of the courts, and to save time and money of litigants.

Emphasising that this would be the first occasion that the DLSA is organising a Lok Adalat to such disputes, Sharma said the Authority was committed to hold such events more often.

WHAT ARE LOK ADALATS?
A quasi-judicial institution and a dispute settlement agency; resolves litigation by way of negotiation, arbitration, mediation and conciliation.

WHY LOK ADALATS?
To enable the common people to seek justice at a quick pace as justice disposal system in India is seen as ruinous, thanks to the cost of litigation, legalese involved, prolonged litigation, and inordinate delay in courts. With Lok Adalats, all parties have an opportunity to evade extremely technical court procedures, lingering litigation, and court fees and other expenses.
Lok Adalats are informal and flexible, and do not require a lawyer by either party. Apart from some minimum requirements in procedures and approaches, the rest of the exercise is simple; they vary as per the nature of problems and culture of the community.

Heading: SAD looks to spread its wings in Delhi, Rajasthan - Indian Express
Content:
Death within birth is the thread that binds Johann Rousselot's photographs

Every picture tells a story. Put them together and you have a novel, sometimes a life story of a culture, a group, a civilisation. Johann Rousselot chose to portray the death of one. It was the 2004 '

India Shining' campaign that triggered it all for the photographer, who was moved by the two extremes that India was and sadly still is. The result -- a contrast of India Shining, India Crying.

In 30 photographs Johann tells the story of the adivasis uprooted from the land they owned for generations, backed by law. But to make India a shining diamond, somebody had to go through the fire. It turned out to be the Vidharba cotton farmers. So you have eyes staring at you, looking for answers, poignant images of the agricultural crisis that move to tell the tale of their wiped out shanties and houses. People stand in emptiness and stare at the emptiness that awaits. Also in the photographs are the last images of those who chose to end their lives, and also those that they left behind, inconsolable, grieving and alone. Their destruction is the construction of a new India. Tall buildings stand where the history of a tall culture lays buried. "The instrument of progress is impatient and greedy," asserts Johann. The greed is to fill the spaces by coffee joints, bowling alleys, bungalows. Faces of the new developing India beam and look up. After all, ignorance is bliss.

On at Alliance Francaise, Sector 36, till October 25.

Heading: Packaged midday meal will start in three months: Education Minister - Indian Express
Content:
In an attempt to expand its base to Delhi and Rajasthan, which are going to the polls soon, Punjab's ruling regional party-Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal)-is raring to take a plunge in Delhi and Rajasthan politics, banking on the Sikh vote in the two states.

While SAD has reportedly demanded 15 seats in Delhi and five in Rajasthan, the BJP, which is the larger partner in the two states, is likely to agree to a maximum of five in Delhi and three in Rajasthan, it is learnt. The three seats which the BJP is ready to give to SAD in Delhi are Adarsh Nagar, Rajouri Garden and Shahdara, which have a sizeable Sikh population.

Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today said "Negotiations are on and a final decision on seat-sharing will be taken soon."

He said SAD (B) president Sukhbir Singh Badal and senior Akali leader Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa, who is also the party's chief whip in the Lok Sabha, have been authorised by the party to hold talks with the BJP on the issue of seat-sharing.

While Badal refused to divulge details of how many seats the party is seeking from the BJP, sources say SAD is asking for a major chunk of the 60 assembly seats in Delhi, which goes to polls on November 29, and the 200 seats in Rajasthan, which goes to polls on December 4. The party is also looking at Madhya Pradesh to spread its wings further, sources said.

SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal has already organised a rally in Delhi on August 2, where he announced that the party would contest the polls on its own symbol. During the previous assembly elections, SAD candidates had contested as BJP candidates on the its symbol-the lotus.

While SAD chief Sukhbir Badal is attempting to consolidate the party's vote bank in Delhi and Rajasthan by contesting on the party symbol, political observers feel the SAD may benefit more in case its candidates contest on BJP ticket as it would help its candidates get the support of the BJP as well.

Heading: Ferozepur DIG meets ‘acid attack victim’ - Indian Express
Content:
Students would soon get packaged food for midday meals if the plans of the government stay on course. Education Minister Dr Upinderjit Kaur, who was here today to attend a function at Guru Nanak Public School, said, "Schoolchildren will start getting packaged food for midday meals in all the districts within the next three months. We have already initiated the pilot project by roping in a NGO, which would supply cooked food as midday meal in all the primary and middle schools of Nawanshahar, Tarantaran and Ferozepur districts."

Ensuring that the food would be of good quality, she said,"We have involved two NGOs- Delhi-based Indcare and Mumbai-based, Istri Shakti Sangathan. I have seen their way of cooking, which is totally mechanical and the quality is good. Istri Shakti Sangthan, which will serve schools in Ferozepur and Nawanshahar districts, makes use of environment-friendly fuel for preparation, while Indcare, which will serve Tarantaran district, prepares the food through steam."

Kaur said she wanted teachers to focus on teaching work. "Once the pilot is successful, we will launch the scheme in all the districts within no time," she claimed.

It must be mentioned here that as per the normal practice, teaching staff of the schools have been instructed to arrange cooked midday meal for students through self help groups and there is a general complaint of teachers that this additional work adversely affects their teaching.

Evading the answer to this problem, Dr Upinderjit said,"The teachers should teach the students with devotion and produce good results in government schools."

About the implementation of government's decision to conduct Class V exam at school level, she said it would start from this session. When quizzed about the alleged partial behaviour with girls for at 'Computer for all' centres in villages, she said, "It came to my notice today. I have given instructions to all the district education officers and circle education officers of the state to ensure that girls have no such problem.

'I will look into Shilpi's case'

Dr Upinderjit Kaur was oblivious of the fact that Shilpi, who had topped the class XII exams (in all streams) this year, had not received the cash award as promised by Harcharan Singh Bains, Media Advisor to CM, on behalf of the Chief Minister, Parkash Singh Badal. However, two students, one from Pathankot and the other from Amritsar, who topped in science and commerce streams respectively had been given their rewards already. When told about the case, she said,"Her school should forward her case to me, I will look into it."

Heading: President lauds the ‘total sanitation’ mission of state - Indian Express
Content:
Ferozepur Range DIG R P Mittal today visited Moga to look into the case of a Dalit girl, Paramjit Kaur of Ghal Kalan village, who was reportedly attacked by three motorcycle-borne youths, who allegedly threw acid on her. Mittal met Paramjit in the hospital and later said, " It appears that acid was thrown on her," said Mittal. "She has narrated three sequences to substantiate her allegations. Police would cross check her claims," Mittal said, refusing to share the three sequences.

Notably, Moga police today concluded that the burns were caused by acid. The police had earlier claimed that the burns could be either due to hot milk, hot water or acid. "In fact, the complainant had applied milk or milk cream to get relief from the burns," said Moga SSP Ashok Baath, adding that the traces of milk during medical examination made experts believe that the burn injuries might have been due to hot milk. Moga police have arrested the three accused, namely Nita, Jeeta and Soni, all residents of Ghal Kalan village. One of them had allegedly raped Paramjit in July.

Heading: Notice issued to DGP, ASP in fake encounter case - Indian Express
Content:
Appreciating Centre's effort to bring 11,000 villages under the Nirmal Gramin scheme, President Pratibha Patil said the mission of total sanitation by 2012 would be successful only if all sections of the society come forward.

She also appreciated the involvement of the NGOs and women. Clad in a white saree, Patil took a round of the stadium along with Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Union Minister of Rural Development Dr Raghuvansh Prashad Singh.

She said 80 per cent of diseases in the rural areas are spread because of open defecation. Highlighting the importance of cleanliness she said cleanliness is making mind, body, water and environment clean. She also called upon for women empowerment and a checking female foeticide. Women can play a key role in this regard, she added. She also released booklet titled 'Swach Gaon Swastha Gaon'. As a mark of honour she was presented a memento and a shawl.

Dr Raghuvansh Prashad Singh said each household in the state will have a toilet by 2012 for which the Centre is providing Rs 1500, state Rs 700 and house owners will spend Rs 300 only. Haryana, Gujarat, Rajashthan are committed to provide total sanitation by the year 2010.

Lauding Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh, for highest number of Nirmal Gramin Awardees, he said other states should follow the lead.

Heading: HC issues notice to state, three universities - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued notices to Director General of Police (DGP), Haryana; Ashok Kumar Sheoran, ASP, Hisar, and 14 other police officers posted at Hisar. The notices have been issued on a petition filed by Pardeep alias Kala and Shiv Kumar, both residents of Hisar, presently in Central Jail.

The two have demanded registration of FIR against Sheoran and other police officers. They have alleged that Sheoran murdered four youths, namely Gurdev alias Nanu, Karambir, Mukesh and Sandeep, in two separate incidents. Sheoran allegedly, threatened people and demanded money from them. Gurdev and Karmbir were abducted on October 29, 2007 from Narnaund and later murdered

Mukesh and Sandeep, residents of Loharwara village were killed in a fake encounter on July 21, 2007. According to the petition Pardeep and Shiv Kumar have been falsely implicated in several criminal cases . They petitioners have demanded that the case should be investigated by the Criminal Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

Heading: BJP-INLD get in action for the rally - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued notices to Haryana and three universities including Kurukshetra University on a petition filed by four students. The students, three from Haryana and one from Patiala, have demanded that they should be granted admission in B.Ed (regular) by Haryana for academic session of 2008-09. The petitioners have demanded admission in view of the fact that there are around 28,000 seats lying vacant in various educational institutions in the state.

In May 41,103 candidates appeared for the entrance test against a total number of 53,000 seats available with Kurukshetra University. The university had declared the results after conducting a common entrance test. Out of 31,000 candidates, only 25,000 took admission in B.Ed (regular). The four students, who have moved the High Court, did not appear for the common entrance test but have demanded admission for B.Ed course since so many seats are lying vacant. Taking note of the contentions, the High Court has issued notices to the university and the state.

Heading: Honour for 46 Armoured Regiment - Indian Express
Content:
After joining hands to contest the Lok Sabha and Assembly elections together, the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) and the BJP have begun joint preparations for the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) public rally at Sonepat on November 1.

BJP leader Lal Krishan Advani would be the chief guest and INLD chief Om Prakash Chautala would preside over the rally. BJP president Rajnath Singh would also be present.

Talking to The Indian Express, Ajay Singh Chautala, Rajya Sabha MP and General Secretary of the INLD, said the preparations for the rally had begun.

He said the INLD-BJP alliance would sweep the next Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections in state. "INLD's organisational skills would ensure the rally would be a huge success,'' he said.

He said the Congress leadership had failed to contain price rise, check the deteriorating law and order situation and terrorism.

The two parties have decided to organise district level joint office bearers meetings from October 18. Chautala, BJP Haryana state president, Atam Parkash Manchanda, Haryana state INLD president Ashok Arora and other senior leaders of the two parties would address these meetings. The INLD-BJP leaders have also decided to jointly throw out the Congress government in the state and Centre.

Chautala said the INLD-BJP combine would organise three meetings daily. Meetings for Faridabad, Palwal and Mewat districts would be organised on October 18, for Gurgaon, Rewari and Narnaul on October 19 and for Bhiwani, Rohtak, Jhajjhar on October 20.

Similarly joint meetings for Sonepat, Panipat, Karnal districts would be organised on October 21, for Kurukshetra, Yamunanagar, Panchkula on October 22, for Ambala, Kaithal and Jind on October 23 and for Hisar, Fatehabad, Sirsa districts on October 24. Duties for NDA's Haryana Day Sonepat rally would be assigned to INLD-BJP leaders in these district meetings. Necessary instructions to party workers would be given for initiating combined fight against the government.

INLD and BJP leaders have also decided to constitute state and district coordination committees for better coordination in the agitation against the Congress.

Heading: Paragliding contest begins - Indian Express
Content:
President Pratibha Patil today bestowed the honour of 'Standard' on the 46 Armoured Regiment at Hisar Military Station. The President lauded the services rendered by 46 Armoured Regiment during war and peace time in last 26 years. The President, while presenting the Standard to the regiment, said this felicitation will further increase the responsibilities of the regiment. The President also released army stamp and envelope to mark on the occasion.

"Thunderbolts", as 46 Armoured Regiment is referred to, is a premier unit of the Indian Armoured corps which has participated in operations undertaken by the army. The ceremony had both foot and mounted parade in clock work precision and immaculate coordination. The parade was commanded by Col Sanjay Bhatia, Commandant of 46 Armoured regiment.

Heading: Shimla bypass opens - Indian Express
Content:
After two days of bad weather, Himalayan Paragliding Pre-World Cup 2008 began today.

As many as 82 pilots, including 12 women pilots, got the signal to take off from the paragliding site at Billing near Baijnath today. The first route given to the pilots was from Billing, then to Dharamshala, and then back to the landing site at Bir, covering a distance of 103 kilometers.

The deadline for landing was 6 pm. According to an official spokesperson of the Tourism and Civil Aviation Department, all pilots took off safely from Billing and landed back safely too.

Sources said that some of the pilots landed safely at Yol near Dharamshala and Palampur, instead of the landing site Bir. The sources said that retrieval teams had been dispatched to bring the pilots to Bir.

Five guest pilots had come from Pakistan, and did free flying. The fifth Himalayan Paragliding Pre-World Cup is being organized by the Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation, Himachal Pradesh, in association with Paragliding World Cup Association (PWCA), the Aero Club of India (ACI), and the Federation Aeronautique Internationale (FAI). The tourists and the local residents also enjoyed hot air ballooning at the landing site at Bir.

Heading: State signs MoU for container freight station at Baddi - Indian Express
Content:
The bypass for Shimla, which is expected to provide hassle-free movement of vehicular traffic to locals and tourists travelling to upper Shimla areas, Kinnaur, Karsog and Rampur, was made operational today.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal today dedicated the four-kilometer long double-laned stretch to the people, by flagging off an HRTC bus. The road, called the Sanjauli-Dhalli bypass, has been constructed at a cost of Rs 15.80 crore.

The state's PWD Minister Gulab Singh, Horticulture Minister Narender Bragta and local MLA Suresh Bhardwaj were present on the occasion. After the inauguration, Dhumal announced that a series of measures are afoot to reduce traffic congestion in Shimla town. He pointed out that all traffic bottlenecks are being identified, and remedial measures will be taken.

Dhumal recalled that during his earlier tenure as chief minister, the government had taken up the matter with the Centre for granting forest and environment clearance for the new bypass.The 12th Finance Commission, at the government's initiative, had given Rs 12 crores for the road.

Shivendra Batish, president, Sanjauli Beopar Mandal, commended the efforts of the government for construction of the bypass. He demanded that traffic should be diverted away from Sanjauli market.

Heading: Subhash Ahluwalia discharged, family protests move - Indian Express
Content:
In order to strengthen the infrastructure at the booming industrial township of Baddi-Barotiwala, Himachal Pradesh government today signed an MOU with Container Corporation of India.

With the MoU, a Container Freight Station (CFS) and Inland Container Depot (ICD) will be set up at Sheetalpur village, near Baddi. The project, which will cost Rs 53 crore, will be completed within 15 months, close to the time when the central industrial package for Himachal Pradesh ends in March 2010.

The depot will cater to the export requirements of the local industrialists. Products valued over Rs 700 crore will be transported by the corporation from the station. Setting up of the CFS and ICD has been a long-pending demand of the industrial associations. Potential investors in Himachal had often been discouraged by the lack of a reliable rail link between Chandigarh and Baddi.

The MOU was signed by Principal Secretary (Industry) Subhash Negi with Harpreet Singh, Director (Projects and Services), of the corporation. Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal and the corporation's MD RK Mehrotra were also present on the occasion.

The corporation will spend nearly Rs 29 crore on the infrastructure for the project. The approach road to the proposed site will be widened and improved, at an estimated cost of Rs 5.68 crore. Other land development works will cost Rs 2.16 crore.

Infrastructure development will be carried by Himachal Pradesh State Industrial Development Corporation on behalf of the corporation, said Dhumal. Himachal Pradesh has decided to transfer 86 bighas of land valued at about Rs 16 crore to the corporation, at a token lease of Rs 1 per acre per annum, for a period of 95 years.

HP had earlier urged the Centre for providing Baddi direct railway connectivity with the broad gauge line. A survey had been conducted for the purpose too.

Dhumal had recently signed an agreement with Punjab Chief Minister Prakash singh Badal, for completing the Baddi-Chandigarh road by next year. He has also been lobbying for extension of the industrial package beyond 2010, to its initially-proposed period of March 2013.

Heading: Steps to save energy: Govt clears decks for CFL scheme - Indian Express
Content:
A Piquant situation developed at Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC) Hospital late today afternoon, after doctors discharged Subhash Ahluwalia, an IAS officer who had been arrested by the state's Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau earlier this month.

A Shimla court had yesterday rejected Ahluwalia's and extended his police remand till October 20. Ahluwalia had been in the hospital since his arrest.

Today, a medical board set up by IGMC authorities examined Ahluwalia at the instance of the Vigilance Bureau. The board advised his discharge on the ground that Ahluwalia was not found to be suffering from any serious ailment. But Ahluwalia's wife Meera Ahluwalia and other relatives attending on him protested this move, and asserted that his condition was critical.

Even Ahluwalia complained of chest pain and high blood pressure. The doctors were called afresh for an examination later this evening. A final decision on his further treatment in the hospital is expected to be taken tomorrow.

Heading: 11 held for attack on student leader - Indian Express
Content:
Decks have finally been cleared for the implementation of Himachal's innovative energy saving scheme, Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana, a Rs 80 crore scheme to distribute free CFL bulbs to 16.50 lakh domestic consumers.

Sources say the state's Chief Secretary Asha Swaroop held a meeting today with members of Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB). Swaroop approved the purchase of 72 lakh CFL bulbs, from five companies.

Every domestic consumer will get a free pack of four CFL bulbs. HPSEB, the implementing agency, has already finalised technical bids, and decided that CFL bulbs of 0.85 Power Factor (PF) will be supplied to the consumers.

Earlier, four companies had qualified for the supply of the bulbs.The surprise entrant is HPL Socomec, which had been disqualified since it did not have a certificate from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Sources say the company has produced the certificate now.

The financial bids for the scheme will open tomorrow, and it is likely to take off next week. All 16.50 lakh domestic consumers will get CFL bulbs by December 25, the birthday of former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee.

The implementation of the scheme, says experts, will save nearly 72 MW of power daily, and make Himachal eligible to get carbon credits to the tune of Rs 100 crores per annum. The scheme had earlier run into trouble following complaints from HPL Socomec, based in Haryana.

Four manufacturers were selected for the purchase of the bulbs, but supply orders were cancelled by the government on the intervention of Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal. The CM had directed the chief secretary to look into the issue relating to purchase of the bulbs.

Regarding the scheme, Dhumal said yesterday, "The government has ensured that the scheme is implemented in a transparent manner, because it carries the tag of former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee. I seek the support of the people, the media, NGOs``, government agencies and industrial associations to make Himachal switch over to CFL use." The CM said that nearly Rs 80 crores will be spent on the scheme.

Heading: Development work near Renuka Dam - Indian Express
Content:
Police arrested 11 activists of Students Federation of India (SFI), Nahan, late yesterday evening from various parts of the town for attacking Central Students Association (CSA) president Rajesh Sharma in the college complex.

Sharma was attacked yesterday in broad daylight, had sustained multiple head injuries. Police have started patrolling the college complex, to avoid any further violence in the area.

Heading: Govt sets pace for IT, industry corridors - Indian Express
Content:
The authorities of Renuka Dam have stated that a separate budget is being provided for the local development of the area. Officials added that 1.5% of the total budget of the project will be spent on development works.

The total cost of the project is Rs 2,500 crore. The district administration will spend Rs 40 crores on the area, in a phased manner. The Delhi Government had provided Rs 200 crore for the purpose.

Heading: Sachin Kohinoor of sport - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has initiated the process of identifying new industrial and information technology corridors in a bid to woo investment in Punjab. Over 300 acres of land in Kapurthala has been identified for purposes of setting up industry. Out of this, 50 acres is expected to be earmarked for a dedicated IT corridor.

The IT department recently put up a demand note in this regard. A large part of the land that is now being identified for promotion of industry and IT was till recently jail land at Kapurthala. The government is also considering allotment of another 300 acres in Ropar for industry and IT.

The IT corridor in the area is being deliberated in wake of the upcoming Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Ropar. The state has some 800 acres spread in the area, of which about 550 acres will be spared for the IIT and the remaining will be for the IT corridor, said sources.

The state government has been grappling with the problem of scarce land that could be put to commercial use. A top official said, "A statewide survey to identify land for IT and other purposes is underway. The attempt is to create land banks in Punjab that could be instrumental to woo investments." Much of the investments, especially in the IT sector, have remained largely confined to Mohali and adjoining areas, essentially for paucity of land. The government has set March 2009 as the deadline for the seven Mohali-based IT companies to start operations. These companies were allotted one-acre plots each for setting up units. As per the terms and conditions, each company will ensure a minimum investment of Rs 9 crore in the project and 500 jobs. Besides, they will have to make use of at least 50,000 square feet of area.

The companies that will start operations by March next year include KMG Infrastructure, Diban Software, Dr IT Planets, HCL Info systems, IDS Infotech, Sebiz Infotech and Competent. A time-bound plan to implement the new industrial and IT projects in these key corridors is also being mulled, said sources.

Heading: Check Sukhbir, Cong urges Guv - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today congratulated Sachin Tendulkar on breaking Brian Lara's world record of most runs in Test cricket. Badal thanked Sachin for "blessing the soil of Punjab to do India proud."

He said, "You are the Kohinoor of not just the world of cricket, but of the entire sporting world and truly a gem in an age when India needs one. We in Punjab are especially proud that you have chosen Punjab for this historic landmark."

Member of Parliament and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, who is also the chairman of the organising committee for the Mohali Test, also congratulated the maestro. Sukhbir expressed hope that his innings would prove to be a match-winning knock.

Heading: 4 in race for Cong Gurdaspur LS seat - Indian Express
Content:
Member Parliament and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal is in the line of fire of the Punjab Congress. In a letter to the Punjab Governor, Congress state president Mohinder Singh Kaypee and leader of Opposition Rajinder Kaur Bhattal accused Sukhbir Badal of exercising extra-constitutional powers in the state. Congress leaders, who highlighted the acts of the junior Badal, branded his activities as an MP as "unconstitutional." The letter states that a member of Lok Sabha is entitled to undertake works of development only in his own constituency and he cannot distribute cheques, lay foundation stones or inaugurate works beyond the limits of his parliamentary constituency as per MPLAD guidelines.

The letter says it is unfortunate that Sukhbir Singh Badal, who is the MP from Faridkot constituency, has been visiting different parts of Punjab and has been laying foundation stones and inaugurating works of public importance in the presence of even ministers, who remain mute spectators. The Congress leaders alleged that the SAD president has been frequently misusing the state helicopter by making the

Chief Secretary or ministers accompany him in order to legalise his air travel, which amounts to misuse of the state exchequer.

MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira, Tej Prakash Singh, Avtar Singh Brar, Darshan Singh Brar, Ishar Singh, Ajit Inder Singh Mofar, Jeet Mohinder Singh Sidhu, Jagmohan Singh Kang, Raj Pal Singh and Parminder Singh were part of the delegation that went to meet the Governor.

They cited the recent controversy when Sukhbir Badal visited Bholath and inaugurated several projects. The Congress also alleged that there was a total breakdown of constitutional machinery in Punjab and Sukhbir Singh Badal was working as a "de-facto Chief Minister of the state". The delegation urged the Governor to direct the state government to refrain from indulging in such acts.

'Congress has Sukhbir phobia'

The SAD has dismissed as "hogwash" the Congress allegations that SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal had any unconstitutional powers. Reacting to the Congress memorandum to the Punjab Governor about the alleged "unconstitutional authority" enjoyed by the SAD president, Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa said the Congress was clearly suffering from "Sukhbir phobia". He said it would have been better if the Congress leaders had gone to the Governor against the inadequate bonus on paddy announced by the Union government. Dhindsa said, "It is sad that the principal opposition party in the state should be so bereft of ideas and political ideology as to talk about issues such as laying of foundation stones by an MP."

"All that Sukhbir Badal is doing is to keep the party and the government on its toes about the commitments made to the people during the election campaign," he said, adding that as the president of the ruling party, it is not only his right but also his duty to do so.

Heading: Empty stands greet players, Sachin’s record saves the day - Indian Express
Content:
The race for the Gurdaspur Lok Sabha seat has intensified after the recent visit of All India Congress Committee (AICC) observer Charan Singh Sapra, who took stock of the party's position in the area ahead of the parliamentary polls. Some names doing the rounds for the seat are Union Minister of State for Industries Ashwani Kumar, former PWD minister and sitting Congress MLA from Kahnuwan Partap Singh Bajwa and two others.

While Ashwani tried to organise an impressive show of his supporters during Sapra's visit two days back, Bajwa has also been pulling all strings to bag the ticket. Ashwani's advantage is that he is close to national party chief Sonia Gandhi and had been doling out sops from his MPLAD funds as a Rajya Sabha member from the area. His disadvantage, however, is that he is not a leader of the masses as he has mostly been in Delhi as a prominent lawyer.

Bajwa is a firebrand leader with a mass following, at least in his own Assembly constituency. His only problem is that apart from his comparatively weaker hold at the high command level, he has not been able to mend fences with various MLAs of the party in Gurdaspur. They may prove to be a stumbling block if he is given the ticket, as he would be fighting four-time MP Vinod Khanna, who has been fielded once again by the BJP.

Apart from these two in the race for the ticket, another name is of Swaran Singh Salaria, a businessman from Mumbai who has been frequently camping in the area and got popular by organising a camp by Baba Ramdev, in the area. P.S. Bhinder, widower of Bibi Sukhbans Kaur Bhinder, who represented the seat for a record six times, is also said to be interested in the seat. But he had not only lost to party rival Gurbachan Singh Babbehali for the fight to the Assembly ticket in 2007, but has also been absent from the area.

Ashwani is trying to strengthen his group following the vacuum created after the death of Bhinder, while Bajwa is taking on the SAD-BJP government head on. His popularity is time-tested due to the family's legacy in political life. When asked, he said he was ready for any challenge and said if the party fields him, he will have to contest as per the dictates of the high command.

Kishan Chand Bains, District Congress Committee chief, said it was natural that more than one person would be in the race, as Congressmen intended to give a "befitting reply" to the SAD-BJP government in the state for its failures. "More assessments are on. The ticket would be decided on the basis of merit," he said.

Cong to launch mass contact programme

The Punjab Congress has drawn out a schedule for mass contact programmes in all districts beginning October 31. To begin with, the programmes will be held in 10 districts. A meeting in this regard was held at the Congress office on Friday. The Congress, which brought to the notice of the Governor the inadequate paddy procurement arrangements, has decided to put off its protests in mandis beginning Monday, given that much of the procurement is complete.

Heading: Octogenarian farmer fights a lone battle to get scrap market shifted from his ancestral land - Indian Express
Content:
India-australia second TEST z Crowd started trickling in by afternoon as the Master Blaster inched closer to milestone

At the end of Day One of the India-Australia Test match, it was only the Master Blaster's record-breaking feat that dominated conversations among spectators.

Call it an after-effect of IPL, the crowd was minimal at the start of a day that was to later witness one of the greatest moments in Indian cricket. By afternoon, however, 10,000-odd spectators had trickled into the PCA Stadium to stand witness to the historic feat.

"We are here to see Sachin's record. A lot of cricket has happened due to the IPL in Mohali. Sachin's record was something we wanted to see and coming against Australia it means a lot to us," said Ankit Sharma, an executive working in a private bank.

There were also some who had come to watch Sourav Ganguly play his last Test in Mohali. Many of the spectators said they were disappointed to see the empty stands.

Amit Kumar, a cricket fan, said the ICC should take up steps to revive Test cricket. "Sachin's record ensured a sizable crowd in the afternoon. Otherwise, it seems nobody is interested in the Test series despite India playing Australia. Apart from Sachin, we have also come to watch Sourav in action in his last series," said Kumar.

The PCA had invited 1,000 students from various districts of Punjab to watch the Test. Despite its tall claims of making adequate arrangements for them, many students found no seating arrangement and proper catering facilities. They had to wait in the heat for water and food.

"There are no chairs for us. The PCA is treating us like beggars and there is not even proper arrangement of water in the stadium for us," said Rupinder Singh, a student from Ropar.

Heading: Soon, a day care centre for elderly residents - Indian Express
Content:
As you commute on the road leading to the IT Park, you encounter a kabari market bustling with activity. The market stands on a five-and-a-half-acre private plot, the owner of which is fighting a legal battle to get the land vacated.

According to octogenarian Gurdev Singh, a farmer, his land has been encroached upon by scrap dealers for around a decade now.

The irony is that as the owner of the land, Singh had been issued a notice by the Sub Divisional Magistrate East a few months ago to get the land vacated from the scrap dealers. The notice was issued under Section 133 of the CrPC (order for removal of nuisance).

The scrap market is a decade old and Singh has been involved in a legal tangle for more than a year now. Singh recalls: "We used to cultivate the land till a decade ago. We gave up farming after the Administration cut off the water supply from tubewells. As the land was vacant, scrap dealers started setting up their business there."

He adds: "There were talks that the land up to the Sukhna choe would be acquired by the Administration for an information technology park. I thought once the land is acquired, it would be the Administration's responsibility to get it vacated. Since the acquisition was not done, I filed a case against the scrap dealers to get the land vacated." Singh lives in Mohalla Bhara Mal in Manimajra with his family, and according to him, the ancestral house is his sole possession now.

"I am suffering at this age because of no fault of mine. First we had to give up farming. Now, it has been illegally occupied and the Administration is not taking any action. They should help me get the encroachment removed, but it seems there is an absolute lack of will on the part of the authorities to do so," says Singh.

According to Singh's lawyer, though the case has been pending in the court, no decision has been taken as of now.

Heading: ‘Humour can go a long way in making life a smooth ride’ - Indian Express
Content:
In what will be a first-of-its-kind concept in the tricity, Panchkula is soon going to get a 'day care centre' for the elderly residents of the city. To be set up on the lines of crèche for kids, the centre will have a library, tennis and volleyball courts among other facilities.

The centre, which will come up at the Red Cross office in Sector 15, will not only look after all the needs of the old people during the daytime, but will also provide them with meals.

"The aim is to facilitate the old residents of the city who find it difficult to pass time sitting alone at home. Also, with the working children and grandchildren hardly having time for their parents, the centre will give them an opportunity to interact with other persons of their age group," said an official of the Panchkula Red Cross.

The centre will remain open from 9 am to 5 pm. Arrangement for TV and music system will also be made. While the Red Cross office has been shifted to the first floor to accommodate the centre, construction of volleyball and tennis courts has already begun.

"As there are plans to provide them with meals during their stay at the centre, a special mess is also being opened up for the purpose. Those seeking enrolment at the centre will have to pay a nominal fee. The exact amount is yet to be decided," added the official.

Reacting to the move, Shalini Garg, a resident of Sector 11, said: "As both my husband and I work, my father stays all alone at home. We are always worried about his safety. But once the day care centre becomes operational, we will not only be carefree about his safety, he will also be able to pass time in the company of people of his age group."

Heading: ‘Australia has something in store for everyone’ - Indian Express
Content:
"Life is a journey and each of us has our own path to tread on. The least we can do is make it easy and comfortable," says sixteen-year-old Kunnal Sharma. This student from Stepping Stones School feels that humour can go a long way in making life a smooth ride.

Always among the top three students in class, Kunnal had scored 95 percent in his Class X Boards. "I missed coming first by a few marks but I am happy nevertheless. My hardwork has duly been rewarded," he says.

His favourite subjects are Mathematics and Chemistry. "I have always liked solving sums, the reason why I find Mathematics so interesting. Chemistry and Physics come a close second. It is because of my interest in these subjects that I opted for the non-medical stream," Kunnal says. With aspirations to be an engineer when he grows up, he states matter-of-factly, "IIT is a tough nut to crack but I will put in my best. I believe that one should do his best and leave the rest to God."

Kunnal had been chosen as the school captain in 2007 and before that he had donned the cap of a house captain for two consecutive years.

Apart from academics, Kunnal is equally good at dramatics and debating. He has won many inter-school declamation contests and public speaking comes easily to him.

He is passionate about theatre and has been a regular participant in youth festivals that are held in city colleges. He was awarded the Best Actor Award at the Sambhang Natya Utsava held in 2007 and also participated in the International Drama Festival held last year. "I have been involved with theatre for the last many years. I find it to be a very powerful means of communication which, if used effectively, can help create awareness about many social causes," he feels.

His hobbies include swimming, cycling and surfing the net. Spending time with friends is a major stress buster, he says. Kunnal draws inspiration from his parents, particularly his father. "He is very diligent and focused in whatever he does. I admire his sense of discipline," Kunnal sums up.

Heading: PCA officials booked for disrespect to Tricolour - Indian Express
Content:
An Australian Education Fair was organised at Hotel Mountview on Friday. More than 500 visitors attended the fair, where different Australian universities and colleges including Victoria, Central Queensland University, Holmes and Carrick among others had come to attract Indian students.

"Students from the region form a major part of those going to Australia for higher education. Good career

opportunities along witha comfortable lifestyle make it a lucrative option," said Gulshan Kumar of Kangaroo Studies.

Speaking on the occasion, Kumar said that the best courses are those which offer skill-based degrees. "The country requires a lot of skilled workers. This is the reason why courses like community welfare, hotel management and horticulture are so much in demand. Apart from this, courses in graphic arts, MBA and web designing are also coming up," Kumar said.

Talking about job security, he said, "It is a myth that Australia has achieved its saturation point and that there is no room for outsiders. Those who pass out after completing their courses do not remain unemployed. It may take sometime to absorb them

but they do get good jobs," he clarified.

"People from all the over the world have come and settled in Australia. This is because it has something in store for everyone, from academics to jobs. Apart from this, studying in Australia is not a very expensive affair. Students get quality education at a very nominal cost in comparison to universities like Harvard and Oxford," he concluded.

'Australia has something in store for everyone'

Heading: Drug racket: Ranjit Bajaj named in inquiry report - Indian Express
Content:
India-Australia match z Indian Flag unfurled upside down at the inaugural ceremony

In what may seem as an example of disrespect to the National Flag, the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) today

unfurled the Indian Tricolour upside down.

The Tricolour was in the same position for half an hour, when Lalru Station House

Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector Sukhwinderjit Singh, posted on flag duty, noticed the anomaly and immediately summoned the PCA officials.

The concerned PCA officials, meanwhile, have been booked under Section 2(L) of the Prevention of Insult to National Honour Act, 1971.

Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh, told Newsline that punitive action would be taken against the guilty officials after identification.

"Our SHO not only restored the national honour but also moved a complaint against the PCA officials," Aulakh said.

He said that there is a provision of imprisonment up to three years or fine, or both, in such cases. The PCA honorary treasurer G S Walia, said an official of the PCA Technical Committee had hoisted the Tricolour upside down. While admitting that it was a serious offence, Walia said it was "unintentional". He added that the guilty official had been served a warning.

On the other hand, various government offices in the city and other places wore a deserted look as the entire District Administration was on "cricket duty" at the

PCA Stadium.

Jamuna Devi, an octogenarian, who had come to meet the deputy commissioner from a far-off village said: "The CM gives statements that officers will work at the doorstep of the public, but officers are not even available in their offices."

Officials at the District Administration, meanwhile, said they could either remain in office or be on field duty. "It is not a fun task, rather very tiring to remain standing and roam around the stadium for five days," said a senior district official.

The massive barricading and traffic restrictions, meanwhile, greatly inconvenienced the public.

No other VVIP, meanwhile, was present to witness the match except Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, who inaugurated the event and left after 20 minutes. Badal was meeting the members of the Indian and Australian teams in the ground when the national flag was fluttering

upside down.

Heading: MLA threatens mass agitation if retrenched QuarkCity - Indian Express
Content:
Report has also indicted six police officers including SI Harinder Singh Sekhon

The name of Ranjit Bajaj, son of a senior retired IAS couple in Punjab, surfaced in the preliminary inquiry report, probing the nexus between the police and drug peddlers.

The inquiry report has also indicted a sub-inspector of the Special Crime Investigation Cell, Harinder Singh Sekhon, along with five other police officers. The report stated the police officers used to take money from a drug peddler, Raju, and assisted him in selling drugs without any hindrance in the city.

The report stated that the interrogation report of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) reads: "It has come to the notice that SI Harinder Singh Sekhon is in the band of suspicious characters and shady persons."

The report also includes the name of a transporter, a discotheque owner, two bouncers of the discotheque and Ranjit. A departmental inquiry has now been initiated. Sources said if the charges are proved, their services will be terminated. DSP B S Chadha has been asked to conduct the inquiry.

The preliminary inquiry, conducted by DSP (Traffic) J S Cheema, found that Sekhon had contact with "high-profile" persons in the city who took drugs. Raju, the drug peddler, used to deliver the drugs through the police officers. The report also stated that the call records of Sekhon indicates that he had contacts with both the consumers and drug peddlers.

Ranjit Bajaj while speaking with the Newsline said that he helped the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) in arresting Raju. "He is trying to implicate me by taking my name in his interrogation. I helped the NCB to catch the peddler. After I came to know that my name was coming up, I asked the NCB Zonal Director through SMS to get my medical examination done. I am not at all chronic drug addict and have no relation with Raju and I don't even know him," he added.

NCB Zonal Director Saji Mohan, on the other hand, refuted the claims of Ranjit that he had helped the sleuths in getting the drug peddler. "It was our electronic surveillance which made Raju fall in our net. He sent me an SMS text and I replied that he was victim of crime," he said.

The nexus had surfaced on July 10, when Raju and his accomplice were arrested by the NCB for possessing heroine and smack.

During his interrogation, Raju had revealed the names of six police officers — Sekhon and head constables Baljit Singh, Sukhjinder, Kuldeep Singh Bichithar Singh, and Mohan Singh.

He also revealed that he used to bribe them for running his racket. All the six police officers were suspended. The NCB has also issued them notices to them to join the investigations.

The report also gives details about an incident when a police party from Punjab rhad gone to Raju's house in Kajheri village for a raid. Raju reportedly did not open the door.

Station House Officer of police station, Sector 36, Inspector Devinder Sharma and Sub-Inspector Kirpal Singh also reached the spot to assist the Punjab police to arrest Raju. The report stated head constables — Baljit Singh and Sukhjinder Singh — who were posted in the Crime Branch, Sector 11, requested the police team not to arrest Raju, which clearly indicates their involvement in the racket.

Ranjit to Saji: Sir, isnt't it unfair to be influenced by pure hearsay and rumours. I will willingly go for a medical examination; at your convenience and place of choice. Then, you can pronounce your verdict instead of the present pre-conceived notions, a totally stereotyped and hearsay-based image you seem to have of me. Is it fair to be forming your impression without even hearing my side of the story, especially when that was formed based on the words of someone for whom they are just that? Will you trust that criminal Raju or his words? I will also want an identification parade proving I haven't met him even once.

Saji to Ranjit: You are being fed with rumours by some media personnel, so am I. Understand that if you an addict, you are a victim of crime.

Heading: Inhuman treatment inside lockup: inquiry report gives clean chit to accused cops - Indian Express
Content:
Quarkcity India, the state's most touted Information Technology special economic zone in Mohali, got political colour, with Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu pitching in to support the retrenched staffers of the company on Friday.

The MLA met the management of the company and asked them to take back its 400 staffers, including some engineers, who had been fired on Wednesday, on the pattern of Jet Airways. He also threatened to launch a public agitation against the US-based company from Monday, if his demand was not met.

Sidhu also apprised Punjab Governor Gen (Retd) S F Rodrigues of the plight of the retrenched staffers and sought his intervention into the matter.
