He also urged Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, to take note of the hundreds of local youth, who have been rendered jobless and asked him to exercise the government's power to help them.

He also visited the site of the QuarkCity project at Industrial Focal Point in Phase VIII-B, and met its Corporate head Gurmohan Singh.

"He cited the adverse impact of the global turmoil on the country's real estate sector as the reason behind the issuance of pink slips, but I categorically told him that this will not be tolerated as the company owes much to the local residents for availing concessions for establishing business here," the MLA said. He added that Gurmohan had assured him that he would convey his views to the company's management in the US. "I will wait till Monday, after which we will gherao the company officials and hold a demonstration against them."

Dubbed as one of the prestigious projects in Punjab, QuarkCity had announced to set up a tax-free zone along with a mega IT project spread over an area of 51.34 acres a few years ago. The total cost of the project was estimated at Rs 3,600 crore with the creation of over 7,000 jobs.

Heading: movie reviews - Indian Express
Content:
The preliminary inquiry into the allegations of inhuman treatment in the Sector-39 police station by four youths, absolved all the police personnel and found the allegations as "baseless". Inquiry officer DSP B S Negi submitted his report to SSP S S Srivastava on Friday.

The four complainants- Ravinder alias Tinda, Monu, Salman and Ramesh — were arrested in connection with a group clash in Dadumajra village on October 2. The accused had met the SSP two days later in his office and narrated the entire incident to him after which the inquiry was marked. They had alleged in their complaints that four police personnel, including Sub Inspector Pargat Singh, asked them to pass urine on each other and made them stand with slippers in their mouth apart from physical assault.

The inquiry report stated that the complainant seemed to have levelled allegations to influence the case against them and put pressure on the officer investigating their case.

SSP S S Srivastava said the inquiry officer examined all the witnesses and circumstantial evidences including CCTV camera footages in the police station. "Besides this, the complainants were medically examined and produced before the magistrate to record their statements but they failed to provide any evidence," he added.

Heading: Dengue on the rise in Ambala - Indian Express
Content:
KARZZZ

CAST: Urmila Matondkar, Himesh Reshmmiya, Shweta Kumar, Gulshan Grover, Dino Morea; DIRECTOR: Satish Kaushik

When Subhash Ghai's Karz came out in 1980, there were mutterings about how it had ripped off cheesy Hollywood drama The Reincarnation of Peter Proud. But they soon subsided not only because Ghai cleverly admitted to copying, having out-cheesed the original effortlessly. It was also because Karz was a cracker of an entertainer: as the born-again hero, Rishi rocked, there's never been a crueller, classier vamp than Simi, and if ever there is a compilation of classic movie themes, the haunting Ek Hasina Thi is sure to top the list.

This Karzzz, despite the extra zees for luck, is a blot. Except for the names of the characters, which are exactly the same, nothing else is: the treatment is sloppy, even by Satish Kaushik's standards, and the acting is plain execrable.

For those who've come in twenty-eight years after the fact, this is how it goes. Pop star Monty (Himesh) starts having visions — of a man and a woman, a huge mansion in the hills, a "Kali ka mandir", and an airplane going up in flames. It's a case of "punarjanam", a psychiatrist declares sagely. And whoosh, we are launched into a series of flashbacks, unravelling how Monty is actually rich businessman Ravi Varma (Dino) re-incarnated, and has come into the world to wreak revenge on the murderous, greedy-for-his-millions wife Kamini (Urmila).

Himesh adds a hair transplant and a smile to his extremely-limited repertoire (in his last year's debut Aap Ka Suroor, he had appeared throughout in his till-then trademark baseball cap, and scowl). A badly-made up Urmila dons skin-tight gowns, large tracts of her chest gleaming with bronzer, gold trousers, and scarlet lipstick. She also sounds distressingly like Archana Puran Singh when she simpers: hard to think that she was once an A-list actress. There's also a new girl, Shweta (director Indra Kumar's daughter) getting a brief look-see: all she has to do is to gaze adoringly at Himesh. That must have been tough. Even the climactic song-cum-whodunit denouement, which has been lifted completely, is mangled. In between, you can hear Rohini Hattangadi, who plays the "dukhiyari maa" utter lines like these: "mere kaleje ke tukda", she goes, "mere laal".

Moral: if you can't make, don't re-make.

SHOOT ON SIGHT

CAST: Naseerudin Shah, Om Puri, Brian Cox, Greta Scacchi, Gulshan Grover; DIRECTOR: Jagmohan Mundhra

JAG Mundhra's films have topical, relevant subjects. That's the good part. The bad part is that they do not possess a single subtle note: everything is heavily underscored, leaving no place for understatement or nuance.

And that's something one misses sorely, especially in a film like his latest. Shoot On Sight is based on the London bombings in 2005, which unleashed a whole spate of racial profiling. Is it a crime to be Muslim? Are all Muslims terrorists? These questions, asked by sundry characters in Shoot On Sight yield answers which, for all their truth, seem like they are stating the obvious.

It's not as if Naseer, as Commander Ali of Scotland Yard, doesn't know the pitfalls of playing a Muslim cop in a still-white country. In his scenes with 'gori' wife (Greta), defiant daughter, couple of openly racist colleagues, and sympathetic boss (Brian), he shows as much deftness as the script allows. But that's not much at all: Ali's childhood friend from Lahore, now a "mullah" advocating jehad (Om) is all surface— he strokes his beard, recites from the Koran, and colours impressionable minds.

More predictabilities abound. Rebellious Muslim teenager facing off da— he won't let her date white boys who want to go all the way. Jolly meat-shop owner doling out gosht and good cheer. Good white wife trying to balance the tensions in her family, and his. We've seen all this before, with much more depth: there's more to multi-culturalism, and the problems of being brown, post 9/11, than these very broad, too familiar brush-strokes. .

CHEENTI CHEENTI BANG BANG (animation)

Voices by Ashish Vidyarthi, Mahesh Manjrekar, Asrani, Anjan Srivastava

DIRECTOR: R D Mallik

Two colonies of ants live on either side of a river bank. Lal Cheentas and Kala Cheentas have presumably lived happily before the evil Ghun arrives in their midst to sow dissent and discord. This could have been a fun flick: ants, and other cute creepy-crawlies, lend themselves well to animation (Antz, A Bug's Life). Some money and effort has been spent on the production, but the characters are all cardboard, not being able to create the slightest interest in the proceedings.

What you get is endless, inane chatter peppered with creaky dialogue ( "nestanabood"; "yudhh ka danka baja diya", "yunki baat ki baat hai", "mere dil mein saadh hai"). And an old ant called Lal Boodha who's supposed to have leered at a comely young thing, who tells the ant queen: "woh mardood hamare badan pe toot pada".

Huh? This is supposed to be a film for little children?

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
'Let's have it again', say tricity's foodies after CITCO's South Indian food festival

The timing couldn't have been better. If there was the Southern extravaganza 'Poompuhar' in one part of the city another part saw a fest that only added to the celebrations. Tricity's South Indian Food lovers got a special treat at Spicy South Food Festival organized by the Chandigarh Industrial and Tourism Development Corporation (CITCO) from October 18 to 20. Tourists coming to the region also got their share of another part of India at Hotel Mountview. For the first time CITCO introduced non-vegetarian South Indian delicacies. CITCO tabled special non-vegetarian menu with two chicken dishes and one each with mutton and fish. This was in addition to classic vegetarian dishes like dosas, idli etc. The festival was a big hit among the tricity foodies who binged on the non-veg dishes giving the fresh taste a thumbs-up.

The three-course menu started with soup, Rasam with papad or butter milk for non-vegetarian as well as vegetarian food. In the non-vegetarian segment, the main course had chicken chattinad and koly kuzhambu. Apart from the usual egg dosa people there was also mutton vindaloo and meen kuzhambu to choose from. For the vegetarians there were porrial, avail (seasonal vegetarian with coconut), alookora, kanji idli and plain idli with samber. The thaijir sadan (rice) together with options like curd, lemon or coconut had people asking for more. For the sweet addicts there was pal payasam, sweet pongal and ice -cream and veeda (plain and sweet paan). The chefs of Tamil Nadu were also associated with the food festival to prepare authentic South Indian food with their own spices and ingredients. With the package rate of Rs 399 per person the festival had everybody asking for more. But you wouldn't have to wait another year now because the hotel has decided to add a few non-veg Southern dishes to its regular menu. Feast on!

Fast and furious
It's going to be the It-acquisition of the year for sure. The new Bentley Continental Flying Spur Speed, launched at Delhi's Inter Continental Hotel recently can go up to a maximum speed of 322 km/hour. Heading: On Karva Chauth, city celebrates the nuptial bond - Indian Express
Content:
Launches Rs 137-crore project to avoid repeated flooding of the Ghaggar

Following reports and allegations of bogus beneficiaries in the much-hyped atta-dal scheme for the poor, the state government today ordered review of the scheme to weed out bogus and fake beneficiaries.

Announcing this here today, Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal directed re-verification of the beneficiaries and include only the poor and needy people, for whom the scheme was originally framed.

Addressing a public rally here today after launching the Rs 137.43-crore project for taming of the Ghaggar to avoid recurrence of floods in the area, Badal said that a fresh survey in this regard would soon be carried out.

"It is shameful that few well-off people were availing the benefits of this scheme by registering themselves at the time of survey," he said.

The CM also launched work on the project to build embankments and to widen the Ghaggar, which has been the demand of the people of the area for over 60 years. Badal said the entire project would cost Rs 217 crore, of which Rs 137.43 crore would be spent on the first phase of 22 kilometres from Khanauri to Makraur Sahib. The 18 Km-stretch from Makraur Sahib to Karail would be taken up in the second phase.

Apart from this, the discharge capacity of Bhakhra Main Line passing through this area would also be enhanced from 14,000 cusec to 25,000 cusec. About 44 villages, over an area of 60,000 acres, would be benefited by the project.

Blaming Congress leaders for the neglect of the area, Badal said former CM Capt Amarinder Singh laid the foundation stone of this project at the fag end of his tenure. "This showed his lack of seriousness towards the project and his bogus attempt to help the people from the fury of floods".

Badal repeated his age-old charge of the Centre adopting a discriminatory approach towards Punjab farmers. "Even though the farmers of Punjab filled the nation's food basket in the hour of food crisis, Punjab did not even receive a letter of appreciation in return".

Badal also rued the Centre's decision to announce a "meager bonus" of Rs 50 per quintal on paddy and termed it as a joke with the farmers. "Our government is merely a mute spectator to the Centre's apathetic attitude towards the farming community", the CM said.

Badal announced that he would hold a day-long Sangat Darshan of Khanauri sub tehsil. Earlier, the Chief Minister also dedicated to the public PSEB's 66-KV Grid sub-station at Banarasi village at the cost of Rs three crore.

Sangrur MP and SAD Secretary General Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa also charged the Congress with neglect of the area. Punjab Irrigation Minister Janmeja Singh Sekhon said that the approach of Badal to focus on the key areas of power and irrigation network would certainly prove to be a boon in the field of agriculture as 70 per cent of our population was engaged in this vocation.

In his welcome address, SAD general secretary and former Patiala MP Prem Singh Chandumajra said that the starting of this Ghaggar taming project was his dream. "Our party had promised this project before the polls and we are fulfilling the promise now," he said.

The CM also announced Rs 21 lakh for the provision of sports kits to 21 Youth clubs and Rs 50 lakh each for the 10 village panchayats in recognition of their outstanding services to the people during the recent floods.

Construction of road from Khanauri to Moonak and restoration of the Sangatpura minor, which had been shut down for the past 35 years, was also in the long list of announcements made.

Heading: 3 witnesses record their statements before panel - Indian Express
Content:
The city was bathed in the festivity of Karva Chauth on Friday as fasting women, young and old, dressed in their traditional best assembled at the temples to celebrate the day.

Sujata Singla, an 18-year-old college student, said: "I got a brand new lehanga stitched for this fast. My mother also brought me a small gold set." She added: "I simply love the idea of this fast. While unmarried girls in my family can break the fast after seeing the first star, I would like to wait for the moon. It is so romantic!"

Poonam Sharma, a bank executive, who would rather wear business suits to work, preferred to wear a saree today. "It feels more Indian and traditional," she said.

Asked about the plans for the evening, Payal said: "My marriage is almost five years old now and just like all the other years, I will wear my wedding lehnga. This fast is not just about praying for the long life of your husband, at least for me, it strengthens our bond each year."

The fervour is not restricted to the wives alone. Pankaj Mehra, a businessman, said: "Though I cannot fast with my wife, I am careful about the fact that I need to take care of her."

Heading: Sportspersons upbeat as Sachin conquers another peak - Indian Express
Content:
The three witnesses named in the PAU sexual harassment case deposed before the inquiry committee on Friday and recorded their statements. They are M S Grewal, Students' Welfare Officer, a woman assistant professor currently with one of the Krishi Vikas Kendras and a student of the university.

"I was called by the committee as I work in the same department. I told the committee all that I knew and moreover the committee, as I am told, has such evidence in the matter that my trying to unduly favour the complainant or the accused will not serve any purpose," said Grewal.

He added: "I am here not to take sides but to only say what I know or what I have seen."

The other two witnesses maintained the same line and refused to speak much on the issue.

A woman employee of the university had levelled charges of sexual harassment against Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, Director, Students' Welfare, in September.

Dean College of Home Science Dr Neelam Grewal, who is the chairing the committee, said: "While there is no official deadline to settle the case, we will wind it up by next week."

About today's development, Dr Grewal said: "Statements have been taken and they will be studied."

When asked as to why Dr Brar has not been served any official communication regarding the ongoing inquiry, Dr Grewal maintained silence.

She, however, added: "Everything will be crystal clear as the case unfolds."

Dr Brar has been on a long leave till December 31.

Heading: ‘Learn the right practice of Homoeopathy to perform miracles’ - Indian Express
Content:
At 2.31 pm, on Friday afternoon, when Sachin Tendulkar surpassed Brian Lara's record of being the highest run-getter in Test cricket, he not only reinforced his image as the one of the true greats of the game but also drew praises and accolades from all corners of the city.

Arun Dhand, former veteran World Badminton Champion, said it was an amazing feat for the ace Indian batsman.

"I went to the PCA Stadium to watch Tendulkar break the record and I am very happy that he did not let his fans down," said Dhand.

Hardeep Singh, who was part of the Indian Hockey team to the 1984 Olympic Games, was also elated.

"He (Sachin) has done the country proud. Being a sportsperson, I feel very happy for him," he said.

Asked if it is time for Tendulkar to hang-up his boots, Singh said: "We should not force senior players like Sachin to retire. We should leave this decision to him."

Expressing his happiness over the achievement of the "Little Master", Teja Singh Dhaliwal, general secretary, Punjab Basketball Association (PBA), said Sachin had done the country proud, time and again. "I feel age should not be the criterion for any player to retire but his fitness and performance should count. If the players are fit and performing well even at an advanced age, there should be no problem in allowing them to continue," added Dhaliwal.

Rahul Bhatia, a junior-level cricket coach with the rebel Indian Cricket League (ICL), said: "Sachin's milestone is a slap on the faces of those who were lobbying for his retirement. I think he can easily play till the next World Cup."

Another cricketer, Khushal Sharma said: "Sachin has given his best to the country and he has done the country proud with his scintillating performances in a career spanning nearly two decades."

Heading: Tame Game - Indian Express
Content:
"Homoeopathy is the only branch of medicine, which deals with the disease by making the immune system react to it positively," said Dr Prafull Vijayakar, a Mumbai-based homoeopath, while speaking on the first day of the two-day national seminar on Predictive Homeopathy held at the Guru Nanak Bhawan.

Nearly 1,000 people attended the seminar where Dr Vijayakar spoke extensively on the "Utility of Miasmatic Philosophy" (Three stages of development of pathology) and shared cases which were solved by Homoeopathy, when the other branches of medicine had given up.

"These are cases that are not in isolation and therefore I want you to learn the right practice of Homoeopathy to perform miracles," he told the gathering, mainly comprising homoeopaths.

Citing a case of a congenitally blind child, he said: "The child was blind since birth. He did not have pupils and therefore had no hope. When treated with homoeopathy, the child was able to see."

Presenting a case study of a patient who had received 65 per cent burns, Dr Vijayakar said: "The patient was treated with the help of a prescription given only after a telephonic conversation with the doctor."

"I do not claim these cases to be my monopoly and nobody else can treat them like this. Yes, they are not less than miracles but one can learn to make them happen. I only want that all of us know the right homoeopathy, in which, unlike other branches, you give one dose to the patient and forget," he asserted.

Dr Vijayakar was once a practising allopath. He is credited with various in-depth studies on the principles of homoeopathy. He has also explained the principles of homoeopathy through modern sciences like embryology, physiology, immunology, pathology and genetics.

Guests on the occasion included Dr SA Katekari from Chandigarh, Dr Arun Bhasme, Dr Tejinder Pal Singh, director of Guru Nanak Homeopathic Medical College and Dr SM Singh from Allahabad.

Heading: Zzz it is - Indian Express
Content:
Now, where would we be if we didn't have the father of the nations – The United States of America? Lying somewhere in the slimy, presumably cold intestines of aliens or wriggling under the tips of daggers wielded by really, I repeat really, terrifying terrorists. Like Bollywood would find a song for a burp even, Ridley Scott and his clan would have America swat even mosquitoes out of the whole world.

So, this time round in Body of Lies Scott sends Roger Ferris (Leonardo Di Caprio) to Jordan as an undercover CIA agent to track a terrorist named Al Saalim down. Back in the Virginia headquarters of the CIA, his manipulative boss Edward Hoffman (Russel Crowe) tells Ferris around and keeps a tab on him. Enter Hani Salaam, chief of the Jordanian General Intelligence Department who joins hand with Ferris, much to the chagrin of Hoffman. It is then that the chase, to nab Saalim, picks up.

And for a generation which though the twin towers gave Bin Laden his precious 15 minutes of fame while going down, think again. Because terrorists, it seems, look the same everywhere — from a watery Mission Istanbul closer home to a great American cine-dream — turning Bin Laden a household name of sorts to the film fraternity across the world. And if you leave out the abundance of f-words in Di Caprio's speech, it's not very difficult to hear echoes of several Sunny Deol dhai kilo flicks in his last rant against the jehadis who misinterpret the Koran.

That is not to say that the film leaves you wondering if Gladiator was a fluke. It has a fairly-paced narrative, and since it's a CIA-chase, not a Maharashtra Police-one, the thrills and the twists keep coming in quick succession. The director thankfully doesn't play up the romance angle and leaves it more for occasional guffaws. And the as the camera feasts on the rusty, rocky topography typical to Middle Eastern countries, we can't seem to have enough of sight-seeing.

Di Caprio, when he is not getting beaten up to jelly by all sorts of people, does a good job as an impressionable, slightly sentimental, enthusiastic agent mostly at odds with his boss. Russel Crowe, when he does manage to look up from the laptop he remains glued to mostly throughout the film, does complete justice to a crisp, manipulative, dismissive, know-it-all boss. Mark Strong makes Hani Salaam stand out with his intriguing physicality. The scenes which get the three together, with egos flying around, are delectable. But the sad news is, there's so little of them.

Film: Body of Lies

Director: Ridley Scott

Cast: Leonardo Di Caprio, Russel Crowe, Mark Strong

Rating: zi zi zi zi zi zi zi zi zi zi

Running at: Inox (Forum, City Centre, Swabhumi)

Heading: Amrita, Abhishek bag double crowns, Akhtar Ali battles on - Indian Express
Content:
A hint of celebrities and some elegant collections made up for an otherwise slow day at the fashion weeks

If nothing else, you can count on Rohit Bal to pull in the crowds. Day three at the Delhi Fashion Week was packed to capacity (for the first time at DFW). In any case, with Bal, in equal parts showman and designer, boredom is unlikely. The flat runway of DFW had been transformed into a gossamer field of of pink organza. Bal's spring summer show began with a model arising from within the cloud of organza, dressed in a layered outfit.

Bal's collection was more couture than pret. Lavishly constructed silhouettes and generous layerings in yellows and oranges for full bodied skirts patterned out of cones and dresses fashioned out of pouffed squares. As usual, Bal ended with a flourish, throwing handfuls of organza confetti at the audience then heading to the afterparty at Ai.

But if it's austerity we're talking about in these crazy times of global recession, Varun Bahl showed how to practice it to perfection at his spring-summer show at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week (WIFW) in front of a full house that had fellow designers like Manish Arora, Rajesh Pratap Singh, Manoviraj Khosla, Ritu Kumar in attendance. With sheer fabrics and basic colours like ivory, olive, salmon pink and beige, Bahl spun out a collection that was at once existential and elegant, spartan and sophisticated. Macrame, crochet, net and hints of lace were interestingly juxtaposed with linen, his characteristic rosettes back in knotted necklines and belts. The menswear had a touch of androgyny to it, but stood out for its sheer versatility. Timeless and very graceful.

Heading: Vasco raring to have a go at East Bengal - Indian Express
Content:
In-form Bengal girl Amrita Mukherjee and Abhishek Alla of Andhra Pradesh walked away with double crowns each in the second edition of the Under-14 Asian Tennis Tournament. The event is being organised under the watchful eyes of the All India Tennis Association (AITA) and Asian Tennis Federation (ATF). Second seed Abhishek Alla defeated the top seed from Mumbai 6-3, 6-2. He then teamed up with Nishchay Rawal and defeated Vishal Passi and Shaikh Abdullah 6-2, 6-3.

In the girls' section, top seed Amrita Mukherjee did not have to work hard to take the singles title beating Simran Kaur Sethi 6-3, 6-4. Amrita Mukherjee pairing up with C Sai Samitha defeated the team of Rimpledeep Kaur and Bhawia Wadhwan 6-2, 5-7, (10-6).

Meanwhile, former Davis Cup captain Akhtar Ali, partnering CB Raju of Andhra Pradesh, reached the semi-finals of the senior doubles 65+ years round in the ongoing second edition of the GVK-AISTA Senior National Ranking Tennis Tournament being held at the Bengal Tennis Association (BTA).

Ali and Raju defeated KV Appalla Raju of Andhra and M Krishnaswamy of Karnataka, in a match which went the distance, by 6-3, 6-7 (4-7), 6-3.

In the 45+ years event, Kamal Thapa of Nepal reached the semi-finals after upstaging third seed Andhra veteran V Srinivas Reddy in straight sets 7-6 (7-2), 6-3. Top seed RE Sudarshan Rao had an easy route to the semis defeating Venkata Pandu Ranga Rao 6-2, 6-0. Fourth seed R Nagraj trounced local hero Dilip Kumar 6-2, 6-1 and second seed Yogesh Shah from Ahmedabad made short work of B Joji Reddy 6-2, 6-4.

In the 55+ years category, Maharashtra's Tahir Ali again created an upset beating fourth seed TAPN Rao in a hard fought battle. Ali too the first set in tie-break and the lost the second again in tie break. It was enough to take the wind out of Rao. Ali prevailed 7-6 (7-5), 6-7 (2-7), 3-0 (retd). Top seed V Rama Mohan Rao of Andhra, fifth seed S Settu of Tamil Nadu and second seed K Radhakrishna Murthy completed the semi-finals line-up.

Sixth seed Kesava Perumal created a mini upset in the quarters of the 65+ singles category. He defeated third seed TN Lakshmanan. The others who made it to the semis were top seed C Radhakrishnan of Tamil Nadu, fourth seed VR Kulkarni of Karnataka and second seed CB Raju of Hyderabad.

Boys' Doubles U-14 (India unless specified): Abhishek Alla & Nishchay Rawal beat Vishal Passi & Shaikh Abdullah 6-2, 6-3.

Girls' Singles U-14 (India unless specified): Amrita Mukherjee (1) (14) beat Simran Kaur Sethi 6-0, 6-4.

Girls' Doubles U-14 years (India unless specified): Amrita Mukherjee & C Sai Samitha beat Rimpledeep Kaur & Bhawika Wadhwan 6-2, 5-7, (10-6).

Heading: Tiwary cracks 152 - Indian Express
Content:
Languishing on just one point from three matches, Vasco SC are desperately looking to earn an elusive win in the ongoing I-League when they take on East Bengal in their Premier Division encounter at the Yuba Bharati Krirangan tomorrow.

Looking to make the most of hosts East Bengal's unimpressive current form, Vasco coach Elvis Goes wants his boys to launch an outright attacking game against the Kolkata side. East Bengal, who are struggling with just three points from three matches so far, are no less desperate in their bid to get back to winning ways. The key in tomorrow's match will be the performance of Vasco's Uzbek trio, and their coach is relying heavily on the three foreigners in his side to deliver in tomorrow's must-win match. "We have decided to go on an all-out attack tomorrow. The target is to get full points, and nothing short. We know East Bengal are a really big side in Kolkata, like the other big sides. But we are not worried. We have good enough players, we have the experienced Cowan Lawrence, who has played in Kolkata. The decision has been taken, you will see us going on a full-scale attack tomorrow," gushed a confident Vasco coach on the eve of the clash.

East Bengal, meanwhile, are expected to start with Sunil Chhetri and Yusif Yakubu upfront. Trump card Chhetri is finally back after injury, but Renedy Singh is doubtful for tomorrow's match. Malswama is set to man the midfield in place of Yakubu, who will play upfront. Jayanta Sen is likely to feature in the playing XI.

Heading: Hamilton tops China practice - Indian Express
Content:
Football managers and coaches are generally a boisterous lot with plenty to boast or whine about in their post-match interviews. But in the build-up to matches, especially against lesser fancied opponents, they often tend to be annoyingly diplomatic with their opinions. And as Air-India prepare for their second consecutive home game against Chirag United at Cooperage on Saturday, that is the theme that seems to emerge. Both Air-India's veteran coach Bimal Ghosh and the Kolkatan debutants' Subrata Bhattacharya underplayed any mention of either team going into the game with any particular advantage, and preferred sticking to the clichéd 'we can't afford to take anyone lightly' approach. But with the I-league having been a season of upsets so far, their guarded response is understandable.

"We have seen the so-called weaker teams posting some huge upsets," said Ghosh. Chirag United came from a goal behind to thump Mumbai giants Mahindra United 3-1 in their last match in the city. But the Air-India coach believes that if Mahindra hadn't missed so many chances in the first-half, the result could have been completely different.

Fighting spirit

"Chirag United must be given credit for showing the tenacity to fight back. But they did show some signs of weakness with their defence and their goalkeeper, and we will be looking to exploit them tomorrow," revealed Ghosh.

Bhattacharya, a former East Bengal player, didn't consider his team's win against the Jeepmen an upset, and believes every game is crucial for first-timers Chirag United.

"Air-India is a tough team to play, and they will be playing at home. We will look to put our best foot forward tomorrow, and hope to continue our run," said Bhattacharya, whose team is sixth on the table above the likes of East Bengal and Mohun Bagan.

The man who won all the accolades after Chirag's win at Cooperage two weeks back was Hardeep Singh Saini, who came off the bench to completely change the complexion of the game. But the coach did not confirm whether the Sikh would find a place in the starting line-up against Air-India.

Ghosh said he was very pleased with the way his team, which is unbeaten so far, has been performing this season. He also reserved special praise for foreigners Michael Tayo and new-signing Emmanuel Ovieghara.

"Tayo was discarded by Salgaocar last season, but I recognised the talent he possesses. I took a chance with him then and it seems to be paying off now," he said about the Man of the Match in Air-India's 2-0 victory over East Bengal last weekend.

Captain Ovieghara may not be scoring too many goals at present, but his coach insisted that the Republic of Benin striker was doing his job to perfection by constantly presenting a threat to opposition defences.

Heading: Tata’s open letter to Bengal: Choose between Buddha way and destructive politics, lawlessness - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party has said that the government must immediately slash interest rates, ask state-owned banks to float rights issues and enlarge their capital base and float a scheme like the Resurgent India Bonds or the India Millennium Deposits to attract foreign inflows.

"Time is of essence and singing lullabies that our (India's) fundamentals are strong will not help," Arun Shourie, senior BJP leader and former disinvestment minister, told The Indian Express Editor-in-Chief Shekhar Gupta on NDTV's Walk the Talk, which will be telecast on Saturday.

According to the BJP, which issued a statement on the global financial turmoil early this week, the current liquidity crisis in India is largely due to the gross mismanagement of the economy by the UPA.

To fight inflation, it continuously tightened the monetary policy by hiking interest rates and the cash reserve ratio (the portion of deposits banks have to keep with the Reserve Bank of India) to 9 per cent over the last two years. It never quite realised that higher prices were more because of supply-side constraints and infrastructure bottlenecks.

"In the last one-and-a-half years, reforms have stopped completely. Populist expenditures have had no accountability. The government used the axe of monetary policy to swat the fly of inflation," Shourie said.

Monetary tightening coupled with fiscal indiscipline has now started impacting the real economy, which is a cause for more serious concern, he said.

Since what is adequate today may turn out to be insufficient tomorrow, the RBI must cut its repo rate (technically the rate at which it lends to banks, but a signal for banks to cut lending rates) by 2 percentage points to 7 per cent by March next year, slash CRR further by 150 basis points (one basis point is one-hundredth of a per cent) to 5 per cent from 6.5 per cent now.

This will pump in Rs 60,000 crore into the banking system and help the small and medium enterprises that are suffering the worst today. Besides, a scheme like Resurgent India Bonds or the India Millennium Deposits will not only help ease the pressure on the rupee but also stabilise exchange rates.

A rights issue by banks will immediately infuse liquidity and also help them become stronger and more competitive, the BJP said in its statement issued earlier this week. "Currently, the market capitalisation of PSU banks is roughly about $40 billion. A $10 billion rights offering, with the government supplying its 60-70 per cent share, will strengthen our banking system dramatically," it said.

Signficantly, Shourie says that the crisis in India is not a reflection of what is happening globally, and the world too has not crossed the hump. "In the world, there are 4-5 rounds. The trigger was the sub-prime crisis. Then came the banks. Actually we are well into that round. But this will be compounded by real firms: those that were leveraged and dependent on our IT exports," he says.

Countries will soon put up non-tariff policies. "That is when I fear again sovereign funds will move in and buy out companies at low prices leading to another round of protectionism against capital flows. China has $1.8 trillion in reserves. There are Singapore, Abu Dhabi and Qatar (with their own sovereign wealth funds). That's when barriers come up. The entire regime of free trade can collapse," he says.

Nevertheless, he cautioned that India cannot celebrate saying American capitalism is collapsing. "Russia is in deep trouble as well," he said, indicating that India must draw the right lessons from the global financial crisis.

Heading: Morcha begins campaign: replace ‘West Bengal’ - Indian Express
Content:
In an extraordinary "open letter", Ratan Tata has explained to the people of West Bengal his decision to pull out the Nano factory from Singur, and urged them-especially the youth-to express themselves on how they would like to see their state progress in the years ahead.

"Would they like to support the present Government of Mr Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee to build a prosperous state...," Tata wrote. "Or would they like to see the state consumed by the destructive political environment of confrontation, agitation, violence and lawlessness? Do they want education and jobs in the industrial and high-tech sectors or does the future generation see its future prosperity achieved on a 'stay as we are' basis?"

The letter warns of "history repeating itself", with the flight of capital and investment from Bengal, "at this crucial time and moment of hope for the state".

Explaining the letter, Tata said: "Over the past three weeks there have been statements... criticising the decision taken by Tata Motors to move the Nano car project, claiming that this decision was hasty and politically motivated. I therefore feel compelled to explain how our dream of contributing to the industrial revival of West Bengal has been shattered by an environment of politically motivated agitation and hostility.

"Many may have forgotten that West Bengal was a major centre for heavy industry and steel fabrication. Agitation and violence drove away many industries around 30 years ago, and it has only been in recent times that the present government has been able to rebuild the confidence of the investors."

CPM MP Md Salim said, "The younger people... know how Mamata Banerjee and her supporters played a destructive role... The Tatas should take steps to consolidate the support they have received from the Government into something positive."

Trinamool's Sougata Roy said, "How much they love Bengal is clear from the alacrity with which they moved to Gujarat." He alleged the letter had been written in "consultation with CPM".

The Congress said it would not comment.

Bengal should relocate

Mamata: Yechury

Attacking Mamata Banerjee for her "opposition" to the Nano project, senior CPM leader Sitaram Yechury on Friday said: "If she has succeeded in relocating Nano project from Bengal, people of Bengal should consider relocating her."

Heading: Jubilant Jet employees play safe, distance themselves from CITU - Indian Express
Content:
The Gorkha Janmukti Morcha (GJM) began to implement its diktat to rename signboards of government offices and commercial establishments from "West Bengal" to "Gorkhaland" in Darjeeling district on Friday.

In response, the district administration said that in line with the state home secretary's directives, legal action will be initiated against the perpetrators.

Darjeeling SP Rahul Srivastav said the police are in the process to register cases related to defacement of public property. "As of today, we are yet to take stock of the total number of cases of defacement. We will conduct investigations into the complaints received," he said.

"Already, some cases have been registered with us by officials of the government departments. In each case, once we identify the perpetrators, arrests and legal action for defacement of public property will be initiated. We are yet to receive any complaints from private commercial establishments," the SP added.

In Kolkata, Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti denounced the GJM action as "completely illegal" and said the Darjeeling district administration will deal with it legally. "The government doesn't have full information, but clear instructions have been given to the district magistrate and the SP. No drastic police action has been taken so far to maintain a conducive atmosphere to facilitate the ongoing tripartite talks," he added.

GJM Secretary Roshan Giri, meanwhile, maintained that the latest stage of the non-cooperation movement had been implemented at several places in the district. "Government and private signboards have been changed from West Bengal to Gorkhaland right from the Dooars to Siliguri and Darjeeling. We did not face any resistance from the district administration. We don't have a total count of the number of signboards changed," he added.

Apart from the drive to change signboards, the GJM also held a public meeting at Chowk Bazar in Darjeeling. The next round of tripartite talks is slated for November. The GJM leadership, however, is maintaining that their actions are democratic and will not affect the progress of the talks.

Heading: Reinstated airhostess gets new life - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Jet Airways Chairman Naresh Goyal reinstated all cabin crew who were given pink slips, the mood was one of jubilance at the Kolkata airport on Friday.

The cabin crew, who till Thursday were seen protesting under the banner of CITU, preferred to stay away from the Left-backed labour union's office on Friday.

On Friday, when the CITU held a victory rally to celebrate the reinstatement of sacked Jet employees, some of the familiar faces of the airways cabin crew members decided to give it a miss.

"We don't want to be a part of the rally. Our base manager has told us to leave the past behind and start afresh. We don't want to irk the Jet management by mingling with political groups," a flight steward told CITU leader Swapan Gupta. The Jet management, meanwhile, organised a welcome party for all the reinstated cabin crew in Kolkata. "Our base manager organised a lunch for us and we were given a very warm welcome by our seniors," said Sangamitra Majumder, a flight stewardess.

Most of the 21 cabin crew members based in Kolkata received a written copy of their termination letters on Thursday evening though they were told to stay away from the office on Tuesday night. The letter said the company was terminating their services and they would be given a month's salary, caution money and other pending dues. "Our assistant base manager has asked us to destroy the letter and concentrate on work," said Soumen Chakraborty, a flight steward. The cabin crew has been assured that they would be able to resume their normal flight schedule shortly. "Our roster is prepared in Mumbai. As soon as the new roster is made, we will be back on duty," he added.

Initially, CITU leaders insisted the cabin crew should take part in the victory rally. "It is your rally and you should be a part of it," Gupta said. Later, they agreed to leave the crew members out of the rally.

"After all, they have to work with the management. Participating in political rallies might jeopardise their careers," said Deepankar Ghosh, a senior CITU leader. CITU leaders, however, said that they did not believe that Goyal was unaware about the job cuts. "This is not possible. He had to reinstate the employees due to political pressure," Gupta said.

Heading: Land acquisition delay hits Diamond Harbour container terminal project - Indian Express
Content:
With Jet Airways announcing the termination of the services of several members of its cabin crew, many of the Kolkata staff had been shocked as well as disappointed. Joyeeta Ghosh's (24) family, however, was shattered when they came to know she was jobless.

While most youngsters of her age enjoy the leisure of college life, Ghosh runs a household at Peerless Colony in Sodepur.

She lost her father, the sole breadwinner of the family, in July 2007, and has to fend for herself and her mother.

"This was not just a job for me. It was the sole support for me and my mother," she said. Fresh out of Victoria College, she had joined an Airhostess training academy with dreams of joining the aviation or the hospitality industry. "I also had plans of studying further later," she said. After the one-year course, she got a lucrative job offer in 2006 with an established hotel chain in Kerala.

"My father fell very ill suddenly. I have no siblings and I could not leave my parents in that situation," she recalls.

To support her family, Ghosh took up a small job with the Airhostess training academy and it seemed to her that her dreams of flying had been crushed forever.

"My father's condition worsened the next year. He was diagnosed as suffering from cancer and doctors told us that there was no hope of his recovery. He finally left us in June last year," said Ghosh. "My father ran a lucrative business, but after his demise, the business was usurped by other partners leaving me and my mother to fend for ourselves," she added. That was when she joined Jet Airways as a flight stewardess since they offered good salary. "I save each and every penny for the future, as I have to take care of my mother," said Ghosh.

The news of the termination of her services shattered both Ghosh and her mother Asha. "It was like the end of the world for us. I could not afford to study further and I would not get any other job that could match my pay," recalled Ghosh. "I have got back my life. The episode has, however, taught me a huge lesson that nothing is certain in life," said Ghosh.

Heading: Govt to beautify ghats, develop Howrah station area - Indian Express
Content:
More than 10 months have passed since the shipping ministry decided to accept Capt Mohan Committee's recommendation for a dedicated container terminal at the Diamond Harbour dock in South 24 Parganas. But work at the proposed site is yet to see the light of the day due to continued delay in land acquisition.

Under the project, Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) is planning to build four jetties to explore the deep-drafted facilities in the south of the state. Of the 125 acres land proposed for the project, about 30 per cent land is under the Ministry of Defence. According to reports, while about 57 acres of land will come from the state government and about 40 acres is private property, the rest of the land belongs to the Ministry of Defence. It is now examining the proposal before it hands over the land to KoPT.

"The state government has agreed in principle to go for land acquisition for us, and the district administration will do the land acquisition for the project," said A K Chanda, KoPT Chairman. There seems to be no initiative on the administration's part to acquire land for the project.

The request for qualification (RFQ) for the project was to be shortlisted in July, but it is yet to take place. RFQ is a process by which prospective bidders are shortlisted for the contract. "The RFQ will only be floated once all the necessary clearances are obtained," said Chanda.

Since the last three years, the port had maintained second position in cargo handling. In 2007-08, however, the KoPT handled 57.329 million tonnes of cargo and slipped to the third position.

Diamond Harbour, situated about 50 km from the city, provides a draft of 9 metres, which is more than any other riverine port in the state. The officials of the KoPT say there has been no instance of dredging at the dock since the last 15 years. KoPT officials feel due to the silting of the riverbed, the vessels at the Kolkata and Haldia ports are carrying less capacity than what they can carry, and hence, the new facility proposed to be built at Diamond Harbour, will make cargo handling easier.

The cost that will be incurred for building the port is estimated to be Rs 1,235 crore. Earlier, it was decided that the port will have the facility of both cargo and container handling. As per the recommendations of the high-powered committee, the project was revised and the new facility will be dedicated only to container handling.

Heading: Future of medical science? Robotic surgeries, say docs - Indian Express
Content:
The state government is yet to begin work on a project that was undertaken a decade ago for uplifting the façade of the river banks in the city.

This has, however, not stopped it from taking up another Rs 5 crore project for beautifying six ghats of the Hooghly. Besides, the state government has also taken up a Rs 90 crore project to modernise the bus terminus and improve the traffic situation in and around the Howrah railway station.

The development project of the station area includes setting up of a modernised bus stand that can house 85 Kolkata-bound buses, 30 Howrah-bound buses, 12 long distance buses and 10 more buses.

The land area available for the project is 14 acre. The project also aims to improve the traffic situation on the adjoining roads. For making a smooth mass transit, the state government has taken up a new flyover project in Sankrail, Howrah, which will connect the Bankim Setu to Howrah station and decongest the traffic load near the station.

The modification of the Bankim Setu is nearing its completion.

"The project will incur a huge cost. We are trying to bring the project under Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) scheme. But if we do not get funds from JNNURM then the state government will fund the project for the sake of development, as Howrah is going to have the largest logistic hub in the country," said Ashok Bhattacharya, state Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister.

"The Howrah station area development project will take two years to complete, while the ghat beautification project will take one year," added Bhattacharya.

The development project will be carried out in two phases. The first phase will incur a cost of Rs 30 crore.

The second phase of the project includes improvement of subways, beautification of riverfront and improvement of circulation of the taxi stand area in front of the Howrah station.

The project for beautifying the ghats and their pavilions will be funded by the state Information and Cultural Affairs Department, Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA) and Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT).

Important components of Howrah project

* Integrated and covered passenger concourse for buses

* Rigid pavements at bus stands

* Waiting areas for commuters and pedestrians

* Improving the traffic situation on the adjoining roads of the station

* Pay-and-use toilets for commuters

* Installation of vending kiosks

* Landscaping, beautification and relocation of statues

* Illumination, high mast lamps, new pumping station

Heading: NGO calls for public-private partnership to make child labour laws effective - Indian Express
Content:
With rapid progress made in converging medical sciences with technology all over the world, doctors are stressing on the robotic surgery as an alternative to the conventional laparoscopic surgery in Indian hospitals.

"Robotic surgery is a computer-assisted surgery in which a surgeon controls hand movements of a robotic device through a console," said Dr Narmada P Gupta of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, the only place in India where robotic surgeries are performed.

The importance of robotic surgery was highlighted at the three-day annual conference of the Urology Society of India (East Zone) at the Ramakrishna Mission Seva Pratisthan in the city, where a workshop on live laparoscopic and robotic urology operations from Guys Hospital, London, was organised on Friday.

"Our aim is to project the robotic surgery as the future of medical sciences. It has been proven that there are advantages of robotic surgeries over laparoscopic surgeries. But this concept is not very popular in eastern India," said Dr A K Das of NRS Medical College and Hospital.

According to doctors, data from many medical centres indicate that surgeons are achieving equivalent or even better results using robotic laparoscopic interface compared with manual operations. They added that in surgeries performed through robotic interface, patients feel less pain and their recovery is faster.

Wristed instrumentation, tremor filtration and three-dimensional magnification are the special advantages of robotics over the conventional laparoscopic surgeries. "In robotic process, everything gets magnified by 30 to 40 per cent or more. Due to the advantage of three-dimensional view, complex and intricate operations become easy to handle," said Dr K Pradhan of the Calcutta Urological Centre.

Experts believe that robotic applications are well-suited for urological surgeries, radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer, and surgeries of kidney, adrenal gland and urinary bladder.

They, however, agreed that the robotic surgeries are expensive due to a high cost of the equipment. "Currently, there is only one foreign company which makes the equipment but after their patent period expires, we hope Indian companies will manufacture the equipment making robotic surgeries less expensive," said Gupta.

Heading: Home Secy warns Trinamool on ‘Siege Lalbazar’ plan - Indian Express
Content:
With 50,000 children working as domestic labourers in Kolkata alone, the ineffectiveness of the amended Child Labour Prevention Act (CLPRA) implemented in the state becomes conspicuous.

At a workshop organised by Save the Children, an NGO working for children's rights, speakers highlighted various issues detrimental to the implementation of CLPRA in West Bengal and across the country.

"West Bengal is one of the largest contributors in child labour and trafficking. There is a greater need to define the responsibilities of the judiciary, police, state government and civil society in implementing the CLPRA. There is a need for public-private partnerships," said Manabendra Nath Ray, state programme manager, Save the Children.

The workshop focused on the role played by the state Labour Department and the Women and Child Development Department in implementing the

CLPRA and stressed on the contribution of education, rehabilitation and awareness to eradicate child labour.

"Our study has shown that most of the children exploited as domestic helps are brought to Kolkata or trafficked mainly from adjoining districts of North and South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore," said Thomas Chandy, CEO, Save the Children (Bal Raksha, Bharat).

The NGO claims that though census 2001 estimates over 12 million children aged between 5 and 14 continue to work in hazardous industries, the actual number of child labours is much higher, as nearly 20 million children are working in roadside eateries or are employed as domestic workers in the country.

Experts also stressed on the need to cover the loopholes of the CLPRA which says that children under the age of 14 are banned from working as domestic helps, in dhabas, restaurants, hotels and other hospitality sectors.

According to a study conducted by Save the Children, 74 per cent of the child domestic labourers are aged between 12 and 16, leaving a crucial gap in bringing a huge number of children aged between 14 and 18 under the Act. 'Inspectors, who are responsible for implementing the CLPRA, face a lot of restrictions. We would like the civil society and NGOs to help us by providing information about the cases where children are being exploited," said S Islam, Assistant Labour Commissioner.

Heading: ‘Religion as political identity is most unfortunate’ - Indian Express
Content:
Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti on Friday warned Trinamool Congress workers saying that they would not be allowed to disrupt work on October 20 - the day when the party plans to siege the headquarters of Kolkata police at Lalbazar.

Chakrabarti said Section 144 of the CrPC remains imposed in the Lalbazar and Writer's Buildings areas throughout the year, so the administration would do its best to maintain law and order. Last Sunday, Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee had said that her party workers will march to Lalbazar to protest against the arrest of Swarup Biswas, brother of Trinamool legislator from Tollygunge, Arup Biswas. Swarup has been charged with instigating and leading a mob, which burnt six police vehicles and attacked police personnel at the Charu Market police station on October 4.

Heading: Reprieve for airline, relief for staff - Indian Express
Content:
Former Supreme Court judge Justice Ruma Pal on Friday said it is India's misfortune that it is a secular country where religion is used as the political identity of an individual. She said there is no concept of religion in the Indian Constitution.

"One does not have be a Hindu to be an Indian, and religion should be separated from nationality," she said while delivering the Kolkata Port Trust Anniversary Lecture on the 138th anniversary of the institution.

Speaking of communal violence fuelled by religious conversions , she said the Constitution gives the right to an individual to be converted to any other religion on his own will, but does not give the right to force anyone to convert.

Pal said a common civil code should be implemented in the country.

"Whenever we talk of a uniform civil code in the country, a section of minorities feels that it is an encroachment of their rights. The common civil code should not be derived from the practice of one religion but it should be derived from the best practices of all the religion," she said

Jayantanuja Bandyopadhyaya, former IFS and at present Professor Emeritus, Department of International Relations at Jadavpur University, meanwhile said the global financial crisis will have its effect on Indian economy.

"The effect is less on the Indian economy as the Opposition has put pressure that there should be more governmental control on banks and financial institutions," said Bandyopadhyaya.

Delivering the keynote address, Bandyopadhyaya said there has been a complete reversal of the Indian foreign policy, from non-alignment to being strategically aligned with super power.

Bandyopadhyaya said globalisation and international world order are hollow statements as most of the Third World countries do not have a voice on major international issues.

He stressed on the formation of global regulatory authority on climate change and disaster management, where Third World countries that do not have any economic and military might can have their say.

Heading: Lessons on how terror works, from up close - Indian Express
Content:
Govt gives cash-strapped Jet 6-month breather on land deal

While help from the Ministry of Civil Aviation seems to be a long way off for cash-strapped Jet Airways, India 's biggest private airline has received a much needed breather for a Rs 826-crore land deal in the financial capital's commercial hub of Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC).

Exactly a month ago, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), which owns the land, had handed over the plot allotment letter to the airline. As per the rules, Jet Airways was to pay half the sum (about Rs 400 crore) to the agency by Friday, when the deadline for the first installment ran out. However, the MMRDA has now decided to make an allowance for the airline as well as to Starlight Systems (a joint venture of the Ajay Piramal Group and Suntech Realty which had bid successfully for two residential plots) granting both a six-month extension.

MMMRDA Commissioner Ratnakar Gaikwad said the issue was discussed at the Authority meeting three days ago. "Due to the exceptional situation arising out of the global meltdown, we have decided to give them both a six-month extension," he said.

Jet Airways had successfully bid for the 5,951-sq metre commercial plot at BKC in March this year. Immediately after winning the bid, airline officials had declared their plans to have their global headquarters there. According to the MMRDA's payment schedule, 50 pc of the sum was to be paid within a month of receiving the allotment letter, the remaining over the next two months. If the bidder fails to pay up, he forfeits his Rs 3-crore 'Earnest Money Deposit' and the deal is called off.

However as the economic slowdown started getting worse by the day, both Jet Airways and Starlight Systems had written to MMRDA, seeking an extension that was not granted until three days ago. The MMRDA's largesse would now mean that Jet Airways will be allowed to pay the entire sum any time within the next six months.

At a time when the airline has just reinstated 1,900 employees after giving them the pink slip with the stated purpose of cutting costs by Rs 60 crore annually, the payment of Rs 826 crore for the land by March next year seems to be a tall order, say skeptical realty analysts. Jet Airways spokesperson Srirupa Sen denied that Jet may back off from the deal. She said the airline still intends to go ahead with its plan to construct their global headquarters there.

According to Akshaya Kumar, CEO of Parklane property consultants, Jet Airways was scouting for a plot for more than eight years. "They bought the plot at a cost much higher than the market price. If in today's market the MMRDA can still get that amount for the plot, it is right in granting an extension."

Heading: City transporter is first Indian migraine patient to have surgery - Indian Express
Content:
Plan to let policemen interact with terror suspects, know more of their psyche

Mumbai Police plan to impart knowledge to personnel of all police stations in the city, down to the beat constable, on the psyche of terrorists and the way they operate.

The project will allow police personnel to meet with investigators who cracked the recent terror case and interact with the arrested Indian Mujahideen suspects.

Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria said, "Terror cannot be combated by a particular agency or a department of the police alone. The fact that Sadiq Israr stayed incognito at Cheetah Camp in Trombay for such a long time without anyone having any clue proves the time has come for the local police to be imparted knowledge about such elements."

According to Maria, the project will start in a few weeks and all DCP-rank officers will be invited to participate in detailed discussions with investigators who cracked the case and interact with the terror suspects. "It is very important for the local police to know things like how terrorists enter states and establish themselves with fake identities or jobs so as to mingle with the local people to carry out operations," Maria said.

Apart from cops from the city, some officers from places like Thane, Navi Mumbai and possibly Pune are likely to be included in the project.

The information will be passed on by the DCPs to police officers under them. "The beat constable is the one in constant touch with the man on the street and it's very important for him to know the people in his locality, which might help him identify suspicious elements. Hence, in a scenario where terrorists live normal lives within the society, the role of the local policeman in identifying members of sleeper cells becomes more important in preventing terrorist activities," said the Crime Branch chief.

Apart from learning how terror group members operate under cover, the local cops will also get a taste of things like what motivates them and how they get indoctrinated.

Heading: Navi Mumbai murder victim was being stalked - Indian Express
Content:
Last week, 42-year-old Mumbai resident Tilak Lodaya, for the first time in 11 years, spent a week without complaining of severe headaches, after becoming India's first chronic migraine patient to undergo surgery to mitigate the attacks.

Doctors at Mumbai's Jaslok Hospital and Research Center performed the surgery successfully by stimulation of the Greater Occipital Nerve (GON) that arises at the back of the head and transmits pain sensation to the back of the head during a migraine attack.The procedure, performed on just 40 migraine patients worldwide, has finally made its way to India. "For the past four to five years, Lodaya stopped responding to conventional treatment. We also tried giving him botox treatment, but were unsuccessful," said Dr K Ravishankar, headache specialist at Jaslok Hospital.

"In this procedure two eight-contact point electrodes are implanted overlying the GON. They are connected to a pacemaker implanted on the chest wall. The pacemaker delivers a current to stimulate the GON through the electrodes. Whenever the patient gets a migraine attack he can switch on the pacemaker and control his migraine by using a remote (stimulator)," said Dr Paresh Doshi, head of Jaslok's Department of Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgery.

However, doctors warn that not all chronic migraine patients qualify for the surgery. Of all chronic migraineurs visiting headache clinics, only 4 per cent suffers from "intractable migraine" wherein all conventional medication methods have been tried unsuccessfully. "The total cost of the surgery is Rs 4 lakh to Rs 4.5 lakh, including the implant. The patient has to take extra care since it is an electromagnetic device. He must inform doctors conducting any MRI on him, and also cannot go under metal detectors. He must always carry such a letter," added Dr Doshi.

Lodaya, who runs a transport business, says he would spend Rs 5000 per month on medicines and painkiller injections. "This is the first week in the last 11 years that I have not had pain daily. I can now lead a normal life," he smiled.

Heading: BMC, MMRDA to join hands for redeveloping 12 bridges, combat floods - Indian Express
Content:
Before she was murdered, Reliance employee Anandita Mishra (33) was being stalked by a stranger, say neighbours and other residents of the building where she lived.

Mishra, an HR employee with the Dhirubhai Ambani Knowledge City, was a divorcee. She lived with her mother and four-year-old daughter in Ghansoli.

MH Sheikh, the secretary of the building, said: "Anandita had approached me a couple of weeks ago and asked me to instruct the guard of the building to screen people entering the locality. When I asked her the reason for this, she told me she was being harassed by a man who was calling her regularly."

Shaikh said he told her to approach the police but she declined, saying that the stalker was probably someone from her office, that she was trying to find out who he was and that only after doing so would she take action.

According to the Navi Mumbai police, where a case of murder has been registered, Mishra was returning from her office on Thursday night when she was stabbed to death outside Koparkhairane railway station.

Inspector Arvind Patil of Turbhe police station said, "We are investigating the possibility that the killer was someone known to her and had troubled her in the past. We have some leads and will surely crack the case in the next couple of days."

Heading: Man drugged by co-passenger in train, robbed - Indian Express
Content:
To prevent floods in the city during monsoon, Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation and the MMRDA will join hands to undertake the redevelopment work of 12 bridges. The Fact Finding Committee appointed by the state government following the 2005 deluge recommended that widening of river and crucial nullah system will encourage proper drainage of storm water and avoid a flood like situation. The FFC also recommended redevelopment of the existing bridges to facilitate the widening of the river or the nullah.

BMC has been given development work of the bridges situated on the Mithi river system upstream of the Kurla-Kalina Road. The six bridges under this stretch are: Kurla-Kalina Bridge, Krantinagar Bridge, Ashok Nagar Bridge, Bamandayapada Bridge, Pipeline Service Road Bridge and the Filterpada Bridge. Tenders for these bridges have been floated and consultants are soon to be appointed. "The Kurla-Kalina Bridge is a busy traffic junction. We will be co-coordinating with the traffic police department for this stretch. The road might have to be closed and traffic might be diverted," said chief engineer roads, D L Shinde.

MMRDA would fund the project whose cost is estimated at Rs 380 crore, while the civic body will carry out the work. MMRDA has also asked the civic body to take up the work on five bridges on the Mithi River and one on the Vakola nullah. The six bridges handed over to the BMC by MMRDA are: Mahim Causeway Bridge, Tansa Pipeline Bridge, Vaitarna Pipeline Bridge, Dharavi Bridge, and CST Road Bridge. These bridges are all over the Mithi River. Apart from this, the list also includes Pipeline Bridge over Vakola nullah.

Consultants have been appointed for the design and drawing of these bridges and work is expected to start in the next 60 days. The FFC has also recommended widening of the Nehru nagar nullah system which leads to the Mahul creek and the Deonar nullah system along with bridges on Ghatkopar-Mankhurd link road. Tendering procedure of these two stretches is expected to start soon.

Heading: In focus - Indian Express
Content:
Sharing a cup of tea with an unknown person during a train journey nearly proved fatal for this 29-year-old teacher from Orissa.

Kul Mani Sahu, a primary teacher with a government school in Orissa's Nayagarh district, was drugged by an unidentified man in the Devgiri Express while he was on his way to meet his friend in Mumbai. And as he became unconscious, his cash amounting to Rs 2,200 and a mobile phone was stolen.

Sahu remained unconscious for over four days at the St George Hospital, and was finally discharged by the hospital on Friday after his "unexpected" recuperation.

He had boarded the train at Secundarabad station on October 9 to meet his friend. At Dharamabad station on the Maharashtra-Andhra Pradesh border, a fellow passenger became friendly with him. "He gave me a cup of tea at the Urmi station and in a few minutes, I fell asleep. I thought this could be due to the cold breeze. The next thing I remember is that I was in this hospital," Sahu said.

"On October 10, at around 8 am, our constable found him in an unconscious state while checking the Devgiri Express at the CST, the last destination of the train," said police inspector Pandharinath Yeram, who is looking into the case. "We immediately admitted him to the St George Hospital where the doctors said that his chances of surviving were almost nil. But he was saved," Yeram said.

Meanwhile, the CST railway police have registered a case and have transferred it to the Purna railway police station in Nanded. "We have transferred it to the Purna railway police as the crime occurred in their jurisdiction," said Dilip Mane, senior police inspector , CST railway police station.

Heading: Petition on stray dogs: HC reserves judgement - Indian Express
Content:
Park Kwang-su gives his take on Indian films

South Korean director Park Kwang-su's A Single Spark, apart from being a great cinematic experience, is a study of economics of filmmaking.

The film, showcased as the 'centre piece' of the 7th Third Eye Asian film Festival, was largely financed by public subscription. The closing credits of this 1995 film acknowledge nearly 5,000 names. Though things had started looking up for the South Korean filmmakers over the last one decade, the current meltdown has cut this good tiding short. "It's a hard time for filmmakers. Next year is going to be financially tough for the film industry," said the director, soon after receiving the Asian Film Culture Award on Thursday evening. However, with nearly 60 educational institutes offering courses related to films, his country has a big talent pool.

Known for the political tone of his work, Park in A Single Spark sets out to exorcise South Korea's dark years under military dictators while paying dues to the heroes who dared to dissent. Two narratives run parallel in the film—one in black and white, another in colour—follows Jeon Tae-Il.

Jeon was a labour activist in the 1960s who committed suicide as a gesture of protest against the authorities' failure to honour workers' rights.

Kwang-su, one of the leading contemporary Korean filmmakers, is a known name on the Indian festival circuit. Though this is his third trip to India, he is visiting Mumbai for the first time. His introduction to Indian films, however, happened while he was studying in Paris. Park had seen the works of Satyajit Ray and Mrinal Sen extensively. And it's Ray's first film, Apur Sansar, that left Park spellbound. He even wrote on Indian film in magazines.

Heading: Share of worries: Financer ends life - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court has reserved its judgement on the issue of rehabilitating stray dogs in Mumbai.

Petitioner, In Defence of Animals, in their written submissions had earlier said that the idea of 'killing dogs' advocated for controlling their population is barbaric, inhuman and unconstitutional. According to them, BMC has in the past adopted this strategy and failed.

"From 1939 to 1999, the corporation has put to sleep 25 lakh dogs and in spite of that they have failed," the petition had said.

The NGO submits that through out the world countries which have opted for sterilization of dogs have been successful in controlling their population. Senior counsel Aspi Chinoy, who appeared for NGO Welfare of Stray Dogs (which is carrying out the sterilization process), submitted that the population of the dogs never went down but the rabies death had come down by one-third. He argued that it is not right to say that the city is at the mercy of rabid dogs.

Other organizations that have moved court submitted that the question is regarding the killing of violent or rabid dogs. The court was also told that such decisions should be left at the discretion of the Municipal Commissioner.

State government on the other hand had supported the BMC regarding the validity of the BMC Act which gives them powers to kill stray dogs. According to provision 191 B A (2) of the Municipal Corporation Act, the Municipal Commissioner in his discretion may sell or provide shelter or destroy stray dogs.

BMC had earlier stated that it has the power to kill the dogs. BMC had also stated before the full bench of Justice Dr S Radhakrishnan, Justice D B Bhosale and Justice V K Tahilramani about the huge financial constraints connected with the rehabilitation of stray dogs in dog shelters. BMC also contended that there is no need for additional dog shelters as they have kennels and dogs can also be given for adoption.

Heading: Two cops suspended for stripping, abusing tribal - Indian Express
Content:
Stock market slump takes its first toll in Ahmedabad

The ongoing slump in the stock market took its first toll in the city when a 39-year-old financer from Meghaninagar allegedly committed suicide by hanging himself on Friday morning.

The police said victim Jitu Parmar had invested in shares and the recent recession in the stock market could be the reason behind the suicide.

"Though we are yet to ascertain the actual reason that provoked Parmar to take the extreme step, it seems that the recent downturn in the stock market may have affected him. Parmar's friends and other acquaintances told us that he had invested a huge amount of money in the share market," said Inspector S F Saiyad.

The police said Parmar allegedly hanged himself from a ceiling fan at his residence near Jethalal Park around 9 am when he was alone in the house. His wife, Neeta (30), is a schoolteacher and the couple have two children. "Neeta found her husband dead when she returned home around noon," said Saiyad.

Though the police are yet to record Neeta's statement to know the exact amount of money that Parmar had invested, Parmar's elder brother, Kanhayya told the police that the deceased was suffering from severe depression for the past three months. He was even taking treatment from a prominent doctor near the Nehru Bridge, Kanhayya said.

No suicide note was recovered from the place and the police are awaiting the postmortem report. A case of an accidental death has been registered and investigations are on in the case.

Heading: RTI activism earns ex-armyman wrath of his village panchayat - Indian Express
Content:
The Superintendent of Police of Surendranagar on Friday suspended two policemen for stripping and abusing a tribal villager in Nanikatechi in Limdi Taluka, days after Newsline reported the incident.

On October 7, Beat Head Constable Janaksinh Rana and Constable Indu Rana, both from the Darbar community, had brutally tortured Kana Gesapara (40). The victim was stripped and beaten up before the two policemen pushed a stick wrapped in petrol soaked cloth up his rectum and then put the same in his mouth.

Later, semi-naked Gesapara was taken to the village temple, beaten up again and made to wear a ghaghra while carrying his pants and shoes on his head till the panchayat office, where they made him dance.

Kumar said: "Initially, I had asked for an inquiry by a Deputy Superintendent of Police. I had transferred them (the accused personnel) out of their original posting at Panesara police station, so that they are not able to disturb the investigations. Today, I suspended them within one and a half hours of getting the report.""

Kumar said the police are now awaiting the court's decision in the matter as a private complaint has already been lodged with the Limdi court.

Heading: Rajkot to get its first flyover, 550 trees a new ground - Indian Express
Content:
Sabarkantha panchayat passes resolution against Pandya for his flurry of petitions

The Right to Information (RTI) Act was enacted to bring about transparency in governance. But the panchayat of Meghraj village in Sabarkantha district, it seems, is seeing the other side of the Act.

The panchayat has passed a resolution to initiate action against an ex-serviceman, Anil Kumar Pandya, who has been keeping it on its toes through petitions filed under the Act.

Not only that, the panchayat has also forwarded a copy of its resolution to the Sabarkantha District Collector and DDO, with a request to take action against Pandya.

Ahmed Chadi, village sarpanch, said: "Pandya had been asking for some land on a subsidised price, which we had agreed to at the panchayat. Later, the State Revenue Department altered the rates, and since then, Pandya has been trying to harass us through numerous RTI applications."

He added: "We cannot refuse to provide information to any one who seeks it under the RTI Act. But we have passed a resolution to request the authorities to look into the matter and take action against this man."

Pandya, meanwhile, said that while he had filed only two petitions — one in January 2007 and another in August 2007 — a third petition was filed by his father, who is a former Talati of the village, in March this year.

"All these applications were in connection with various land allocations by the panchayat. While I got partial response to some, I had to go for appeal later," Pandya said, adding that the responses he finally got from the panchayat revealed many errors in the land allocation process.

"Now, they are uncomfortable and want to hush me up. These steps are being taken to achieve that end," Pandya added.

Deputy District Development Officer B N Chaudhury said this is a "strange" situation.

"Seeking information is not a crime. One cannot do anything about someone who is seeking information under the RTI Act," he said.

He added that being an elected body, a panchayat has the right to pass a resolution, but it is difficult for the department to act on the same.

Heading: ‘Light-n-sound’ at Sabarmati Ashram still in pause mode - Indian Express
Content:
Rajkot Municipal Corporation decides not to cut trees, but transplant them to another location

Over 550 full-grown trees along the 150 Feet Ring Road in Rajkot will not come in the way of the city's first flyover, as the Rajkot Municipal Corporation (RMC) has decided to transplant them to some other location.

The Corporation has decided to spend a huge amount on the re-plantation or transplantation of these trees located between Amin Marg and Adani Mall on a stretch of nearly 1.5 km on the 150 Feet Ring Road, where service roads will be constructed for the flyover project.

Dr K D Haplaia, Garden Superintendent, RMC, said they had invited tenders after the municipal commissioner took the decision, and on Friday, they awarded the contract to an agricultural contractor. Most of the trees there are Neem, Saptaparni and verities of Ficus.

As per the contract sanctioned in the RMC standing committee meeting on Friday, the contractor will get Rs 1,535 for each survived tree. "We have put this condition for only survived trees because then only the contractor will take care of each tree properly.
