The total cost will be around Rs 8 lakh, but it will be worth expending if every tree survives," said Hapalia.

"To begin with, the branches of these trees will be trimmed and then it will be uprooted with the help of a machine. After giving anti-fungal treatment to its root, it will be re-planted at a new location where similar kind of soil and topography is available," said Dr Haplaia.

He added: "We have selected a few locations like Dharmendrasinhji College campus, Nana Mahuva Crematorium and the land adjoining to the railway tracks passing from the city, for the transplantation."

He further said the re-plantation will be done at those places where people can easily witness that it is quite possible. "Thus, in future, if the residents want to expand their property, but some grown tree is creating a problem, they can transplant it with our help. Our motto is also to make it a public awareness drive," he said.

Earlier, the National Highways Authority of India had carried out a similar project successfully when roads were broadening a few years ago.

Heading: For state staff, CCC means ‘Crying Computer Crisis’ - Indian Express
Content:
GCCI wants to take the initiative but ashram authorities say no plan in the pipeline

The Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GCCI) wants to coordinate with the Sabarmati Ashram and the state Tourism Ministry to re-launch the 50-minute 'light and sound' programme that was once an additional attraction to the ashram visitors. But ashram authorities say there is no plan as yet to restart the show, which was disbanded in 2005.

While GCCI president Rupesh Shah feels that the show, if re-launched, could invite more visitors to the ashram that played a pivotal role in the country's Independence, ashram authorities say the programme was disbanded because of lack of interest among the visitors.

About 20 lakh visitors are reported to visit the ashram premises annually to see photos, manuscripts and other literature on the life of Mahatma Gandhi.

One of the main reasons for disbanding the show, according to Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust secretary Amrutbhai Modi was the fewer number of visitors attracted to see the show.

"There were occasions when only two to three people or only one person turned up for the show," said Amrutbhai, adding that there was no logic to continue the show under these circumstances.

He cited lack of public transport from the ashram and to the various destinations in the city during night and poor technology to be the primary reason for the poor response to the show among the people.

He also held the information boom on the Internet to be another reason for the low turnout. He said a lot of literature and material is now available online, which has also reduced the interest of the people on programmes revolving around the life and movements of Gandhiji.

Amrutbhai said there are only two other places, the Red Fort in Delhi and the Somnath Temple in Gujarat where the light and sound show is continuing successfully.

Another reason for people's disinterest, according to tour and travel operators, is the serious nature of the show. It focuses more on Gandhiji's spirituality, making it quite a dull exercise for the youth, they say.

According to those who had the opportunity to attend the show before it was taken off, the "sound" part of the show consisted of bhajans, religious songs that were sung in Gandhiji's prayers, a little bit of drama with commentary and a few episodes from Gandhiji's life. The show ended with a rendition of "Raghupati Raghav Rajaram."

The commentary part also quoted the famous lines of Albert Einstein on Gandhiji which said: "Generations to come, it may be, will scarce believe that such a one as this ever in flesh and blood walked upon this earth."

The different sections of the ashram were lit in the "light" part of the show.

"So, it held little attraction for people looking for enjoyment in every event," said a tour operator, adding that even religious events like Navratri have undergone complete change.

Heading: Farmers claiming ancestral right on Nano land to move Gujarat High Court - Indian Express
Content:
Deadline for mandatory submission of certificate nearing; no exams since July

Examinations for the Course in Computer Concepts (CCC) have not been held in the Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the state since July 2, 2008, which has led to the piling up of as many as one-lakh applications.

For the government employees, it is necessary to obtain the CCC certificates if they want promotions and higher pay scales.

The last date for submitting this certificate to the state government by their employees is December 31, 2008. But since the last three months, no examination has taken place, which is now a source of worry for government employees. There are 164 ITIs in the state, and examinations used to take place at 55 such centres every Wednesday till July 2.

There are around 5 lakh government employees in Gujarat as of now. Of this, around 3.5 lakh government employees are eligible to appear for the CCC examination.

Till now, around 95,000 government employees have appeared for the CCC examinations. In order to appear for the CCC examination, a government employee has to pay a fee of Rs 150.

A senior official of the Gujarat Council for Vocational Training (GCVT), said: "Earlier, we used to take a written CCC examination and now we will take an online examination. The demonstration of the software and hardware required for taking this examination is going on and we do not think there is any delay from our side."

C V Som, Director, Employment & Training, Gujarat, refused to comment on the issue.

Satish Patel, Principal, ITI, Anwa, Dangs district, said: " A lot of government employees used to come to our ITI everyday and fill up the forms for giving the CCC examination, but now they do not fill up the forms as they know that thousands of applications are still pending."

He added: "The demonstration of software and hardware required for the online CCC examination has already been done at our ITI and we are just awaiting instructions from the Employment & Training headquarters at Gandhinagar to start the examinations."

An official from the Directorate of Employment & Training said on condition of anonymity: "It is very strange to see that in the middle of the year,the senior authorities of the Directorate of Employment & Training decided to change the way the CCC examinations are conducted. They do not even have proper expert to deal with the software and the hardware."

J P Chotai from ITI, Bhuj said: "There is no doubt that it will not be possible to take examinations of the state government employees who are yet to appear for the same. I think the state government has no other choice rather than to extend the date of submitting the CCC certificates. Moreover, this incident shows complete lack of planning on the government side."

Heading: 12-yr-old rape victim dies at hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Villagers of Chharodi say British govt had taken land on 90-year lease from their forefathers

After having failed to get any concrete assurance from the state government, farmers agitating against the transfer of 1,100 acres of land in Chharodi village to the Tata Motors have decided to move the Gujarat High Court.

They will challenge the government's decision on the ground that the land in question did not belong to the government and had been wrongly appropriated by the latter through mutations in the land records.

Speaking to Newsline, Mukeshsinh Vaghela, who is leading the agitating farmers, said he has consulted an advocate who would file a case on behalf of them within few days.

According to Vaghela, in 1902, the then British government had taken the land on a lease of 90 years to protect cattle of a particular breed facing extinction due to severe drought. The land was later given for research in agriculture to the Anand Agriculture University.

So, he said, the use of land was not changed while transferring it to the university, as it also used the land for agriculture purposes. After the lease period expired, the land should have been given back to the descendants of the original owners, but the government did not do so.

He further said the government instead gave it to the Tatas for non-agricultural use, which is in violation of land acquisition and transfer rules and regulations.

After the expiry of lease period, the government should have consulted the original owners before allotting it to anybody.

He demanded that the government should compensate the original owners of the land. "That is why we have decided to move the court, because we have failed to get justice from the government in this regard," he said.

Meanwhile, the Tatas have begun construction of an approach road to the site of their plant for Nano.

Heading: Court orders in-camera hearing of Ahmedabad blasts, Surat bomb cases - Indian Express
Content:
A 12-year-old tribal girl, who was undergoing treatment at SMIMER Hospital after being raped earlier this month, died on Thursday.

The girl, a resident of Koba in Olpad taluka of Surat district, was admitted to the hospital after she was found lying unconscious in an agricultural field on October 8.

According to the police, the girl had left her house for the agricultural fields where her parents work as labourers.

When she did not return home in the evening, her parents began looking for her.

Later, a villager spotted her lying in an unconscious state in the field and informed her parents.

The girl's father Natvar Vasawa rushed her to the Jeewan Rakhsa Hospital at Sayan from where she was referred to the SMIMER Hospital for further treatment. A medical examination confirmed rape.

After learning about the incident, the Olpad police took Natvar to the agricultural field where the girl was found in an unconscious state.

A bottle of poison was recovered from the spot. However, they could not ascertain whether the girl had herself taken the poison or she was given the same forcefully.

District Superintendent of Police K G Bhatti said: "On Friday, a team from the Forensic Science Laboratory visited the site where the body was found, to find more clues.

We are interrogating the local youths as a part of our investigation."

According to the villagers, the deceased was studying in Class VII in a village school. She used to help her parents in the fields and also worked as a housemaid. However, she had left the job two weeks ago.

Of late, there has been a rise in rape incidents on minors in south Gujarat. Among the six incidents of sexual assault on minors that have taken place this week, three have been reported from Surat.

Heading: Three sent to judicial custody for involvement in flesh trade racket - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court, hearing the Ahmedabad blast and Surat bomb cases, on Friday ordered that the proceedings of both the cases be held in-camera.

Metropolitan Magistrate G M Patel pronounced the order in an open court, before the hearing of the remand application of 16 accused started.

The court passed the order exercising powers conferred to it under Section 327 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and Section 44 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

The order came on an application moved by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) on October 14. The DCB had sought this on the grounds that it was necessary for the security of the accused, protection of their identities and that of the witnesses in the case.

The application was filed under Section 44 of Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, 1967.

The court said that in-camera trial was necessary for the security of the accused. It said it was not possible to keep tabs on all the people coming to an open courtroom and that the security of the accused is paramount.

On October 15, the defence had opposed the application, saying it was premature and that the designated Metropolitan Court was not the competent court under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act to take such a decision.

All the accused have been remanded to judicial custody till October 23.

Heading: ‘Industrialisation rush poses threat to endangered marine flora and fauna’ - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on a tip-off, the Junagadh police raided a house in Block 4, Krishna Park society in the Timbawadi area on Thursday night, and busted a flesh trade racket. Three persons, including two women, were arrested during the raid.

The three have been identified as Rajesh Barot (47), who was running the racket from his house, Durga Lohana (37) and Kalpana Gamit (27).

'B' Division Inspector M F Jadav said the three have been booked under the Prostitution (Prevention) Act, rule 5, 6 and 7. Barot was allegedly pushing the women into flesh trade, the police said.

The three were produced before the court on Friday, which sent them to judicial custody.

Lost card costs ATM guard Rs 90,000
A MAN guarding an ATM counter of HDFC Bank lost his ATM card which cost him Rs 90,000.
According to a complaint lodged with the Junagadh 'B' Division police, Mansukh Patel, an ex-serviceman, and a bank security guard, had used his card to withdraw Rs 1,000 on October 13. Later, he lost his card and discovered that a sum of Rs 90,000 was withdrawn from his account.
Patel said he had written the PIN code on his card and had to bear the brunt of his folly. The Junagadh police have registered a case against unknown persons.

Three commit suicide in Junagadh
THREE people have committed suicide in separate incidents in the city. Manjula Mer (29), a widow and a resident of Lirbai Para in Junagadh hanged herself to death at her house.
The two others, identified as Asha Badhu (14), a resident of Raman village, and Bharat Bachu (32), a resident of Sutrapada town consumed poison.
They were admitted to the Junagadh Civil Hospital and died on Friday during treatment.

Heading: Sagar Arts declares compensation package for slain employee’s family - Indian Express
Content:
Leading marine scientists and environmentalists on Friday expressed serious concern over the "mad rush for industrialisation" in coastal areas. They say it poses a great threat to the endangered marine flora and fauna.

The experts were addressing a two-day national-level workshop titled 'Identification of Training Needs' for the implementation of the proposed World Bank-aided Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) project. They said that haphazard industrialisation in the coastal areas will have an adverse impact on the marine bio-diversity if it is not regulated.

"Most of the coastal states, particularly Gujarat, appears to be in the grip of industrialisation, which, if not checked, will pose a grave danger to the marine ecology and environment in the days to come. The onus is also on industrialists to cooperate with various government agencies engaged in the conservation and management of marine flora and fauna," said A G Untawale, former chairman of the World Wildlife Fund (Goa).

He said industries were coming up at a large scale along the coastal areas, mainly in the Gulf of Kutch, and unless they show some concern about the marine bio-diversity in their vicinity, it will be difficult for them to survive.

Untawale, a member of the National Mangrove Committee set up by the Union Environment and Forest Ministry, lamented that the strategies the government and other agencies chalk out from time to time for the conservation and management of marine flora and fauna remain only on paper. "It's high time that we launch concrete measures to increase the mangrove cover and also protect the marine life along the country's coastline," he said.

Gujarat Chief Conservator of Forest H S Singh emphasised on the need for creating a trained manpower to undertake a large-scale plantation and restoration of mangroves in the Gulf of Kutch. "We keep on fixing targets to increase the mangrove cover without mapping or identifying potential coastal areas. We will have to adopt a scientific approach to conserve marine bio-diversity in a planned manner," he told the gathering.

Suggesting that the local fishing community members should also be involved in efforts to increase the mangrove cover, Singh said fishermen should be imparted a special training and made partners in this area. "One should know that mangroves not only serve as a nursing ground for fisheries, but also act as a protection wall in times of natural calamities like cyclone and tsunami," he said.

At present, the mangrove cover along the Gujarat coast is estimated at 936 sq km, which is considered to be the most successful mangrove conservation experiment in the country. "The mangrove cover can be enhanced to another 550 sq km of potential area on our state's coast, if we carry out plantation in a planned way," Singh added.

Earlier, inaugurating the workshop organised by the Gujarat Ecology Commission, Principal Secretary (Forest) S K Nanda stressed on the need for integrated and balanced development of the coastal zone in Gujarat.

Senior Technical Advisor (Union Environment and Forest Ministry) Asheem Srivastav explained the objective of the ICZM project for which three coastal states – Gujarat, West Bengal and Orissa – have been selected.

Heading: VMC raps telcos for putting up hoardings on private properties - Indian Express
Content:
To get lifetime pension and Rs 1 lakh each for education of the two kids of the deceased

The wife and children of Sajid Saiyyad, a driver who died in the premises of Sagar Film Studios on Wednesday night following the shooting of NDTV Imagine's Ramayan, will get lifetime pension from the Sagar Arts, it was announced on Friday. In addition, the company will provide Rs 1 lakh for the education of the two children of the deceased.

"A compensation package has been announced for the family. This includes lifetime pension at a tentative rate of Rs 5000 and Rs 1 lakh for the education of two children of Sajid," said Raju Shukla, general manager of Sagar Arts.

Shukla also informed that the owners of Sagar Arts, Anand Sagar and Premanand Sagar, will be visiting the Saiyyad's family on Sunday. "They will also listen to the problem of workers and artistes, besides taking stock of the studio facilities," he said.

Sajid's brother Naushad, meanwhile, said that the company has sent no written communication in this regard so far.

"However, Raju Shukla and Mukesh Kalol, managing directors of Sagar Arts visited us and assured that the compensation will be paid, including Rs 1 lakh for the education of my brother's children," said Naushad.

He added that A.P. Abid, one of the directors of the Ramayan serial, has also made certain contributions towards his brother's family.

Heading: Parents of Vasad engineering student demand suspension of cop for issuing threats - Indian Express
Content:
Almost all leading cellphone service providers are in a tight fix after the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) sent a notification to them for putting up hoardings on private properties.

In its revenue collection drive, the VMC has now targeted the hoardings put up by the service providers along the roadside and on private properties. With over 700 hoarding already scrutinised, the VMC will now demand for the tax paid by the advertising agencies and the companies.

"The agencies put up the hoardings without any prior permission and the taxes have also not been paid for putting up the hoardings. There is an existing law on advertisers putting up hoardings on private property but the cases have increased now," said C M Makwana, Deputy Municipal Commissioner, VMC.

He said: "We have initially started with the mobile phone companies. We will now send notices to the agencies to recover the tax."

To sum up, the VMC will put all private property owners including society and buildings under scrutiny, and the owners of the property where hoardings have been put up will have to pay tax. "If a hoarding is put up in a private property, it means that the property owner has given consent for it. This will bring them among the tax defaulters and their property under the tax net," he said.

The owners of some of the private properties, where the hoardings were put up, admitted that the agencies paid them anywhere between Rs 10,000 and 20,000 annually for the advertisements. In addition to the tax retrieval, the VMC is also in process of revising the rates of the hoarding.

"Most private players charge Rs 800 per metre while the VMC charges Rs 200 for the same. We will soon be revising the rates as well," Makwana added.

Heading: People left awestruck by display of 450 indigenous scientific instruments - Indian Express
Content:
Police Commissioner assures relatives that necessary action will be taken against the guilty officer

Relatives of Anuj Patel, a student of Sardar Vallabhbhai Institute of Technology (SVIT) at Vasad, who was beaten up by Padra police Inspector Janak Sarvaiya on October 13, on Friday submitted a memorandum to the Commissioner's Office, seeking immediate suspension of the latter.

The case was earlier handed over to J P Road Inspector A M Patel, who had said that all evidence provided by Anuj's family went against Sarvaiya, who has been accused of assaulting, harassing and issuing life threats to the victim and his mother Meena Patel.

"The family has provided us with video evidences, therefore Sarvaiya's arrest and suspension is inevitable. Sarvaiya is facing charges of assault, forced entry and giving life threats under Sections 452, 323, 504 and 506 (2) of the IPC," said Inspector Patel.

Today, Anuj's father Rajendra Patel, aunt Daksha Patel and at least 20 other relatives and family friends arrived at Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana's office with the memorandum. Though Asthana has not commented on the issue, he has assured the relatives of Anuj that necessary actions will be taken against the guilty officer.

In the complaint, Rajendra Patel said that Sarvaiya, one Kamal and other people barged into their home and beat up Anuj. According to the complaint, when Meena, Anuj's mother, tried to pacify the inspector, he beat her too.

Sarvaiya was earlier involved in several controversial cases, like not accepting a dowry complaint, besides allegedly barging into the residence of Rajendra Patel on Sun Pharmaceutical Road with his men and beating up Patel's son and wife.

According to J P Road police, where the Patels have filed an FIR, Sarvaiya misused his powers to settle his personal scores with Anuj, a student of Vasad Engineering College, on behalf of his son's friends.

During college elections, Anuj had reportedly worked for the group, which was contesting against the group supported by Sarvaiya's son.

At present, the accused officer is in charge of the Padra police station, located some 20 kms from Vadodara city.

Heading: Down the memory lane: Musical maestro returns to city after 30 years - Indian Express
Content:
A Germany-based Sanskrit scholar from the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) left the audience awestruck with his powerpoint display of 450 Indian scientific instruments at the 9th Late Dr U P Shah Memorial Lecture at the M S University on Thursday.

Dr S R Sarma made a presentation of Indian instruments used for scientific research and astrology during medieval and ancient times.

He also spoke about Dhruva Brahmayantra, an indigenous invention, at the seminar.

Organised by the Oriental Institute of MSU, the theme of the series is the history of indigenous science and scientific instruments.

Sarma said: "Dhruva Brahmayantra comprises three instruments that can calculate the time of the day, position of stars and movement of the sun, " adding that the instrument was invented in 1423 by Jain scientist Padmanabh on the banks of the Narmada in Ujjain.

He said most of the Indian instruments were the replication of Persian instruments, hinting at the rich cultural exchange between the Arabs and the various Indian kingdoms.

"Most of the instruments were of Arab origin, either improvised or replicated by Indian scientists for astrology and land surveys,"said Sarma.

MSU Vice Chancellor Ramesh Goyal released three books including new editions of Kritya Kalpataru (13th part) and Valmiki Ramayana compiled by MSU researchers from Oriental Institute before the start of the lecture series.

The third book was an alphabetical compilation of the manuscripts.

Heading: MSU V-C shows keen interest in abacus-based teaching - Indian Express
Content:
A city-based Marathi group, Chandraseni Kayastha Prabhu Utakarsh Mandal, will organise a grand musical programme on October 18 to felicitate Srinivas Khale, considered to be the doyen of the Marathi-Gujarati music industry.

Khale will return to the city after 30 years. The 82-year-old musical maestro is a former student of M S University's Faculty of Performing Arts and has been trained under musical legends like Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, who used to teach classical music in the late 1930s.

"Those were the days. The Faculty of Performing Arts was known as the Sangeet Vidyalaya. It was a great experience to learn from teachers like Bade Ghulam Ali Khan sahab," said Khale, who has trained music directors and singers Shankar Mahadevan and Suresh Wadekar. "Shankar [Mahadevan] used to visit me since the age of 10," he added.

Khale won the Dadasaheb Phalke Trust Award in 2003 for his contribution to the music industry in Maharashtra and Gujarat.

Commenting on the present day music scenario, he said there are an equal number of music lovers who still want to listen to Marathi and Gujarati light music.

"These days music is composed before the lyrics are finalised. In our times, it were the lyrics that decided the music," said Khale.

The nostalgic octogenarian will be felicitated by Mayor Balakrishna Shukla and Ranjitsinh Gaekwad, the scion of the Gaekwad royal family of the erstwhile Baroda State, for his contribution to the cultural sphere of Vadodara.

"I just cannot express my feelings, but at this moment

I feel elated to be honoured in the city where I picked up music as my career," said Khale.

Heading: State Reserve Police tents removed from riot-affected Fatehpura - Indian Express
Content:
Says he will approach the Education Ministry for implementation of the project in school curriculum if there is a properly documented pilot study

M S University (MSU) Vice-Chancellor (V-C) Dr. Ramesh Goyal has shown a keen interest in the Universal Concept of Mental Arithmetic System (UCMAS) education programme, which focuses on sharpening children's mental mathematics skills through abacus-based teaching.

The V-C hinted that he will approach the Education Ministry for the implementation of the project in school education if there is a properly documented pilot study.

Dr Goyal was invited by top UCMAS officials during their visit to Vadodara on Friday.

"The university has its own experimental school where new teaching methods are always implemented by the Faculty of Education. The state government is also coming up with various projects in school education. If the pilot study can be properly documented, I can approach the state government as well," said Dr Goyal.

Meanwhile, two researchers from the US are testing the abacus skills of over 350 students of UCMAS from across Gujarat as part of their 'Mental Abacus and Cognition' research project.

David Barner from the University of California, San Diego (UCSD) and Michael Frank from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) are conducting their research on UCMAS students in Canada and Gujarat. The experiment, which test the students' abacus skills in various stages and also assess their ability to use the optimum level of the brain.

In a part of the experiment, the students listen to an audio, repeat what they hear in the audio, and calculate five digit numbers, all at the same time. "Most humans do not or rather cannot use all parts of the brain at the same time. But with our study, we have found that the students use the optimum levels of all parts of the brain and that too at the same time because of the increased mental ability. This exercise trains both parts of our brain to work together," said David Barner, assistant professor, Department of Psychology, UCSD.

Apart from the research, a pilot project on abacus-based mental arithmetic by UCMAS is in the pipeline in some of the city schools.

UCMAS founder Prof. Dino Wong who was in the city, said, "We found that the Indian students fare much better than students in the US and other western countries because of their visualising ability."

Heading: Nano is welcome in Bihar if it has problems in Sanand: Lalu - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara police have removed five camps of the State Reserve Police (SRP), which were set up in the Fatehpura area of the city following the riots during Ganesh idol immersion ceremony.

According to City police Inspector B N Chawda, the two-kilometre stretch between Kumbharwada and Champaner Gate is now peaceful. "We realised that the SRP men did not have much to do, as people in the area have realised that there was no point in fighting," said Chawda.

He further said the perpetrators of the riots have been arrested and instead of the SRP, one police constable has been posted at the five spots. "We have arrested the perpetrators. If the need arises, we will station the SRP again," he said.

However, many residents differ on the issue, and say the move has been taken in a hurry. "The presence of security men prevented anti-social elements in the area to commit any crime or even those who would incite people to fight," said Saleem Khan, a local shopkeeper.

Jignesh Parikh, a businessman in the area, who feels riots are usually the handiwork of political leaders, expressed similar views. "When security men stay in the area, we know that such leaders won't dare to come here and shout slogans against each other's religion to incite youngsters. Moreover, elections are also near. Opportunists will take advantage of the situation and will keep on raising the same issue," said Parikh.

He added that during Diwali, some miscreants throw firecrackers on pedestrians, which may snowball into riots. "Here, riots occur for no good reason," he said.

Interestingly, another resident said the presence of policemen was uncomfortable for both the security persons and residents. "They stay in camps without fans. It is a tough job. And, we also get the feeling of staying in a fortress all the time," he said seeking anonymity.

Heading: New image: Sena takes up cause of ‘outstation’ students - Indian Express
Content:
Railways Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav has said if Tata Motors' Nano project is facing trouble in Gujarat similar to that in Singur then it is welcome to Bihar, as the state has lots of wasteland.

"The government here has given agriculture land to the Tatas for the setting up of Nano car project. Farmers are agitating against the move," Lalu told reporters during his visit to Somnath on Thursday. "If the state government is not able to handle the Nano project here, the Tatas are welcome to Bihar," he added.

"There is a lot of barren land around Dwarka (in Jamnagar). If they had given land near Dwarka, the area, which has not seen much development so far, would have been developed. People there don't get water to drink," he said.

The Gujarat government has given 1,100 acres of Anand Agriculture University land to the Tatas for relocation of the Nano project from Singur in West Bengal to Sanand.

Heading: South Africa revisits the Mahatma - Indian Express
Content:
The Shiva Sena, known for its hardline stance against "outsiders", has undergone a change of image. It has now thrown its weight behind 90-odd law students, most of them from other states, who have been denied permission to appear for their semester exams at the Indian Law Society-run Law College.

The Bharatiya Vidyarthi Sena (BVS), the student arm of the Shiv Sena, has taken up the cudgels on behalf of the students, who allegedly lack the required attendance. The exams begin on Monday.

"Despite meeting college authorities and officials from the university's exam department, there is little chance of the students getting their hall tickets. Therefore, we have decided to hold protests at the college on Saturday," said BVS city president Ajay Shinde.

Shinde said, "We are looking at it as a students' problem and supporting them because we feel they have genuine reasons for remaining absent." BVS city vice-president Sachin Shingvi was present along with volunteers Nilesh Naikwade, Prashant Rane, Abhijit Marne and Yogesh Shinde.

Vandana Sharma (name changed), an epileptic under treatment at Ruby Hall Clinic, said, "I submitted medical certificates to the college authorities. They have refused to accept them."

Siddharth Sharma, a second year student, who has only 33 per cent attendance (seven per cent short), said it was because of a stomach injury. "I submitted medical certificates a month-and-a-half before the college put up the defaulters' list. They had refused to accept the certificates then."

According to Sharma, there are 15 students with attendance between 38 and 40 per cent. He felt attendance ought to be calculated for the entire year and not for a semester.

Anuprita S (name changed) has 39.76 per cent attendance. "I have asked for a verification of my attendance as I am sure mine is well above the requirement." Her friends Manasi and Neetu, who have the minimum attendance, are backing her.

A couple of African students have been restricted from taking the exam for the same reason.

Students have cited various objections like attendance not being calculated for initial lectures in case of late admissions.

Some students mentioned that there were times when students were in class but no lectures were taken. They asked: "What about the marking of attendance for these classes?"

While principal Vaijayanti Joshi was unwell, vice-principal Jaya Sagade mentioned a court case filed by a girl student. "The court will decide whether the 90 students should be allowed to take the exam or not. I shall not comment until the verdict."

This is the second time this week that the Shiv Sena is behaving in a way alien to its usual line of action. At a recent meeting, the Shiv Sena had distributed a booklet and given a presentation, telling party workers how to reach out to voters. Some party workers, used to the hard-hitting rhetoric targeting rivals, did not seem very pleased with the change in approach.

Heading: Police heat on owner of flat that turned control room - Indian Express
Content:
South Africa renewed its connection to Mahatma Gandhi this week, thanks to the Commonwealth Youth Games. A large number of Games participants from South Africa visited the Aga Khan Palace, where the Father of the Nation was once incarcerated and which serves as a memorial of the apostle of non-violence. Players from Scotland, England, Ireland, Sweden and New Zealand too visited the palace.

"The number of visitors has doubled since the Games started," said Ganesh Dhotre, Estate Manager, Gandhi National Memorial Society at Aga Khan Palace. The average number before the Games was around 20 a day. Dhotre said the response shown by foreign participants has been encouraging.

The impression made by Gandhi on South Africa was evident from the fact that the largest number of visitors was from the South African delegation, Mahajan said. "The tourists wanted to know everything about Mahatma Gandhi, from his career as a lawyer to how he led the freedom struggle."

"Some of the visitors made it clear they were visiting the palace as they believed in Gandhi and wanted to know more about him," said Neelam Mahajan, a guide.

Youth Games co-ordinator Aditi Bhende said, "We organised visits for participants and delegates to various places in and around the city. Arrangements were made for visiting one place at a time, but there was a huge demand for a visit to the Aga Khan Palace. It made us organise more visits to the monument. We made arrangements even if a single visitor requested us for a visit to the palace."

Most of the foreign delegates knew about Mahatma Gandhi and found a good opportunity to know more about him through visits to the historical place, instead of other venues like the museum, temples or marketplaces.

The visitors were also interested in the Osho ashram and more than one trip was organised to the place. Apparently in a bid to give a good picture of the city, the Youh Games organising committee kept them away from any crowded places or slums. The visitors were taken to Shaniwarwada but the light and sound show was not on the itinerary list, a Games official said.

Heading: On their own lot, civic buses jostle for space with autos seized by cops - Indian Express
Content:
The city police are finally in action after being left out of the loop when forces from other cities cracked down on terror suspects based in Pune. They have turned the heat on the man who owns the flat that served as the Indian Mujahideen's control room.

Pushed into a corner, the flat owner has an explanation why he had failed to submit the mandatory details of his tenant to the police. He says a real-estate agent had duped him and talked him out of doing so.

Reza Naba, owner of Flat H302 in Ashoka Mews, said the police have warned him that action would be taken against him for flouting an order duly promulgated by a public servant. Joint Commissioner Rajendra Sonwane said flat owners who don't submit tenant details are violating prohibitory orders under section 144 of CrPC, punishable under section 188 of IPC.

"I had rented my flat to Dr Anwar Bagwan about 13 months ago through a real estate agent. I was misguided by the agent, who said there was no need to give any details to the police because the flat had been rented to a family after a registered agreement," Reza said.

"We had made a registered agreement on Rs 9,000 per month and a deposit of Rs 30,000. The agent would come to me with the rent every month. I never contacted Bagwan for rent; the deal was through the agent," he added.

The police warning has left him flustered. "They told me they would fine me for not submitting the tenant's details. I am co-operating with the police and will do what they say. Earlier, when I rented the flat to some students, I had provided the police all details with photographs," he said.

Reza said the flat was his only source of income. "Mumbai police have sealed it and I will have to o through a long legal procedure to get it back," he said.

Bagwan and the agent could not be contacted. A few days ago, JCP (Mumbai crime branch) Rakesh Maria had said his team was probing the role of the tenant and the real estate agent.

S S Mirza, the media spokesman of Ashoka Mews Society, said a neighbour had complained some youths and not a family were staying at H302. Reza, however, said, "Dr Bagwan is married, has two children and told me his younger brother would be staying with him. Whenever I went to the flat, I saw the family," he said.

Heading: Simply Shah - Indian Express
Content:
The public bus utility's 10 depots did not have enough night parking space for its 1,100 buses in the first place. Matters have become worse now with the buses forced to make room for around 600 autorickshaws and jeeps that have been impounded for lack of permits.

Over the last month, the traffic police have been conducting a drive against illegal vehicles but the department has little parking space beyond Yerwada parking lot. Hence the police are piling up the seized vehicles at the depots of the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) till the time the owners produce the required documents and get them released.

The police justify the action. DCP (Traffic) Manoj Patil said, "Bus depots like Nigdi, Hadapsar, Swargate and Katraj have ample space. These are illegal vehicles and because of our action the PMPML has benefited. The PMPML chief has written to us to say that they have gained over three lakh passengers because of the crackdown; for September, the company added Rs 4.4 crore to its coffers."

But many buses have to be parked outside the depots at night and manoeuvring space during daytime has been constricted. There has been theft of diesel and spare parts from PMPML buses thus parked outside.

Around 400 auto-rickshaws are parked at Nigdi bus depot, besides around 50 jeeps that were booked for taking commuters between Mumbai and Pune without permits. "Half the space here has been captured by other vehicles. We have around 15 buses parked outside, but those are contract buses. During drives against illegal vehicles, the number of impounded vehicles increases and it results in more buses getting parked outside at night," said an officer at Nigdi depot.

Around 170 of the 250-odd buses plying out of Swargate depot are parked outside at night because of the space crunch, said Rajendra Paitankar, depot manager. With 15 more illegal vehicles now parked, more buses will have to be parked outside, he said.

At Hadapsar there are over 190 illegal vehicles parked. "We have told the traffic police to shift these vehicles elsewhere, to no avail. There is space here and we don't need to park buses outside but it restricts the movement of the buses," said Vijaysinh Pardeshi, depot manager.

For the traffic police there is no immediate alternative for this in sight. Patil said reducing the number of these unauthorised vehicles was the only solution. "As our drives increase, the number of unauthorised vehicles will reduce and that will automatically solve the problem of space. We feel that our action is benefiting the PMPML. But if they say that they don't want to give us space, then we will write to other agencies," he said.

Heading: Director’s Cut - Indian Express
Content:
Actor Naseeruddin Shah welcomes the new wave in cinema, which he feels is a true reflection of life

It was an exciting evening for film enthusiasts as they witness a legend being honoured in the city where he started his career. As an actor, his first performance in a professional play was in Pune after passing out from National School of Drama. Hooked by the culture of the city, he went on to pursue a course in acting at the wellknown Film and Television Institute of India. The rest is history, as he proved himself as one of Indian cinema's most talented and versatile actors. It was only befitting that the same city honoured Naseeruddin Shah, with the Zenith Asia Award on Thursday.

Candid as always, Shah spoke his heart out on various subjects while speaking to media persons after the function. He was happy to receive the award but at the same time lashed out at the competitive awards given to artistes. "I hate competitive awards. Anyone comes; gives awards to film personalities and artistes accept it. It is unnecessary," he said.

He was rather sarcastic when he talked about the parallel film movement of the 1970's. "We were as revolutionary in our age as we used to think. I think we drew that conclusion at a very early stage." He did not forget to add that we should not categorise films.

Shah welcomed the new wave in Indian cinema, which according to him reflects our own lives. Expressing a wish to go further, he said, "I am happy to see Indian cinema coming up with new genres and interesting subjects. There is a lot of opportunity for creative people. But one should also see that it goes beyond urban life and touches the issues faced by those in rural areas," he said.

Going down memory lane, Shah talked about his FTII days. "I have a special relationship with Pune. I remember performing plays here. This is the place where I grew as an actor."

Memories of Ghashiram Kotwal, a famous play by the late Vijay Tendulkar made him more nostalgic. "I had seen this play at least 15 times. I used to shuttle between Mumbai and Pune every other day to watch the play. I hope I get a chance to act in the play, which will again be a production by Jabbar Patel; with Mohan Agashe in the role of Nana Phadanvis and me playing Ghashiram Kotwal."

Heading: Rice and shine - Indian Express
Content:
Through his films, Dan Wolman untangles the complex knots of relationships

For a country that has grown up in the shadows of war and political conflicts with its Arab neighbours, at the inception of its cinema, coming up with films that defined the country's identity as a nation striving for its existence is not surprising. But having come of age, Israeli cinema is no more fixated on the story of a nation's strife. And one such Israeli filmmaker who breaks the mould with his series of films is Dan Wolman. A window to his tryst with life, his films, as he puts it, are his personal reflections.

"I document my experiences in my films. The larger than life image that these days is very characteristic to new age cinema is not my choice of a film. Why not be realistic when we make films? There is so much to understand and unfold when it comes to the various layers of a relationship. Why not explore that then drifting away from reality?"

The director's film Foreign Sister which won the Volgin award at Jerusalem in 2000, offers an incisive glimpse of a woman's quest to rediscover her real self is a film which he says portrays the juncture where two of his experiences meet. The film also brings into forefront the plight of foreign workers. "There was a time when we Israelis did not have a place to go. We roamed around here and there and I feel these foreign workers are the Jews of today. Destiny brought them at an unknown place." Also the protagonist of the film is a character, which he says, came into being because of his wife. "My wife was the inspiration behind this character who in the daily grind of her family life had somewhere completely lost her own self."

The 6th Asian Film Festival, which is showcasing Wolman's Retrospective, will screen four of his films including Tied Hands, which paints the plight of a mother who is destined to witness the painful death of her ailing son.

Regarding Indian cinema, Wolman, who headed the 10th MAMI International Film Festival's jury earlier this year, says, "I really felt great when I saw some Indian films breaking the stereotypical formula." All praise for Tingiya, which was adjudged the best film at the MAMI festival, he says, "It was because Tingya was not based on the typical film formula with all the acts of the film being timed. The reason Taare Zameen Par lost to Tingya was because in the end Taare Zameen Par somewhat contradicted the message it was giving."

Heading: Spices & choices - Indian Express
Content:
100 Biryanis, as the name suggests, offers an astounding one hundred different types of biryanis to ensnare even the most fastidious eater

Sometimes there's a concept that you just know you can't go wrong with. "100 Biryanis" belongs to that category. And as incredible as it may sound, the fact remains that true to its name, the eatery actually dishes up an unbelievable range of 100 kinds of biryanis on its menu.

Located strategically on Satara Road, opposite Bharati Vidyapeeth, "100 Biryanis'' earlier existed as a café-Just4U- and still carries some of that ambience given the wrought iron lamp posts and striped awnings. But settle down in the pleasant and comfortable tables at the place and there's no mistaking the delicious aroma in the air.

"We wanted to reinvent ourselves and come up with something that wasn't there in the city. Whipping up one hundred biryanis seemed just the thing," says the dynamic Pavandeep Singh Kohli, a hotel management graduate from the city, who came up with the innovative concept and is now the driving force behind this family venture.

Divided into 50 vegetarian and 50 non-vegetarian biryanis, you can start your treat with the menu card itself that lists all the ingeniously devised dishes. For the carnivores the variety to choose form is mind-boggling. You can go in for the more traditional for Mutton Lucknowi Biryani (Rs 160) or then get adventurous with a Dragon Prawns Biryani (Rs 190) or a Surmai koliwada Biryani (Rs 160). According to Kohli their Murg Hyderabadi Biryani and Chicken Sukka Biryani (Rs 140 each) are amongst their most popular orders.

Vegetarians have been, pleasantly enough, given equal treatment at this biryani joint with 50 varieties at their service too. So you have the Pahari Paneer Biryani (Rs 120) and the Tale Hue Aloo Ki Biryani (Rs 110) or the Methi Chaman Biryani (Rs 140) all aimed at wooing you with their aroma born out of dum cooking. What makes the dishes even more enticing are the clay pots in which all the biryanis are served. In fact even take-aways are sent in these clay pots if desired at a nominal extra charge, informs Kohli.With a permit room and a variety of Kebabs also on offer, 100 Biryanis has already captivated a loyal clientele in the three months of its existence. From here the gastronomic journey can only get better.

Heading: Senior citizen brutally assaulted - Indian Express
Content:
A sneak peek into the daily diet of some CYG participants

Jack Longthorne -
wrestler, England
I am fond of Indian food. We have been served seven or eight types of Indian dishes and I must say that Indian curry is the best out of them all.

Takata Ramakhula,
coach, Lesotho
I am a patient of diabetes and haven't really ventured into hard core Indian food. But yes I have tasted a number of salads made the Indian way and I must say that Indian food is delicious. It sometimes tends to be spicy but then that is the specialty here.

Dianne Carter,
athletics official, Australia
We have been offered continental, European and Indian food. I personally feel that Indian food is spicy but then the kind of dishes served here are tasty and has that Indian touch.

Zack Davis,
boxer, Wales
I have been eating pasta for my meals since I've been here. The food is good but it's the same every day. For breakfast I have toast and cereals and afternoon I have pasta. I skip the heavy dinner.

JosEph Ganville,
athlete, Wales
I have tried Indian food, it's spicy but good, the spicy curry is what I like. But the course is the same everyday and it's monotonous to eat the same food. I like the fish and chicken that is served.

Heading: In villages, battle against bottle rages - Indian Express
Content:
The complaint filed by him with the PMC infuriated his neighbour

In a shocking incident, a 70-year-old retired army officer was brutally assaulted by his neighbour, over a complaint made by the former with the PMC against an illegal construction made by the latter. On Tuesday, Lt Col (retd) R P Lamba was relaxing at his residence, Panacea Apartments in Wanavdi when his neighbour K Nagaraju barged in and began abusing him. When Lamba tried to stop him and asked him to leave he began to beat him.

Lamba sustained injuries on his back, left hand and a fracture on his right hand. Lamba said "I had filed a complaint with the PMC against an illegal construction below my house. When the PMC official came to see the site about ten days ago, he found that the construction was illegal and the building plans had been violated."

"When asked about the shop, I told the PMC officer that it originally belonged to Nagaraju who had converted it into a makeshift studio apartment and had given it a water connection from the society water tank and sometime later he sold the shop to someone else. This new owner converted the place to a proper apartment and took a connection from the main water tank. As my line was directly connected to the main tank, I began to face water problems and so I complained against the shop owner."

He added, "On inspecting the plans of the building further, the PMC officer found that even Nagaraju had constructed a shed and an illegal side door at his residence, so they sent him a notice regarding the same. On Tuesday afternoon, Nagaraju, along with his wife, came to my house and began abusing me. He said it was because of me that the PMC had sent him a notice. When I asked him to leave the house he pushed me down and began to beat me."

The case was registered with the Wanavdi Police station. PSI S R Jadhav, who is investigating the case said, "After confirming that Lamba was indeed assaulted, we arrested his neighbour K Nagaraju. He has been booked under sections 452, 325, 323, 504, 506 and 34 of the IPC. We will ensure that stringent action will be taken in the case."

Heading: Sassoon doctor abused by patient’s kin - Indian Express
Content:
Like the women from Jhambut village in Shirur taluka who voted out two liquor shops in their village, the nearby Shikrapur and Dhorlewadi villages are also following suit with women submitting appeals to the Pune district collector.

Last August, women from Jhambut scored a major victory after they managed to get a liquor shop operating in their village shut down through a special voting procedure. Relying on the June 30, 2003 rules in the gazette of the excise department, if 25 per cent of women folk in a village voted against liquor sale, it becomes mandatory for the excise department to close the shop immediately, a rule, which the gram panchayats of Shikrapur and Dhorlewadi too are relying on to close the liquor shops in their villages.

Superintendent of State excise department (Pune district) Vijay Chinchalkar said that both the appeals have been submitted from these two villages and they would soon be conducting the necessary inquiries before the voting procedure is implemented.

"The genuineness of the appeal and the percentage of the women who are against the liquor shop will be checked. Depending on the percentage we will conduct the elections just as it was done in Jhambut," he said.

Earlier, women from Akurdi and Kendur had given similar complaints and three shops were closed down after voting process.

Chincalkar said that the district has in all two permit rooms and three country liquor shops, which were closed down after the process. "More villages are becoming familiar with the rule and the excise department is doing the needful," said Chinchalkar. Meanwhile, villagers from Shikrapur and Dhorlewadi are waiting for the resolution to come into force.

Tai Waghmode, a resident of Shikrapur said that the liquor shop was causing nuisance to the entire village and the women have been mobilised to vote against the liquor sale. Radha Chinchawade from Dhorlewadi said that the women have also had a special gram sabha to educate all the other women in the village to vote against the bottle and to protest against the country liquor shop in the village.

Under the rule, if not less than 25 per cent of women voters in a village, municipal corporation ward or municipality make a representation demanding the closure of liquor shops, the district collector has to arrange a secret poll among women voters in the respective area. If more than 50 percent of the women voters support the closure proposal the collector in consultation with the excise department must pass the order.

Heading: Telgi’s aide held, remanded to custody - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors threaten to go on strike if security system not in place by Oct 22

Yet another incident on late Thursday night has rattled the resident doctors at Sassoon General Hospital when a patient's relatives in a drunken state abused a doctor on duty. While the Bundgarden police have warned them, the doctors have decided that enough is enough and have given the college authorities an ultimatum of October 22 to put the security system in place.

"We will not hesitate to go on strike if the security guards do not man the place,'' said Dr Mahesh Mistry, general secretary of the Pune unit of the Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD) at Sassoon.

Four days ago, the hospital casualty room was damaged by friends of a patient who died on arrival.

The doctors are waiting for the authorities at Sassoon hospital to provide security. Though the State Government has given the go ahead for a draft bill that provides security to doctors, it will take time before the provisions are implemented, they said.

Citing the latest incident, Dr Akhilesh Darode, joint secretary of the Pune unit of MARD said that two relatives of a patient got drunk and began a verbal altercation with the attending doctor at ward number 15. Following a commotion, other resident doctors took the relatives to the Bundgarden police station.

While no official complaint has been lodged, the police conducted an alcohol test on the relatives and sternly warned them, said Mistry. There are nearly 300 resident doctors at Sassoon, apart from the 150 odd medical interns.

Heading: Christian delegation to  President: Stop violence - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officers produced Haseeb Ahmed Mushtaq Ahmed Shaikh, a close aide of fake stamp paper scam kingpin Abdul Karim Telgi, before the special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court on Friday. Shaikh has been remanded to judicial custody till October 22. Special judge P R Bora passed an order in this regard.

Shaikh, believed to be a trusted lieutenant of Telgi, was absconding.

The CBI sleuths had arrested Haseeb at Prudential tower, Fatehgunj in Vadodara, Gujarat on Thursday morning. Special public prosecutor for CBI Raja Thakare sought judicial custody of the accused as the main investigating officer S K Peshin was in Delhi. Thakare said that custodial interrogation of the accused was necessary. He requested the court to send Shaikh to judicial custody reserving the right of the police for his custody for investigations after Peshin comes to Pune. According to the CBI, the accused is the younger brother of Shabbir Ahmed Mushtaq Ahmed Shaikh, a convict in fake stamp paper case. Investigations revealed that he was an active member of Telgi's organised crime syndicate. Haseeb had opened a bank account in the name of M/s Vision Enterprises in Bharat Co-operative Bank at Modi street in Mumbai on June 8, 1999. Investigations revealed that this account was used for laundering money derived from the sale of fake stamp papers. An amount of over Rs 47 lakh was deposited in the account via different transactions, which was withdrawn subsequently.

Investigators also found that Haseeb had made several calls from his phone to the other accused in the scam. Haseeb had started an office at Ideal house, Modi Street in Mumbai in April 1999. A number of visiting cards and stationary of the accused in fake stamp paper scam were printed at Sujali Printers located at the same address. The payment for printing was made from the account of Vision Enterprises. The CBI had booked Haseeb under relevant sections of MCOCA and the IPC and he was declared an absconder.

CBI is investigating whether Haseen was also selling counterfeit stamps even after the arrest of other accused persons.

Heading: DP row: File views, citizens urged - Indian Express
Content:
A delegation of the Pune Diocese of the Church of North India and the leaders of various churches met the President Pratibhatai Patil in the city recently. The delegation memebrs expressed their concern over the various instances of communal violence in Orissa, Karnataka and Kerala.

The delegation included Bishop Vijay Sathe, Rev. C. Cornelius, Rev. M.A. Daniel, Rev. Nana Dar, and others met the president at the Raj Bhavan.

In a letter addressed to the President Rt Rev Vijay Sathe wrote about the increasing incidences of violence against the Christians in the states of Kerela, Karnataka and Orissa. He said, "The state governments and the law enforcement agencies as far as taking action against the accused and protecting the interests of the minority was concerned, were doing little."

In the letter, he also said even though all the national leaders were condemning the violence against the Christians little was being done to prevent such incidences from occurring.

He asked the president to take firm steps against the wrong-doers and ensure that such incidences do not occur in the future.

Heading: Bail plea of terror suspects adjourned - Indian Express
Content:
Reasons behind DP changes should be made public: Dharia

Appealing the citizens to file their suggestions and objections regarding the modifications made in the Development Plan for Baner-Balewadi before December 2, the civic activists have sought to know what prompted the state government to make alterations in the DP without even bringing it to the notice of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC).

The Green Pune Movement had organised a discussion on the Baner-Balewadi DP. Former mayor Vandana Chavan urged that people to come forward and register their suggestions and objections.

She said, "Due to the increasing level of pollution, the reservations for gardens and playgrounds will act as the lungs of the city and therefore necessary. If the hospitals or schools start running on the reserved lands, it is going to benefit the lower income groups from that locality."

Aneeta Beninger said, "A total of 46 modifications have been made in the development plan of Baner-Balewadi, which is the first unit out of the total ten units of the 23 merged villages of PMC. The most important reservation is that of a Bio Diversity Park, the decision on which is yet to be taken. For the cominggenerations the reservations will play and important role."

Vanrai president Mohan Dharia said, "The whole issue smacks of corruption and as pointed earlier, there has been an irregularity of Rs 500 crore in it. Hence, the reasons behind these changes in the DP should be made public."

MLC Chandrakant Patil said, "Nowadays, the civic administrations in all the municipal councils or corporations, is taking people for granted and passing decisions on their own."

Maj Gen (Rtd) S C N Jatar said that the Green DP movement should not be limited just for a short period of time.

"The civic administration took five years for this, while the state government kept sitting on it for more than three years and now the same government is giving only two months for filing the suggestions and objections, which is unfair. There should be a minimum of six months provided for this."

Activist Vijay Kumbhar, standing committee chairman Shyam Deshpande, Sandeep Khardekar were present on the occasion.

Heading: Bike accidents: Couple dies in Bhosari, student in Nigdi - Indian Express
Content:
The hearing on bail application of three suspects arrested by the Pune unit of state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) was adjourned on Friday till October 22. A special court was set up last week in Pune for hearing terrorism cases as per the directives from the Bombay High Court. The court was set up after three suspects Ayaz Khan, Imtiyaz Baba Miyan Shaikh and Feroz Mehboob Pathan filed a bail application in the court.

Assistant public prosecutor S M Jagtap sought adjournment for studying the unlawful activities (prevention) act. "The act is old. But its implication has started recently. So we need more time for studying the act properly," Jagtap told the court. "The ATS submitted its report to oppose the bail of the suspects. But ATS has not given the case details, "Jagtap said and sought adjournment. Judge S J Kale then adjourned the hearing till October 22. Pune ATS had arrested Ayaz Khan and Imtiyaz Baba Miyan Shaikh for their alleged involvement in a fake currency case. While Feroz Pathan was arrested with possession of 40 Urdu books and CDs carrying Jehadi literature.

Heading: Mulayam to Maya: arrest me or apologise - Indian Express
Content:
A young couple was killed when their motorcycle was hit by a container on Bhosari-Alandi Road late on Thursday night. The victims were identified by the police as Santosh Gaikwad (32) and Nita Gaikwad (28), residents of Sainagri on Alandi Road in Bhosari. The driver of the container fled after the accident. The couple is survived by two children.

At 11.30 pm on Thursday, the Gaikwad couple was heading from a hospital in Bhosari to Alandi. Santosh died on the spot while Nita suffered serious injuries. She was admitted to Yeshwantrao Chavan Memorial Hospital where she was administered first aid. She was then transferred to Supertech hospital in Chinchwad where she succumbed to her injuries on Friday morning, the police said.

The Vishrantwadi police have registered a case against the driver of the container.

Meanwhile, Amar Ashok Ghodke (23), a student of Siddhant College, lost his life in an accident at Bhakti Shakti chowk in Nigdi on Friday. According to the police, Amar was going to the college on his motorcycle at 8.30 am when the accident occurred. His friends admitted him to Lokmanya Hospital in Nigdi where he was declared dead on arrival. He is a native of Pandharpur.

Heading: Lalu dares Maya, eyes more land for rail coach factory - Indian Express
Content:
Samajwadi party (SP) chief Mulayam Singh Yadav dared Chief Minister Mayawati on Friday to either send him to jail or offer an unconditional apology for alleging that terrorism had flourished in the state during his regime.

"Mayawati should either arrest me or tender an unconditional apology to the people and the minorities in particular," he said, while addressing an "anti-persecution rally" at Fatima Girls Degree College near Sanjarpur village of Azamgarh district.

Sanjarpur hit the headlines last September as names of 18 youths of the village figured prominently in the serial blasts at Delhi, Jaipur and Ahmedabad. While six Muslim youths are under detention, two were killed in a police encounter at Jamia Nagar in Delhi last month.

"When innocent Muslim youths of Azamgarh were being targeted by the police of various states, Samajwadi Party was the only political party which protested against the persecution of the community and demanded judicial inquiry into the police encounter in Delhi and other incidents," Yadav said. He alleged that Mayawati, instead of coming to the rescue of the community, had accused SP of aiding terrorism in the state.

At the rally, which witnessed huge turnout of the local Muslim population, Yadav assured his audience that SP will continue to fight for their cause. But for this they will have to extend their full support to the party, he added.

According to the SP chief, the main issue of the party's statewide agitation to be launched on October 31 will be to fight the persecution and discrimination against Muslims by the police and the state machinery under the Mayawati rule.

Defending SP's decision to join hands with the Congress-led UPA at the Centre, Yadav said: "Alliance with the secular front was the need of the hour. The main enemy was caste and communal forces."

SP General Secretary Amar Singh, reiterating his demand for a judicial probe into the police encounter in Delhi, said: "SP has joined hands with the Congress only to fight the BJP and the BSP." He, however, added that SP has only joined hands and not surrendered before the Congress.

Haji Baddruddin of United Democratic Front of Assam was the star attraction of the rally. He made a fervent appeal to the Muslims to support SP. Baddruddin, a cleric and native of UP had floated the party ahead of the last Assembly elections in Assam and won 30 seats in the polls.

Mamata, Amar demand probe into Jamia Nagar encounter

NEW DELHI: On Friday, Samajwadi Party leader Amar Singh and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee shared a platform in Jamia Nagar, demanding a judicial probe into the Batla House encounter. "That was a fake encounter, and if I am proved wrong I will stop practicing politics. I demand a judicial enquiry," Mamata asserted amid cheers from the audience.

This was echoed by SP general secretary Amar Singh, who lambasted the Opposition for being critical of his demand for a probe. "Opposition leader L K Advani is criticising me for extending support to your demand and is demanding an apology from me. Even international media houses like the BBC and CNN are raising questions about the encounter. I urge the Leader of Opposition to help get the enquiry conducted," said Singh at a small rally in Jamia Nagar. Singh said there was no ambiguity in his position — while he has demanded a judicial enquiry, he has also extended financial assistance to the family of Inspector Sharma who was killed in the encounter.

Heading: IIM to train officers for a corporate career - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government is bracing up for another legal battle with the Centre after the Ministry of Railways published an advertisement in newspapers on October 15 announcing its decision to acquire 353 more hectares for the contentious railway coach factory at Rae Bareli.

Sources in the Northern Railways justified this move, stating that the Railways and Defence ministries had the right to acquire land in the states. Other ministries have to depend on state governments for the acquisition, they said.

This fresh acquisition is in addition to the 189 hectares — the allotment of which was cancelled at the last minute by the state government, just a few days before Congress chief Sonia Gandhi and Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav were to perform a bhumi poojan for the factory at Ahar village, Lalganj. Sonia Gandhi is MP from the constituency. The fate of the Rs 2,200-crore factory has been temporarily sealed by Chief Minister Mayawati after she directed her Principal Secretary Net Ram last Wednesday to look closely at the issues that plagued acquisition of the land concerned.

Sources said he would consider in his final report the points raised by the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court in its interim order on October 14. He would also check whether there were any procedural flaws in the resumption of gram sabha land, its mutation in favour of the factory and later the cancellation of the resumption order.

Net Ram had visited Rae Bareli on Thursday and held discussions with district officials. He also met the villagers of Ahar — the site of the 189 hectares.

A senior government official said: "The state will contest the Railways ministry's claim that it can independently acquire land. Further decision will be taken after Net Ram submits his report."

Sources said the UP government has mustered its legal resources to challenge the recent land acquisition by the Railways ministry. A high-level meeting held by State Advisory Council Chairman Satish Mishra, also the general secretary of the BSP, was held on Friday to prepare the government's case. An official said: "The Railways ministry may have taken refuge under the provisions of Section 20(E) of the Railway Act but the issues related to land comes in the state list."

Heading: Cong responsible for growth of homegrown terrorists: BJP - Indian Express
Content:
Continuing with its general management programmes for the officers of the armed forces, the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) will begin its fifth programme in this regard from October 20.

The 24-week programme, which will conclude on April 3, 2009, will train the officers on varied managerial inputs across all functional domains and, preparing them for a career in the corporate world.

This year, 65 officers (44 from Army, 11 from Air Force and 10 from Navy), will participate in the programme.

Cmde Rajeev Karsolia, Principal Director Employment, will be the chief guest for the inaugural session.

Proffesors Prakash Singh and Arunabha Mukhopadhyay will coordinate the programme.

Heading: Couple dies after a sack full of crackers explodes - Indian Express
Content:
General Secretary of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Arun Jaitely, has blamed the Congress party, Samajwadi Party and the CPI for the emergence of homegrown terrorism in the country.

Speaking at a seminar on "Terrorism, Problems and Solutions" at a college in Benajhabar on Friday, Jaitely said: "Earlier, the country was only dealing with cross border terrorism but due to the soft approach of the Congress and it allies, including former coalition partner CPI, homegrown terrorists have mushroomed in different parts of the country during the last few years."

He said that the situation is an alarming one, as the terrorists involved in the recent bomb explosions in the country do not belong to Pakistan or Bangladesh but are residents of our country.

"To make situation even worse, these terrorists are educated youths and not illiterate youngsters who have been misled by a bunch of jehadis," he added.

He said these parties have adopted the policy of portraying the "villains as victims" in order to strengthen their votebank. Citing the example of the recent arrest of Abu Bashar from Azamgarh in connection with the Ahmedabad serial blasts, he said that it did not take long for senior Congress and Samajwadi party leaders to visit the alleged terrorist's house and portray him a victim.

"The politics of appeasing minorities or a particular section of the society can never end terrorism from the country, as the issue needs to be dealt strongly," he said.

"Rather than appreciating the role of policemen in fighting terrorism, politicians from both these parties are busy in proving real encounters as fake ones," he added.

On the issue of banning Bajrang Dal after the recent attacks on Christians, Jaitely said that the group is being made a scapegoat in the entire episode.

"The UPA government has failed to place a ban on Indian Mujahideen or SIMI, but by banning Bajrang Dal it want to portray communal harmony in the country," he said.

Earlier in the day, during a symposium at Ragendra Swarup Centre of performing Arts, the BJP leader criticised Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and Union Finance Minister P Chidambaram for implementing poor economic policies.

"Rather than an economist, the country needs a seasoned politician as the prime minister. During his tenure Manmohan Singh has failed on both the fronts," he said.

"Following the policies of Chidambaram, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) government in Uttar Pradesh has increased the Value Added Tax (VAT) on 42 products from 4 per cent to 12.5 percent," he said and expressed his sympathies towards the traders of the state.

Heading: BJP and RSS to work together - Indian Express
Content:
A couple was killed when a bag of firecrackers, which they were carrying, exploded near the Malhaur railway station in Lucknow on Friday.

Rajendra Gupta and his wife Sunita were carrying around 50 kg of crackers to sell during Diwali when the motorcycle on which they were riding skidded. "Since the barrier was down, the man tried to get across through a narrow opening on one side," said Vinay, a local resident. After the motorcycle skidded, an explosion followed, killing the couple on the spot.

The blast was so powerful that pieces of their bodies were scattered in a 100-metre radius. The vehicle was also badly damaged.

"A purchase slip recovered from the spot showed that Rajendra had bought crackers worth Rs 10,625 from the market," said Additional Director General (Law and Order) Brij Lal.

Gupta, a resident of Vivek Khand in Gomti Nagar, used to run a 'chat' shop and before every Diwali he used set up a firecracker stall. The police did not know if he had a license to sell crackers. The couple is survived by four children. His eldest son, Ravi, who is about 18 years old, helped his father in his work. He confirmed that his father had gone out in the morning to buy crackers. Neighbours said the marriage of the couple's eldest daughter was also to take place shortly.

Later, the police conducted a search at the firecracker shop from where the couple had purchased the crackers in the Nagram area and arrested the shopowners for keeping crackers over their sanctioned limit. The police recovered 200 kg crackers from the shop. "The shopowner had license to keep 15 kg of prepared crackers and 50 kg of raw materials," a police officer said.

Heading: Constable held for abducting boy - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Rashtriya Swayam Sewak Sangh (RSS) seem to be coming closer to help the former regain its lost ground in the state.

Ahead of the parliamentary elections, senior members of both the RSS and BJP will sit together to review the performance of the party in the past elections and also frame a poll strategy. According to reports, senior RSS Pracharak K C Sudarshan is likely to be a part of the three-day convention to be held jointly by the BJP and the RSS.

During the convention, which is scheduled to be held in Lucknow between November 21 and 24, he is expected to meet senior BJP leaders and train the new members of the party on the lines of the Sangh.While BJP members have been asked to attend RSS meetings, RSS regional pracharaks have also started becoming an active part of the district level meetings of the BJP.

On Tuesday, RSS members participated in a district unit meet of the BJP organised in Lucknow. Pradeep Bhargava, president of the BJP Lucknow district unit, said: "Some of the pracharaks of the Awadh region were present at the meeting and gave some valuable inputs."

After senior leaders like L K Advani and Murli Manohar Joshi will address a rally at Varanasi on October 18, members of the district units of the party from the Awadh region will take part in a meeting of RSS pracharaks that will be held a day later.

"All the members who have been a part of the RSS from their early days will attend the meet," said Bhargava. Moreover, RSS meets at Kanpur scheduled for October 24 and 29 and Lucknow meeting are also likely to see some major decisions being taken.

A senior leader of the state unit of the party said: "We have a very strong base in the RSS. Many of our members are still a part of the shakhas and they will attend the RSS meetings. Also, our senior leaders and RSS pracharaks will sit together to help frame a plan which will help us to gain back our Hindu votebank in UP, specially in the eastern and the central region."

Apart from these meetings, the regional meetings of the BJP scheduled for districts like Allahabad, Varanasi, Jaunpur and Gorakhpur will also see active participation of the district RSS units.

Heading: No headway in Kanpur blast, cops claim probe heading in right direction - Indian Express
Content:
A police constable and five others were arrested on Friday for kidnapping a five-year-old boy in Bulandshahar district. The accused also included the maternal uncle of the victim.

Abhay Sharma — a resident of Aligarh — who was abducted on October 8, was rescued from a hideout at Gunnaur in Budaun district.

According to the police, Abhay used to stay at the home of his maternal uncle, Monu, in Khurja. Since Abhay belongs to an affluent family, Monu hatched a plan to kidnap him.

Circle Officer (CO), Khurja, R K Singh said that Monu took the help of his friend Jai Prakash, a constable posted with the GRP outpost at Rajghat, to get a mobile phone and SIM card that was bought with fake documents. Monu helped other gang members, including a student of Jatiya Polytechnic College, to get the boy abducted from his house, the CO said. They demanded a ransom of Rs 30 lakh for the release of the victim.

The police, however, managed to trace the gang members after putting the mobile phone on surveillance and arrested Monu, Jai Prakash and four others, Singh said.

Two youths rob Rs 1.74 lakh from Amity College cashier

Two youths ran away with Rs 1.74 lakh from a cashier of Amity College on Friday. The police said that after withdrawing cash from a bank, Sushil Kumar Singh was on his way to the college when a tyre of his scooter got punctured.
