Heading: CRR cut not to increase inflation: Bansal - Indian Express
Content:
President George W Bush sought to reassure Americans about the cost and scope of the US financial bailout plan and said that in the long run "our economy will bounce back."

Bush, in his weekly radio address, acknowledged that people are concerned about their finances and, while he offered assurances about an eventual recovery, he did not say when that would happen.

Since Oct 9, 2007, when the Dow topped 14,000, investors have lost USD 8.3 trillion from pension funds, college savings plans, 401(k) self-funded retirement plans and other investments.

"The federal Government has responded to this crisis with systematic and aggressive measures to protect the financial security of the American people," Bush said. "These actions will take more time to have their full impact. But they are big enough and bold enough to work." Congress gave Bush a USD 700 billion plan to buy bad assets from banks and other institutions to shore up the financial industry.

Bush was to meet later at Camp David for talks on the economy with French President Nicolas Sarkozy and European Commission President Jose Manual Barroso, who were to stop in the United States on their way home from a summit in Canada.

In the Democrats' weekly radio address, Rep Rahm Emanuel used the occasion for campaign criticism against John McCain, the Republican presidential nominee.

"On weekends like this, maybe you're like me and my neighbours, working around the house, trying to save a few bucks," said Emanuel, the chairman of the House Democratic Caucus.

Heading: Cure love sickness with sex, says research - Indian Express
Content:
The recent cut in CRR, mandatory deposit requirements for banks, by Reserve Bank to infuse liquidity in the financial market would not cause inflation to move up again, Govt said.

"I do not think that cut in CRR will lead to any increase in inflation but we are closely monitoring the situation to ensure that inflation does not rise, productive sector continues to get funds and growth remains sustainable," Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal told reporters.

RBI reduced the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) by 250 basis points at different intervals within a fortnight to inject the much needed liquidity in the banking sector.

Inflation fell to 11.44 per cent for the week ended on October 4 due to decline in oil prices and manufactured goods.

Stating that the government acts on 'situation to situation' basis, he said that the government had to raise the CRR on numerous occasions in the past even at the cost of economic growth in order to contain the inflation that had reached double digit mark.

"The Government had to take this decision (raising CRR) earlier as part of its inflation management measures. At that time, we were even ready to shed some growth to rein in inflation," he said.

Heading: Coffee 'can shrink women's breasts' - Indian Express
Content:
It may sound strange, but it seems to be true. Victorian doctors recognised love sickness as a medical illness and prescribed sex as a treatment.

Dr Lesel Dawson of the University of Bristol, who carried out the research, said that feelings of love sickness were particularly prevalent when people were not allowed to express love. This caused anger and frustration and turned into a mental illness.

"Love sickness was quite often a 'class-crossed' love when a rich person was in love with a servant but they weren't allowed to express that," she said.

Dr Dawson, whose results are published in the book Lovesickness and Gender in Early Modern English Literature said that the best cure was seen to be sex - and this would often be recommended to the patient's family.

She said, "According to early writers, sex expelled the lover's excess blood and seed, which accumulated in the body and putrefied, releasing harmful vapours that could cause melancholy".

Heading: Virdhawal whips up a frenzy in Pune, takes 50m gold - Indian Express
Content:
Hosts India shed their tag of poor performers at Olympic sports and pulled of a major upset at the Commonwealth Youth Games that concluded in Pune on Saturday by topping the standings with a rich haul of 76 medals.

Showing a marked improved performance at a time when the International Olympic Committee president Jacques Rogge was present, India betterd their last edition's medals tally by leaps and bounds wrapping up the seven-day extravaganza with 33 gold, 26 silver and 17 bronze.

Last edition's champions Australia finished on the second spot with 24 gold, 19 silver and 22 bronze, while England with 18 gold, nine silver and 14 bronze secured the third spot.

In last edition of the Games at Bendigo four years back, India could manage to garner only 10 medals (two gold, four silver and four bronze medals) to settle for a poor eighth place finish. Australia had ruled the roost there with 58 gold, 41 silver and 30 bronze, while England and South Africa had finished on second and third spots respectively.

India had to settle for a silver and a bronze on the concluding day of the CYG which saw only boys and girls singles finals and third place play-off in tennis being played.

Having pulled out of the singles semi-final after twisting his ankle, Yuki Bhambri made up for yesterday's disappointment as he earned India the first medal -- a bronze -- on the concluding day when he beat New Zealander Logan Mackenzie in straight sets.

Yuki broke Mackenzie twice in each set to wrap it up 7-5 6-2.

Kyara Shroff wrapped up India's CYG campaign by bagging the silver in the girls singles tennis at the Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex at Balewadi. Kyara was defeated by Heather Watson of Guernsey 1-6 2-6 in the final that lasted less than an hour.

Heather broke Kyara's serve twice to take a 5-0 lead in the first set and then held on to her serve to pocket the set.

In the second set too, the Guernsey girl broke the Indian's serve twice to take a 4-0 lead and then wrapped up the set and the match 6-2.

At the CYG in Pune, the biggest gain for India was double trap shooter Asher Noria who bettered Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore's silver medal winning effort at Athens by one bird.

By achieving this feat, the 16-year-old Hyderabadi, who idolises UAE great Ahmed bin Hasher Al Maktoum, became a new hope for Indian shooting. Shooting, by the way, fetched the hosts six gold and three bronze medals.

Contrary to expectations, Indian athletes were a revelation at the CYG finishing with six golds, seven silver and six bronze medals. In athletics, India, as a matter of fact, finished second behind England who topped with seven gold, three silver and three bronze. Australians with five golds, six silvers and eight golds finished on third place.

The Beijing effect was clearly visible in wrestling where India made a clean sweep claiming all the seven golds up for grabs.

Boxers also sizzled in the ring with three gold, one silver and one bronze. One of the gold was bagged by Beijing bronze medalist Vijender Singh's brother Balwinder Beniwal (69kg).

Although Saina Nehwal was not at her best against a 15-year-old Sikki Reddy in the all-Indian girl's singles badminton final, the Beijing Olympic quarter-finalist managed to secure the gold as the discipline went on the expected lines fetching India three gold, two silver and one bronze.

In front of the home support, Kolhapur swimmer Virdhawal Khade made a spalsh, bagging three gold and three silver medals.

Incidentally all of his gold medals went into the CYG record book, while Khade's timing of 22.68s in the 50m freestyle was a youth record.

Indian weightlifters also basked in glory with two gold, seven silver and one bronze medals. The hosts also had to witness some setbacks in the third edition of the CYG. Although, table tennis earned three gold, three silver and one bronze medal, top Indian woman paddler Neha Aggrawal failed to live up to her billing and crashed out in the semi-finals.

The big disappointment, however, came from tennis – the only discipline among a total of nine (athletics, badminton, boxing, shooting, swimming, table tennis, tennis, wrestling and weightlifting) in which India failed to pocket a gold medal. The hosts could only garner three silvers and one bronze in the discipline.

Altogether, 71 countries participated in the seven-day meet seen as the prelude to the 2010 Commonwealth Games in New Delhi. The next edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games will be hosted by the Isle of Man in 2011.

Heading: Anand grabs first lead as Kramnik blinks - Indian Express
Content:
It's a gesture that cannot be clearly equated to any particular emotion. A loose closing of the fist, a brush of the chin and a light punch to the chest. Muttering a prayer, some self-encouragement — the words are hard to decipher really. Virdhawal Khade allows himself that one personal moment in a race before stepping up on the block, just before he begins to entertain the audience with his strokes and the rare spectacle of an Indian beating a fleet of South Africans and Australians.

Pune took to Khade over the last three days of CYG like, well, Khade took to water some years ago. The frenzy is hard to explain, and harder to contain, and in his final solo 50 m freestyle event at Balewadi here on Friday, the sheer din in the stadium resulted in the race taking off a little late as the competitors struggled to hear the start signal.

The last time a swimmer generated such hysteria would probably have been at Khazan Singh's medals at the Asian Games, or Sebastien Xavier's various nationals. But in Khade, the Indians have struck a rare swimming hero, as his three gold medals, three silvers and two games records would show.

What's more, Khade even loves the attention. Competing in his first major meet at home after his trip to the Olympics and the few ripples he caused at the world youth meet in Mexico, the 17-year-old has thrived in the adoring spotlight of his home audience. Lesser men would have felt the heat, he chose to braggingly announce the ambition of five medals before the event.

On Friday, Khade first bettered the 50m games mark in the heat, with a 23.16, and then added a gold with a 22.68, the left fist punching the air even before the screen flashed the results.

"Kolhapur to England," screamed the banners, as Khade's fans raised the stakes and aimed at 2012, though the boy is still only on the fringes of the world pecking order. The boy with streaked hair and the elvish ears doesn't stand out really. But when swimmers file out to the starting blocks, he certainly looks the part, equal in height to the Aussies and the English boys — no unwanted flab, no slumped shoulders. The Indian self-doubting, unlike so many previous years, doesn't nag at the start.

An effortless spoke-like movement of arms and undiminishing speed made him unbeatable here in the 50 m, but Khade needs some work in the 200. "I've worked hard on the sprints, so the 200 will need a lot of hard work," he admits.

Heading: Karlovic knocks past Djokovic - Indian Express
Content:
World Champion Viswanathan Anand crashed through the defences of Vladimir Kramnik of Russia in the third game of the world championship here at art and exhibition hall to go into lead, winning the third of the 12-match world championship title clash.

Winning with black, Anand now leads 2-1 with nine games to come and will now play white in the fourth game on Saturday. Kramnik was simply unnerved by the turn of events and it was clearly visible the way he handled the final part of the game.

Anand stuck to his guns, employing the Slav defense for the second time in the match. Kramnik, who had gauged with a rather insipid play in the first game of the match, had other ideas this time around as he went for an age-old setup, known to have wild complexities. The opening did not give much for Kramnik as Anand clearly emerged as the better prepared. The Russian was glued to his chair in the early stages while Anand was seen blitzing out the moves in far quicker time.

As is typical of the opening, the players reached a fairly unbalanced position with white having a couple of passed pawns on the queen side while black had its share of counter-play in the form of piece activity. It was only on the 19th move that Anand had to think for a reply, a clear indication that the Indian ace was in preparation till that point.

Time lead

Already close to 90 minutes had passed since the start at this stage and Anand had a huge lead on time, having spent little over 10 minutes against Kramnik's 85 minutes. The Russian was left with just 45 minutes at this point but here onwards, Anand spent a lot of time.

It was careful planning, brilliantly executed with a fine king side attack that netted Anand the full point. The Indian ace thought a long time and even fell behind on the clock for some time but, by then, everything was under control.

With pressure building, Kramnik lost control of the position on the 33rd move and played a blunder. Even though Anand did not draw the curtains immediately, the end was quite near front his point onwards. Kramnik lost his queen once the avalanche of black pieces came firing at his king and the rest was easy pickings for Anand. For the record, the longest game of the match thus far lasted 41 moves.

Heading: With upsets in the air, Air-India wary ahead of Chirag United clash - Indian Express
Content:
Towering Croat Ivo Karlovic toppled third seed Novak Djokovic 7-6, 7-6 to make the quarter-finals of the Madrid Masters on Thursday. The 14th seed will meet Frenchman Gilles Simon next after unsettling Djokovic with his booming serves. Both sets went to tiebreaks, which favoured Karlovic, who blasted 20 aces, to Djokovic's eight.

On Friday, Roger Federer beat ninth-seeded Juan Martin del Potro of Argentina 6-3, 6-3 to reach the semi-finals, where he will face Andy Murray in a rematch of the US Open final. The second-seeded Federer used an effective slice serve on the fast indoor surface and was never broken. "The slice goes nicely on this court, I felt good using it to counter Juan Martin's height," Federer said.

Federer also played serve-and-volley, chip and charge returns and clean passing shots against his 20-year-old opponent. Del Potro served 12 aces, including 11 in the first set, but couldn't trouble Federer. "He started serving great, many aces," Federer said. "That's what makes him the good player he is. I had the ability to stay calm and use my slice well here in Madrid where conditions are very quick."

Federer was helped by Del Potro's four double-faults. 'Roger generates pressure just by being in front of you," the Argentine said. "I double-faulted on my serve in each set to lose the match. Roger gave nothing away and I wasn't able to even take a set off him. He broke my rhythm all the time and took full advantage of his break points, which I wasn't able to do, that's the difference."

Federer, who missed last week's Stockholm Open due to fatigue, said he felt happy with his physical condition. "I don't know what would have happened if I'd gone to Stockholm, but I'm playing well here," he said.

Federer's semi-final opponent will be fourth-seeded Murray, who beat Gael Monfils of France 6-2, 6-2. "I'll have to come up with a proper game plan," Federer said. "He played well against Monfils, so I'll have my hands full with him."

Monfils broke Murray in the opening game, but the US Open finalist broke back immediately. Murray broke two more times to take the set. The second set followed the same pattern. "He almost enjoys running too much and almost likes you to dictate play," Murray said of his 22-year-old opponent. "Once he gets used to big matches we're going to be seeing a lot more of him."

Nadal breezes

Top seed Nadal booked his place by breezing past an out-of-sorts Richard Gasquet 6-4, 6-2. It was a much more convincing performance from the top seed, who had laboured through his opener against Ernests Gulbis on Tuesday, and he showed little sign of suffering from the muscle strain that forced him out of the doubles as a precaution. "I am much better. I spent the afternoon with the physio yesterday and we'll have to see how it goes," said the Spaniard. "(Against 15th seed Gasquet) I was much better than on my first day and he committed more errors than usual, particularly on his backhand." Next for up for Nadal is compatriot Feliciano Lopez, who saw off Switzerland's Stanislas Wawrinka 6-4, 6-4.

Bhupathi-Knowles in semi-finals

Fourth seeds Mahesh Bhupathi and Mark Knowles moved into the semi-finals of the Madrid Masters with a 6-3, 7-5 victory over Sweden's Simon Aspelin and Julian Knowle of Austria. Next, they will take on fifth seeds Jonas Bjorkman and Kevin Ulyett, who were responsible for taking out the top-seeded duo of Bob and Mike Bryan.

Heading: Ryder Cup criticism was unfair, says Harrington - Indian Express
Content:
McLaren's Lewis Hamilton made the best possible start to his quest to win the Formula One title at the Chinese Grand Prix by dominating Friday's free practice.

The 23-year-old Briton, who could become the sport's youngest champion on Sunday, swept around the 5.451km circuit in one minute 35.630 seconds in the morning session and clocked the quickest lap in the afternoon as well.

"Today has been a very productive day and a very strong day for us, the car's been great," he told reporters. "I feel confident with the track and I'm in the right mind frame."

Hamilton will, however, be painfully aware that he also dominated all weekend in Shanghai last year but ended his race marooned in a gravel trap and ultimately gave up a 17-point championship lead to Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen.

Raikkonen's team mate Felipe Massa is Hamilton's closest rival this year, trailing by five points with 20 up for grabs in the last two races, and the Brazilian was second best on Friday with a morning time of 1.36.020.

That compared with Hamilton's best of 1:35.630.

"The balance of the car is very good, both on the first timed lap and over a distance," said the Brazilian.

"The times are very close and maybe I could have been a bit further up the order in the afternoon session if I had not encountered traffic on my last run on the soft tyres. These seem to be very quick, which is no surprise, but also very consistent."

Kubica's struggle

Poland's Robert Kubica, the only other driver left in the title race, showed what a struggle it will be for him to make up 12 points on Hamilton in the last two races as he was only able to muster the 10th fastest time of the day for BMW-Sauber.

Spain's double world champion Fernando Alonso, who has won the last two races, continued his and Renault's revival with a flying lap late in the afternoon session for the third fastest time of 1:36.024.

Hamilton showed no signs of being distracted by the continuing controversy over the safety of his driving, although he did run off the track on his sixth lap halfway through the opening session.

He recovered immediately to top the time sheets on his next go around and, although he was quickly trumped by Massa, his second stint saw him become the first driver to dip under 1.36 and he bettered even that four laps later. The Briton opened the second session in similar style, quickly topping the time sheets with a run of 1.35.750.

"Everybody has the right to their opinion and all I can do is respect it," Hamilton said of the criticism. But I do have to say the reason I'm here today is how I drive. If I was in a Force India, then nobody would be talking about it."

Heading: Sachin’s record plays on - Indian Express
Content:
Criticism of the European team for their Ryder Cup thrashing by the United States was unfair, says three-times major winner Padraig Harrington, but it will be used to drive them to victory next time.

Harrington, a member of the team which lost 16 ½ points to 11 1/2 in Louisville, Kentucky last month, said the US had been deserved winners and no one should be blamed for the defeat.

"It was a disappointment, for sure, but not as disappointing as (the last defeat) in 1999," the Irishman said in a conference call on Friday.

"The US team deserved the win this time. Why we lost, we could talk about it for a long time... next time we'll have home advantage and the fact that we lost makes us more motivated and as a team, very strong."

Europe's captain Nick Faldo came under fire at Valhalla Golf Club for overlooking Cup stalwarts Darren Clarke and Colin Montgomerie as his two wildcard picks, opting instead for Paul Casey and Ian Poulter.

But Harrington defended Faldo and said critics should focus on the performance of the team, not just the result.

"When people analyse things after the event, they look at the result and decide that something wrong happened, we have seen that in the Ryder Cup over the years," he said.

Captain was right

"A captain has done a bad job and won and he gets a lot of praise. The captain can do everything right and still lose. Every losing US captain has had a lot of criticism, it's just about results and results don't always reflect the performance."

Harrington captured his second successive Open Championship title in July to clinch his third major in two years, but insists his sudden success surge has come as no surprise.

"Three majors looks like a great improvement and a big spike to the outside world, but it's not like that," said Harrington.

Heading: ‘Seniors’ hit back at critics with long partnership, take India past 300-run mark on Day One - Indian Express
Content:
Towards the end of his press conference, Sachin Tendulkar was asked how the team was planning to celebrate Anil Kumble's 38th birthday. "There's a cake in the dressing room, and I'm pretty sure he'll get to eat quite a bit of it. Some from his mouth, the rest through his ears and his nose," he said, eyes crinkled, giggle suppressed, looking and sounding much younger than his actual age of 35.

Excerpts from the interaction:

On breaking the record

• I don't know how to describe my journey. It's been fantastic so far. I enjoyed it. There have been ups and downs and I have been able to overcome those obstacles. Success is a process and during that journey, sometimes there are stones at you and you convert them into milestones.

On missing out on a century

• I was disappointed on getting out at 88. After the crackers went off, we decided to spend as much time in the middle. It was reverse-swinging a bit, but the new ball took me by surprise.

Test and ODI records, what next?

• My next target will be to continue playing as I am. I'm enjoying the game. When I started as a 16-year-old, there were no targets. I just wanted to go and enjoy every moment.

How would he sum up his journey ?

• I don't think I can. It has been a fantastic journey. For me, it has never been about breaking records, the milestones have come along. I've had great support from my family, friends and my coach Ramakant Achrekar, which has worked for me so well.

Does he see the record being broken?

• All the records are meant to be broken. I'm pleased that it came my way. I don't know about the future. There might be another 16-year-old who may not have any targets, who knows where he's going to go?

His thoughts as he looked to the sky

• I thanked God and sought my late father's blessings. Had he been alive, he would have been proud.

At what point in his career did he start thinking about this record?

• As the career progresses, the subconscious starts thinking about it. People start talking about records. That is how you are aware of all these things. There have been occasions when I swore to my team mates that I didn't know how many runs I needed. Some didn't believe it but I was willing to swear on anyone. That's when they believed me.

Was the low turn-out disappointing?

• It's not about the quantity, but the quality. I got a memorable reception at the ground. There was big excitement in anticipation of making those 15 runs.

An answer to his critics?

• I don't have to answer any critics. I don't have to prove anything to anyone. I'm not concerned about what people say or they are writing about. People have opinions on what's going on in my mind, (when) sometimes even I don't know what goes on in my mind.

His favourite knocks

• My first hundred in England (1990) was memorable as we managed to keep the series alive. And then I had a good series in Australia, where I scored centuries in Sydney and Perth on two different pitches. That gave me confidence that I could score anywhere.

On how much not winning the World Cup hurts

• That is something I would like to have. We were close to it in 2003. It was so close yet so far. I'm not looking that far ahead (till 2011).

What would be a good score here?

• I think, around 1,200 should be enough.

Heading: 12,000 and counting, but he isn’t just about numbers - Indian Express
Content:
A lot of questions were raised about the Indian middle-order in the run-up to this series. Six days into the contest, the replies are flying thick and fast off seasoned blades.

On Friday, Sachin Tendulkar and Sourav Ganguly, both of whom had played crucial hands in saving the Bangalore Test, dug in and then opened out to take India to a healthy 311 for five on the first day of the second Test. For a few overs in the second session, after three Indian wickets had fallen in the space of 4.2 overs for 17 runs, it seemed as if Ricky Ponting's plan, which has revolved around restricting the batsmen, would pay off.

The rains had stayed away for more than 24 hours, and with the sun beating down at the Punjab Cricket Association Stadium, the stage was set for a big first innings score. On a pancake flat first-day track, Virender Sehwag threw it away after a fine start. Gautam Gambhir and Rahul Dravid saw it through to lunch before the latter fell against the run of play. Then went Gambhir, wafting lazily at a Mitchell Johnson away swinger, only edging it to the keeper. Laxman hung around for 19 deliveries, looking comfortably in the zone when his bat magnetically followed one that was drifting down the leg-side.

At 146 for one, with the field spread out as it has been during this series, the match seemed to be drifting aimlessly. Australia were happy the scoring rate had dropped from 5.87 in the first hour to around 3.5, Gambhir and Dravid would have been pleased at the number of singles on offer.

Suddenly, at 163 for four, the match was alive and the Australian attack, toothless until then, was kicking up a storm.

Tendulkar eased into his innings, singles and twos, keeping himself busy and letting mundane world records take care of themselves. At the other end, Ganguly took circumspection to a different level with the tea break looming. He blocked 17 deliveries before getting off the mark, and while his first runs came thanks to an edgy couple down to third man, everything else that was thrown at him found the middle of his bat.

Wake-up call

Tea had its desired effect on the duo. Ganguly seemed to have woken up, as a couple of sweet drives through the covers off debutant Peter Siddle got the crowd going as well. And as far as Tendulkar was concerned, it was happy hours once the business of breaking a world record was dealt with. The oldest guards in the Indian middle brought up their 50 partnership off 92 deliveries and their century stand off 165. As the shadows grew longer, Tendulkar seemed to grow taller. When Cameron White came on, both Tendulkar and Ganguly cashed in. When Siddle was brought back, they celebrated.

It was only when the second new ball was taken, bang on 80 overs, did it look like Australia might get something out of the final session. Ganguly played and missed a couple of times, and jogged to square-leg to settle his nerves. At stumps he was still there on 55, with night-watchman Ishant Sharma for company. Tendulkar, who looked set for a big one, edged one to Hayden, his knock ending at 88 and the entertaining partnership at 142.

There has been a lot of talk about this Australian squad and the inexperience in their ranks. It didn't show in Bangalore. But today, when things started going bad, they did look rather ragged.

Heading: Mehrab leads Bangla fightback - Indian Express
Content:
Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy who climbed a mango tree once too often. But we'll come back to that fairytale after a minor digression.

For those who follow basketball, there've been so many heirs to Michael Jordan's throne over the years that the tag has become a bit of a joke. Penny Hardaway, Grant Hill, Allen Iverson, Carmelo Anthony, the list goes on. Moral: world domination is easy to foretell, difficult to achieve.

Keeping that in mind, let's return to the story of Sachin Tendulkar. When he was 16, experts had predicted he would break every batting record. Yesterday, as he lifted his bat with fireworks in the backdrop, the little boy from Bandra who was banished to the cricket field to keep him away from climbing tress, had again proved them right.

But let's not be confused about the record. Sachin is no greater than he was yesterday because of the 88 runs that took him past Brian Lara's mark, and he won't be any inferior when someone else goes farther. This isn't the story of a man trying to scale Mount Everest and finally taking the last, gruelling steps to the top. In cricket, you fight your battles on a day-to-day basis with 10 other members of your team. The 12,000-run aggregate was a natural progression for someone who fought the hardest for so long, it wasn't the target he had set out to achieve.

But what has been highlighted again is Tendulkar's longevity in the face of all sorts of problems — be it a couple of runs of poor form, or the tremendous punishment his body has taken over the years because of constant wear and tear. His being the highest run-scorer in Test cricket must be celebrated, but not in isolation.

Of all his world records, the four that stand out are his runs and centuries marks in both Tests and one-dayers. But the one that interests me as much is that he is still the youngest Indian Test player ever. So many cricketers reach the international stage at a tender age — Parthiv Patel, Harbhajan Singh, Sourav Ganguly back in 1991, from our era itself. Some fall away, some go on to do really well for themselves. But how often does the youngest ever go on to become the greatest ever? Hardly anyone, across fields, lives the dream that Tendulkar's professional life has been. If you saw it in a movie, you would've said it was a bit far-fetched.

In the West Indies, where Lara is from, the media and public scrutiny is not nearly as intrusive as it is in India and Tendulkar has had to see his share of ups and downs of late. But there has scarcely been a logical, honest debate about him in spite of all the TV slots and the reams of newsprint (his 'end' had been predicted almost three years ago).

And in the last few months, with the frenzy about sacking the seniors reaching unreasonable proportions, the aura of Tendulkar has been slowly waning. People jump on the bandwagon to scream congratulations when he reaches a milestone, but his name is often accompanied with sarcastic jibes as well. He summed it up yesterday: "When people throw stones at you, you turn them into milestones." If nothing else, the comment shows that Tendulkar has been affected by the way the public and media have reacted to him over the last few months.

It's true that he has changed, perhaps even declined, as a batsman — going past the world record will not alter that. But that decline is only in relation with our unreasonable expectations of him, and in comparison with his own glorious past. Stripped of the baggage, man to man, he's still good enough to be in this Indian team, and then some.

Let's enjoy what he has left to offer, and not just praise him when he breaks a world record.

Heading: How Sachin prepared, with a little help from his friends - Indian Express
Content:
Left-hander Mehrab Hossain capped his return to international cricket with a maiden half-century to help Bangladesh recover in the opening Test against New Zealand here on Friday.

The 21-year-old was on an unbeaten score of 79 to lift Bangladesh from a precarious 44-4 during an unbroken fifth-wicket stand of 139 with Mushfiqur Rahim (59 n.o) to take the hosts to 183-4 at close on the opening day at the Divisional Stadium.

Mehrab, who scored eight and six in his only Test appearance against Sri Lanka last year, played aggressively in an otherwise snail-paced batting performance.

New Zealand captain Daniel Vettori made bowling changes at regular intervals, but failed to stop the duo from posting Bangladesh's best Test fifth-wicket stand.

It was left-arm spinner Vettori (2-50) who jolted the Bangladesh batting after lunch, grabbing two of the three wickets to fall in the space of just ten runs. Bangladesh gave a Test debut to off-spinning all-rounder Naeem Islam, while batsman Jesse Ryder made his Test debut for the visitors.

Heading: Saina gets gold, boxers light up ring with seven medals - Indian Express
Content:
On Friday morning, Mumbai's 26-year-old medium-pacer Usman Malvi finished an early breakfast only to find himself getting into a serious argument with his cable operator. The service network in the western suburb Andheri, where Malvi stays, wasn't available. Frustrated that he'd miss Sachin Tendulkar scoring those all-important, Malvi was losing his cool.

"I got to see it much later when a news channel was flashing it," he said, irritated that he missed his idol surpassing Brian Lara's record. All the bowlers in Mumbai's Ranji squad, or even those at the fringe level, have bowled to Tendulkar in the nets at some point. Malvi is no different. In fact, when Tendulkar was preparing for the Australia series after recuperating from his elbow injury, Malvi was among only three bowlers invited to have a go at him.

He remembers how he wore his spikes and dashed to the Bandra-Kurla ground, wanting to be played by the man himself. "Usman, zyaada bahar mat daal, nahi toh padegi (don't bowl too wide off the crease or you'll get hit)," Tendulkar had told him. Malvi bowled a couple of overs by the time Tendulkar found his rhythm, began shuffling his feet well at the crease and lofting him all over the park. "Imagine how frustrated I was today when I couldn't see him break the record. As much as I was desperate, I missed it," he said.

Tendulkar's home in Bandra was surrounded by a huge media contingent. His wife Anjali had no choice but to come down the building and address them. "It's a reward to his dedication, patience," she said.

The batsman had been going through a rough patch, injury worries had been haunting him, and a mere 95 runs in three Tests against Sri Lanka had led to fingers being pointed in his direction. He was so low that Tendulkar didn't even visit his ailing coach Ramakant Achrekar before the series against Australia began. "He came before the Sri Lanka series and it was the last time we saw him," says Kalpana Achrekar, Ramakant's daughter, not wanting to comment further on the batsman's visits to her father that have been a norm for quite some time now.

For help, Tendulkar also fell back on his brother Ajit, his first-ever batting coach. Thrice, the two brothers made their way to the nets and spent a good time discussing various aspects of his batting, his mental and physical approach. "He practised at the centre wicket of the Bandra-Kurla ground but more importantly, they spent a lot of time with each other," says Mumbai Ranji team coach Praveen Amre.

Finally, it was also Tendulkar's childhood friend Atul Ranade who bowled to him in the nets, as he's done over the last decade. Ask Ranade if Tendulkar was nervous in any way before the series and Ranade says, "Sachin can never be nervous. I don't remember a single day in my life when he was upset or disappointed. It was a momentary failure in Sri Lanka. We both knew that things would return to normal soon."

Heading: Anti-Christian violence concerns Britain: Lord Brown - Indian Express
Content:
Saina Nehwal survived some nervous moments to claim the girls singles gold of the third Commonwealth Youth Games on Friday. Fifteen-year-old Sikki Reddy gave Saina a tough fight before the latter wrapped up the tie 23-21, 22-20 to clinch the gold.

It needed a string of unforced errors from Sikki to let Saina pocket the first game after she was down 17-18 at one point of time. Saina capitalised on her opponent's errors to take the lead at 20-18. Sikki levelled it at 21-21 ans then produced a spectacular smash to close the game.

The second game was no different as each time Saina tried to put Sikki on the mat, she would bounce back. With the game oscillating from one to the other, it was Saina's turn to forge ahead. She was just two points away from victory at 19-13 when her rival won four consecutive points as the crowd egged her own.

However, an overhead smash helped Saina stretch her lead and when Sikki's shot went beyond the line, the match was all over.

Sikki, however, finished with a gold in doubles when she paired up with Thulasi to blank Mary Bruce and Man Shan Michelle Li of Canada 21-18, 21-8 in just 21 minutes. Guru Sai Dutt had to sweat to overcome his unseeded opponent of Aditya Prakash. In a 50-minute sweatfest, Guru finally overcame Aditya 21-18, 20-22, 21-18.

Boxers' haul

Meanwhile, putting up a superlative show in the ring, Indian pugilists pounded out three golds and a silver.

Their overall haul of three gold, one silver and three bronze further swelled India's ever-burgeoning medals tally to ensure the hosts stayed on the top of the pack.

Not only was there plenty of action in the centre square, but also camaraderie. The moment of the evening arrived when Canadian welter weight Benjamin Shamoon carried up Balwinder Beniwal in his arms in the ring after the two ended a closely fought match.

With the scores at 2-2, Beijing bronze medallist Vijender's cousin Balwinder was declared winner on count back.

Silver in tennis

India bagged two silver in tennis on a day when medal hope Yuki Bhambri twisted his ankle and conceded his boys singles semi-final. India, though, is in with a chance to win gold in girls singles after Kyra reached the final defeating Monika 7-5, 2-6, 6-3 even as Poojashree lost to Heather Watson of Guernsey 2-6, 1-6 in the other semi-final.

Heading: ‘Muslims getting isolated, being confined to certain areas’ - Indian Express
Content:
Lord Mark Malloch-Brown, the British Foreign and Commonwealth Office minister of state's mailbox has been flooded with mails from concerned British MPs and citizens, on the violence against Christians in India.

Lord Brown, who was visiting India for two days, met National Commission for Minorities chairperson Mohamed Shafi Qureishi on Friday and expressed concern on the issue.

"My mailbox has been brimming with mails from MPs and people, which I consider as a weather-vane. The issue of violence against Christians has been the

single biggest issue in the recent weeks," he told The Indian Express.

India, Lord Brown said, has been known as a multi-ethnic country. "And if that multi-cultural tolerant mosaic is breached, it breaks alarm," he said, adding, "We are all anxious to see how the Indian government acts."

Lord Brown, who met Minister of State (External Affairs) Anand Sharma, Foreign secretary Shivshanker Menon and National Security Advisor M K Narayanan, also discussed international financial crisis and called for reform in the international financial architecture.

"Today's financial architecture is 1945 in vintage. Wines may be good if they are more than 60 years, but not international financial institutions," he said, as he reiterated British Prime Minister Gordon Brown's pitch for IMF and UN reforms. The UK PM, who visited India early this year, had called for reforms in the international institutions, thereby backing India's claim to the high-table.

The visiting minister also felt that India should "do more" in terms of maintaining "good UN citizenship" as it lays claim for the UN high-table. "For example, India should contribute generously to the UN's core budget," said the minister.

On the international financial crisis, which formed a substantial part of his discussions with the Indian government, he said the crisis was "like an epidemic" and there was a need to have a "global system of governance" to tackle the crisis.

He responded to the concerns raised by many, including Brazilian President Lula, that the developed world had not acted for last 10 months as the US sub-prime crisis broke in December last year. "There was no early response to the financial crisis since nobody foresaw the financial crisis to snowball into the present level," he said.

He also felt that allegations of "casino capitalism" is "a bit unfair" -the charge was made by the Brazilian President early this week - as he pointed out that India, China and Brazil have also reaped benefits from capitalism.

Heading: Patrons losing confidence in Nehru Museum - Indian Express
Content:
In what was one of the grandest Sir Syed Day celebrations till date, the Aligarh Muslim University on Friday celebrated the 191st birth anniversary of its founder, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. The sprawling university campus, decked with green and red lights that hung from the parapets of various departments, looked festive.

The focus, this year, was not just on Sir Syed's contributions to promote modern education among Muslims but also on the stereotyping of the community in the wake of recent terrorist attacks and the encounter at Jamia Nagar.

"It's a segregated society these days with Muslims getting isolated and being confined to particular areas," said Prof. Hameeda Ahmed, former dean of arts department at the university. "Many members of my family can't get houses because they are Muslims," she added.

Prof. A A Nizami, dean of engineering and technology, said the University had an important role to play in the social fabric of India, while Khalid Mustafa, a student, said that it was in secular institution like Aligarh that people could come together and dispel such myths.

The event also witnessed the conferring of the Sir Syed Ahmad Khan International Award on Mohd. Zakir Ali Khan, a Pakistan national and an Aligarh alumnus, for his literary work.

The college alumni, from different parts of the world, also attended the function, which had on its guest list former Chief Justice A.M. Ahmadi and governor of Uttar Pradesh T.V. Rajeshwar. The two-day World Summit of AMU Alumni will begin here on Saturday.

And as the 800-odd alumni dressed in the fashion of those days, conjured memories of each other, figured associations, reconnected and exchanged addresses, they hope that the three-day event will take them to a life they had lived and then cherished over the years.

"In those days, the girls wore gararas and sat behind a veil in classes. A lot has changed over the years. Now women wear jeans here but some of the traditions have remained," said Sajida Nabi, former university faculty and AMU alumna. And the audience jeered as a student's dupatta slipped off her head while she was on the stage to talk about Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. In her confusion, the student looked around. Someone pointed at the dupatta. Only after she pulled it back did the audience let her continue.

As the famous taraana "Main Is chaman ka bulbul hoon" was sung, tears streamed down some of the alumni's faces, even as they remembered every word and sung along.

Heading: Pakistan objects to US Army Chief's Siachen visit - Indian Express
Content:
The Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in Delhi, considered to be among the most renowned research centers in the country, seems to be losing the confidence of some of its most eminent patrons.

In an unprecedented move, seven scholars, all past or present research fellows with this highly prestigious academic centre, have raised their voice against the declining standards in the institution, especially in the past couple of years.

In a detailed note to the NMML administration, seven scholars, including Professor Sumit Sarkar, Dr Ramchandra Guha, Dr Dilip Simieon and Professor Neera Chandhoke, have listed the areas in which, they claim, the institution has been deviating from its objectives and not performing to its past standards.

They have blamed the present NMML administration for failing to augment the current collection of oral history and neglecting the manuscripts section which has a rich collection of papers that once belonged to the country's leaders and famous personalities. It criticised the move to open a children's centre "which cannot be one of the functions of a research institution".

But perhaps the most damaging charge is that the NMML administration has been courting political patronage by allowing banners and slogans to be put up inside its premises and renting out its auditorium to the Youth Congress. "The NMML has always been identified with a broad liberal sensibility in the best traditions exemplified by Jawaharlal Nehru. It has kept its doors open to individuals motivated by the purpose of genuine research and inquiry. However, by permanently festooning the premises with photo-exhibits, banners and slogans, the present Director appears to be keen to transform the institution into a platform for partisan propaganda. This may gratify some people for the time being but will set a dangerous precedent," the research scholars have written in their note.

Some scholars also met NMML president Dr Karan Singh in July and made him aware of their concerns. When contacted, Ramchandra Guha told this paper that "no action of any kind" had been taken on their submission.

However, Dr Karan Singh said the points raised by these eminent scholars have been taken note of and the matter has been discussed in the executive committee meeting of the NMML.

The scholars also pointed out that the life history of just one person had been recorded for the oral history division of NMML in the last one year whereas earlier the average was about 20. They have proposed that an advisory committee of reputed academics be set up for recommending institutional objectives and have also suggested that NMML needed to broaden its activities.

Heading: Tamil cause: ally DMK steps on gas, 14 MPs ‘put in’ papers - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan taking serious notice of reports that the US Army chief Gen W Casey is scheduled to visit the Siachen glacier in Jammu and Kashmir during his ongoing three-day visit to India, has raised objections to it .

"Any such visit to a disputed area still under discussion between Pakistan and India will certainly cast a shadow on the ongoing composite dialogue," a Foreign office spokesman told The News daily.

He said there was no official confirmation of the American general's plan to visit Siachen.

Pakistan had earlier objected to India allowing civil and military expeditions to the Siachen glacier, where troops from both countries have been engaged in a face-off since 1984.

Troops from both the countries traded fire along the Line of Actual Control in Siachen till a ceasefire was put in place along the frontiers in Jammu and Kashmir in late 2003.

Heading: Kerala CM spearheads anti-Centre stir in Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Stepping up the offensive on the Centre to come out with concrete steps to ensure ceasefire in Lanka, 14 DMK members in the present Lok Sabha, including Union ministers, handed over their 'post-dated' resignation letters — addressed to the Lok Sabha Speaker — to party president and Chief Minister M Karunanidhi on Friday night.

On Thursday night, three Rajya Sabha members of the DMK had handed over their resignation to the party president, following Karunanidhi's daughter Kanimozhi who was the first to do so on Wednesday. Led by senior DMK leader and Union Shipping and Transport Minister T R Baalu, Telecom Minister A Raja, junior ministers Subbulakshmi Jagadeesan, S S Palanimanickam, K Venkatapathy, S Regupathy and Radhika Selvi, MPs handed over letters to Karunanidhi at Anna Arivalayam.

The date of all resignations has been put as October 29, the day after the last day of a two-week ultimatum issued to the Centre at a multi-party meeting on Tuesday.

Though they have handed over the resignations, the members and ministers would perform their duties till the last day of the deadline, said party sources, adding that the resignation letters were symbolic, expressing their willingness to stand by the decision taken by the party high command. In fact, two of the RS members who 'resigned' on Thursday night, Tiruchy N Siva and A A Jinnah, attended the first day of the current session on Friday.

"We have given the Centre ample time to deal with the issue; these resignations are not intended to put the Centre under any undue pressure," said a member.

The meeting on Tuesday had resolved that members of both Houses hailing from Tamil Nadu will tender their resignation at the end of the notice period on October 28, if the Union Government does not fulfil demands including immediate ceasefire in Sri Lanka, providing relief material, food and medicines to the Tamil families affected by the war and ceasing all support to the Lankan forces in their war against the LTTE. The meeting had the representation of 37 out of the 39 LS members from Tamil Nadu.

The tough posturing by the DMK has not gone down well among the other parties who attended the meeting. The state unit of the Congress party, for one, has been caught in the middle with regional interest on one side and national perspective on the other. "When the state unit informed the high command about the ground situation, the Prime Minister responded immediately, voicing his concerns openly and clearly. The External Affairs Ministry has been taking follow up action to solve the crisis. Moreover, the DMK is a part of the ruling alliance in the Centre," said a Congress leader.

Sources in the PMK, an ally of the UPA and a party to the decision to resign, scoffed at the resignations, stating that it was an affair within the DMK. "If these were indeed resignations, it should have been addressed to the Prime Minister, Speaker or RS Chairman. By handing over the letter to their party president, it is clear that it is only an affair within their party," said a senior PMK leader.

Meanwhile, Opposition leader and AIADMK general secretary J Jayalalithaa challenged the DMK to dissolve the state Government, if they were serious about safeguarding the interest of Tamil lives. Charging that the human chain and resignation of MPs were just fodder for the media, she dared Karunanidhi to resign from the post of CM along with his party MLAs, if he was serious about the resignation threat.

DMK's state ally VCK, whose leader Thol Thirumavalavan is an LTTE sympathiser, has announced that the party cadres will organise a rail roko agitation across the state on October 23. In yet another related development, a group of advocates from Coimbatore burnt the effigy of

Defence Minister A K Antony, protesting the Indian military assistance provided to Sri Lanka in its war to eliminate the rebels.

Heading: Govt summons Lankan envoy, voices concern - Indian Express
Content:
Kerala Chief Minister V S Achuthanandan on Friday led his entire Cabinet to a march to Parliament alleging "discrimination" against the Left-ruled state by the Congress-led UPA Government and accusing the Centre of not granting many of the legitimate demands of the state.

Addressing the demonstration attended by almost all Left MLAs and MPs from Kerala, CPI(M) general secretary Prakash Karat spoke against concentration of powers with the Centre and favoured a new look at Centre-state relations. Opposition Congress organised a parallel dharna in Thiruvananthapuram against what it called the ruling Left Front's "political gimmick" with an eye on elections.

Achuthanandan, addressing the demonstration, said that the Centre had been neglecting the state and not doing enough as per the requirement of the state on various "critical" issues. The major demands raised by him are restoration of the rice quota for above poverty line families, restoration of the power share from the Central electricity pool, setting up of an IIT in the state and sanction for establishment of a railway zone in Kerala.

"They had promised us many things, but none of them materialised. The protest in Delhi comes in this backdrop," Achuthanandan said. He said the Centre first slashed the rice quota meant for APL families from 1,13,420 tonnes to 17,056 tonnes and then stopped it completely, and reduced the share of power from the Central pool from 1188 MW to 667 MW.

Apart from Karat, CPI(M) leaders Sitaram Yechury and Brinda Karat, CPI Deputy General Secretary Sudhakar Reddy, RSP leader T J Chandrachoodan and Forward Bloc's G Deverajan participated in the demonstration. Besides MPs and MLAs and 16 ministers from Kerala, Left MPs from other states also sat on a dharna in what is seen as an attempt to shift the blame on the Centre for everything that's amiss in the state.

Heading: Solution before deadline: Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Faced with tremendous pressure from Tamil Nadu parties, including key ally DMK, on the Sri Lanka situation, and keen to placate its concerns, the UPA Government on Friday summoned Sri Lankan High Commissioner to India C R Jayasinghe, expressed its "grave concern at the humanitarian situation", and asked for an end to the harassment and killing of Indian fishermen.

This is the third day in succession when the UPA Government has made noises about the situation in Lanka. Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukerjee have already expressed their concern at the situation in the last two days.

That the DMK wants the UPA to work diplomatic strings was evident, as Union Cabinet Minister and DMK leader T R Baalu on Friday told reporters, "We know the Government of India cannot intervene militarily. We want the Government to use diplomatic channels to bring an end to this conflict."

Jayasinghe was called in the evening by Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon, who said that "Sri Lanka should ensure that the rights of its civilians are respected and they are protected from attacks", sources said.

Jayasinghe was told that "India was gravely concerned over the situation arising out the conflict in Sri Lanka and wanted Colombo to address these concerns", sources said.

It is learnt that the Foreign Secretary communicated that "India wanted Sri Lanka to stop harassing and killing its fishermen in the common waters between the two countries. The Sri Lankan envoy was conveyed that Colombo should find a negotiated political solution to the ethnic problem rather than look for a military victory.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, at the joint press conference of the IBSA summit, had said the situation in the island nation is a cause for "serious concern" and asked Colombo to find a negotiated settlement rather than looking for a "military victory". He had said India was concerned over "escalating hostilities, losses suffered by civilians and increasing number of displaced persons" in Sri Lanka. Singh had said the situation calls for a "negotiated political settlement which respects the unity and the integrity of Sri Lanka and at the same time respects the essential human rights of minorities".

Heading: EC clears the air, J-K poll dates likely by Monday - Indian Express
Content:
With the DMK MPs threatening to resign demanding Government of India's intervention to safeguard the interest of Tamils in Sri Lanka, crisis managers of the ruling Congress have swung into action. External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee on Friday discussed the situation with Union Minister and DMK leader T R Baalu, who left for Chennai in the evening to brief party chief and state Chief Minister M Karunanidhi about the steps taken by the UPA Government to address their concerns.

According to Congress sources, a solution would be found before the deadline of October 28 when the DMK MPs have threatened to resign.

Tamil Nadu Pradesh Congress Committee president K V Thangkabalu told The Indian Express here: "How can Karunanidhi bring down the UPA Government when he himself is a senior leader of the UPA? The UPA Government is taking all possible steps to address the DMK's concerns."

"The situation today is different from what it was yesterday. The Prime Minister has already expressed concern about the Lankan situation and the issue has been taken up with the Lankan Government. We are the only party, which made a supreme sacrifice for the cause of Tamils. We are expecting that the Government of India will take appropriate steps to safeguard the interest of the Tamil community there," said Thangkabalu.

Heading: CPM game plan: pin down Govt on technicalities - Indian Express
Content:
Jammu and Kashmir is likely to elect a new Assembly before the Governor's rule ends there on January 9. The Election Commission is likely to make an announcement to this effect by Monday.

The ambiguity over the J&K election dates in the EC appeared to have ended here on Friday when the representatives of seven Hindi-speaking states, who met the Election Commissioners here, said they had no problem in meeting the contingency plan of 4,000-odd Urdu speaking poll officials, who may have to fill in for local election officials in the state.

In a related development, the EC brass dashed off a letter to Jammu and Kashmir Chief Secretary on Friday, demanding to know if the state would need any additional election staff from outside the state for poll-related duties. In a meeting with the EC brass last week, the state Chief Electoral Officer had expressed apprehensions that the local staff might stay away from election duties. J-K Chief Secretary is expected to reply by Monday.

The EC also factored the "discernible shift" in the National Conference position on early elections in the state, even if it was "a less-than-forthright aye". "With one of the two main state-based political parties coming around, our task became a lot easier," said a top EC official.

While onset of the winter being a genuine problem, the EC brass took heart from the fact that the parliamentary elections in 1984 were conducted as late as on January 3 in the state, while in 1980 and 1989, too, the Lok Sabha elections were held in the winter months in the state. "Winters do prove a genuine problem, but there's very little that one can do, especially after four months getting lost due to the past disturbances in the state," said a top EC official.

It also now transpires that there was a three-way — and not a two-way — division among the Election Commissioners over the election dates in the state when it met on October 14 to decide the dates of "mini" general elections. Chief Election Commissioner N Gopalaswami was said to have advocated a "wait-and-watch stand in view of the uncertainty" in the state. Election Commissioner S Y Quraishi is learnt to have initially backed the CEC and then mooted "club-the-Assembly elections-with-Lok-Sabha elections" idea. Election Commissioner Navin B Chawla favoured an early election.

The CEC, in an interview with The Indian Express on October 15, welcomed the National Conference statement favouring elections in the state. Friday's meeting of Hindi-speaking states on sparing Urdu-speaking staff for elections in the state, however, clinched the issue for the poll panel. "Except for some extraordinary situation, we are well on course towards having elections in the state," said the EC official.

Heading: Oppn corners Govt on timing of House session - Indian Express
Content:
Apart from the breach of privilege motion moved against Prime Minister Manmohan Singh for "violating" the assurance given to Parliament, the CPI(M) is planning to tie down the Government on technicalities during the session.

Party MPs have given notices against the Government for violating constitutional procedures and parliamentary norms and are planning to raise these issues on Monday. The first notice pertains to Government promulgating an ordinance to amend the Agricultural and Processed

Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985 on October 13 on the eve of the Parliament session.

Veteran parliamentarian and former Kerala Assembly Speaker Varkala Radhakrishanan, who has given the notice, said it is "highly objectionable" that the Government has promulgated an ordinance after convening the Parliament session.

"An ordinance cannot be promulgated after convening the Parliament session," he told The Indian Express.

Besides, the President had not prorogued the Lok Sabha session after it met for two days to take up the confidence vote in July. "The Lok Sabha is alive and the Rajya Sabha has been convened and it is unjustified and illegal to promulgate an ordinance," he said.

According to rules, he said, an ordinance cannot be promulgated after convening the session of if the session is underway.

Radhakrishnan alleged that the Government kept the Lok Sabha alive for three months to ensure that no substantive motion is moved against it as it is in a minority. Besides the posturing by the Samajwadi Party, DMK members have also threatened that they would resign en masse if the Government does not take any steps to stop attacks on Tamils in Sri Lanka, he added.

"What was the urgency in promulgating an ordinance after the session is convened. Heavens would not have fallen if they had waited for four days. They did this because they do not have the required number to pass the legislation," he claimed.

He also questions the decision to keep the Lok Sabha alive and without transacting any business for such a long period.

He also refers to the Lok Sabha Speaker's decision in the late 1990s that it should meet for at least 180 days a year. "By clubbing the Monsoon and Winter sessions, the Government has violated this practise also," he said.

Radhakrishanan has also moved a breach of privilege motion against the PM for "violating" the assurance he had given in the Lok Sabha during the July 22 trust vote that he would seek the guidance of the House before operationalising the 123 agreement.

Heading: BJP, Left force Houses to adjourn - Indian Express
Content:
Demanding a rescheduling of the current session, the Opposition attacked the Government for its casual approach to Parliament at meetings held in the chambers of presiding officers of both Houses on Friday. Hard pressed to defend the Government, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Vayalar Ravi tried to engage the Opposition, but was overwhelmed by his more articulate opponents.

"We demand that they reconsider and reschedule the session," BJP spokesperson Sushma Swaraj told the media after the meetings of leaders of parties in the Lok Sabha and the business advisory committee (BAC) of the Rajya Sabha. She said the session overlaps the poll campaign in five election-bound states and important festivals like Karva Chauth, Dhanteras, Diwali, Govardhan Puja, Bhaiyyadooj and Chhath.

She said it is a peculiar situation with the Lok Sabha having a continuation of the 14th session and the Rajya Sabha a fresh one. "It is a clever move to avoid a fresh vote of confidence in the Lower House," she alleged. The issue is bound to crop up during Zero Hour in both Houses on Monday.

Leader of the Opposition L K Advani led the attack on the nature and timing of the session at the Lok Sabha group leaders' meeting chaired by Speaker Somnath Chatterjee. He was supported by CPI(M) leader Basudeb Acharia and CPI leader Gurudas Dasgupta.

Advani said, "This session cannot be considered a continuation of the last session when the confidence vote was taken." He said the session had come in the midst of the festive season. How can a session be held while elections are being held in five states? Practically suggesting that the Government take the Opposition into confidence over its actual design, Advani said, "We don't want to be told midway that Parliament is being adjourned due to Assembly polls."

Dasgupta said, "We are not going to make any suggestion (with regard to session) as Advani has said... This Government is in the habit of doing this (declaring holidays) and then putting the blame on the Opposition." Dasgupta asked the Government to explain why had the Government taken Parliament for a ride Acharia, according to sources, said the schedule betrayed a lack of seriousness. He said the Government appeared keen on avoiding Parliament.

When Dasgupta and Acharia termed the whole thing unprecedented, Ravi reportedly exclaimed: "The Prime Minister was not allowed to reply to the discussion on the confidence vote—this is also unprecedented." Acharia, at this stage, shot back: "This is also unprecedented that MPs brought cash to the House; what are you doing on this count?" Acharia said the Lok Sabha had had the least number sittings during the last Budget Session.

Heading: Violence in Assam: BJP presses for President’s Rule - Indian Express
Content:
Both Houses of Parliament were adjourned on Friday as pandemonium struck Rajya Sabha with the BJP raising terrorism and price rise issues and Left moving a privilege motion against Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on the nuclear deal.

Rajya Sabha was adjourned twice — first during the Question Hour and then for the day — as BJP and Left MPs repeatedly rushed to the well shouting slogans. As obituary was paid by Rajya Sabha Chairman and Vice-President Hamid Ansari to the terror victims across the country in the Rajya Sabha, the BJP said tribute should also be paid to the VHP leader who was killed in Orissa. They also said that the Centre should stop threatening imposition of President's rule in Orissa.

Left MPs raised the issue of privilege motion against the Prime Minister on the nuclear deal, arguing that he had not taken Parliament into confidence before inking the agreement as promised.

After Rajya Sabha completed the obituary references, trouble broke out when Ansari also made references to those killed in bomb blasts, stampedes and floods. As Ansari asked members to observe silence, the Left MPs demanded that the House should also condole the deaths in communal violence, leading to an uproar. The House was then adjourned till noon.

Lok Sabha was adjourned for the day as a mark of respect to two sitting members and seven former members who died during the inter-session period.

Heading: After LA, Bihar’s Super 30 reaches New York film fest - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Assam Chief Minister claimed that the situation in strife-torn Udalguri and Darrang districts was fast improving and people were beginning to leave relief camps for home, the BJP on Friday described the situation as 'alarming' and said it was a fit case for invoking Article 356 and imposing President's Rule.

"The situation is still alarming. A large number of families have been uprooted and there is a dangerous design to grab land of the indigenous communities by illegal migrants. The state Government has completely failed to protect lives and property of the people and act against forces that are detrimental to the security of the country. This is a fit case for invoking Article 356," Joel Oram, senior BJP leader, said here.

Oram, who led a delegation of BJP leaders to the two riot-hit districts on Thursday, told a press conference that the BJP was also for an inquiry commission headed by a sitting Supreme Court judge. "The CBI cannot probe such a massive violence. Only a commission headed by a sitting Supreme Court judge can find out who is guilty," Oram said.

Oram also took strong exception to the state Government's attitude towards the incident of alleged hoisting of a Pakistani flag in one of the riot-hit villages. "Pakistani flags are being raised, and the Government is siting idle. While the Government wants to deny the flag episode, it is a fact that Darrang has a history of Pakistani flags being raised in the past," Oram said.

Referring to the plight of people living under 'inhuman' conditions in relief camps, the BJP leader also asked the state Government to take President Pratibha Patil to the riot-affected people. President Patil is arriving here on a five-day trip to Assam and Meghalaya on Sunday.

Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi, however, dismissed the BJP's allegations as baseless. "The situation has been improving and people are beginning to return to their villages. About 1.35 lakh people have already left the relief camps for their villages," Gogoi said here on Friday.

Gogoi also announced setting up of a cabinet committee to go into the issues in the two districts and take up steps to rehabilitate the affected people. He also accused the BJP of instigating the people to take up arms in Udalguri and Darrang.

Heading: Centre releases Rs 25,000 cr under farm loan waiver scheme - Indian Express
Content:
For the numerous batches of Super 30 that have passed out of the Ramanujam School of Mathematics and got into the prestigious IITs across the country, October 23 will be yet another tribute to the long hours of struggle and hard work they have put in.

A 60-minute film on these IIT aspirants will be screened at the South Asian Film Festival (SAFF) in New York on that day. The film called "Super 30" is directed by Christopher Mitchell and produced by Veronica Hall. The film shows how students struggle to make their way to the chosen batch of Super 30 and crack IIT-JEE tests. It also depicts "the real power of education to remake lives and communities". The British film director and his team spent several days shooting the film at Kumhrar. The film had been screened at the Los Angeles film festival in California this April.

When Super 30 mathematician Anand Kumar along with additional director general of police Abhyanand had started the batch six years ago, they did not even remotely fathom the kind of accolades they would receive or the kind of impact they would make.

"My students make it amidst odds. We provide them tiny rooms to stay for eight months. We keep the fire burning in them till they make it big. It is a befitting tribute to the rich mines of talents in Bihar," says Kumar.

Super 30 has sent 152 students from poor socio-economic background to IITs in the last six years. The group got a 100 per cent result this year. According to Anand, the film, more of a documentary, had no heroes. "The arduous journey of my students is the hero. It is about a maligned and impoverished state registering its big presence steadily," says Anand.

The fest starts from October 22 and will conclude on October 28.

Heading: Meghalaya launches ID cards to deter illegal migrants - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre has released the first installment of Rs 25,000 crore to states under the Rs 60,000-crore agricultural loan waiver scheme announced by Union Finance Minister P Chidambaram in annual General Budget for the year 2008-09 as a measure to tackle rural distress.

Of this, NABARD will get Rs 17,500 crore while commercial banks will receive Rs 7,500 crore. NABARD released maximum Rs 2,500 crore to Maharashtra, which is 25 per cent of the total release, Principal Secretary (Co-operatives) Sudhir Kumar Goel told The Indian Express.

"The maximum share to Maharashtra is due to the fact that the state has maximum number of beneficiaries — about 37 lakh," said Goel. "This will increase liquidity of banks for loan distribution for the forthcoming Rabi season," said Goel.

How much of the commercial bank share of Rs 2,500 crore will come to the state is not yet clear.

Banks — co-operative and commercial — distributed loans worth Rs 4,000 crore this Kharif season, which was lower than last year as many farmers, who had defaulted on repayment in anticipation of loan-waiver, had become ineligible for fresh loans. The state Government has been considering the case of regular repayers among such farmers for loan waiver and the Chief Minister has called a meeting on the issue on Monday.

Heading: Uma kicks off poll campaign, plans to contest all seats - Indian Express
Content:
With Assam's demography under threat from illegal Bangladeshi immigrants, Meghalaya is planning to introduce a three-tier citizen identity card to check the problem. Former Lok Sabha Speaker and NCP leader P A Sangma said the Meghalaya Progressive Alliance (MPA) coalition Government has earmarked Rs 5 crore for the said identity card.

Sangma said the ID card will be for (a) permanent Indian residents (b) Indian citizens who come to the state for work (c) non-Indians. He said the card has been already introduced in his constituency, Tura, by the municipal board. It will soon be introduced throughout the state.

Sangma said: "If a system to check illegal immigrants is not in place, we might face a problem similar to that being faced by Assam where illegal Bangladeshis have changed the demography of the state."

He said the purpose of the card was not to stop people who come from outside to work or visit the state, but to deter illegal immigrants from settling down and registering themselves as voters. Sangma said the process of issuing the ID card will be completed within three months.

Heading: Model code in force, no MLA photos on C’garh Govt websites - Indian Express
Content:
Bharatiya Janshakti leader Uma Bharati launched her campaign for the Assembly elections in Madhya Pradesh on Friday from the familiar territory of Ujjain's Mahakaleshwar temple, but in a setting very different from that in 2003, when she was BJP's chief ministerial candidate.

"Last three years have been so torturous and painful that I have forgotten I was ever with the BJP. There are no memories left," she told The Indian Express from Ujjain.

The sadhvi was expelled from the BJP in November 2005, after she stormed out of the party's legislature wing meeting that elected Shivraj Singh Chouhan as chief minister.

Now she is out to challenge the BJP, for her presence is only going to help the Congress. It's not the possibility of her winning any seats that is bothering the BJP but the chances of her eating into the party's votes and thereby making several seats vulnerable.

The Bharatiya Janshakti, the outfit she floated at Ujjain on April 30, 2006 is yet to open its account even on her home turf of Madhya Pradesh, though it fielded candidates in most of the by-elections.

But Bharati has announced her party will contest all the 230 seats now, inviting criticism that she is out to teach the BJP a lesson for her humiliating expulsion.

"I am not out to take revenge. Ours is a political party committed to the ideology of Ram and roti," she insisted. Asked about her chances, she said, "In the present situation it's difficult to answer that question because people are fed up with the BJP and Congress and are looking for an alternative."

The large turnout at her recent rally in Bhopal's Lal Parade ground was a reminder for the ruling party not to dismiss her ability to tilt the balance in several seats.

Once accused of communal politics, the sadhvi is trying to tread unfamiliar grounds. She blamed the recent communal riots in Burhanpur on the BJP and a local MLA of the Nationalist Congress Party. "The riots were pre-planned," she alleged, and feared that the ruling party and the Congress could cause violence again.

She visited the victims of Burhanpur violence on Thursday and demanded that the government give a compensation of Rs 5 lakh each to the kin of those killed. Seven Muslims and two Hindus, including one Bharatiya Janshakti activist, were among the nine persons killed in Burhanpur.

"My party wants to help the administration to maintain peace," she said while accusing the police and the administration of framing her supporters. "If Janshakti activists are booked I will be forced to take to the streets," she warned.

Heading: Himachal clears decks for CFL bulb scheme - Indian Express
Content:
Photographs of elected representatives have vanished from all government websites with model code of conduct coming into force for the two-phase Assembly elections scheduled for mid-November in Chhattisgarh.

"We have blocked access to photo gallery. Web links to details about various welfare schemes have also been removed following a direction from the election authorities," a Government spokesman said on Friday.

State Electoral Officer Alok Shukla had sent a letter to the Chief Secretary, asking him to take immediate steps to remove the photographs of all elected representatives from the websites of all government departments in the wake of model code of conduct coming into force.

Even as the Election Commission announced the schedule for Assembly elections, civic authorities swung into action and also removed hundreds of hoardings — that highlighted the achievements of the Raman Singh Government — from across the state. In the state capital here, municipal authorities removed a large number of hoardings erected by the opposition Congress.

Meanwhile, enforcement of the code of conduct has also resulted in scaling down of 'Rajyotsav' celebrations to mark the eighth anniversary of the formation of Chhattisgarh.

Heading: Bhatkal duped IM men on his financial status: cops - Indian Express
Content:
Decks have been cleared for the implementation of Himachal's innovative energy saving scheme — Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana. A Rs 80-crore scheme, it envisages distribution of CFL bulbs free of cost to 16.50 lakh domestic consumers.

Highly placed sources said Chief Secretary Asha Swaroop, who on Friday held a meeting with members of the Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB), gave her nod to purchase 72 lakh CFL bulbs from five manufacturing companies. Every domestic consumer will get a pack of four CFL bulbs.

The HPSEB, the implementing agency, has already finalised the technical bids deciding that CFL bulbs of 0.85 Power Factor (PF) will be supplied to the consumers.

The financial bids are slated to be opened on Saturday. The scheme is expected to take off by next week. All 16.50 lakh consumers will get the CFL bulbs by December 25, which also happens to be the birth anniversary of former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

The implementation of the scheme, says experts, will save nearly 72 MW of power everyday, beside making Himachal eligible to get carbon credits to the tune of Rs 100 crore per annum.

Heading: Bihar’s history project: 60 villages linked to Nalanda University identified - Indian Express
Content:
Indian Mujahideen kingpin Riyaz Bhatkal, now on the run, may have miscalculated when he misled his young terror recruits into believing that his insufficient means meant the group would have to use methods including kidnapping to raise funds for their operations.

"The others being interrogated were shocked when we told them the truth," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria. "We even took one of the arrested men all the way to Mangalore to show him the posh flat belonging to Bhatkal." Maria said the arrested Indian Mujahideen members were "cooperating" with the investigations.

During interrogation, it has emerged that the conspiracy to kidnap a jeweller and a builder from Pune was hatched by Bhatkal to raise terror funds. He had told the others that his means were meagre and that he even spent nights at local mosques.
