The tiff began after Dr Santosh found his patient was listed number two by the resident doctor in the operation theatre list for the day even as he had wanted him to be on the number one slot. Reportedly, the professor lost his cool and he abused the senior resident for making the change without telling him.

The three-member committee comprising Dean Prof V Sakhuja, Sub Dean Prof Amod Gupta and Prof Savita Malhotra of the Department of Psychiatry was appointed to inquire into the matter. Dr Santhosh was found guilty of using unparliamentary language in the heat of the moment and was asked to proceed on leave.

"We have examined the case closely. The consultant has admitted that he misbehaved in a fit of rage and has now tendered his unconditional apology in writing. He even went to Dr Sanand Kumar's hostel to aplogise, but the resident doctor was not there," said Prof Amod Gupta.

Heading: ‘Govt, industries misleading country’ - Indian Express
Content:
To spread awareness about environmental issues, Greenpeace India has set up a stall at the CII Fair being held at Parade Ground in Sector 17. The group is also enlisting volunteers to creating awareness about deforestation, industrial pollution and climate change.

The campaign also includes educating people about increasing the mileage of their cars and reducing carbon dioxide emission.

Divya, a volunteer said, "The mileage of Indian cars is between 12 and 15 kms per litre and the carbon dioxide emission is high. We had started a signature campaign in July and submitted these to the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Delhi. Our demand was that the car manufacturers in India be asked to inform about the mileage of their products. Increasing mileage will help in saving petrol."

The organisation also has a campaign to promote use of CFL bulbs. "This will be helpful in preventing global warming. Ninety-two per cent of energy in India is produced through thermal power plants. The aim should be to reduce the dependence to 50 per cent. Use of renewable sources of energy should be promoted," she said.

Heading: In road rage, man threatens another at gunpoint, arrested - Indian Express
Content:
In order to protest against the laying off of employees by IT, real estate, finance and aviation industry, the Chandigarh unit of Revolutionary Youth Association (RYA), Punjab, held a demonstration at Sector 17 on Saturday. The members of the RYA raised slogans and displayed posters against the policies of the government.

Kanwaljeet Singh, state convenor of the RYA, said the current recession would push the masses towards unemployment and starvation. "For every industrial crisis, the government and the industry hold workers and their unions responsible. They are misleading the country by dubbing the crisis as temporary and the result of mismanagement," he said.

He urged the youth to reject the policies of the government and come out of their comfort zone to build a strong revolutionary movement which can put forward an alternate model of development before the whole country.

Heading: BJP delegation meets Guv, demands probe into land given to mayor’s brother - Indian Express
Content:
In yet another case of road rage, a man driving an Innova car allegedly threatened a scooterist on gunpoint after a small accident in Dadumajra on Saturday.

Krishan Malhotra, a resident of Mullanpur village and a property dealer by profession, was later arrested under Sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act and Section 506 (criminal intimidation) of the IPC. The case has been registered at the Sector 39 police station.

The incident took place around 4.30 pm when the car (PB-65-E-4004) driven by Krishan hit a two-wheeler (PB-27-4569) near Dronacharya stadium in Daddumajra.

Rajinder Singh, a Daddumajra-based farmer, was driving the other vehicle while his sister-in-law was riding pillion. Both the drivers then confronted each other and a heated argument took place. Following this, Krishan reportedly took out his .32 bore pistol in a fit of anger and put it on the neck of Rajinder and threatened him with dire consequences.

A huge crowd gathered on the spot and the police was called following which the accused was arrested.

"Krishan had a licensed revolver but the licence was valid only in Punjab. It's a clear case of road rage and the accused has been put behind bars," a police officer said.

It's nothing new

Violent incidents of road rage are not uncommon in the city. While today's incident saw a pistol being used to threaten the other party, a youth had died following a road rage incident at the Sector 15 and 16 light point on September 20 this year. Nitin Bansal (21), a resident of Talwandi Sabo, was stabbed to death by Vishal Sharma on the fateful day when the two car drivers confronted each other over jumping a red light.

Heading: With Dutch inputs, Mohali club to take up solid waste management - Indian Express
Content:
A delegation of the Chandigarh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led by the president of the Chandigarh unit, Kamla Sharma, met UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (Retd) on Saturday.

They demanded a judicial inquiry in connection with the land, allegedly given by the Municipal Corporation (MC) to the brother of Mayor Pardeep Chhabra at cheap rates for holding an exhibition.

While pressing for the removal of the mayor from the post, the delegation also demanded that the money given to the mayor's brother be recovered.

BJP leaders alleged that the Congress-led MC has become a "den of corruption and nepotism". They accused the Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal of ensuring that no inquiries are held against the Congress leaders involved in criminal cases. He has pressurised officials of the Administration not to take action, said the delegation members.

The BJP leaders demanded strict action against the mayor after a judicial inquiry is conducted against him.

The delegation also included Gurcharan Dass Kalaa, Surinder Jagota, Mata Ram Dhiman, Kewal Krishan, Sanjay Tandon and former MP Satya Pal Jain. Home Secretary Ram Niwas and Deputy Commissioner R K Rao were also present during the meeting.

Heading: Midway into session, government schools still short of teachers - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to address the problems posed by the poorly managed system of garbage collection, management and disposal, the Rotary Club has taken up the project of solid waste management in Mohali.

Project chairman Dr B S Chandok said, "Experts from a Holland-based organisation — PUM — will help in solid waste management.

Theo Folmer, a solid waste management expert from PUM, is already here to help the Rotary Club improve the waste management system in Mohali."

"Instead of the top-down approach, bottom-up approach is necessary to achieve the results and hence proper collection of garbage from domestic, commercial, hospitals, nursing homes and industrial waste is of utmost importance," said Dr Chandok.

Dr Chandok announced that a massive drive for proper garbage collection will be launched from a residential belt in Phase V.

The drive will be taken up as a pilot project following the keen interest shown by the members of the Residents' Welfare Association.

Principal Secretary, local government, Punjab, D S Bains and Minister for Local Government Manoranjan Kalia have shown keen interest in preparing an extended system of collection, separation and disposal of household wastes. They assured of full government support to the initiative.

As per the arrangement, the municipal council will provide equipment and manpower while the Rotary Club will take action to improve awareness among local residents.

Folmer participated in an interaction programme with the Residents' Welfare Association, hospital managements, hotel and restaurant associations and village residents.

According to Folmer, the industrial units should be asked to ensure the cleanliness and hygiene of the roadsides adjoining their industries.

He also emphasised on the need to approach the youth in schools and colleges to stimulate their awareness.

He was shown the existing garbage collection and disposal system in the residential areas, local hospitals, institutions, eateries and restaurants besides one of the villages, Mataur.

Mataur, a densely populated village adjoining Sector 70, was taken up for launching the cleanliness drive in view of the filthy conditions prevailing there, added Dr Chandok.

Heading: ‘Inter-parental conflicts have plagued Indian courts’ - Indian Express
Content:
Even with nearly half the academic session over, government schools in the city continue to grapple with the shortage of staff. While the Education Department is still recruiting teachers, the numbers are not yet adequate.

Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 46, has three seats for teachers lying vacant in the Social Studies department while the number of vacant seats at Government Girls Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 8, is two in the same subject. The situation with Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 56, and Government High School, Hallomajra, is worse with no teacher available for Social Studies.

"The department is aware of the problem. We have given a number of representations to the department about the lack of teachers, but, nothing has been done so far. At times, teachers of other subjects take classes for Social Studies," says a principal, on the condition of anonymity.

In the language subjects, Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 33, has only one teacher for Punjabi against the prescribed slot of two. While there is no Hindi teacher in Government High School, Hallomajra, Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 16, faces the shortage of Punjabi teachers.

The rural schools are the worst affected. While four posts for Junior Basic Trained (JBT) teachers, against the sanctioned six, are lying vacant in Government Model Senior Secondary School, Karsan, Government High School, Mauli Colony and Colony Number 4 are short of ten and thirteen teachers, respectively, in the same subject.

All the posts of English lecturers are lying vacant in Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 23, Sector 33 and Government Senior Secondary School, Dhanas.

"The Department is biased towards schools that fall under the non-urban category. Since there are no teachers, our students are at the suffering end. It is high time we got adequate staff," says a teacher of Government Model Senior Secondary School, Karsan.

Talking to Newsline, Director Public Instructions (Schools) Samwartak Singh said the problem needs timely intervention. "We are aware of the schools that have inadequate staff members. The department will speed up the process of appointing teachers so that students do not suffer," said Singh.

Heading: Workshop held for eco club teachers - Indian Express
Content:
A seminar to discuss the inter-country child removal issue was held at the Army Institute of Law, Mohali, today. The seminar titled 'India, Intercountry Parental Child Removal and The Law' revolved around laws pertaining to the custody of children for the parents of inter-country.

The guest of honour on the occasion was Dr Justice A R Lakshmanan, Chairman, Law Commission of India. Also present on the occasion was Justice Tirath Singh Thakur, Chief Justice Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Renowned advocate Anil Malhotra while speaking about Hague Convention said that it provides an expeditious method to return a child taken from one member nation to another. The convention seeks "to protect children internationally from the harmful effects of their wrongful removal or retention and to establish procedures to ensure their prompt return to the state of their habitual residence, as well as to secure protection for the rights of access." He said that India is not a signatory body for the Hague Convention and thus has no laws to protect the rights of removed children.

Speaking on the occasion, Justice Tirath Singh Thakur said, "My only advice to the students is that they should never let go any chance to perform. Like life, profession too is a stage and one should believe in performing the best". He added that corruption will be dealt very strictly at his end.

Dr Justice A R Lakshmanan said, "To send back or not — to return or not to return is a dilemma which plagues the Indian courts in the matter of inter-parental child removal from the overseas. About 30 million non-resident Indians live in 130 countries. Their multiplying numbers have elevated the problem to a high degree in inter-parental conflicts which originate in foreign lands but descend on the Indian soil. There is no legislation available in the Indian statute books, which is geared to handle inter-country conflicts in matters of child removal."

Heading: Cultural fiesta at Pbi varsity - Indian Express
Content:
Being environment friendly is quickly becoming popular and catching up with the times. Idma Foundation for Sustainable Development, in collaboration with the Environment Department, Chandigarh Administration, organised a one-day workshop for eco club teachers from different private and government schools of Chandigarh. The workshop, which saw close to 80 attendees, was aimed at strengthening 'Green Purchase'. It was held at Botanical Garden, Sarangpur today.

The teachers were briefed on the 'Star Rating Programme' by Dr B K Arora, Centre Head, Planning & Coordination, Mahatma Gandhi State Institute of Public Administration, Punjab.

Dr Ashok Sharma, Chief Executive, Cleantech International Foundation, spoke on the concept of waste minimisation. Later, the participants were briefed on the importance of traditional lifestyles in a lecture by Dr. Mamata Saxena, Director, Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation. Dr Saxena spoke of her research on the role of Yagya in improving the environment both indoors and outdoors. Dr. Satish Narula from Punjab Agriculture University, Ludhiana briefed the participants on the benefits of gardening for a healthy life. In conclusion, Dr. R S Saini, Executive Director, Idma Foundation discussed the concept of 'green purchasing'. "Every time we open our wallets, we cast a vote: for or against the environment," said Dr Saini.

Idma Foundation in collaboration with the Environment Department also launched an exercise to know carbon footprints of the schools of Chandigarh.

Heading: In a first, traffic marshalls to be appointed in Panchkula - Indian Express
Content:
Over a month after their election, 15 councillors of the Kharar Municipal Council (MC) are waiting in vain to take oath and charge of their new office.

As the election for the coveted posts of president and vice-presidents of the civic body was being delayed, the ruling SAD-BJP combine, which had failed to wrest control over the MC even after claiming 10 of the total 15 seats, was buying time to get together its members.

On September 15, a special meeting called for the election of the president and vice-presidents besides administering oath of allegiance to the newly elected municipal councillors was postponed indefinitely, citing "illness" of the convener.

On the same day, seven municipal councillors, including three of the SAD-BJP combine, three Independents and a Congress councillor, along with Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu, who being an ex-officio member has the voting right, had come to attend the scheduled meeting but had to return after the postponement notice.

Kharar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Rajeev Kumar Gupta, who was appointed convener by Mohali Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari, said no fresh date was yet decided to call the MC meeting.

Though he claimed that lawfully, he can hold meeting till October 24, but the legal experts say the stipulated period of 14 days expired today.

"As per law, the first meeting of the newly elected municipal councillors was to be convened within 14 days of the publication of the notification but in this case, since the election of the MC chiefs were stayed on September 17 when the notification was published but the stay was vacated on October 3, from when the period of 14 days had started," defined a Municipal Act expert.

However, the SDM has another system of counting. "I was served convener appointment order on October 14 from when I will count 14 days," he said.

In the present situation, the municipal councillors, who were elected on September 14, were spending sleepless nights with money power, pulls, pressures and horse trading on its height to form majority group, which will capture the top posts.

While Kharar Congress MLA claimed of "splitting" the ruling SAD-BJP alliance group to form United Front comprising "splinted" councillors and Independents, Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh and Chamkaur Sahib Independent MLA, who had joined hands for SAD-BJP combine's clean sweep in the MC polls, were still confident that the ruling alliance will rule the new MC House despite all odds.

Heading: Woman killed, husband injured as tipper hits scooter - Indian Express
Content:
'Initially, we plan to keep traffic marshalls only as observers. We might increase their powers to issue challans, but that will be considered later'

After Chandigarh, the Panchkula police are all set to appoint traffic marshalls in the city. While in Chandigarh, the marshalls not only observe but also issue challans to traffic violators, those in Panchkula would only act as observers. This is for the first time that marshalls will be appointed in the city.

"The traffic marshalls will act as observers and watchdogs in the city. They would accompany the challaning teams and the checkpoints that would be installed in Panchkula," said Rajesh Kalia, DSP (Headquarters). He further added that the nomination for the same would be accepted by his office from October 22 onwards and all those interested can apply for it. "While there is no age limit to become a traffic marshalls , all those who have time throughout the day, would be most eligible. Initially, we plan to appoint around 15 to 30 traffic marshalls." He said the shortlisted candidates will be trained for the first three months before being given the charge.

Kalia said the decision was taken after Haryana DGP Ranjiv Dalal asked them to appoint traffic marshalls. "Initially, we plan to keep traffic marshals as only observers. However, we might increase their powers to issue challans, but that will be considered later," added Kalia.

Heading: UT Home Secy examines construction work in city - Indian Express

According to police, Palwinder told the police that he and his family had gone to Australia on September 29. On October 15, when they returned, the main entrance was broken and the house rummaged for valuables. He has reported loss of gold ornaments and Rs 25,000 cash from the broken almirah and other household articles.

Harnoop Kaur told the police on October 15 that she had gone to her sister's place in Sector 33-D, Chandigarh, at 7.40 am. When she returned at 3 pm, she found the locks of her house broken and the entire house searched extensively. The wife of a serving Colonel reported the loss of gold ornaments worth lakhs and Rs 2,000 cash.

It is believed that both the houses were targeted by the same group of robbers, who had struck when the houses were locked. The police have registered separate cases of theft and are investigating.

Heading: Broader view to put metro on right track - Indian Express
Content:
Praise from all and sundry marks the grand closing ceremony of CYG

Stars vied with fireworks to add glitter to the closing of the Commonwealth Youth Games, making it a night to remember for Puneites. Breathtaking daredevilry by stunt bikers, electrifying helicopter rides and synchronised movements by hundreds of schoolchildren made the event a spectacular one.

The Bollywood stars were there to add to the glamour quotient. Shilpa Shetty sizzled, Reitesh Deshmukh rocked, Diya Mirza dazzled and Malaika Arora Khan wooed the audience.

It ended with the customary goodbye to Jigrr and welcoming of elder brother Shera, the mascot of the Delhi 2010 Commonwealth Games, as Shiamak Davar gave a foot-tapping performance.

With the state clinching one-third of the medal tally, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, the presiding chief guest, announced a special felicitation programme for winners in Mumbai shortly for distributing the promised cheques of Rs 10 lakh, Rs 7 lakh and Rs 5 lakh to gold, silver and bronze winners respectively.

"It is a proud moment for us and for Pune," he said in his speech giving credit to the CYG Organising Committee chairman and Indian Olympic Association president Suresh Kalmadi.

He lauded the good infrastructure in the city and said Kalmadi had done well. He also mentioned the support of the Prime Minister and party chief Sonia Gandhi and thanked Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar, who was the chief guest, for his support.

With Kalmadi repeatedly stating that Pune has the infrastructure to host even the Olympics, Deshmukh said the Maharashtra government will do all it can to bring Olympics to the state.

Pawar, in his speech, also lauded Kalmadi over the "excellent infrastructure work in the city" and said even as CYG saw India leading from the front, the Mohali test too saw Sachin doing remarkably well, which was a true toast to the sporting spirit of the country. He added what China had done by winning the maximum medals in the Beijing Olympics, India had done at this grand event which saw the participation of 71 countries.

Kalmadi said that with the PM announcing Rs 700 crore for training purpose, the sports city at Balewadi will turn out to be the best in the world. "Just as cricket, these games have to be given equal importance and more funds," he said. He thanked the Centre for the Rs 3,000 crore released for the Games and thanked both the municipal corporation chiefs, divisional commissioner, collector, and mayors of both the corporations for the infrastructure work in the city. "The CYG has done magic for Pune infrastructure," he said bowing and thanking Puneites for all the support they rendered for the games.

Even as the crowd revelled in the Bollywood extravaganza that unfolded at the venue, amidst fireworks, the customary passing over the quaich (torch) was done by Suresh Kalmadi to M Quail, tourism minister of Isle of Man from Scotland which will host the next CYG in 2011.

President of the Commonwealth Games Federation, Michael Fennel declared the Games closed. Ministers, Patangrao Kadam, Harshvardhan Patil, Dilipwalse Patil and Vasant Purke were also present at the closing function.

A postage stamp to commemorate the CYG was also released by SC Jarodia, post master general, Pune division.

Heading: After the Games, war of wards - Indian Express
Content:
The proposed Metro Rail is a huge step forward for the people of Pune. To make sure the right step is taken, a move is on to end the longstanding debate on whether the standard gauge, as proposed by the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), or the broad gauge system should be adopted.

"Some experts say broad gauge should be adopted for Pune Metro. This has been debated for many years in Delhi after many NGOs and experts raised doubts. We need to resolve it once and for all, so that we can move ahead. I know E Sreedharan quite well. I am arranging a meeting between Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) and those advocating broad gauge like Vijay Rane, former managing director of Indian Railway Construction Company (IRCON), either in Delhi or Pune," said leader of opposition in the PMC, Vikas Matkari.

Over the past few months, railway and transport experts have been questioning the PMC's decision to go for standard gauge (SG) for the project. Broad gauge, they say, is more suited to India because of its greater passenger carrying capacity. In a series of letters to the city public planners and public representatives, they have argued that broad gauge offers more at a lower cost, is sustainable in the long run and technically more sound, against the standard gauge network.

"Broad gauge is a smarter option. It offers wider coaches and therefore can carry more passengers. BG can meet future traffic demand for 75-100 years, instead of a mere 25 years with SG's narrower coaches. As BG expertise is available in India, the coaches and technology need not be imported, which will push costs down," said Rane.

Backing broad gauge for Pune along with Rane are traffic experts P G Pathankar, P V Gole and the general secretary of the Professionals Party of India, D V R Rao.

"There are recommendation letters from the Indian Railways to the Ministry of Urban Development from 1997 to 2006 recommending broad gauge (BG) policy for metros. The entire Indian rail network runs on BG. The Kolkata metro, even the first phase of the Delhi metro project from Vikaspuri to Connaught Place is on BG. Pune will benefit from BG," said Rao.

PMC Commissioner Praveesinh Pardeshi said the civic body will stick to the standard gauge for Pune Metro Rail. "This is as recommended by the technical advisor, DMRC," he said. As per the uni-gauge policy, the Indian Railway has adopted broad gauge for its rail network. This was set aside for metro rail projects, which are now being designed on standard gauge.

Heading: FTII lens on CYG, with mission on mind - Indian Express
Content:
The CYG has drawn to a close, but a tussle has begun among corporators, the bone of contention being development of their wards on the lines of the Baner-Balewadi area. The Games have transformed the area, with roads and other infrastructure getting a big facelift.

Disgruntled corporators from other areas, especially the city periphery, are demanding similar development in their wards. They are meeting with civic officials and asking them to replicate the transformation in their own localities.

"Seeing the development in Baner, Balewadi and Pashan, they have started comparing it with their own wards. We built roads around the CYG venue in record time without compromising on quality. The development was restricted to Baner and Balewadi. Corporators want similar roads in their areas," said PMC city engineer Prashant Waghmare.

MNS corporator from Katraj, Vasant More, said if only events like CYG can ensure development, then every ward should host national and international events. "We have been fighting for development of our wards for long, but nothing much has happened. The residents of Katraj, or any other ward for that matter, pay taxes to PMC and yet are deprived of good roads, water connection and other basic facilities, unlike their counterparts in Baner-Balewadi now," he said.

The PMC doesn't have enough funds for development of its wards, but constructed roads in Mhalunge village, which does not fall within the PMC limit, he added.

Sagar Malkar, corporator from Vishrantwadi, said, "The infrastructure in my ward is bad. Our demand is roads, as good as those in Baner-Balewadi, in Vishrantwadi as early as possible."

PMC additional city engineer (roads), Vivek Kharwadkar, who headed the team that built the Pashan-Sus Road confirmed that many corporators had called up PMC officials and demanded similar development in their wards. "The development in Baner-Balewadi areas, particularly the Pashan-Sus Road, has increased the onus on us," he said.

Heading: Modify research strategy to help farmers: Pawar - Indian Express
Content:
Film documents sports shift, explores possibilities

Amid TV crews and photographers covering the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG), two cameras were panning the stadium. But the mission was different.

Collin D'Cunha and Gita Raju behind these cameras were making a documentary. The work of the two final year students of the film editing course at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), aims at tracking India's performance after the Beijing Olympics.

But the idea was born much earlier than the Beijing show. "A couple of years ago, we met Purnima Pendse, the director of culture and ceremonies at CYG who later introduced us to Suresh Kalmadi (chairman, CYG Organising Committee). Discussions for CYG were on then. We presented a proposal to Kalmadi, which was approved, much to our surprise. Thus began the project," said D'Cunha.

As part of the project, the duo travelled to Beijing to document the performance of Indian sportspersons. "Our work on CYG started when we went to Delhi to cover the youth baton relay. That's where we recorded some views table tennis player Neha Agarwal put forth," added Raju.

The documentary is expected to be ready by February 2009. It captures the sports movement in India in the recent times and the shift being seen from cricket to other games. "We are trying to keep a record of these times, when athletes and players from games other than cricket are becoming icons. When we were at Beijing, Abhinav Bindra and Saina Nehwal were like any other participants, but after their win, they became celebrities. In fact, getting an interview with Bindra was one of the most difficult tasks we had while making the film," said D'Cunha.

The documentary also focuses on how India can aim to be a host for the 2020 Olympics. "We are trying to find loopholes in the organising of the CYG, so that the Commonwealth Games in Delhi can be held flawlessly. A similar method can be applied while aiming for the 2020 Olympics," said D'Cunha.

Emphasising that the documentary is not taking any sides, the duo said they plan to document the downfall of hockey too. "We will interview Indian hockey officials for their view," said D'Cunha.

Heading: Water supply to be disrupted - Indian Express
Content:
Union agriculture minister Sharad Pawar on Saturday stressed on the need to change the strategy of research in agriculture to help the farmers to get more produce. "Researches should make farmers capable of facing challenges of changing times," he said.

Pawar was speaking at a function to celebrate the start of silver jubilee year of Maharashtra Agricultural Education and Research Council (MAERC).

Pawar said the food security issue should be addressed properly and this could be achieved by research. "Global warming and change in climate have affected the agricultural production. Researchers in the area of agriculture should come up with the best seeds that will help increase the production," he said.

He also said that the growth rate in agriculture sector had dropped gradually in last few years and had come down to 1.5 per cent. "With the efforts of the present government, the country was able to achieve 4.5 per cent growth rate recently. But still there are a few things to be done in the sector," he said.

He added that the world has shifted its focus to food security after shortage of food and increase in the food prices.

"The agriculture colleges and universities also should take into account this changing focus and concentrate on farmer-oriented research," he said.

State finance minister Jayant Patil said that the state had allocated Rs 10 crore for bringing the lands of agriculture colleges under irrigation that would boost the research process.

State electricity minister Dilip Walse- Patil, who was also present at the event, promised to increase the power supply to 10 hours a day for electric water pumps used by farmers.

State agriculture minister Balasaheb Thorat, Ramraje Naik Nimbalkar, mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale, principal secretary of state agriculture department Nanasaheb Patil, agriculture commissioner Prabhakar Deshmukh and Vijay Kolte, vice president of MAERC were also present on the occasion.

Heading: Three hundred years of faith - Indian Express
Content:
Rebirth pangs
Movie name: Karzz
Directed by: Satish Kaushik
Cast: Himesh Reshammiya, Urmila Matondkar
Showing At: City Pride Kothrud City Pride Satara Road E-Square, Fame Akurdi, Gold Adlabs, INOX Pune, Mangala
When Subhash Ghai's Karz came out in 1980, there were mutterings about how it had ripped off cheesy Hollywood drama The Reincarnation of Peter Proud. But they soon subsided not only because Ghai cleverly admitted to copying, having out-cheesed the original effortlessly. It was also because Karzwas a cracker of an entertainer: as the born-again hero, Rishi rocked, there's never been a crueler, classier vamp than Simi Garewal, and if ever there is a compilation of classic movie themes, the haunting Ek Hasina Thiis sure to top the list.
This Karzzz, despite the extra zees for luck, is a blot. Except for the names of the characters, which are exactly the same, nothing else is: the treatment is sloppy, even by Satish Kaushik's standards, and the acting is plain execrable.
For those who've come in 28 years after the fact, this is how it goes. Pop star Monty ( Himesh) starts having visions--of a man and a woman, a huge mansion in the hills, a kali ka mandir, and an airplane going up in flames. It's a case of punarjanam, a psychiatrist declares sagely. And whoosh, we are launched into a series of flashbacks, unraveling how Monty is actually rich businessman Ravi Varma ( Dino) re-incarnated, and has come into the world to wreak revenge on the murderous, greedy-for-his-millions-wife Kamini ( Urmila).
Himesh adds a hair transplant and a smile to his extremely-limited repertoire ( in his last year's debut Aap Ka Suroor, he had appeared throughout in his till-then trademark baseball cap, and scowl). A badly-made up Urmila dons skin-tight gowns, large tracts of her chest gleaming with bronzer, gold trousers, and scarlet lipstick. She also sounds distressingly like Archana Puran Singh when she simpers: hard to think that she was once an A-list actress. There's also a new girl, Shweta (director Indra Kumar's daughter) getting a brief look-see: all she has to do is to gaze adoringly at Himesh. That must have been tough.
Even the climactic song-cum-whodunit denouement, which has been lifted completely, is mangled. In between, you can hear Rohini Hattangadi, who plays the dukhiyari maautter lines like these: mere kaleje ke tukda, she goes, mere laal.
Moral: if you can't make, don't re-make.

War against terrorism, again
Movie Name: Body of Lies
Directed by: Ridley Scott
Cast: Leonardo Di Caprio, Russell Crowe
Showing At: E-Square, Gold Adlabs, INOX Pune
Ridley Scott's Body of Lies raises a potentially disturbing question. If terrorism has become boring, does that mean the terrorists have won? Or, conversely, is the grinding tedium of this film good news for our side, evidence of the awesome might of Western popular culture, which can turn even the most bloodthirsty real-world villains into fodder for busy, contrived and lifeless action thrillers?
The second answer seems more plausible, but there are other puzzles in Body of Lies that are not so easily solved and that may distract from sober contemplation of geopolitical pseudo realities like Leonardo DiCaprio's accent or Russell Crowe's body mass index. DiCaprio, as CIA operative Roger Ferris, once again shows his commitment to full employment for dialect coaches, following Blood Diamond and The Departed, with some good-old-boy inflections that are helpfully identified by Crowe's character as originating in North Carolina.
Crowe, meanwhile, plays Ferris's supervisor, Ed Hoffman, who has no specified regional background to explain his odd drawl. At times Crowe, showing the linguistic chameleonism -- the birthright of every Australian actor -- spits out his words with an emphatic twanginess that suggests, if not George W Bush himself, then perhaps Jon Stewart impersonating Bush. It's possible that this resemblance is meant to imply their immunity to self-doubt and allergy to second thoughts about the righteousness of their actions.
Hoffman is fighting a war whose terms he lays out in a few set-piece speeches. The gist is that no one is innocent and that the ends justify the means. Deceit, torture, the sacrifice of non-American lives — all is permissible in the fight against a superjihadist Al-Saleem (Alon Aboutboul), carrying out suicide attacks around Europe. The contradictions and unintended consequences of Hoffman's tactics are borne by Ferris, who finds his credibility undermined, his friends and his life in danger.
All of which would be fine if Body of Lies — based on a novel by David Ignatius — was clearer about its themes or its plot. As it is, the movie is a hodgepodge of borrowings and half-cooked ideas, flung together into a feverishly edited jet-setting exercise in purposeless intensity.

Shoot down
Movie Name: Shoot On Sight
Director: Jagmohan Mundhra
Cast: Naseerudin Shah, Om Puri, Gulshan
Showing At: City Pride, Satara Road, Fame
JAG Mundhra's films have topical, relevant subjects. That's the good part. The bad part is that they do not possess a single subtle note: everything is heavily underscored, leaving no place for understatement or nuance.
And that's something one misses sorely, especially in a film like his latest. Shoot On Sightis based on the London bombings in 2005, which unleashed a whole spate of racial profiling. Is it a crime to be Muslim? Are all Muslims terrorists? These questions, asked by sundry characters in Shoot On Sightyield answers which, for all their truth, seem like they are stating the obvious.
It's not as if Naseer, as Commander Ali of Scotland Yard, doesn't know the pitfalls of playing a Muslim cop in a still-White country. In his scenes with `gori' wife (Greta Scacchi), defiant daughter, couple of openly racist colleagues, and sympathetic boss (Brian), he shows as much deftness as the script allows. But that's not much at all: Ali's childhood friend from Lahore, now a `mullah' advocating jehad (Om) is all surface--he strokes his beard, recites from the Koran, and colours impressionable minds.
More predictabilities abound. Rebellious Muslim teenager facing off dad--he won't let her date white boys who want to go all the way. Jolly meat-shop owner doling out `gosht' and good cheer. Good white wife trying to balance the tensions in her family, and his. We've seen all this before, with much more depth: there's more to multi-culturalism, and the problems of being brown, post 9/11, than these very broad, too familiar brush-strokes. The Hindi dub flattens the film even more; catch the English version, if you have to.

Heading: Melting Pots - Indian Express
Content:
Pune gurudwaras begin their grand celebrations for the 300th anniversary of Gurta Gaddi from today, as a precursor to the main event that will take place at Nanded later this month

Three hundred years ago, Guru Granth Sahib, the holy book of the Sikhs, which contains invaluable teachings (vani) of six gurus, among other words of wisdom, was accorded the status of the eternal guide of the Sikhs by Guru Gobind Singh. Three hundred years on, the Sikh community is reliving that cherished moment and commemorating the consecration by celebrating tercentenary of Gurta Gaddi, with great pomp and show. "This tercentenary celebration of the consecration asserts more significance as during the centenary celebrations India was under the Mughals, the 200th anniversary commenced when Indians were fighting the British rule but the tercentenary will be celebrated by free India," informs Bhola Singh Arora, one of the members of Prabandhak committee.

Takhat Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Saheb, Nanded, is the site where the main celebrations will start from October 27 and continue till November 3. October 30 marks the day of consecration and November 3 was the day when Guru Nanak left for his parlok gaman. Back home the Gurudwara Shri Guru Singh Sabha, Ganesh Peth is also organising pre-event celebrations. The celebrations in Pune will take place from October 19 to October 25. Myriad arrangements are being made to mark this seven-day spiritual extravaganza. Gracing the city streets on the opening day will be the nagar kirtan, a procession of the devotees, that will start from Gurudwara Shri Guru Singh Sabha, Nana Peth and will culminate at Gurudwara Gurunanak Darbar, Camp. "This procession will be aimed at spreading the message of peace and brotherhood. Around 15 to 20 thousand devotees are expected to join the procession," says Gurudev Singh Rajpal, a member of the Prabandhak committee. Several archgates and stages have been constructed in various parts of the city to welcome this procession. The procession will be attended by former State director general of police and chairman, teen sau saala committee Nanded P S Pasricha, Pune district's guardian minister Ajit Pawar and mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale. Many communities have also come forward to welcome the procession at various places. During these seven days, the committee plans to conduct a seminar on universal welfare and brotherhood in reference to the teachings of Guru Granth Sahib and elaborate kirtans for which renowned kirtankars from Delhi, Amritsar and Chandigarh will be there. "We have set up almost 100 invitation boards across the city. All communities are invited to celebrate the occasion with us" says Bhola Singh.

Serving the community remains an important activity. During the seven days, blood donation camps will be set up in the premises of the gurudwara at Ganesh Peth and all those who will be donating blood will be given a nominal insurance cover free of cost. The funds collected as donations from devotees will be used for funding cataract operations of around 300 needy patients. Also an amount of Rs 2000 each will be spent on 25 children selected by the various gurudwara committees in the city, for funding their school fees.

As a part of this elaborate affair, the teen sau saala committee has been distributing decorative candles, a key chain and a gold plated coin to families on a first-come-first serve basis. There is also a special effort by the committee to prevent the sale of intoxicants during these seven days. "We have ensured that at the gurudwara road at Ganesh Peth, no intoxicants are sold during these seven days and keeping in mind the spiritual importance of this event we earnestly request all the Puneties to ensure the same all over the city," adds Arora.

Heading: BPO employee found dead in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
'Karzzz,' Satish Kaushik's much-hyped remake of the 1980s smash hit film 'Karz' had its international premiere at the Middle East International Film Festival (MEIFF) at Abu Dhabi which has also seen the screening of two films with an Indian connection.

Karzzz", starring singer Himesh Reshammiya as the lead actor, narrates the tale of a rock star's revenge with Cape Town as its backdrop. The movie also stars Urmila Matondkar, debutante Shweta Kumar, Gulshan Grover, Raj Babbar and Danny Denzongpa.

"It is a privilege to have 'Karzzz' selected as the only Hindi film to be premiered at the Abu Dhabi Film festival," said producer Bhushan Kumar after the screening on October 16.

Toronto-born Richie Mehta's 'Amal,' an unabashedly lovely film about a poor auto rickshaw driver from New Delhi, was screened twice at the festival.

'Amal' presents the daily life in New Delhi and shows the rewards for human compassion. Replete with characters including a dying street urchin, an eccentric millionaire, a good-hearted auto-rickshawwallah and a lovelorn shopkeeper, it has something to offer for everyone.

With Naseeruddin Shah, Roshan Seth, Seema Biswas and Koel Purie as the cast, the film has won over 15 international awards, and has been named as one of the Canada's Top Ten films by the Toronto International Film Festival.

Another movie with an Indian connection Sir Richard Attenborough's magnum opus 'Gandhi' was screened in the "Special Presentation" section of the festival. The film, dubbed into Arabic, had its first local premiere at an international film festival.

As the principle organiser of MEIFF 2008, one of our intrinsic values is the celebration of culture," said Mohamed Khalaf Al Mazrouei, Vice Chairman of MEIFF.

Heading: Raj Thackeray a mental case, ban MNS: Lalu - Indian Express
Content:
A 28-year-old BPO employee was found dead in a church guest house in Noida, police said.

The body of Conrad Dominc Xavier, who was living in the guest house in Sector 27 for over a year, was found on the floor of his room in a pool of blood by a church employee who informed the police, they said.

Police are interrogating a cook who lives on the second floor of the guest house.

Senior Superintendent of police R K Chaturvedi said the area had cordoned off and forensic experts were on the site looking for clues.

Heading: EC announces 7-phase assembly polls in J&K - Indian Express
Content:
Condemning the attack on railway board examination centres in suburban Mumbai by MNS activists, Railway Minister Lalu Prasad demanded a ban on the outfit, saying its chief Raj Thackeray was a 'mental case'.

"I strongly condemn the incident. There should be an inquiry into the attack. There should be strong action against that party...MNS should be banned," the Minister told reporters.

His comments came as a response to the attack on 13 railway board examination centres in suburban Mumbai by MNS activists who protested "inadequate representation" to locals and chased away candidates from north India.

Prasad said the directions of the Supreme Court or any other courts did not have any impact on the MNS leader. "We can see such incidents when the elections are near," he said.

The Minister said he had spoken to Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh who assured him of a proper inquiry into the incident.

Heading: Two killed as Delhi Metro Rail bridge collapses - Indian Express
Content:
Resolving differences within, the Election Commission announced a seven-phased election in Jammu and Kashmir beginning November 17 till December 24, saying it has taken a 'risk' on the issue of participation of political parties in the exercise.

Announcing the poll schedule, Chief Election Commissioner N Gopalaswami said that the snow-bound Leh and Kargil regions would go polls in the initial two phases.

Against the backdrop of parties and outfits in the Kashmir Valley expressing themselves against polls at this juncture, the CEC said the Commission has taken a 'risk'.

This was in apparent reference to political parties in Kashmir like the PDP which said no to polls and another mainstream party, National Conference (NC) which gave its nod after having voiced initial reservation.

On the issue of lack of consensus among the political parties, he said "first you need to ask if political parties are ready. We are not conducting election in a vacuum. To start with there were one no, one yes and one yes-no. After that one no became one yes. So we have two yes and we have taken a risk".

To another question whether there was a difference of opinion among the three Commission members on holding polls to the assembly with 87 seats, the CEC said "various issues need to be considered. So each one presents his views which he considers the best. There are three Election Commissioners and at least there may be three opinions".

Heading: Metro bridge collapse: DMRC opens helpline - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were killed and 16 others injured when a portion of an underconstruction bridge of the Delhi Metro collapsed and fell on passing vehicles, including a bus, in Delhi.

Of the 16 people injured, a man has lost a leg while both the legs of another had to be amputated following the accident which took place on Vikas Marg in east Delhi's Lakshmi Nagar locality at about 7:05 am when workers were lifting a 400-tonne span of the bridge.

The launcher developed some mechanical fault leading to the collapse of the 34-metre-long span which fell on a blueline bus, crushing the driver Surender Kumar to death, a senior police officer said.

Chotte Lal (25), a labourer of the AFCONS company, which is undertaking the construction works, was also killed in the mishap, Delhi Metro spokesperson Anuj Dayal said.

Delhi Police spokesperson Rajan Bhagat said 16 people were injured in the mishap.

Two trailers, which are being used for launching the span, and two cars were also damaged in the accident which blocked the two-way traffic on Vikas Marg.

"It is a big shock to us. We are taking it seriously and we have decided for an independent high-level inquiry by three eminent people into the incident," he told reporters.

According to Dayal, seven injured were rushed to Lok Nayak Jai Prakash hospital while two others are being treated at the Hedgewar hospital at Karkadooma.

"I was sleeping and woke up hearing a huge sound. I thought it was an earthquake and rushed outside only to see the bus under the debris," said Anand Kumar, who lives near the accident site.

Heading: Bangalore: Three of family found murdered at home - Indian Express
Content:
A public helpline was set-up to provide necessary information related to the collapse of an under-construction bridge of the Delhi Metro in the national capital.

The helpline -- 011-22191736 -- has been operationalised in the DMRC control centre in Shashtri Park.

"The helpline will give the people all information about the condition of the injured, the restoration of traffic on the road at the accident site and other matters," Director (Operations), DMRC, Raj Kumar told reporters.

Heading: Rehearsals for Moon mission successful, Countdown from Monday - Indian Express
Content:
A woman and her two children were found murdered at their home in Bangalore.

Anu Yadav (40),the wife of a retired navyman, and children, aged 10 and eight years, were found murdered this morning, police said.

Their bodies were found by B S Yadav at his Singapur layout house when he returned from the Railway station after booking tickets for the family to visit Punjab during first week of next month.

Yadav, who left the house for the railway station at about 0730 hrs returned by 1030 and found that his wife had been done to death in a room and his two children in an adjoining one.

The police engaged sniffer dogs to gather clues.

Some valuables are missing according to a statement made by Yadav to the police.

Heading: German rape case: Victim likely to give statement soon - Indian Express
Content:
India's maiden unmanned moon mission's launch rehearsals at Sriharikota progressed satisfactorily and scientists geared up for the 52-hour countdown for Chandrayaan-1's historic space voyage on Wednesday.

"All the preparatory work is going on as usual and the formal countdown would begin tomorrow morning about 0400 hrs," Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) Associate Director Dr M Y S Prasad told PTI at Chennai. Sriharikota is about 100 km from Chennai.

"All the work including the checking of payloads went satisfactorily. The spacecraft launch would take place as per the schedule," he said.

The integrated launch vehicle has already been moved into the second launch pad (umbilical tower) at the spaceport of Sriharikota and launch rehearsals are underway, sources in India Space Research Organisation at Bangalore said.

SDSC officials said if the weather does not play truant, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle(PSLV-C11) would take off from the second launch pad on October 22 at 0620 hrs.

"After the rehearsals, we will make sure that everything is in place before the countdown," they said.

Chandrayaan-1 is the first spacecraft mission of ISRO beyond Earth orbit. It would be followed by Chandrayaan-2 which features a lander and a rover. India and Russia would jointly participate in this project. However, there might be a provision to accommodate payloads from other space agencies like in Chandrayaan-1.

"This apart, studies are being conducted by ISRO on sending unmanned spacecraft to planet Mars as well as to asteroids and comets. Through such programmes, ISRO intends to undertake the exploration of space besides its primary mission of developing and utilising space technology for the overall development of the country", ISRO officials said.

Heading: 'FDI inflows to feel pinch of financial turmoil' - Indian Express
Content:
The German girl, who was allegedly raped by the son of Goa Education Minister Atanasio Monseratte, will give her statement in the rape case soon, the lawyer representing her mother has said.

"The statement will come soon. She is being psychologically counselled," Aires Rodrigues, lawyer of the German mother, who has alleged that her minor daughter was raped by Monserratte's son, Rohit, said.

The police have deferred Rohit's arrest awaiting formal statement from the girl or medical examination, which is not forthcoming despite several attempts.

Fearing that the case may hit a dead end, Superintendent of Police (North) Bosco George held meeting with Rodrigues, German mother and NGO which is on the job to counsel girl for statement.

"The girl is worried that she may have to face repercussion, if she gives statement against Rohit. She is being reassured about that," the lawyer said.

Police have booked a case against Rohit for raping, outraging modesty, abatement of crime and sending lewd messages to the victim.

Rohit's father, the minister, has also been charged of abatement of crime as the mobile connection used by the accused is in his name.

George, on Saturday, had said that they will arrest the accused only after they get the formal statement from the girl.

Heading: Debits cards in India to touch 169 mn - Indian Express
Content:
India will feel the heat of the global financial turmoil, Commerce and Industry Minister Kamal Nath has said.

"Of course, we will see the impact (of global financial crunch) on our FDI inflows in the next six months," Nath said at a function of chartered accountants here.

It was only last week that the minister had expressed his optimism, and said India would exceed its target of USD 35 billion FDI this fiscal.

FDI inflows of USD 14.6 billion in first five months of 2008-09 showed an impressive growth of 124 per cent over the same period last year.

Nath cited example of how the mood reversed in the stock market since January, 2008. "We saw boom in our Sensex in January, when it was over 20,000 and today there is a gloom," he said, adding, "there is not enough money to pour out".

The BSE benchmark Sensex has dipped by over 50 per cent from a high of 21,000 in January to below 10,000 on October 17.

With the foreign institutional investors (FIIs) pulling out over USD 11 billion from the beginning of this calendar year the rupee has come under intense pressure and lost over 20 per cent since April this fiscal.

Nath said FIIs have been pulling out of India in the last several weeks. While this did not reflects India's fundamentals, it "shows the inter-connection."

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, in Srinagar on October 10, had also expressed his concern over the Indian currency coming under pressure.

Heading: Banks to wait till RBI policy to decide on rates - Indian Express
Content:
Driven by technological changes and growing internet access among consumers, the volume of payment cards in the country is projected to touch 210 million in the next two years, with debit cards accounting for more than half of the total.

The debit cards in circulation is expected to touch 169 million by 2010, consultancy firm Celent said in a report.

However, Celent said in terms of transaction value, credit cards would emerge on top as people would use the same for purchases and bill payments.

Currently, the country has about 130 million payment cards including debit and credit, in circulation.

"... the number of cards in circulation will hit 210 million by 2010. Of these, 169 million will come from debit cards, and about 40 million will come from credit cards," Celent pointed.

The report titled 'Payments in India Going the e-Way' noted that credit cards would overtake debit cards by value of transactions, because customers would continue to use credit cards for purchases and bill payments.

As of now, the Indian card market consists 27.5 million credit cards worth 14.5 billion dollars.

A majority of credit card purchases come from shopping, jewellery, dining and traveling, which contribute nearly 70 per cent of credit card payments. Fiscal year 2008 saw as much as 288 million transactions being processed through card payments.

According to Celent, technology changes, growing internet access and mobile subscriber base, rising consumer confidence, and convenient delivery payment models are the prime factors for the growth in e-payments.

Heading: Surf web to boost brain power - Indian Express
Content:
Mahesh Bhupathi and his Bahamian partner Mark Knowles sailed into the finals of ATP Madrid Masters with a straight-set win over Swede-Zimbabwean pair of Jonas Bjorkman and Kevin Ullyett here.

The fourth seeded Indo-Bahamian pair beat their fifth seeded rivals 6-2 6-4 in little over an hour's time to enter the finals.

Bhupahti and Knowles will take on seventh seeds Marcin Matkoswki and Mariusz Fyrstenberg of Poland.

Matkoswki and Fyrstenberg saved three match points en route to their 6-7(4) 7-6(5) 12-10 win over South African eighth seeds Jeff Coetzee and Wesley Moodie.

Bhupathi and Knowles are chasing their third ATP title of the season after triumphing at Memphis and Dubai.

The 34-year-old Bhupathi captured the Madrid title in 2003 and finished runner-up in 2002, both times with Max Mirnyi, while the Knowles captured the title three times with Daniel Nestor in 2002, 2004 and 2005.

Heading: Growth slowdown a concern: Economists - Indian Express
Content:
If you think that reading is the only way to stimulate your mind, think again, for a new study has suggested that surfing the Internet boosts the brain more than going through a book.

Researchers at California University have found that browsing the web triggers centres in the brain that control decision-making and complex reasoning, particularly in older and middle-aged adults.

In fact, the study, which looked at brain activity during web searches, resulted in a fascinating finding: Middle -aged to older people who know their way around the Internet had more stimulation of decision-making and complex reasoning areas of the brain than peers who were new to web surfing.

What's more is that reading didn't stimulate the same number of brain areas as Internet searching.

The first of its kind to access the impact of Internet searching of brain performance, the study is to appear in an upcoming issue of 'American Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry', according to the University.

"The study results are encouraging, that emerging computerised technologies may have physiological effects and potential benefits for middle-aged and older adults.

"Internet searching engages complicated brain activity, which may help exercise and improve brain function," said lead researcher Dr Gary Small of the University's Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behaviour.

He added: "A simple, everyday task like searching the web appears to enhance brain circuity in older adults, demonstrating that our brains are sensitive and can continue to learn as we grow older."

Heading: Orient Longman reborn as Orient Blackswan - Indian Express
Content:
Economists feel a repo rate cut by the Reserve Bank next week would complement its recent liquidity-boosting measures and go a long way in spurring economic growth, which of late, has been sluggish.

A bold decision to cut the repo rate by 0.50 per cent would send positive signals to the economy and perk-up the tempo of growth, both this fiscal and in the next (FY 10), they said.

However, whether the new RBI Governor, D Subbarao, would take such a bold step during the half-yearly monetary policy review this week or wait for a few weeks more remains a 'toss up', they said.

With the economists pegging India's GDP growth between 7 to 7.5 per cent for FY 09, they feel that if growth-boosting measures are not taken in the near-term, then it would affect the country's growth in the next fiscal (FY 10).

"The RBI has addressed inflation which is now declining. It has also addressed the liquidity problem. Now, I think it is time to address growth which is showing signs of slipping," Enam Securities' Chief Economist, Sachidanand Shukla, said.

While inflation still continues to be in double-digits, it has declined to 11.44 per cent after hovering dangerously close to 13 per cent a couple of months ago.

"Growth and not inflation is emerging as a bigger concern. If you want a healthy growth in FY 10, a repo rate cut is definitely needed now," Shukla added.

Heading: 200 illegal Indian immigrants held in Belgium - Indian Express
Content:
Orient Longman Pvt Ltd, after separating from its long associations with the Longman and subsequently the Pearson Group, has recently launched its new brand identity - Orient Blackswan Pvt Ltd.

Orient Longman brand was introduced in India in 1948 by Longman Inc of UK. In 1968, Pearson Education group of the UK took over the Longman name globally. However, in India, Longman continued to function as Orient Longman.

In 2006, Pearson filed a suit against Orient Longman to assert its right to the Longman brand and afterwards reclaimed the rights to the Longman brand in India in an out-of-court settlement. Under the terms of the settlement, Pearson returned 33 pc equity in Indian publishing company free of cost, while Orient Longman agreed to stop using the Longman brand by November 2008.

On the occasion of the launch, the Hyderabad-based publishing house also launched a new series of books meant for pre-primary to Class 8 students. The series named 'Buzzword' Communicative English for Schools consists of 26 books. The books will be part of the school curriculum in CBSE as well as private schools. The 'Buzzword' series has been written with an aim to impart skills of communication by giving pupils choice of grammar and vocabulary to converse fluently and accurately.

Orient Blackswan, through their associations with Universities Press, offers readers professional books in biotechnology, computer science, engineering, home science, management and medicine. They also distribute books published by Sangam Books, Permanent Black, D C Publishers, Spark India, and Social Science Press.

Heading: Second Test: Australia all out for 268 - Indian Express
Content:
About 200 Indian illegal immigrants on their way to the UK were rounded up by Belgian police as they smashed a human trafficking ring arresting 15 people in pre-dawn raids around Brussels.

Claiming that they have broken up the 'core' of the racket, prosecutors said some of the Indians had paid up to 15,500 pounds to be taken to Britain.

"This morning we executed a series of search warrants to intercept all the suspects. This operation proved this is happening on a large scale, because we found more than 200 illegal Indians," Tim De Wolf, an assistant prosecutor dealing with the case, was quoted as saying by the media.

The raids in 'safe houses' in and around Brussels were conducted after a year-long police investigation. Some 50 Indians were discovered hiding in a gurdwara in a suburb of Vilvorde, media reports said.

Police have arrested 15 suspects allegedly involved in people-smuggling. The ring was capable of smuggling thousands of people into the UK every year, de Wolf said.

"We think we found and identified 15 of the organisers of this smuggling of human beings," he said.

According to the BBC, the would-be migrants were mainly Indian men aged between 15 and 35, as well as some women and children.

Most of the migrants were from Punjab, de Wolf said. They were being kept in miserable conditions while waiting to be taken on the final leg of their journey.

"We found 24 people crammed inside one windowless room, measuring around 12 sq metres," he said.

Two of those arrested were "the brains behind the trafficking operations in Belgium. They controlled a whole series of little groups, sometimes working together, sometimes competing against each other. We hope that we have broken up the core of the network," de Wolf said.

Heading: Bhuapthi-Knowles in Madrid Masters' final - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana leggie Amit Mishra celebrated his Test debut with a five-for as India spared Australia the humiliation of following on only to tighten the noose around their neck on day three of the second cricket match.

Mishra emerged as the wrecker-in-chief as India shot out Australia for 268, carving out a 201-run first innings lead.

Despite having the Aussies at his mercy, stand-in skipper Mahendra Singh Dhoni refused to enforce follow-on, deciding instead to set them a target and unleash the two-pronged spin attack on a wearing track.

India added exactly 100 runs without any loss in the final session to stretch their overall lead to 301 and openers Virender Sehwag (53) and Gautam Gambhir (46) will return on Monday to further swell the tally and take the match away from Australia.

With no real sting or firepower in the Australian attack, Sehwag and Gambhir gave India a rollicking start in the second innings, finding boundaries with consummate ease and running hard between the wickets as well.

Sehwag was both fluent and fierce while Gambhir matched his Delhi captain's aggression shot for shot. The right-left combination never allowed the Australian pacers to settle into any rhythm and they scored at a four-plus run rate.

Meanwhile, Mishra's sensational debut is sure to create dilemma for the selectors, who would have to find a way to accommodate Anil Kumble in the side for the third Test after the regular skipper recovers from his shoulder injury.

Heading: ‘Relieved to show that I belong’ - Indian Express
Content:
If you think that reading is the only way to stimulate your mind, think again, for a new study has suggested that surfing the Internet boosts the brain more than going through a book.

Researchers at California University have found that browsing the web triggers centres in the brain that control decision-making and complex reasoning, particularly in older and middle-aged adults.

In fact, the study, which looked at brain activity during web searches, resulted in a fascinating finding: Middle -aged to older people who know their way around the Internet had more stimulation of decision-making and complex reasoning areas of the brain than peers who were new to web surfing.

What's more is that reading didn't stimulate the same number of brain areas as Internet searching.

The first of its kind to access the impact of Internet searching of brain performance, the study is to appear in an upcoming issue of 'American Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry', according to the University.

"The study results are encouraging, that emerging computerised technologies may have physiological effects and potential benefits for middle-aged and older adults.

"Internet searching engages complicated brain activity, which may help exercise and improve brain function," said lead researcher Dr Gary Small of the University's Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behaviour.

He added: "A simple, everyday task like searching the web appears to enhance brain circuity in older adults, demonstrating that our brains are sensitive and can continue to learn as we grow older."

Heading: Double whammy - Indian Express
Content:
As Sourav Ganguly walked into the Press Conference Hall at the PCA Stadium after the day's play, Ganguly was relieved and blushing at the same time.

"Relieved because I wanted to show that I belonged," Ganguly said, "This century was very satisfying for me. This knock will be one of the most memorable ones, as getting a century against Australia is always very satisfying. I still have some more innings left and I will try to get more runs and finish it off on a happy note."

If Friday gave him an entry to the 7000-Test runs Club, Saturday got better. Ganguly was determined and had his sights set on a century. "This knock came in tough conditions and against quality bowlers. After an ordinary outing in Sri Lanka, I just wanted to score runs. And I'm happy I got a few runs in Bangalore and a century here."

Ganguly didn't answer in the positive when asked if his century was an answer to his critics, saying, "I don't have to prove anything to anyone. I'm just happy to score runs. Taking retirement from cricket was a personal decision. When I announced my retirement I believed that the time to go had come. There is no point reconsidering the decision."

Heading: In lead, Anand plays safe to draw another - Indian Express
Content:
France's Gilles Simon knocked world number one Rafael Nadal out of the Madrid Masters on Saturday after a thrilling 3-6, 7-5, 7-6 (6) tussle to set up a final clash against Britain's Andy Murray, who had earlier outgunned Roger Federer 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 to avenge his defeat at the US Open.

Simon took almost 3-1/2 hours, saving 17 break points along the way, to record his first victory in three meetings against the Spaniard.

Although Nadal won the first set comfortably, the French world number 16 refused get overawed by the Mallorcan's brutish groundstrokes. The two slugged it out in one high-class rally after another and the Frenchman eventually prevailed to level the contest. Nadal broke in the final set but Simon immediately broke back and took the Spaniard's serve again to serve for the match. Incredibly Nadal hit back to win that game. But the French Open and Wimbledon champion was outfoxed in the deciding tiebreak. Simon clinched a place in the final on his second match point after Nadal's forehand was confirmed long by Hawkeye.

Murray showed flashes of form early on but Federer gave the 21-year-old no time to settle, forcing him into unforced errors to break midway through the first set.

Murray grew in confidence, however, and by the third set, the match had swung in his favour. Murray slammed 14 aces, 10 in the final set, but it was testament to Federer's fearless style that the Swiss saved six break points before finally cracking at 5-5 when he struck a forehand long. The Scot brought up match point with a huge cross-court forehand and sealed his third victory over Federer when his opponent netted a forehand. (Reuters)

Bhupathi-Knowles in semis

Bhupathi and Mark Knowles defeated Simon Aspelin and Julian Knowle 6-3, 7-5 to storm into the doubles semi-finals. The fourth seeded Indo-Bahamian pair took one hour and 15 minutes to beat the sixth seeded Swede-Austrian duo. They next face the fifth seeded pair of Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden and Kevin Ullyett of Zimbabwe, who beat top seeds Mike and Bob Byran 6-4, 6-4 in their quarter-final match. Meanwhile, in the quarter-finals of the $50,000 Calabasas Challenger event in California, USA, Prakash Amritraj put up a brave fight before going out to top seed Vincent Spadea 3-6, 6-3, 6-7 (4).

Heading: India tops tally, beats expectations as CYG end - Indian Express
Content:
Viswanathan Anand played out an easy draw with Vladimir Kramnik of Russia in the fourth game of the World Championship here on Saturday.

Playing with white, Anand began safely and it was a near-chanceless draw that kept the Indian's one-point lead intact. With eight more games to be played, the scoreline reads 2.5-1.5 in the Indian's favour.

Anand opened with the Queen pawn and Kramnik went with the same move order that he had employed in the second game, but Anand deviated on the third move. By transposition, Kramnik went for the Queen's gambit declined, making his peaceful intentions clear and Anand too was content with only a miniscule advantage often insufficient for a win.

By the 15th move itself, as many as three pieces and a couple of pawns changed hands, leaving the position completely dry compared to the wild complexities of the third game.

Anand was forced to exchange the 'weak' black pawn and soon after a couple of rooks were off the board. It did not take long for either player to decide the outcome of the match. The peace was signed after 29 moves, making it the shortest game of the match thus far.

Heading: Sourav’s sweet sixteenth - Indian Express
Content:
The world better get used to watching India punch well above its lightweight reputation. For, if the show put up at the Pune Commonwealth Youth Games is any indication, the hosts may climb high on medals ladder in Delhi 2010.

When the curtains came down on this rehearsal in Pune, India had topped the table with 76 medals — 33 of them gold. And IOA president Suresh Kalmadi, who already has a penchant for hyperboles, was so buoyed by the spectacle of the closing ceremony and the general cheer as fireworks lit up the sky that he said he'd pitch for Pune for the 2020 Olympic bid.

That's still some time away. For now, the spectators at the closing ceremony here seemed quite content to tap their feet as Diya Mirza, Mallaika Arora, Neha Dhupia and Shilpa Shetty did their jig items. Earlier, the Scots assembled here entered with a bagpiper and later, much noise was made while a Rs 5 stamp of the 2010 mascot 'Sheraa' was released. Swimmer Virdhawal Khade, the flag-bearer, can grin wider, after he'd collected Rs 51 lakh for three golds, three silvers, announced by the Maharashtra government for its state medallists — 10 lakh for gold, 7 lakh for silver, 5 for bronze.

The ceremony left a few relieved volunteers, many happy winners, zealously over-hyped reputations, and some anxious representatives from Isle of Man who'll find Pune a tough and pocket-pinching act to follow. Still, in the shortest and most precise speech of the evening, the little dot on the map promised a 2010 Games that would ensure comfort for the athletes, not just lavish ceremonies.

After an unprecedented week which saw Pune's citizens paying and queuing up to watch India's next generation of sporting heroes, the third edition of the CYG had set a standard, besides serving as a trailer to what promises to be a blockbuster in 2010.

Heading: Consecutive triple ton for Pujara - Indian Express
Content:
It's not one single fairytale, his career. It's pretty much a series of short, snappy stories and each of them seems to end with the prince sporting a big, rather cheeky, grin. Sourav Ganguly might say, repeatedly, that he doesn't need to prove anything to anyone anymore, but it's hard to believe that he finds no joy in watching people eat their words.

On Saturday, he took his tally of Test centuries to a respectable 16 ensuring, along with stand-in skipper Mahendra Singh Dhoni, that India reached a healthy 469 in their first innings. With the runs on the board, the bowlers took over, leaving Australia at 102 for four at stumps on Day Two. The hosts are comfortably ahead on points and looking good for a knockout in this second Test.

Dhoni in the zone

Ganguly was on 55 when play started on Saturday, with the spotlight firmly on him. Through the course of a day that India dominated from start to finish, at least two other players tried to squeeze into his story. Dhoni walked in and took charge of proceedings, and for the next couple of hours Ganguly slipped seamlessly into the background.

First ball from Brett Lee, short and fast, was pulled away to deep square-leg for four. Next over, Peter Siddle sent one towards the rib cage; this time, he got more meat into the shot, and even before he finished swiveling, the ball had cleared the boundary rope. The captain meant business. He charged down the track to Shane Watson and condescendingly slapped Cameron White around. He was the last man out for a breezy 92, to a horrendous leg-before decision from Rudi Koertzen, who had given Ganguly a reprieve on Friday when he didn't call for the third umpire on a stumping appeal. All in all, he's making a fair case in favour of the referral system.

Mishra turns up

Later in the evening, after Zaheer Khan had dismissed Matthew Hayden for the third time in as many innings and Ishant got Ponting for the fourth time in five Tests, Amit Mishra started work on what could turn out to be one of those dream debuts.

In his third over, he got one to turn just enough to squeeze in between Simon Katich's bat and pad. And in the final over of the day, bowling round the wicket, he had Michael Clarke in four or five minds with a well-flighted googly that caught the clueless Aussie bang in front.

Both might have been stars on another day, on Saturday they would've been mighty pleased with honourable mentions.

Steady knock

There were no obvious heroics in Ganguly's batting on Saturday. There were singles on offer and he picked them up without too much fuss. He did get bogged down occasionally, but never lost his cool.

His best shot was the one that took him from 96 to 100 — White tossed one up on leg-stump, marginally over-pitched, and he gently nudged it off his pads. Even as he turned for his second, the ball hopped over the ropes at square-leg. The celebration wasn't elaborate (he didn't even take off his helmet): a pump of the fists and, predictably, a smile wider than an eight-lane highway.

When Ganguly was dropped from the team in 2006, he had played 88 Tests, scored 5221 runs with 12 hundreds and 25 fifties at an average of 40.78. Since his comeback, he's scored 1842 with four centuries and nine 50s at 47.23.

Those runs have taken him past Gundappa Vishwanath, Mohammad Azharuddin and Dilip Vengsarkar. In India, only Sunil Gavaskar, Rahul Dravid and Sachin Tendulkar have scored more. Another 48 will take him past old friend and foe Greg Chappell, and you can bet he'll have a silent chuckle when he crosses that bridge. In the three innings since he announced his retirement, he's scored 173 runs at 86.50.

Really, who's writing the script?

Just over two years ago, during his forced exile from Indian cricket, he sat in an empty stand, smiled into a camera and uttered an innocently mischievous bhoole toh nahin? for a television commercial. Right now, he's just making sure he'll be remembered for a while to come, cheeky grin and all.

Heading: Still a land of starving millions - Indian Express
Content:
Saurashtra captain Cheteshwar Pujara slammmed 309 against Mumbai in the under-22 CK Nayadu Trophy, his record second successive triple ton which came just five days after his 386 against Maharashtra. Pujara's achievement also impressed, among others, chairman of the national selection committee Krishnamachari Srikkanth.

"At any level, scoring 300 runs is a huge task, it's a remarkable achievement," Srikkanth told the The Indian Express from Mohali. "We saw him during the 'A' matches and were all very impressed with his temperament."

World T20 in 2010

Mohali: The ICC has decided to have the third T20 World Championship in 2010 at the expense of the Champions Trophy. The T20 Cup will be played in the West Indies, according to the ICC Chief Executive Haroon Lorgat. "The ICC had a choice between holding Champions Trophy or a T20 event, so in the end the T20 seemed to be a better bet," Lorgat said. He also added that the ICC was yet to hear from the BCCI over the Indian Cricket League's status. Lorgat said that ICC will wait for an official report from the BCCI before considering an application from the ICL to become an official competition.

Hasan scalps six

Chittagong: Bangladesh left-arm spinner Shakib Al Hasan took six for 31, leaving New Zealand at 155-9 at the end of second day's play here. Earlier Daniel Vettori scalped five wickets for 59 runs to shoot Bangladesh out for 245 in the first innings. At close, Vettori was unbeaten on 48 with the Kiwis trailing by 90 runs.

Brief scores: Bangladesh (1st inngs) 245 alll out in 122.1 overs (M Hossain 83, M Rahim 79, D Vettori 5/59, O'Brien 3/36) vs New Zealand (1st inngs) 155 for 9 in 60.3 overs (D Vettori 48 n.o; S Hasan 6/31)

Narrow win for Lions
