Heading: Mumbai United win - Indian Express
Content:
Swim sensations Virdhawal Khade and Shikha Tandon will feature in the All-India Inter-University Aquatic Championship, organised by the University of Mumbai and HR College and co-sponsored by Reliance Industries, that will be held at the Andheri Sports Complex from October 21 to 24.

Beijing Olympian Khade, of Kolhapur University, won three gold in the Commonwealth Youth Games in Pune, including the men's 50m butterfly and records in the 100m and 50m freestyle an is expected to bag a rich haul in the competition. In addition, Khade also won the 200m and 4x100 freestyle silver.

The formidable Shikha Tandon of Bangalore University looks all set to make waves after entering 12 events including the 50m, 200m and 800m freestyle, 100m and 200m breaststroke, 50m, 100m and 200m butterfly, 50m and 200m backstroke and the 200m and 400m individual medley.

Pranoy Adhikari and Vivek Shanbag are strong contenders from hosts Mumbai University.

Adhikari, who has been training overseas, is one of the favourites in the 100m, 200m, 400m and 1500m freestyle, while Shanbag is expected to come up with a strong challenge in the freestyle events.

Mumbai University's Mollan Fenello has maintained a low profile for a long time but will get an opportunity to make waves in her pet 50m, 100m and 200m breaststroke for women.

The diving competition will be held at the Goregaon Sports Club and there will be strong competition in the high board diving for women where Devina Devi (LNIPR, Gwalior), Neha Naik, Pooja Patil and Rupali Shinde (Pune University) and Rashika Sriram and Rupali Sigi of Solapur University make a formidable line-up.

Last year's winners University of Kerala will set out to defend the men's waterpolo title, with fancied Calicut University and Punjab University (Patiala) and 2007 runners-up SGBU (Amravati) also in the fray.

Heading: Aviation slump: Here's how Railways cashed in - Indian Express
Content:
India's economic growth may decelerate to 7.5 per cent in 2008/09, as the country experienced 'ripple effects' of the global financial crisis and liquidity crunch, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh said on Monday.

"The financial crisis is likely to have an indirect impact on the Indian economy," he said in a statement to lawmakers in Parliament. "We must be prepared for a temporary slowdown in the Indian economy."

"RBI and the government are carefully monitoring flow of credit and will ensure additional liquidity results in actual credit," the PM said.

The Prime Minister assured that all the deposits in Indian banks are safe there should be no fear of failure of Indian banks like the American counterparts.

Singh said the recent steps taken by the government and central bank would help ease a liquidity shortage.

Inflation was also expected to moderate further in the next two months, he added.

INFLATION WOULD FALL FURTHER

With the price situation showing signs of improvement, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Monday said the inflation rate would fall further in the next two months.

"We expect a further reduction in Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in the next two months," he said while making a statement in the Lok Sabha.

The inflation rate, measured by movement in the WPI, has for the third successive week remained below 12 per cent and came down to 11.44 per cent for the week ending October 4, from 11.80 per cent a week ago.

"WPI has declined in the last three weeks, and although the current rate is still high, the movement in the level of prices shows a clear deceleration in the current momentum of inflation," he said.

Welcoming the steps taken by the RBI to infuse liquidity and reduce short-term lending (repo) rate, Singh said, "It is broadly consistent with our objective to control inflation which has already begun to moderate."

RBI on Monday reduced the repo rate by 100 basis points allowing banks to borrow funds from the central bank against government securities at an interest rate of 8 per cent against 9 per cent earlier.

The central bank had earlier reduced mandatory deposit that banks maintain with the RBI by 250 basis points unlocking Rs 1,00,000 crore of the banking funds.

Heading: Himachal confidential - Indian Express
Content:
What many suspected is now clearer than ever: some segments of air passengers have contributed to Rly's improved performance this year

In 2003, when Captain Gopinath started Air Deccan as the "common man's" airline, he would hardly have anticipated what the latter part of the decade had in store for the industry he was pioneering: Multiple factors leading a booming aviation industry to buckle. And simultaneously, the Indian Railways have been quick to grab the opportunity. Statistics now affirm what has long been suspected: A significant rise in railway revenues compared to last year, for the same period that saw airline load factors declining drastically.

A comparative analysis for April-August 2007 and 2008 show a dip in air passenger traffic and a concurrent rise in railway passenger traffic, most keenly observed in the number of Second AC and Third AC. Airline officials admit the tilt too — barring the corporate traveller who will prefer to not travel at all, a large number of fliers is now back in the trains.

Airline industry figures show a dip of four per cent in passengers travelling between April and August this year when compared to last year's figures. The Indian Railways saw a whopping rise of 21 per cent in its sales of passenger tickets for two and three-tier air-conditioned compartments in the same period.

According to the figures obtained from the Railways, (see box), an additional 1.67 crore passengers have travelled between April and August 2008 as compared to the same period last year. On revenue, the railways have recorded a growth of 13 per cent in the period.

Three-tier AC has recorded 35 lakh passengers more compared to last year — the same segment of people targeted by low-cost airlines. This segment also recorded a revenue of Rs 1,283 crore in this period, nearly Rs 300 crore more than the corresponding period last year.

"It's simple logic," said a senior industry analyst. "A certain section will choose rail travel compared to air travel, like a family going on a holiday. It makes more sense due to many factors like the all round inflationary pressure. More trains have been launched. Therefore their numbers are bound to go up," he said.

Jeetendra Bhargava, Executive Director of NACIL, said that the drop in airlines' figures and the subsequent rise in railways' passenger figure have nothing in common. "The drop and the rise do not correspond and are therefore exclusive of each other. People travel by air because of the time factor. To see the trend you need to wait for October and November's figures when people take their leave travel allowances and travel on fixed budgets," said Bhargava. "Anyway, it's a global scenario," he added, pointing out IATA's announcement of a 5 pc slump in global air travel.

Marzban Antia, MD of Mumbai-based Avesta Travel Ltd, agrees. "We'll have to wait till February to see if the trend continues," he said.

Still, a shift in passengers who used to earlier prefer low-cost airlines is only to be expected, say others. "Air fares have increased due to fuel price hike. It's an immediate reason," said Rakesh Tandon, executive director (passenger marketing) of the Railway Board.

Fares for long distance trains has seen a cut, that also contributed to improved performance for the Railways, along with simpler e-ticketing procedures.

Heading: Ahluwalia back in hospital - Indian Express
Content:
'Fevi'Kaul Singh

Despite being out of power, the Congress is in a jubilant mood after it won over senior BJP leader Narender Thakur in CM Dhumal's home district. Last week, Karan Singh, a former BJP minister, also joined the party. Moreover, Vijai Singh Mankotia, BSP's state convenor, has also resigned from politics. The developments have brought a new name for party chief Kaul Singh Thakur, who is now being called 'Fevi-Kaul Singh', a 'reliable bonding agent'.

Unexpected support

After IAS officer Subhash Ahluwalia's arrest, he has found his allies retreating into the background. Even the Congress is on a backfoot and totally mum over the issue. However, at a time when friends and colleagues are afraid of meeting him, he got support from a human rights' body. After his discharge from IGMC, when his family was demanding medical aid, Arvind Thakur of Global Human Rights Council knocked on his door and heard the family patiently. The outcome is still awaited.

Raj yog after 14 yrs

A senior bureaucrat, Sarojini Thakur, has returned to her home cadre after 14 years. She was on a foreign assignment and now will take charge of the state's environment plans, a field that has got a national award to CM P.K. Dhumal. Her fellow bureaucrats feel that the portfolio of environment has come to her as "raj yog" after 14 years. It's a different story that her husband Ashok Thakur, an additional secretary in the HRD ministry, left the state for Central deputation only three months back.

What an idea!

After a meeting on climate change, CM P.K. Dhumal, in his address, narrated an old story and said, "I wish everyone who is here had just one ear so that the good ideas heard through one ear were not lost through the other." The story also was a subtle message for all senior officers who were indirectly given a signal about the seriousness of the big boss in seeing the idea bear fruit.

The 'secret'

Prof Ravindra Nath, a noted climate change expert, while making a presentation at a workshop on the subject, counted Himachal's advantages for becoming the first carbon-neutral state. In his excitement, Prof Nath declared, "Please keep it a secret so other states don't come to know about it!" One wonders if it's possible!

Heading: Govt floats securities to raise 200-cr loan for development - Indian Express
Content:
Complained of chest pain after discharge from IGMCH; no interrogation

IAS officer Subhash Ahluwalia has once again been admitted to hospital and continues to be under intensive care. On early Sunday morning, while the Vigilance Bureau cops accompanied him out of IGMC Hospital to take him for interrogation, he complained of severe pain in the chest, after which he was immediately admitted to Indus Hospital, a private institution.

On the previous night, his discharge was approved after detailed examination by the medical board at IGMC Hospital, where he was admitted since October 9 after he was remanded in police custody.

Ever since he was booked, Ahluwalia had reported to the Vigilance Bureau that he was not keeping a record of his health due to which he had missed the preliminary interrogation twice. Now, with Ahluwalia being admitted to ICU of the private hospital, his ill health has become a cause of concern for the investigating agency. The decision of IGMC Hospital to discharge him was protested tooth and nail by his family, who said that he was suffering from diabetes and hypertension.

Ahluwalia's police remand ends on Monday. Though the Vigilance once again failed to interrogate him, in wake of the fresh development, it is not yet clear whether the Vigilance would ask for more remand as no official was ready to comment.

In the past three days, the government has also been put to embarrassment and Ahluwalia's close relatives are wondering over the source of orders being followed by the hospital.

A relative who spoke to The Indian Express on Saturday wondered as to why the government has turned "inhuman". "Though we were aware of the fact that some problems might crop up after registration of the FIR, the manner in which the government has handled his case has posed a threat to his life," he rued.

Heading: Defeat of no-confidence motion dashes BJP hopes - Indian Express
Content:
The Himachal Pradesh government has decided to raise a Rs 200-crore loan by sale of government securities in the open market through Reserve Bank of India. The government stocks and securities would be floated for a period of 10 years beginning from October 23 and the bidding is scheduled for October 22 at the RBI's Mumbai office.

As per the government notification, the object of the loan has been enlisted as raising money for investment in development projects of the state, for which permission from the Central government has already been sought.

There is already a debt burden of Rs 2,400 crore on the state, which has increased further in the past six months. The burden on the government exchequer has also increased beyond this as a result of government's liberal announcements on sops in the social sector within this financial year.

Principal Secretary, Finance, Arvind Mehta confirmed the move. "The Government of India has notified a ceiling of Rs 1,400 crore, which the state government can raise as loan through such securities. At present, we are raising Rs 200 crore." When asked about the perceived impact of the prevailing liquidity scenario in the market, he said, "We do not expect any impact of it on our loan raising and we are hopeful of raising the full amount easily." The loan will be repaid at par on October 23, 2018.

It is mentioned that apart from the existing financial burden of the state, the new items added to it were announcement of hike in daily wages from Rs 75 to Rs 100 and 10 per cent hike in social security pension at the onset of the current financial year. Interim relief of 5 per cent has been announced twice within the same year for the state government employees. Another burden on the state continues to be Rs 130 crore for giving subsidised ration to all card holders.

Banking institutions are being seen as the major investors in Himachal government's stocks (security) as the investment will be reckoned as an eligible investment in government securities by banks for the purpose of statutory liquidity ratio.

Heading: Guru Granth Sahib a mirror of Indian culture: Hooda - Indian Express
Content:
In a dramatic turn of events, frontline leaders of Nalagarh and Doon assembly segments suffered a severe jolt with the defeat of the no-confidence motion moved against the chairperson of Nalagarh development block committee on Saturday. However, the vice-chairman was removed, sparing them some embarrassment.

All 40 members cast their votes but declaration of two votes as invalid dashed the hopes of the BJP to the ground. In the voting conducted by DPO M S Negi, in his capacity as the returning officer, the chairperson secured 19 votes in her favour and 19 against her, resulting in a tie. As per the Panchayati Raj Act, both officials cannot removed under such circumstances.

However, 22 of the 40 members voted against vice- chairman Sant Ram, following which he was unseated. The election for the post of vice-chairman would be held within a week.

The no confidence motion against chairperson Soma Devi and vice-chairman Sant Ram was moved by 28 of the 40 members committee on October 8. In the 40-member house, the strength of the Congress members is 19 and the BJP has 21 members.

Hectic lobbying was on to unseat the two and BJP MLA from Nalagarh, H N Singh, and Doon MLA Vinod Chandel reportedly went all out in a bid to install persons from their own party in place of the present chairperson and vice-chairman, who are aligned with the Congress.

Heading: Fate of 14,000 guest teachers hangs in balance - Indian Express

The 62nd annual religious congregation of the All India Baba Banda Bahadur Sikh Community was held in Hisar today, attended by CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda, where the CM described Guru Granth Sahib as the mirror of Indian spiritualism and culture.

Hooda said that there was complete peace and communal amity in the state and it had to be maintained. He urged the people to give a "befitting reply" to evil forces trying to disturb peace in the country. Paying rich tributes to Baba Banda Bahadur, he urged people to take a pledge to maintain mutual understanding and communal amity. Referring to the demands put up by Sant Singh Revri on behalf of the Baba Banda Bahadur Sikh Community, he said these would be considered. Hooda was presented with a siropa by Jitenderpal Singh Sodhi as a mark of respect. Shawls were also presented to MP Jai Parkash and MLA Amir Chand.

Heading: DHBVN spends Rs 370 cr on Gurgaon - Indian Express
Content:
In the "Year of Education" in Haryana, the state government could find itself on a sticky wicket again if it does not find any solution to the demand of regularisation of thousands of guest teachers in government schools in the state soon.

Haryana Education Minister Mange Ram Gupta, heading the committee to look into the demands of the guest teachers, has now called a meeting with their representatives on October 24. The last meeting earlier this month was postponed by the government. Talking to The Indian Express, Mange Ram Gupta said the government was looking sympathetically into their demands and would take an appropriate decision.

"The committee would meticulously and sympathetically examine and consider their demands and would also hold meetings with their representatives to find a solution to their problems,'' said Gupta.

However, sources in the education department say it would not be possible to adjust and absorb all the guest teachers as the government was also going to appoint around 10,000 regular teachers for government schools in the state.

For more than a year and a half now, the guest teachers of the government schools, numbering around 14,000, have been demanding that their services be regularised. The teachers have been holding agitations from time to time. The last such massive protest was held in Rohtak, the home town of Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, on September 7. The police had to resort to firing on the teachers to stop them from breaking the police barrier. Unfortunately, one of the woman guest teachers died in the police firing.

The government then set up a committee under Education Minister Mange Ram Gupta to look into their demands. The Chief Minister also ordered to initiate the process of withdrawing the cases registered against the guest teachers.

President of Haryana Guest Teachers' Association Arun Malik hoped that their demands would be met by the Haryana government.

Meanwhile, the guest lecturers have also put forth their demands to the Education Minister. They have demanded a hike in their wages. "We are paid Rs 100 per period and have a cap of Rs 10,000 on our monthly earnings, while guest teachers are paid Rs 105 per period and there is no limit on their monthly earnings," the guest lecturers stated in their memorandum to the Education Minister recently.

Led by Kuldeep Singh, the guest lecturers also regretted the fact that they were not allowed casual or any other leave. Mange Ram Gupta said he would look into their demands as well. "We are committed to promoting education in the state, for which the Hooda government has taken a number of initiatives. These measures will certainly bear rich dividends in the years to come,'' said Gupta.

Heading: Congress leader switches loyalties, joins INLD - Indian Express
Content:
The Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) and the Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam (HVPN) have completed development works worth Rs 370 crore since March, 2005 for augmenting power infrastructure in Gurgaon district. A spokesman of the DHBVN said that the HVPN had commissioned six new sub-stations and augmented the capacity of 12 existing sub-stations, increasing the transformation capacity of the transmission system by 540 MVA in the district during this period. The new sub-stations include a 220 KV sub-station at Daulatabad, a 132 KV sub-station at Dahina and four sub-stations of 66 KV-level at sector 28, 38 and 9 in Gurgaon and Harsaru.

The nigam also erected new distribution lines measuring 1,500 kilometres and augmented capacity of 550 kilometre-long lines by replacing the old conductor, he said.

Heading: CBI files fresh case against state IAS officer - Indian Express
Content:
The Congress received a jolt today when Sajjan Singh Dhull, its nominee from Pai constituency in the last assembly polls, joined the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD).

While announcing his decision to join INLD at a public rally organised at Pai village of Kaithal district on Sunday, Dhull said INLD president Om Parkash Chautala was the only one who could give a right direction to the state. Addressing the rally, Chautala launched a scathing attack on the Congress accusing it of failing to control terrorism and inflation.

Chautala said the INLD had joined NDA to completely rout Congress party as it was the only alternative to the UPA alliance. He declared that if voted to power, he would increase old age, widow and disability pension to Rs 700 per month.

He also reiterated his commitment for the enhancement of government acquisition land rates to Rs 1 crore in NCR areas and Rs 50 lakh in non-NCR areas.

Heading: 227 cases settled at lok adalats - Indian Express
Content:
Sanjiv Kumar, a suspended IAS officer who exposed the alleged teachers' recruitment scam in Haryana, has another problem after the CBI registered a fresh case against him for textbook printing irregularities, which, the agency said, caused a loss of Rs 5.25 crore. The CBI filed the case against Kumar, a 1985-batch IAS officer, in connection with alleged irregularities in tendering procedures for text books for Haryana Prathmik Shiksha Pariyojna Parishad (HPSPP).

The irregularities allegedly caused a loss of Rs 5.25 crore to the exchequer by giving out the tender of printing and supply of text books for primary classes to only such firms which paid bribe, the CBI said in its chargesheet.

The CBI alleged that Kumar, during his posting as State Project Director of HPSPP, entered into a criminal conspiracy with the printing firms. The CBI also claimed that the tender was given to ineligible firms and alleged that Kumar had received bribe from these printers.

Earlier, Kumar had moved the Supreme Court and projected himself as a whistle-blower by claiming that former CM Om Prakash Chautala and others had manipulated the list of recruitment of over 3,000 junior basic teachers, prompting the Apex court to order a CBI probe. Kumar was allegedly not found overboard and was included in the chargesheet in the appointment scam on June 6 this year.

Heading: ‘Execution petitions’ on the rise as defaulters fail to pay damages - Indian Express
Content:
874 vehicles stolen in the past nine months. Of which 210 automobiles could be traced

Next time, when you park your vehicle, be mindful of the elements on the prowl, eager to zoom away with your vehicle. Vehicle thefts are on the rise in the city, be it two or four wheelers. On an average, more than four vehicles are being stolen from the various parts of the city every day.

Failing to curb the theft and poor vehicle-recovery rate depicts the pitiable state of the police in dealing with such a crime.

In last nine months, 874 vehicles have been stolen, which includes 349 four-wheelers, 18 three- wheelers and 507 two-wheelers. Of these, the police have managed to trace only 210 vehicles.

The thieves strike at their will and are making mockery of the police system. A police officer admitted that around 30 per cent of vehicles are stolen during the day time.

"The police appear to be ineffective in controlling the menace. The thieves are not scared of the men in khaki because there is no proper policing," Gautam Sharma of Sector 23, said.

"In northern part of the city, people have palatial houses and sufficient parking space. But in the southern sectors, due to paucity of space, residents park their vehicles outside their houses. Sectors such as 32, 33, 40, 41, 43, 44, 45, 46 and 47 are on the hitlist of the auto-lifters because thieves can easily cross over to Mohali within four to five minutes," a police officer said.

With the number of vehicles in the city increasing manifold, there are not just more vehicles to steal, but more places to steal from. The auto lifters, who once operated in market places and crowded parking lots, have shifted their focus to residential areas.

Sources said these thieves now work in tandem to dispose of stolen vehicles much faster. This means that chances of your stolen vehicle being recovered are just a little more than 80 per cent. "It's rarely a one-man crime any more. Over the past few years, the police have busted several inter-state gangs, who manage to sell stolen vehicles into other states without any valid documents," SSP S S Srivastava said.

He further suggested that registration numbers and the owner's name should be etched on different parts of the vehicle to identify it in case of any theft. "Many people park their vehicles without locking them properly. This should be avoided," he said.

Heading: 18 months on, Sec-39 veggie market project yet to see the light of day - Indian Express
Content:
A large number of consumers do not get their compensation as is evident from the number of execution applications filed in the consumer forum. Punitive proceedings by the court are the only deterrent for the erring defaulters, who fail to cough up penalties.

Owing to the increasing level of awareness among consumers, the number of executions filed is on the rise.

The two UT consumer forums jointly witnessed as many as 137 executions in 2006. The number spiralled to 204 in 2007. Till October this year, 153 executions have been filed. The UT District Forum-1 has witnessed 63 executions till date, out of which 47 are pending.

Making full use of Section 27 of the Consumer Protection Act, the court has issued arrest warrants in ten cases this year. In the remaining cases, the notices issued following the execution compelled defaulters to pay. While none has been arrested because in most of the cases, dispute gets settled once the warrants are issued. In rare cases, defaulter does take a stay order to evade arrest.

"The number of executions being filed has augmented. In almost 99 per cent of the cases, defaulters pay in the notice period for the fear of arrest. The procedure for penalisation acts as a deterrent and serves justice to consumers. More consumers should come forward to send the defaulters behind bars and set an example," said K C Gupta, President, UT State

Commission. "Most of the times, the defaulter gets scared once an execution application is filed. Most of the cases get settled then and there. The UT Consumer courts are functioning effectively," said advocate R K Bashamboo.

In one such case last month, the consumer court issued non-bailable warrants against Citi Financial as the company failed to return the cheques to the complainant in time. The general manager and the assistant manager of the company were sentenced to six years' imprisonment along with a fine of Rs 10,000 for non-compliance of the orders.

Last week, the court also sentenced Satyam Computer managing director to imprisonment of two years for failing to comply with its orders.

Ques What is Section 27 of the Consumer Protection Act?

When a trader or a person against whom a complaint is made or the complainant fails or omits to comply with any order made by the District Forum, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, such trader or person or complainant shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month but which may extend to three years, or with fine which shall not be less than Rs 2,000 but which may extend to Rs 10,000, or both.

Though the court can issue arrest warrants, the task of attaching property is tedious.

The consumer forum cannot directly attach properties of those not complying with their orders. To attach the properties of defaulters, the court may issue a certificate for the said amount to the collector of the district.

The collector will proceed to recover the amount in the same manner as arrears of land revenue. The procedure involves a lot of time and the process of recovery is tedious, say consumer experts.

Proposal to hike complaint fee

Harassed consumers seeking compensation at the UT consumer forums will have to shell out more money while filing their complaints in the near future. According to a recent proposal made at a meeting by the Presidents of State Commissions and Secretaries in charge, the prevailing fee under Rule 9 A of the Consumer Protection Rules 1987 is likely to increase. While no fees is being charged to seek damages up to Rs 10,000, those seeking compensation between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 10 lakh will have to pay Rs 500 instead of Rs 200.

A complainant will have to burn a big hole in his pocket if he/she wishes to claim compensation in the above Rs 10 lakh to Rs-20 lakh bracket. Rupees 2,000 will be charged as against Rs 200. "At present the previous rates will be applicable. The proposal to enhance the fees has been made to reduce the number of frivolous applications. It will be sent to the Ministry of Consumers affairs for its approval," sad K.C Gupta, President, UT State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

Heading: Thousands to lakhs: Sector-17 Plaza rentals exhibit a wide range - Indian Express
Content:
The multi-crore modern terminal market project for Sector 39 has been further delayed as the administration failed to announce the qualified applicants to carry out the project. While the Administration was supposed to make the announcement on October 15, it has postponed the date 'till further notice'.

The Chandigarh State Agriculture Marketing Board had invited global tenders for setting up the market at a cost of Rs 53.67 crore. To come up on 50 acres of land near the agro zone, the market will be a transit zone to supply fruits, vegetables and other perishable items to consumers. The market will act as a one-stop transparent selling facility for producers.

The tenders, which are expected to be built, owned and operated on Build-Owned-Operated (BOO) basis were announced in January last year. The construction work is required to be completed within 15 months from the date of contract. It has already been more than 18 months since the tenders were invited by the UT Administration.

The modern terminal market is required to be operational on a 'hub-spoke format' wherein the market (hub) will be linked to a number of collection centres (spokes) which in turn will be located at key production centres for the convenience of farmers.

The market envisages providing electronic auction, cold storage facility, temperature controlled warehouses, ripening chambers, sorting, grading, washing and packing lines, material handling equipment and banking services. The market will also have restaurants, shopping complex and facilities for other civic amenities. Each of these services will be provided in lieu of a user charge.

According to the administration officials, the market will offer multiple choices to farmers for the sale of produce such as electronic auctioning and facility for direct sale to exporter, processor and retail chain network under a single roof.

The new market is expected to be built, owned and operated by a corporateor private or co-operative entity, either by itself or through adoption of an outsourcing model. The enterprise will be a consortium of enterprises in the field of agribusiness or infrastructure development or service provider.

Chandigarh being a union territory does not have any significant production of its own. The produce comes mainly from Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana. The idea of having a terminal market at Chandigarh is based on a similar concept derived from the existing terminal market at Bangalore.

The food trail

* Apple — Come from Shimla, Kinnaur, Kullu districts of Himachal Pradesh and Srinagar. Himachal Pradesh produces apples worth Rs 600 and Rs 800 crore every year. Twenty per cent of the produce comes to the Chandigarh market.

* Mango — From Saharanpur, Roorkee, Dehradun and Muzaffarnagar.

* Grapes — Nasik in Maharashtra

* Kinnow — Hoshiarpur, Abohar and Fazilka districts of Punjab and Ganganagar district of Rajasthan. Arrival last year in Chandigarh was about 976 metric tonnes.

* Orange — Nagpur and Amravati districts of Maharashtra.

* Potato — Patiala, Ropar, Hoshiarpur and Ludhiana districts of Punjab. Shimla, Una and Kinnour districts of Himachal Pradesh also send some produce.

* Onion —Patiala and Ropar districts in Punjab, Kaithal in Haryana and Nasik in Maharashtra

* Tomato — Patiala and Ropar in Punjab, Shimla and Solan in Himachal Pradesh, Siliguri district of West Bengal and Nasik in Maharashtra .

* Peas — Hoshiarpur and Nawanshahar districts of Punjab, Shimla and Lahaul, Spiti districts of Himachal Pradesh and Jaipur in Rajasthan

* Carrot — Patiala in Punjab, Shimla, Lahaul and Spiti districts of Himachal Pradesh and Jaipur. The arrival in Chandigarh last year was about 4,744 metric tons.

Heading: Come March, international airport likely to jet set, go - Indian Express
Content:
At the Sector-17 Shopping Plaza, Chandigarh, the commercial rentals for showrooms depicts a huge variation with charges ranging from Rs 2,000 a month to around Rs 18 lakh.

While the rentals demanded for new showrooms ranges in lakhs, the ones already on rent for the last 25 years are valued at prices as low as Rs 2,000 a month.

Despite the market value of these commercial properties being appreciated by nearly 100 per cent a year, the rentals have not appreciated by even 10 per cent during the same period.

"One of my showrooms near the Estate Office on rent, since 1973, is fetching a meagre rent of Rs 12 per square feet whereas the current rent of these showrooms is somewhere around Rs 600 to 700 per square feet," said one of the owners of a showroom in Sector 17.

For R P Malhotra, general secretary, Property Owners' Welfare Association, the concept of leasehold properties is a vital reason for the phenomenal variation.

"Like the residential and industrial properties, the commercial properties should also be freehold. The ground rent given annually at a rate of around 2.5 per cent by the landlords on the commercial properties till 99 years is one of the reasons for the high rentals, which are rising even further," explained Malhotra.

He added that after 1975, the commercial properties have been auctioned on the leasehold basis instead of the freehold.

The other reason, added Malhotra, for scrapping the leasehold concept is that properties on leasehold are auctioned at lower rates as compared to the freehold ones depending on the ground rent paid annually by the property holder.

Heading: Woman sets self on fire; husband, in-laws held for dowry harassment - Indian Express
Content:
The City Beautiful is likely to have its international airport by March next year. The modernisation work of the existing terminal building of the airport is in full swing and the basic structure of the same is complete.

With only the roof to be laid now, the process of which is already underway, the new state-of-the-art terminal building could be ready in another four months.

Apart from outstanding facilities to be put up in the new building like the smart building management system, the terminal will also have Flight Information Display System (FIDS) and facility for premium parking. The contract of Rs 25 lakh for FIDS has already been handed over to Solari Udine, an Italian company with an experience of more than 50 years in FIDS and the resource allocation system.

"FIDS, which is a board or a television screen displaying in real-time the different arrivals or departures occurring over a specific period of time, would be placed at various locations inside the airport and at the entrance of the terminal. Both display and audio information would be supplied either to the passengers or to the operative personnel at the airport. This would assist passengers during air travel and people who want to pick-up passengers after the flight lands," said an official of the airport authority.

The parking facility has also been planned keeping in mind the international standards. The premium car parking has been reserved for passengers who want to save on time and avoid the hassle of walking from the parking area to the terminal. Despite the parking area for 500 cars, space for 150 cars has been allocated at the nearest terminal. Anyone, who is ready to pay parking charges of Rs 120 (as against the normal charge of Rs 25) can park the car in this reserved parking area.

According to a senior official, the Minimum Reserve Licence Fee (MRLF) has been decided for the premium car parking which would be given to a private contractor. "As the existing contract will expire on June 15, 2009, the new terminal will have the same contractor for both the parking areas; premium as well as the normal one," said the official.

Heading: Depressed 47-yr-old hangs self - Indian Express
Content:
In an alleged case of dowry death, 25-year-old Rajni, a resident of Ram Darbar Phase-II, set herself on fire at her residence late on Saturday night.

Police said a case of dowry death and attempt to murder under Section 304 of the IPC has been registered against her husband and in-laws on the complaint of the girl's father, Brahm Singh.

In his complaint, Singh said that his daughter and Pintu married four years ago. "Since then, Pintu and his parents had been harassing Rajni for dowry. I fulfilled many of their demands, including a cash transfer but it failed to satisfy them. Rajni had stopped conveying their demands to us lately, which led to a strain in their relationship," he alleged.

According to police, Rajni had gone to attend a marriage function along with her husband and in-laws. When they returned, some heated arguments were exchanged between them.

"Rajni went to the kitchen, locked it from inside and set herself on fire. Her husband and other people broke open the door and rushed her to Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32, with 100 per cent burn injuries. She was unfit to record her statement last night and succumbed to her injuries on Sunday morning," the police said. Police have arrested Pintu and his parents.

They did not have any children.

Heading: Poetry book weaves Punjabi with Hindi, English: writer - Indian Express
Content:
A 47-year-old woman committed suicide by hanging herself from the ceiling fan at her residence in Sector 41, on Sunday. Neelam, family sources said, was depressed for about two days.

Police said Neelam asked her husband to go downstairs and attend the doorbell. On return, he found the door of the bedroom locked. When Neelam didn't respond after several knocks, her husband broke open the door with the help of neighbours and found her hanging. Her daughter was to marry on November 2. Neelam was rushed to the hospital where she was declared brought dead. Inquest proceedings have been initiated in the case.

Heading: Months on, Education dept yet to take action against ‘erring’ schools - Indian Express
Content:
The book release function of Poetry, Politics and Culture: Essays on Indian Texts and Contexts written by Professor Akshaya Kumar, department of English, Panjab University was held in the ICSSR Complex of the university on Sunday.

A discussion on the book was held later.

Initiating the discussion, renowned Hindi critic Namvar Singh said that it is first ever attempt to combine Hindi, Punjabi and English poetry, and weave them together through the subaltern theoretical framework. Professor S S Noor, vice-president, Sahitya Akademi, appreciated the discursive methodology applied by the author to understand the spirit of poetry in all the three languages and make bridges between them.

Prof GJV Prasad of Jawahar Lal Nehru University, New Delhi, said the book fills the gap between the three different cultural experiences of English, Hindi and Punjabi.

Heading: ‘Terrorists no longer enjoy the support of people of Kashmir’ - Indian Express
Content:
The schools that were earlier issued notices by the Education department for various irregularities, including the violation of building norms, are taking it easy at present as the authorities are yet to take any significant action.

A few months ago, some schools including Bhavan Vidyalaya, Sector 27, Moti Ram Arya School Senior Secondary School, Shivalik Public School and others were served showcause notices by the department.

In Bhavan Vidyalaya, it was found that the attendance was being marked with a pencil. Also, the school has an auditorium and some offices in the basement, which is against the local building bylaws.

The school was asked to submit a copy of the sanctioned building plan of the auditorium along with permission for habitable use. Despite stern warnings issued earlier by former Director Public Instructions (Schools) S K Setia that their recognition would be cancelled if they use the auditorium without official permission, functions are being held there regularly.

When Newsline brought the matter to Vinita Arora, principal of the school, she refused to comment. "I cannot comment on this as the entire matter is being looked after by the management," said Arora.

The case of Moti Ram Arya Senior Secondary School is also no different. The school was also found to be violating the building bylaws by running a parallel school on the same premises. Some teachers of the school had also complained to the department about the irregularities in the salary given to them. Also, the school still possesses only a provisional recognition and is yet to submit the completion of the building certificate to the department.

"We will very soon get the completion certificate and submit it to the department. So far as running the parallel school is concerned, there was a 'misunderstanding' which was cleared with Setia," maintained Saroj Sawant, principal of the school.

Shivalik Public School was also served orders as it was allegedly a defaulter on several grounds — non-compliance of Economic Weaker Section (EWS) orders, no occupation certificate from the Estate Office and also not following the CBSE guidelines regarding payment of salaries to teachers.

"Setia himself is not aware of the rules related to schools that come under the UT. We have not violated any norms and the school is working as per the guidelines of the Punjab Education Code", says D S Bedi, principal of the school.

When asked whether the department has cleared the schools of all the charges, Samwartak Singh, DPI (S), said, "No, we have not cleared their names. These schools are still under the scanner and we plan to take due action against them. But we are waiting for reports from the Estate Office as we will be able to do something only after that."

Heading: Cn & heard - Indian Express
Content:
Militancy in Kashmir appears to be in its last leg. The reason: the inability of the Pakistan Army and Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) to fight simultaneously on the three fronts — proxy war against India, unrest among the tribals in the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP), supported by Al Qaeda and Taliban, and vicious internal instability. The credit also goes to our soldiers who are guarding every nook and corner of the state

The strategy of the Pakistan Army — 'bleeding India through a thousand cuts'—has, however, not changed. It has not given up its claim over Kashmir.

Till a few months ago, though infiltration from across the border was reduced to a trickle, the infrastructure and machinery was being kept well-oiled so that the ISI could raise the ante whenever it chooses. In the past two months, they are desperately trying to facilitate the infiltration of terrorists into India to cause violence during the forthcoming assembly elections.

The terrorists no longer enjoy the support of the people in Kashmir, who have started resisting them. The Army, as part of Operation Sadbhavana, has brought about a lot of development in the state. Most of the people, who resisted the Indian forces in Kashmir in the 1990's, today identify Kashmir with India.

This irritates the militants, most of whom are now relying less on violence and more on other means like influencing viewpoints through the coercion of the local media, prevailing on bar associations to file human rights' abuse cases and nudging some political parties to carry forward the agenda of separatism.

After some talk on 'demilitarisation', the Kashmiri political leaders have realised that the term is applicable only to the Line of Control (LoC). As and when the LoC is accepted as a permanent border between India and Pakistan, it will be for the negotiating teams of the two countries to plan a phased demilitarisation of troops.

The term 'disengagement' is more appropriate while discussing the Army and the other security forces in the hinterland of Kashmir. The Army is conscious of the fact that if the situation continues to improve, it must gradually initiate reduction of troops and that it will be counter-productive not to do so. At present, however, the situation is not conducive for any major reduction in strength of the Forces.

While the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has replaced the Army in most cities, the last battalions of the Army in the state, engaged in the C I Operations, is expected to be replaced by the CRPF in November.

The government should try to work towards restoring normalcy in the state. And in one such move, the Army battalions camping in public places, like school compounds, are being moved out and the premises are being handed over to the civil authorities.

The government must also continue to engage all the political parties willing to participate in the forthcoming elections. It must do everything possible to encourage the constituent members of the Hurriyat Conference to join the political mainstream.

Heading: Will hang myself if found guilty, says defiant mayor - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 12 vehicles were lined outside Burail Jail, to welcome Sanjeev Bansal, former Additional Advocate General, on his release after bail. Having a broad smile on their faces, Bansal's advocate friends from District Courts were serving beverages to all those standing outside the Burail Jail waiting for the release of their relatives. Ravinder Singh, the alleged kingpin may have given a statement completely against Bansal, but Ravinder's brother was also seen anxiously awaiting Bansal's release from the Jail. "Please dont ask him any questions, he won't speak anything", was the persistent request from Bansal's advocate friends to media persons standing outside the Jail. The sympathy for Bansal was indeed touching !

The workhorses

There is a neologism that is doing the rounds of the UT Administration these days. It is called the donkey syndrome. The asinine term implies the situation where a hard working officer is given additional charge. This term gained currency recently when an HCS officer, who was being given additional charge by his senior, pleaded with him not to increase his already heavy work load. The superior jokingly remarked, "We call it the donkey syndrome, where a hard working and honest official situation is akin to that of a donkey, that implies he is heaped with loads of work without any reward or recognition."

I am not temporary

There is a lot in the name after all! Ask the Punjab Congress chief who deeply resents his being referred to as the "acting chief of the Punjab Congress". At a recent press conference he spent considerable energies explaining to the media that there was no transience to his designation and he was in fact the real President of the Punjab Congress. His detractors point out that this is his response for being perennially in the shadow of his illustrious party colleagues including Captain Amarinder Singh and Rajinder Kaur Bhattal.

'Clutter-free' office

The incumbent Director Public Instructions (Schools) clearly does not share the enthusiasm of his predecessor for public interactions. One of the first things, which Samwartak Singh did on assuming charge was to remove all the "unnecessary" furniture. This is certainly an indication that he doesn't like too many visitors flocking his office. This is in stark contrast to Setia, who was so fond of public interactions that his office was always 'densely populated'.

Sensex : R.I.P

Forwarded emails and unwanted SMSes are most often of the obnoxious variety. But there are times a genuine pearl lands in our inboxes. Last week, this particular one was doing the rounds which brought smiles to people's faces even in these morose economic times. It conjured an imaginative obituary for sensex in the following words- Humare priye Shri Sensex ji ka swargwaas ho gaya hai. Yeh pichle 9 mahino se bimaar they. Reliance, SBI, Infosys, ICICI ke pita thhey. Hang Sang aur Nikkei ke bhai aur Dow(n) Jones ke jamai they. Unki Prarthana Sabha Lehman Brothers ke wahan rakhi gayi hai. Zarur Padhare. (loosely translated in English- Our beloved Mr Sensex has expired. He was ill for the last nine months and is the father of Reliance, SBI, Infosys and ICICI. He was the brother of Hang Sang and Nikkei and son-in -law of Dow(n) Jones. Please visit his condolence meeting scheduled at Lehnman Brothers premises).

Empty stands

The vacant stands at PCA Mohali, even on the momentous day when Sachin Tendulkar surpassed Brian Lara's record to become the highest run-getter in Test Cricket, has left the cricket administration highly demotivated. Whereas the representatives of International Cricket Council (ICC) expressed their reservations, some of the former cricketers said that PCA should not be given a Test match in future. The region certainly has a predilection towards the shorter formats of the game, but if a relegation to the stadium being made only a One Day centre comes, it would lower PCA's prestige considerably. Cheap thrills apart, the Test cricket is where, the real prestige lies. Just like a cricketer doesn't gain any eminence till the time he performs in Test Cricket (ask Yuvraj), a stadium is esteemed only if it is a Test centre.Let us hope that the spectator presence increases over the remaining days of what has so far been a very absorbing match with plenty of milestones.

Roadblocks

The work of recarpetting of Chandigarh's roads, after an extended monsoon left gaping potholes, has started. While the residents of the city welcome the move, they are unimpressed by the timing of the work. The contractors working on this project seem to work from 9 am to 5 pm which means that during peak hours, the roads are blocked. This exacerbates the heavy traffic and results in excruciating delays. Is it too much to ask that this work should be done at night or during wee hours of the day? After all, that is how things are done in the more efficiently managed cities of the world.

Heading: Cancer patients treated using radiation therapy - Indian Express
Content:
A day after BJP demanded his ouster, Pardeep Chhabra hits back

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra today challenged the BJP leaders to prove the allegations levelled against him that the Municipal Corporation favoured his brother and allotted land to him at cheap rates for an exhibition in Sector 34.

If found guilty, the mayor said, he would hang himself. The mayor added that he would file a defamation case against the BJP leaders.

The BJP delegation, including former MP Satya Pal Jain and president of the Chandigarh unit of the party, Kamla Sharma, had met UT Administrator Gen S F Rodrigues (Retd) on Saturday demanding action against the mayor. They had alleged that the mayor's brother had been allotted land at a lesser price by the MC to hold a Diwali mela. This, they claimed, had caused a loss worth lakhs to the corporation.

The mayor, while addressing a press conference, refuted all the allegations and said: "The land that has been allotted to my brother is owned by the Administration and not the MC. While the MC auctions the land to hold exhibitions, the Administration rents them out. The auction had fetched the MC Rs 5.5 lakh this year. My brother paid around Rs 2 lakh to the Administration, which was the requisite amount."

"We have been holding exhibitions for the past many years. Even in February this year, such an exhibition was held. No one raised any objections then. Anyone can take the land from the Administration to hold an exhibition," he added.

"The BJP is trying to politicise the issue. With the elections approaching, they have realised that they have no development issues to take up or speak against. Development projects of around Rs 170 crore have been passed during my tenure. I am accessible to the residents of the city. When the BJP was in power, they did nothing except for pulling each other down. They have no unity amongst themselves," said the Mayor. The BJP had earlier alleged that the Mayor was involved in the stonepelting incident at the residence of BJP councillor Ram Lal. The allegations were proved false after an inquiry into the issue.

Heading: Ex-servicemen on hunger strike from today - Indian Express
Content:
"GRECIAN multi-specialty hospital has successfully conducted over 100 Intensity Modulated Radiation Therapies (IMRTs) in cancer treatment in the last one year, said Dr Shivpreet Singh Samra, MD, Grecian Hospital, on Sunday while addressing the media in Mohali.

He said the highly advanced radiation therapy rated as the "apex curative radiation therapy" for cancer treatment has been successfully handled by the expert panel of radiation experts and oncologists at the Grecian Hospital.

"The IMRT at Grecian costs Rs 80,000 whereas the same costs around Rs 1.5 lakh in Delhi," concluded Dr Shivpreet Singh Samra.

Of the 100 patients treated by IMRT over the past one year, 10 patients were presented before the media.

Backed by the latest Eclipse Treatment Planning System, "IMRT applied for treating spinal cord tumours minimises the risk of paralysis just as in breast cancer, IMRT spares lungs and hearts. For bladder cancer, IMRT along with chemotherapy offers curative features," added Dr Nimbran.

Heading: Jalandhar Mail - Indian Express
Content:
Hundreds of ex-servicemen from Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula will sit on a hunger strike at the YPS Chowk in Phase VIII, Mohali, from Monday. It will be the first step under a mass protest launched by the Punjab chapter of the Indian Ex-Servicemen Movement (IESM) against the alleged "step motherly" treatment meted out to them by the successive governments at the Centre who have failed to meet their long pending demands. The hunger strike will begin from 9 am at the YPS Chowk and will continue till 5 pm daily till the Union Government agrees to fulfill their demands, announced Lt Col (Retd) Sadhu Singh Sohi, the coordinator of the IESM in a statement issued this evening.

The ex-servicemen also intend to observe Diwali on October 28 as a "black day" without lighting any candles or fireworks, said Sohi, while clarifying that the agitation will be observed in a peaceful manner without creating law and order disorder or causing public inconvenience.

"Similar protests will be held in 600 cities across the country, which will be a first in the country's history," claimed Sohi.

The IESM coordinator asserted, "The last three pay commissions have been unfair to us and have neglected our interests." Pointing out major discrepancies, Sohi said soldiers are still deemed as unskilled workers and a Naib Subedar, who is a Class II officer, gets pension less than a civil peon. Demanding a separate pay commission for the Defence Forces, ex-servicemen and their widows, Sohi added that a national-level delegation of the IESM had recently met UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi to apprise her of their decision and give the UPA-led government a last chance to fulfill their demands. As she was not available for the meeting, the members were forced to resort to the nationwide stir, added Sohi.

Heading: Reel success - Indian Express
Content:
A new show on television brings in a truckload of stars to the city. There's veteran actor Ranjeet dropping his mean streak, Rakhi Sawant's boyfriend making an identity, Baba Sehgal doing what he's best at....JAGMEETA THIND JOYbrings a roundup

Till now all the joint families that you've probably caught on television have a) squabbling mother-in-laws b) forever plotting daughter-in-laws c) basically, a lot of unpleasantness. In an effort to make the audience out there less skeptical about joint set-ups, SAB TV has brought in the Bhalla parivaar. This is one happy Punjabi family from Jalandhar complete with the Bauji, his bossy-yet-affable wife and a couple of doting sons and their better-halves. Coming from the Tony and Deeya Singh stable (the makers of Left Right Left, Jassi Jaisi Koi Nahin), the show 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar' is being pegged as a one of a kind comedy soap which stars a couple of veterans alongside a bunch of new comers. There's veteran actor Ranjeet and Alka Sachdev as the elders, Baba Sehgal and Rakhi Sawant's down-to-earth boyfriend Abhishek Avasthi as the sons and newcomer Karan Godwan and Muskan Mehani as the love-struck couple. Quite like the downpour we had on Friday, these stars poured in the city along with the biggies from the channel. Here's a who-said-what of it all.

Mean No More : Minus a few giveaways on his face that show he's aged, veteran actor Ranjeet looks exactly like how we've seen him onscreen. "Only now I am not running after a woman trying to molest her," the actor laughs in his stride. Having played the really bad man in films, Ranjeet has turned a new leaf with his foray into television. "The concept really appealed to me and that's what got me to sign up. As far as acting goes, I don't find any difference in the two mediums," says the actor who plays the Punjabi patriarch who doesn't like educated women! "Otherwise I have no such issues," he laughs. On a more serious note, he's not yet doing a Bollywood flick for "I am not ready to do tit-bit roles." But there's a movie in the pipeline and he's the one directing it.

Stepping Out Of the Shadows : Even though Abhishek Avasthi brought home the ZEE Cinestars Ki Khoj title, it's taken him long to find his feet as an actor in the industry. The fact that he's Rakhi Sawant's boyfriend has much to do with it. "I think I have had my share of dance shows and I now want to concentrate on my acting career," admits Avasthi who plays a brawny Maninder Bhalla on 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar'. And unlike his controversial girlfriend, Abhishek wants to play safe. "This is a great debut for me on television. The banner's good and so is my role," he answered. The fact that his love life has been much explored by the media, Abhishek's not cribbing. "We are celebrities and such things are bound to happen." Bring up Rakhi and he mellows down even more. "She's been misunderstood. In reality she's very down to earth and helpful person," the boyfriend shares.

Sream Debut : Until now, 20-year-old Karan Godwan was used to being in the background. This former dancer from Shiamak Davar's team finally decided to step out. "I have schooled in Spain and came back after finishing high school," informs Karan who plays the youngest son Vicky. With no connections to pull, this newcomer decided to give it all. "I must have given a million auditions and then Jugni Chali Jalandhar came my way," Karan's happy to have made it finally. On the show he's pairing up with Muskan Mehani who plays the lead as Jugni. Muskan's not new to television, having done shows like Dil Mil Gayee and Mamta.

Second Stint : The last time we bumped into singer and once-in-a-while actor Baba Sehgal, he was busy crooning on NDTV Imagine's show 'Dhoom Macha De'. While Jaspinder Narula went on to win that, Baba Sehgal has emerged once as an actor on 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar'. "I am a Punjabi and what better way to show it off than by acting in such a soap that brings out the best of a Punjabi family," mentioned the singer who even gets to rap while playing his character of Balwinder Bhalla. With an album in the making, he has enough to keep him busy and us too!

Heading: Chatterati - Indian Express
Content:
TV's most sought after producer-couple Tony and Deeya Singh is now looking at making a film

Their work speaks for them. For 15 years, producer and also a couple, Tony and Deeya Singh have dished out delectable entertainment on television. Be it the truly ahead of its time Banegi Apni Baat or the immensely popular Jassi Jaisi Koi Nahin to their just wrapped up Left Right Left, the producers have scored aces each time. "Yes, our USP has been our ability to make shows that are for a varied audience," admitted Deeya Singh who was in the city to formally roll out their new show 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar' on SAB TV. Also accompanying Deeya was N P Singh, Chief Operating Officer of Sony Entertainment Television. This time around, the producers have gone all Punjabi. "Being a Punjabi it all came easy," smiles Deeya who feels it's tough making the viewer laugh every day. "But then there's so much negativity elsewhere that we decided to do this." Interestingly, they have a whole gamut of shows across all channels. "The only thing we haven't touched upon is reality and that's something we really want to do," mentioned Deeya who also lets out a special something. "We are all geared up to make a film now," says the producer. So what genre are they looking at? "All round entertainment. We are looking at a four-ticket movie," signs off Deeya.

Heading: Brit Hit - Indian Express
Content:
Star gazing

Sass, Bahu aur Sensex may be a small-budget movie, but this did not deter Bollywood stars from making it to its premiere. The star cast of the movie —the elegant Kirron Kher, Tanushree Dutta in a little red number, Masumeh Makhija and glamorous Lilette Dubey were seen mingling with everybody. Parvin Dabas and Sanjay Suri were spotted together on many occasions involved in animated conversations. Anupam Kher and son Sikander were also present to cheer for Kirron. Rahul Roy with wife Rajlaxmi (with layers of make-up), Bobby Darling, Shahana Goswami, Sudhir Mishra and Sonu Sood were among others at the venue.

Heading: Buy the Way - Indian Express
Content:
A hint of celebrities and some elegant collections made up for an otherwise slow day at the fashion weeks

If nothing else, you can count on Rohit Bal to pull in the crowds. Day three at the Delhi Fashion Week was packed to capacity (for the first time at DFW). In any case, with Bal, in equal parts showman and designer, boredom is unlikely. The flat runway of DFW had been transformed into a gossamer field of of pink organza. Bal's spring summer show began with a model arising from within the cloud of organza, dressed in a layered outfit.

Bal's collection was more couture than pret. Lavishly constructed silhouettes and generous layerings in yellows and oranges for full bodied skirts patterned out of cones and dresses fashioned out of pouffed squares. As usual, Bal ended with a flourish, throwing handfuls of organza confetti at the audience then heading to the afterparty at Ai.

But if it's austerity we're talking about in these crazy times of global recession, Varun Bahl showed how to practice it to perfection at his spring-summer show at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week (WIFW) in front of a full house that had fellow designers like Manish Arora, Rajesh Pratap Singh, Manoviraj Khosla, Ritu Kumar in attendance. With sheer fabrics and basic colours like ivory, olive, salmon pink and beige, Bahl spun out a collection that was at once existential and elegant, spartan and sophisticated. Macrame, crochet, net and hints of lace were interestingly juxtaposed with linen, his characteristic rosettes back in knotted necklines and belts. The menswear had a touch of androgyny to it, but stood out for its sheer versatility. Timeless and very graceful.

Heading: foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
Organic in nature, corals come in various hues

Is it our love for studded jewelry, the associated ancient beliefs or inspiring style icons like Grace Kelly clad in a green gown and showstopping orange coral danglers? Well, reasons aplenty but coral's appeal is blatantly evident in almost every jewellery form.

Coral is an ancient "organic gemstone". Its actually a calcium substance that grows under water in plant like formations or branches. Coral is opaque and is naturally available in various colours. Colour distribution is even or a shaded effect of the same hue. Nonetheless, good quality coral is devoid of any dents, dimples, holes, cracks or perforations. Today, coral is majorly sourced from the Mediterranean Sea, off the coast of Algeria, Taiwan, Japan and Tunisia. Coral is available in various colours. Red, orange, black, purple, white, pink and gold are always in demand. Red coral grows about 1/4 inch per year and hence is highly treasured. The 'Oxblood Red Coral' is the most sought after in this category. 'Angel Skin Pink Coral' variates from white to a lovely blush and is a collector's delight. 'Gold Coral' ranges from buttery hues to deep chocolate. High quality coral sells as high as gold by weight. A coral admirer must visit the Coral Castle in America built single handed by Ed Leedskalnim in 28 years for his love for the gemstone.

Coral has been enjoyed for at least 25,000 years. For Egyptians it was a holy stone and was used in most burial ceremonies. Romans wore protective coral amulets. Coral is one of the seven treasures found in the Buddhist scriptures. Many cultures believed in its medicinal properties. It was believed to prevent abortions, excessive bleeding, impotency and stomach viruses. Coral has been beaded and strung over centuries and sparkled in various design sensibilities, may it be Victorian setting, jadau jewellery, the Indian Navratna or set along other gemstones. Being a fragile stone it is best set in bezel set down and bigger pieces may be supported from the rare side. Being an expensive gemstone one must be careful of imitations. Coloured shells, bones, plastic, porcelain etc is often sold as coral. Here's a simple test: Immersed coral in milk makes the milk appear pink or red. Imitation will give no colour!

(The writer is a city-based researcher specialising in jewellery art and can be contacted at sameeraahaan02@gmail.com)

Heading: Joining Forces - Indian Express
Content:
Not just the life, but the works of Jnanpith awardee Gurdial Singh form the spine of a docu-drama

His life is not separate from his writing and art. Precisely why, the docu-drama 'Gurdial Singh Ji', is not solely a biographical sketch of the Jnanpith awardee, but gives a deep insight into the works of the renowned and contemporary Punjabi writer. Commissioned by the Sahitya Akademi, Delhi, the docu-drama, according to GS Chani, its producer and director is the latest in the series of docu-dramas on the lives of prominent Indian writers, which will form part of a library and will be sold individually as well. The script has been written with inputs from the writer himself, who didn't want it to be just a commentary on his life's events, how he grew up et al, but focus on the integral part of his being, his literary work.

Born into a family of artisans in Malwa, as a boy, Gurdial moulded iron sheets for long hours and encouraged by his school teacher, resumed his studies and went on to be a professor at Punjabi University. His first major work, 'Marhi Da Deeva' was translated into English as 'The Last Flicker' and is considered a modern classic. 'Anhoe', 'Anhe Ghore Da Daan', 'Parsa'...and then notable collection of short stories and also plays followed. Gurdial has won the Punjab Sahitya Akademi Award, the Soviet Land Nehru Award, the Bhai Veer Singh Fiction Award and of course, the Jnanpith. "We've taken up five major novels and enacted scenes from them as part of the movie. The main characters of the novels talk about Gurdialji, the structure of the novels and themselves. We chose not use commentary, but included interviews of Gurdialji's contemporaries for a terrific flow,'' adds Chani.

'Gurdial Singh Ji' will be screened at Punjab Kala Bhavan on September 20 at 5:30 pm.
