Heading: ‘Post-riots, cops closed 2,100 cases without probe’ - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee said on Sunday that the Tatas are dictating the CPM's course of action. Trinamool's move, on the contrary, is dictated by the people of Bengal, she said.

Criticising Ratan Tata for his open letter on the Singur issue, Banerjee said he should contest elections.

"The Tatas are deciding what the CPM will do. But it is the people of

Bengal who decide what we will do. The state government needs the Tatas, not us or the people of Bengal. Our party is discussing legal moves against the Tatas," said Banerjee at a press conference at her residence in Kalighat on Sunday.

Criticising Ratan Tata for remaining silent when the people of Singur were being subjected to atrocities, she said: "Why was he silent when Tapasi Malik and Rajkumar Hul died in Singur? He did not say anything at that time. He was called for talks by Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, but he did not come. Why is he talking now?" asked Banerjee.

Calling on Ratan Tata to stand for elections in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Bidhan Sabha and Lok Sabha, she said the people of Bengal will give him a befitting reply.

"The people of Bengal are not his slaves," she said.

"The youths of Bengal are not his bonded labour. How many people would they have employed? When our government comes to power, ensuring job security will be our priority," she added.

Continuing her tirade against Ratan Tata, Mamata said: "He says he is transparent. Then why did he not make public the deal he signed with the state government and instead ran away? In Gujarat, he has to pay Rs 400 crore. Interestingly, here the Bengal government paid him Rs 200 crore," Banerjee said.

In an open letter published by select dailies, Ratan Tata had blamed the Trinamool Congress for forcing the company to pull out the Nano project from Singur.

Heading: New municipal bond structure, investment pattern on the cards - Indian Express
Content:
Former DGP says the state government complied with almost none of the recommendations made by NHRC on 2002 riots

"It hurts a bit… no, it hurts a lot, every day," says PGJ Nampoothiri — the man behind the National Human Rights Commission's (NHRC) report that followed the 2002 post-Godhra riots — on the Gujarat government's total disregard of the Commission's recommendations in the aftermath of the genocide.

For Nampoothiri, the former special rapporteaur of the NHRC and ex-Gujarat DGP, the hurt got bigger on September 26, when the Nanavati-Mehta Commission of Inquiry submitted the first part of its probe report on Godhra and post-Godhra carnages. The Commission jumped the gun in the first part of its report, which according to itself was supposed to deal only with the Godhra train carnage and not the riots that followed, to say there was no lapse on part of the Gujarat government in complying with recommendations of the NHRC.

In a candid interview to Newsline, Nampoothiri rubbished the Nanavati-Mehta report's claims. He pointed out that far from complying, the Gujarat government had almost completely scuttled the NHRC recommendations. The ex-top cop of Gujarat also spoke about the role the Gujarat Police could have played to contain the riots that left an indelible blotch on the state.

* How do you see the Nanavati-Mehta Commission's observation that the Gujarat government had complied with all the NHRC recommendations regarding the rehabilitation measures after the post-Godhra riots?
I think it would be only correct and true to say that the Gujarat government has complied with almost none, yes none, of the recommendations of the NHRC. All our reports are public documents and they are open to everybody to see and decide for themselves. Perhaps, the Nanavati Commission was not correctly informed or was misled into reaching such a conclusion. May be it did not fully appreciate the reports of the NHRC.

* In part one of the report itself, which supposedly dealt only with the Godhra train carnage incident, the inquiry commission looked beyond and concluded that the government complied with the recommendations of the NHRC. Was it in too much of a hurry to do so?
May be at this stage, it need not have gone into that question. May be there was no need for those observations at this point. However, I hope the Commission will put things into perspective in the second part of its report.

* What are the most important recommendations of the NHRC that the Gujarat government chose to overlook?
We had recommended that five specific cases of Godhra, Best Bakery, Sardarpura, Naroda Patiya and Gulberg Society be investigated by the CBI. For other cases, we had said that district magistrates should be made in-charge of the investigation team under the supervision of the ADG (Crime). Over 4,200 cases were registered after the riots, and 2,100 were closed without investigation. Where is the question of compliance? There were other recommendations also.

* Which were the other recommendations?
We had said that all religious places that were broken or disfigured (during the riots) should be restored by the government. There are nearly 400 such places. The government agreed in principle, but never restored even a single one of them. We had also said that none of the relief camps (for the riot victims) should be shut down till it was ascertained that the situation is fit for people to go back. No such thing was done and all relief camps were closed on June 30, 2002.

* Speaking from your experience, has any other state government shown such complete disdain and disregard to NHRC recommendations?
I don't think so. Generally, what the NHRC says is taken very seriously. Its reports are tabled in the Parliament. It is a body that is known internationally. Also, NHRC reports have credence and once they are out, public pressure mounts for their implementation. In fact, the situation in Gujarat had so anguished Justice J S Verma, who was the chairperson then, that he wrote a letter to the then Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee about it. But all that we got in reply was the standard acknowledgment of its receipt from the PMO.

* Do you think lack of public pressure in Gujarat is a major reason why the NHRC recommendations have been flouted so brazenly by the government?
It is one of the reasons, definitely. In fact, in Gujarat, the NHRC team was greeted with protests wherever it went. There were even petitions filed in the High Court appealing to bar the entry of the NHRC team into the state.

* Hypothetically, if a majority of the riot victims were from the other community, would the way the state government responded to the NHRC recommendations have been different in Gujarat?
I certainly think so. The NHRC report, though, would have been the same. The community of the victims would have made no difference to it.

* The manner in which the post-Godhra riots took place, their ferocity and the lame response from the police made its role to be alleged as being dubious. What do you feel about it?
If the police had done its duty, which is to follow the law, the magnitude of the events that unfolded would have been far less. The police should have arrested a good number of people before all hell broke lose. There would have been no need even to call in the army. I believe the police have all the powers to deal with any law and order situation. They could have used them.

Heading: 8 Pakistanis arrested for sneaking into India - Indian Express
Content:
A fresh blueprint is expected to enable civic bodies to raise money through taxable bonds

Now that municipal bonds are being viewed as a good source of financing civic infrastructure projects under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM), the Centre is working out a fresh blueprint for the bond structure and investment pattern. The government is consulting the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in this regard.

It is estimated that the 63 mission cities need Rs 3.35 lakh crore to create the basic infrastructure during a seven-year period. Of this, the local bodies of these cities would have to invest around Rs 98,000 crore from their own pocket. This means a capital investment of a staggering

Rs 8 lakh crore by all the 5,161 urban centres across the country.

Once the Urban Development Ministry's blueprint is ready, it is expected to help the urban local bodies to tap the debts market for their projects. The focus of the blueprint, it is learnt, will be preparing guidelines to enable the civic bodies to raise money through taxable bonds, which can elicit greater market response because they yield more interest than the tax-free bonds issued hitherto.

This, however, does not mean bidding goodbye to the tax-free bonds. The existing guidelines for the issue of tax-free bonds will also be given a fresh look.

Industry sources say that while some cities have already issued municipal bonds in recent years, fresh consultations with industry and financial institutions have indicated that there's a greater appetite for taxable bonds than tax-free bonds. The interest rate on tax-free municipal bonds is capped at eight per cent while it is around 11.5 per cent on taxable bonds. Not only that, it can also be linked to market conditions.

There is a ceiling on the amount of tax-free bonds that can be issued for a single project. Thus, a local body can only issue tax-free bonds up to half of the cost of the project or Rs 300 crore, whichever is less.

It may be recalled that the Urban Development Ministry, the nodal agency for JNNURM, had initiated a credit rating exercise for a number of urban local bodies with a view to strengthen the capacity to borrow from open market, some time ago. The exercise was undertaken by the four credit-rating agencies - CRISIL, ICRA, CARE and Fitch. The exercise has been completed in 22 cities, but the results are not quite satisfactory. Only the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation got A+ rating.

The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) had pioneered fund raising through municipal bonds way back in 1998 by issuing bonds worth Rs 100 crore. This was used to partly fund a Rs 439-crore water supply and sewerage projects. Tax-free bonds came into vogue from 2002 when the AMC issued a tax-free 10-year bond with an annual interest rate of nine per cent worth Rs 100 crore.

Municipal Commissioner I P Gautam, however, ruled out that the AMC is going for taxable bonds.

"We will prefer tax-free bonds and since maximum eight per cent interest is allowed on them, we are requesting the Central Government to review the rate of interest," he said.

The Ministry of Urban Development had also favoured sourcing loans from banks and bilateral institutions like ADB, he added.

Heading: Corruption among Sabarmati Central Jail staff is deep-rooted, says inmate - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Coast Guard apprehended eight Pakistani nationals, including three women and two children, near Nalia in Bhuj on Sunday. A private Pakistani motorboat had dropped them on a small island opposite Jakhau near Naliya in the morning.

The operation was carried out around 10.30 am following a tip-off, officials said.

The eight, all residents of Karachi, were identified as Mohammed Hussain Chavada (46), Mohammed Salim Hussain (21),

Mohammed Aslam Hussain (19), Amina Hussain (35), Savra (16), Suhra (14), Suleman Hussain (12) and Mohammed Srif Hussain (10).

"They were later handed over to the Kutch police for further investigations," said Defence spokesman Wing Commander Satish Menon. According to the preliminary inquiries made by the Coast Guard, the eight had boarded a hired motorboat from Karachi on Friday afternoon. The boat, which had four crew members on board, dropped them on an uninhabited island opposite Jakhau around 1 am on Sunday.

A boarding party of the Indian Coast Guard was sent to the island following a tip-off and the eight were taken into custody.

The detainees, according to the Coast Guard, had migrated from India in 1990 to get settled in Pakistan. Officials have also seized their Indian passports that had expired in 1992.

They told the police that they had come to India to meet their relatives who stay in Anjar in Kutch. It is learnt that they have visited India several times.

The Superintendent of Kutch police, Wabang Jamir said: "They will be interrogated to ascertain the reason of their visit to India and later sent to the Joint Interrogation Centre (JIC) in Bhuj for further investigations."

Heading: Red Corner notices against Gujarati NRI marital cheats - Indian Express
Content:
A clerk passing cellphones to the Sabarmati Central Jail inmates against a bribe of Rs 1,000, as revealed by the Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) of the city police, seems to be just tip of the corruption iceberg in this high security jail.

Asghar Ali, the prime accused in the Haren Pandya murder case, who is serving a life term in the jail, has accused the in-charge superintendent of the jail, J B Mandalia, of demanding a bribe of Rs 10,000 for allowing him to be taken to the civil hospital for treatment.

Ali has made the accusation in a letter sent to the Inspector General of Prisons earlier this month.

The letter, a copy of which is with Newsline, further states that Ali, a resident of Hyderabad, is an 'outsider' in Gujarat and he has no relatives in the state, who can provide him with financial help. "Ali is not in a position to pay even Rs 100 to the jail staff," it adds.

Pointing out that he was given the last medical treatment on July 14 this year, the letter says he was never allowed to be taken out of the jail after that, even as he had been suffering from acute urinary problems and chest pain for the last four months.

According to a murder accused, who is presently out on bail, corruption among the jail employees is deep-rooted. "Special diet, which includes fruits, can be prescribed for you at the rate of Rs 200 for eight days. Other things like good quality tea leaves, sugar and ghee are also available inside the jail at a much higher price," he said on grounds of anonymity.

According to this accused, the inmates are taken to special areas within the jail premises like the hospital, court, Gandhi Kholi, two particular barracks in the Bada Chakkar and open space behind the carpentry unit for making the phone calls. "These are the places where mobile phone jammers are ineffective," he added.

Sources in the jail said that the allegations levelled against Mandalia by Ali are being investigated.

Meanwhile, the DCB, which is interrogating jail clerk and typist Ashok Zapadia and his accomplice Mehmood Khan Pathan, who were arrested on charges of smuggling mobile phones into the jail on Friday, said on Sunday that Zapadia would take the bribe as his commission for passing the banned item to the inmates.

"Zapadia has confessed before us that he used to charge Rs 1,000 per mobile phone for just taking them into the jail premises," said H R Muliana, Assistant Commissioner of Police, DCB. He added they are still investigating as to whether some more jail employees were involved in the offence.

Heading: Conspirator in Akshardham attack arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Red Corner notices seeking extradition or deportation no longer chase the usual band of hardened criminals in Gujarat. The new targets of the state CID (Crime) are Gujarati marital cheats settled abroad.

Of late, the police have begun issuing these notices to secure extradition of NRI Gujarati grooms, who lure local girls into marriage and ditch them at the last moment.

Several cases of fake NRI Gujarati marriages are being reported throughout the state with brides, including highly-qualified women, being duped by their NRI husbands. The women's cell of the CID (Crime) has already issued red corner notices in as many as six cases, seeking to bring back these men to stand trials.

One of the accused, Vishal Sureshchandra Raval, a US-based NRI who belonged to Mehsana district, surrendered before a court here recently. He is facing charges of mental and physical torture of his wife.

Meanwhile, the Interpol is still on the lookout for the remaining five. According to CID (Crime) officials, the details of these men have been provided to the Interpol. In addition, their residential addresses in the countries they live in have been given to the Interpol. These men, however, keep fooling officials by changing residences using their overseas connections.

"But we hope to nab them sooner or later," said Meera Ramniwas, Deputy Inspector General of Police, CID Crime (Women's Cell).

She said her department is now in the process of readying one more red corner notice seeking deportation of a US-based Gujarati, Jagdish alias Jack Punjibhai Patel, who had an extra-marital affair with a beautician in Gandhinagar two years ago. He promised to marry the girl and take her to the US. He, however, ditched her after she gave birth to a boy in July last year. Thereafter, the girl filed an FIR against him. The CID is now trying to arrest Patel and get him back through Interpol.

According to Ramniwas, many NRI Gujaratis, who have wife and children in their adopted countries, fool around with young girls here, who are easily lured by the prospect of marriage and living abroad. Many actually enter into vacation marriages, stay for a month or two and then go back promising the 'spouse' to arrange for her visa.

In other cases, NRI grooms just file a divorce petition overseas as per local laws there, get a divorce from the courts and send those papers to their 'wife' here.

Ramniwas said these cases have been on the rise lately. She provided a list of precautions for parents, who are looking for NRI grooms. These are:

* Don't finalise the marriage in haste and/or over phone or through e-mail.

* Don't settle wedding related matters like taking or giving of dowry in secrecy.

* Verify the antecedents of the NRI groom, his marital status, job, business, income, residence, family members through Indian and Gujarati NGOs abroad or even the Indian Embassy there.

* Do not depend on middlemen or marriage bureaus.

* Compulsorily register marriages in India along with a social ceremony with family members of both the parties and settle all conditions before marriage.

* Take care to avoid greedy NRIs. If the groom or his family insist on having the marriage or registration only abroad, say no to it.

* Collect passport details of the groom, his visa, phone numbers, his photographs, photographs of his parents and other family members. Never sign any suspicious documents and keep all your important documents like educational certificates and passports with you.

* Parents must procure a copy of a 75-page book containing guidelines prepared by NRI Gujarati Foundation here and study it before finalising the marriage.

The book, according Ramniwas, is a complete guide on NRI marriages with rights of women, children rights, domestic violence, provision of maintenance under Section 125 of the CRPC, Hindu marriage act, and the rights of Muslim women.

Heading: Over 300 fuel station dealers to go on strike in 4 districts - Indian Express
Content:
The Special Operation Group (SOG) of the Bharuch police arrested Majid Patel, wanted in the Akshardham temple attack case, from a village in Bharuch district on Sunday. The arrest was made following a tip-off. The SOG was interrogating Patel till this report was filed.

Wanted by the Detection of Crime Branch (DCB), Patel is accused of arranging money through Hawala channels for the attack. He was believed to have fled to Dubai. Ashish Bhatia, Joint Commissioner of Police, DCB, said, "A team has been sent to Bharuch to interrogate Patel." Thirty-four people, including two National Security Guard commandos and two state commandos, were killed and over 80 were injured when two Pakistan-based terrorists attacked the Gandhinagar temple on September 24, 2003.

With this arrest, the total number of accused held so far has risen to seven, while over 20 are still at large.

Heading: Lake resort still a dream as storm water drainage carries industrial effluents - Indian Express
Content:
Dealers from Rajkot, Junagadh, Jamnagar and Porbandar to stop lifting petrol and diesel stocks from Monday

More than 300 fuel station dealers in four districts of the Saurashtra region will go on strike from Monday. Dealers from Rajkot, Junagadh, Jamnagar and Porbandar will stop lifting petrol and diesel stocks to protest against the Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and Essar Oil Company.

Shivlala Bhanderi, President of Rajkot City and District Petrol/Diesel Dealers Association told Newsline that earlier all fuel station dealers used to transport fuel from IOC departments to their pumps in their own

vehicles. But last month, IOC gave the contract of transporting the fuel to a private transporter, who quoted a lower price than the fuel station dealers.

"Every fuel station has its own transporting vehicle, as we face several problems with hired vehicles. Some of these problems are stealing and adulteration of fuel, late delivery among others. Last month, IOC gave the contract to a private transporter, as our quoted price was higher than that quoted by the transporter. However, we told IOC that we are ready to transport fuel at a price lower that what the private transporter has quoted. But the company did not pay heed to our request," Bhanderi said.

He added: "Now, the huge investment which each fuel station made to purchase the transportation vehicles will go waste. Thus, from Monday onwards all fuel station dealers, including 130 in Rajkot, around 70 in Junagadh and the remaining 100 in Porbandar and Jamnagar will not lift fuel, not just from IOC but from depots of all other companies till our demands are fulfilled."

In Jamnagar and Porbandar, fuel station dealers are protesting against Essar Oil Company. The dealers claim that the fuel supplied by the company's Vadinar refinery is of a very high temperature. Due to this, around 100 to 150 litre of fuel vaporises in each tanker and the dealers bear losses to the tune of Rs 5,000-6,000 every time.

Masukh Barai, leader of Fuel Station Owners from Okha, said: "We have been facing this problem for long. No concrete steps have been taken despite continuous complaints from our members. Per tanker, we lose around Rs 6000 every time. We visited the refinery last month and explained the problem to company officials. But the problem still persists. Thus, we have decided to go on strike from Monday onwards."'

Bhanderi said: "Our State Federation leaders are trying to sort out this issue at the secretariat level. However, if company officials fail to co-operate with us in fulfilling our demands, this agitation will spread across the state."

Heading: L D College may double seats in automobile engineering course - Indian Express
Content:
City's Rs 300-crore storm water drainage project could have come out as a great success story had there been no connivance between some black sheep in the civic administration and unscrupulous industrial units.

The project, cleared under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM), is seen as panacea to the perennial problem of waterlogging in several low-lying areas of the city.

The several kilometres long winding project was completed in its first phase to connect Naroda-Nikol with Malek Shaban Stadium in Bapunagar area with a view to convert it into a lake resort in the recreation starved east zone area by routing rainwater to the place. The line was expected to fill the place with rainwater. Instead, the line currently carries industrial effluents from the nearby industrial units through illegal connections allegedly under the indulgent supervision of civic officials.

Mayor Kanaji Thakor noticed the dumping of industrial effluents first when he came to the spot on a casual visit last week to get a first-hand information on the progress of the project.

Thakor said he noticed the dumping of effluents when he probed how water was flowing on the road when monsoon was over. "I have asked the officials to plug the connections at the earliest so that the spot could be developed as planned," he added.

Storm water drains being misused for disposing of effluents is not new to the city, but the present project is the one on which all eyes are set in the hope of getting rid of waterlogging in almost the entire city once and for all.

While local BJP councillor Nagesh Devalpally informs that the problem is almost three months old and he had also given a written representation to the civic authorities, additional city engineer (east zone) Dilipkumar Arora said he was not aware of it.

"Yes, it comes under my charge, but I did not know about the dumping of effluents until today," Arora said, adding, he would order a proper inquiry into the incident at the earliest.

Devalpally said he was present on the spot when the mayor visited the place. "This has been going on for three months and I have drawn attention of officials, but to no use," he said.

Heading: Miscreants loot cash, jewellery worth lakhs at gunpoint - Indian Express
Content:
Tatas' entry into Gujarat for the Nano project seems to have geared up all sectors in the State. Support the project, educational institutions too are getting ready for it.

In order to meet Tatas' requirements, L D College of Engineering, Ahmedabad — the State's biggest engineering college — has put forth its proposal to the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) to double the number of seats for the automobile engineering discipline.

At present, the college has 30 seats in Bachelor of Engineering (Automobile). The college management has now requested the number of seats to be increased to 60.

Earlier, the college management had requested the AICTE to permit them to increase the number of seats in Masters of Engineering (Automobile) from 18.

But the council did not give the permission stating that it was not possible to increase the number of seats there.

It is therefore, possible that the number of seats in Masters course may increase in other engineering institutes of the State.

"At present, L D College of Engineering is the only institute in the State where Masters of Engineering (Automobile) is taught. But now, AICTE will consider other engineering institutes too, for this course," said M N Patel, principal of L D College of Engineering.

In Gujarat, automobile engineering is taught at institutes in Ahmedabad, Bhavnagar and Surat. Now, Modasa has also joined the race.

"There is no doubt that after the announcement of Tata's Nano project in the State, everyone is looking at the automobile sector. The request that we made to AICTE is also an effect of that," Patel said.

He said: "Until now, the craze towards automobile studies, especially in the car sector, was not much. But things have changed now. We are not the only institute asking AICTE to increase the number of seats in the automobile discipline."

He added, "Now, I am sure students will also be able to get good placements and we will also able to contribute to Nano project's requirements."

Heading: All 4 foetuses found in canal are girls - Indian Express
Content:
Four unidentified persons allegedly looted cash and valuables to the tune of several lakhs from a vehicle on Kalupur bridge in broad daylight on on Sunday. The incident occurred around 8 am, the police said.

The looted booty belonged to an Angadia company, Gujarat Angadia, which has branches in Ahmedabad, Surat and Mumbai. "We are yet to estimate the total worth of the looted cash and jewellery, which may be in several lakhs," said P B Jadeja, Shaherkotda police inspector.

According to the police, Jeevan Patel (50), an employee of Gujarat Angadia, had brought people's cash and jewellery in two parcels from Mumbai. Three other employees of the company — Vishnu, Jaiyanti and Baldev — had come to the Kalupur railway station to receive Patel, who reached Ahmedabad around 6.30 am.

The four, along with cash and valuables, started for the Ahmedabad branch office of the company situated in Sardar Patel diamond market in Bapunagar in the company's Maruti van. When they were passing the Kalupur bridge, a speeding Qualis overtook the van, and came in front. As a result, Baldev, who was driving, had to apply sudden brakes, the police said.

"Three of the four goons got out of the Qualis and robbed the two parcels in the van at gunpoint," a police officer said.

Even before the victims could respond, the driver of the Qualis allowed his accomplises to enter the vehicle and sped away with the stolen booty.

Patel immediately phoned the owner of the company, Praveenbhai Patel, who later lodged a police complaint.

Shaherkotda police have registered a complaint and are on the lookout for the accused. "A newspaper hawker and a local resident have told us that the Qualis sped towards Naroda," Jadeja added.

Heading: Surat textile business falls prey to fake firms - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after the recovery of four foetuses from a canal near Rasana village in Deesa (Banaskantha district) it was confirmed that all four were that of females.

Preliminary investigations suggest that the foetuses found wrapped in a plastic cover may have been bio-medical waste. However, police are leaving no stone unturned saying that it may be more than just coincidence.

While the autopsy report is still awaited, the Superintendent of Police said: "Since all the foetuses have turned out to be of females, we are doubtful. The foetuses look to be three to three-and-a-half months old. But, it will be confirmed only after they are sent for further probe to forensic science laboratories. It is essential to know their age to check doctors' registers so that it can be ascertained whether the abortions were authorised or not."

Bhikhabhai Akediewala, the chief medical officer of Deesa Civil Hospital, said: "Presence of preservatives has been confirmed, which is why it is a possibility that it was a bio-medical waste or a hospital specimen."

Heading: Saurashtra villagers continue to fight salinity ingress - Indian Express
Content:
The incidents of textile firms vanishing in the city are increasing with each passing day. Several such firms have disappeared within a fortnight, badly affecting the genuine textile businessmen and processors in the city.

Kamlesh Patel, a textile factory owner at Udhna, had sold grey bales worth Rs 1.34 lakh on credit to Bhagirath Prajapati and Rajesh Rajput, the owners of Anjali Creations at the New Textile Market, a couple of months ago.

Initially, the owners kept on delaying the payment on different pretexts. And much to his shock, when Patel visited Anjali Creations two days ago, he found that the shop had been closed for four days. He contacted the shop owner, who told him that the place was given to Prajapati and Rajput on rent for six months.

Patel immediately lodged a complaint against the two with the Salabatpura police. Later, three other textile traders also lodged a similar complaint. The police said the cheating amount has been to the tune of Rs 4.70 lakh and it may go further up in the coming days with traders approaching them with the documents.

Jay Lalbhai, Secretary, Federation of Surat Textile Traders' Association, said: "The industry is facing a recession. We have requested textile traders and processors to do business only with veterans. We are regularly making the textile traders and weavers aware of the precautions that they should take while dealing with other persons."

According to Lalbhai, owners of the fake firms come to Surat with Rs 5 to 7 lakh and take a shop in the textile market. He said they stay in rented flats in posh areas of the city to create a good image in the market. The firm owners hire people with a good reputation in the market. After a month, the owners make him proprietor in the firm and later, the entire business dealings are done by the local person. After establishing their firms in the market, they purchase huge lots of sarees and dress materials on credit with the help of proprietor and disappear after selling it.

Jaylalbhai added, "We have found that generally the cheating is done in dress material business. The number of such incidents goes up ahead of Diwali."

Heading: ‘Bad roads, poor street light led to boy’s death’ - Indian Express
Content:
Salinity ingress in villages along the Saurashtra coastline has severely affected the ground water, besides destroying the fertile land in the region. According to a research, out of 954 villages located on the Saurashtra coastline, 359 are completely affected from salinity ingress while 177 are partly affected.

To cope with the issues related to the salinity ingress, farmers and village heads of the region recently gathered at the Junagadh Agriculture University (JAU) campus to discuss the problem under the banner of State Water and Sanitation Mission.

V S Gadhvi, Secretary, State Water Supply Department, told the gathering that during the early 60s, ground (sweet) water was available at around 20 to 25 feet deep. "But thereafter, en-mass irresponsible behaviour regarding water conservation has led to the prevailing scenario," he said.

Gadhvi sighted an example of Beria village in Jamkandorana taluka where villagers had solved the salinity problem with the help of 133 check dams built in and around the village. "People should not waste water. It is their responsibility to utilise natural resources cautiously. The ocean should not be blamed when humans are at fault," he added.

JAU Vice-Chancellor B K Kikani said: "People, particularly farmers, should utilise natural resources very carefully. The JAU had convened a farmers' meet at Mangarol on September 30, which was attended by over 200 farmers from 30 villages. Our research scientists and experts have delivered speeches on ground water conservation and its proper use in the coastal areas."

Kikani also said that people's active role in prevention of salinity ingress is inevitable. "Recharging of wells and water point during monsoon, connecting rivers with linkage canals, and use of drip irrigation system are some of the vital steps which need to be taken," he said, adding that the government along with its concerned department has already started works in this direction.

Considering the seriousness of the matter, the state government has implemented a coastal area development project designed to cover 300 coastal villages spread across nine districts.

In 2002, the government had formed the Water and Sanitation Management Organisation (WASMO), which works as the nodal agency to implement the project in partnership with the coastal salinity prevention cell.

According to the research conducted by WASMO, the TDS level in ground water in 379 villages of Saurashtra is over 2,000 milligram per litre, while 398 villages are partly affected where the level is below 2,000 milligram per litre.

According to a JAU research team's finding, in 1960, the salinity ingress had affected 12 lakh hector land, while in 2005, it rose to 89 lakh hector. Salinity has not only affected humans, it has also badly damaged agriculture produce and survival of livestock. Some villages have witnessed mass exodus due to the problem.

Heading: Agricultural, industrial, power sectors relieved as SSNNL in Madhya Pradesh releases water - Indian Express
Content:
Bad roads and poor street lighting could have led to the death of seven-year-old Mohammad Shad in Tandalja on Saturday evening, police said on Sunday. Deputy Commissioner of Police (South), B K Shrimali, echoed with the residents, who on Sunday said that more accidents will happen if the roads and street lighting in the area are not improved.

Shrimali said that he is planning to write to the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC), asking the body to improve the civic amenities in the area.

"The truck driver did not see the boy because he was trying to save the vehicle from the potholes. Although the people who gathered at the spot after the accident should not have reacted that way, they have been facing these problems for the last many years," he said.

The police are now planning to write a complaint to the VMC for neglecting the civic issues in the area.

"Our policemen also face difficulty in manning the area due to poor lighting and bad roads. Therefore, in a written appeal to the VMC mayor, we will cite all these problems for the safety of the residents in the area.

Adbul Zariwalla, who has a small grocery shop near the Sahil complex in Tandalja where the accident took place, said that only two street lights in the area function.

"The truck driver should have been careful. But personally, I will not blame the him. It is VMC's duty to build better roads and put more lights. The people who have visited the accident site should come at night. The cause of the accident will be clear then," said Zariwalla.

Heading: Pavagadh shopkeepers asked to vacate before October 24 - Indian Express
Content:
There's some good news for the industrial and agricultural sectors that receive water from the Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL). In the past few days, the SSNNL upstream in Madhya Pradesh has released 21,000 cusecs of water as per the instructions of the Narmada Control Authority (NCA).

After the water was released, on October 14, the level of water in the Sardar Sarovar Dam has increased up to 120 metre. This has served the purpose of power generation in six River Bed Power Houses (RBPH) and five Canal Bed Power Houses (CBPH).

Power generation was affected after the level of the dam in Narmada reportedly went down to 117 metre in the first week of October.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, SSNNL officers said the RBPHs stopped functioning from October 11 to 14 due to low water levels in the dam. But after NCA's instructions, water from SSNNL upstream was released from Omkareshwar and Indrasagar dams in MP.

"Now, six RBPHs are working round the clock and five Canal Bed Power Houses (CBPH) are working during the peak hours to suffice the needs of industrial and agriculture sectors this month," said an official.

Heading: 1 dies in ammonia gas leak - Indian Express
Content:
The Pavagadh Temple Trust has asked shopkeepers on either sides of the steps in the Machi area, which lead to Kalika Mata Temple, to vacate the area before October 24. Milind Torwane, Panchamahals District Collector and chairman of the trust visited the site on Sunday and issued the notice to all the shop owners.

Nearly 40 shopkeepers have already shifted their shops from the area, while there are 100 more who are still to move out of the area.

Though Torwane could not be contacted, the notice said that the encroachments are illegal. At a meeting with the temple authorities, Torwane called for strict action against the shopkeepers in the Machi area. The notice said that shopkeepers would be evicted if they fail to vacate before October 24.

The decision to de-clutter the Macchi area was taken during the recent visit of Justice M S Soni, who headed the commission investigating into the cause of the stampede that occurred in 2007.

Torwane had earlier said that the shopkeepers were charging exorbitant prices for various items. "We received complaints from several pilgrims and tourists that in order to keep up with the competition, the shopkeepers started charging a lot of money from customers. Water packets which cost Re 1 are being sold for Rs 5," said Torwane.

Heading: From Mughals to malls, this mime act has it all - Indian Express
Content:
Ammonia gas leak at Verma Gas Industries Private Limited (VGIPL), Ankleshwar, led to the death of a woman living near the gas factory.

Sharda Singh was inside her room with her son Srinath when ammonia leaked inside suffocating her to death. Srinath is admitted to Mahavir Hospital, Surat, for treatment. His condition is stated to be critical.

The incident occurred when a driver left his tanker that was filling up the storage tank. The tanker toppled on an ammonia pipeline thereby rupturing it. An FIR has been lodged under sections 304, 337, 378, 384 and 114 of the IPC against the owner and the truck driver, who is absconding.

The Ankleshwar police are investigating the case. The Gujarat Pollution Control Board and the Industrial Safety department has been asked to prepare separate reports on the case.

Bharuch District Collector Arti Kanwar said: "No dwelling should be allowed near factories producing ammonia."

Chlorine leak: EARLIER, the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) had issued a notice to Meridian Chemicals after a chlorine gas leak incident at Ankleshwar. It asked the company to submit a report about its safety standards. The company does not meet the safety standards set by the Department of Industrial Safety and Health (DISH), as it could not provide safety certificate after the incident, said V R Gadge, regional officer, GPCB.

However, he added that a third party, apart from DISH, also does safety status checks in industries.

Heading: Argument between landlord and Jordanian MSU students turns ugly - Indian Express
Content:
Five actors perform without any props or specially designed costumes

A MIME act directed by a city-based bank official has become the talk of the town. With five actors, who perform without any props or specially designed costumes, the act is aimed at paying tribute to the 'Sanskar Nagari'.

On October 13, P S Chari, a former student of the Faculty of Performing Arts of the M S University, directed the play titled Baroda — a tale of two cities, showcasing young artists curated by Sumali Gangopadhyay.

"Having lived in the city all my life, I was asked by the organisers of the exhibition to explore a number of themes, including history of the city. Therefore, we started with the ancient Jain culture of the city, then moved to the grand Mughal lifestyle and finally to the glorious Maratha rule," said Chari.

The cast, however, did not restrict their work to the history of Vadodara. They also portrayed the city in its present form. "Scenes from Kamatibaugh, which brims with activities from 5 am with roars of the laughter club and joggers sweating it out to loose that extra ounce to shady characters who roam around at night, bringing a whole variety into the small yet layered nature of the town," said Chari.

The act also depicts scenes of the typical traffic jams in the city, mocking at the petty brawls that start right in the middle of the road, to the newly developed shopping malls. Music in the act was performed by the students of MSU's Performing Arts, who revisited the Kirana Gharana based in Vadodara to rock and roll scenes of the city. "The music scene is so varied in the city, and we had to represent all forms of the music that co-exist here," he said.

Chari and his cast of five actors — Ashwin Parekh, Guddu Rana, Nikhlesh Patel, Paresh Thakker and Jalpesh Thakker — performed the play despite their busy working schedules. "Theatre cannot be taken up as a career, as it doesn't pay much," he said.

Chari feels that mime acting in Gujarat was a big phenomenon in the 80s, but over the years it has lost its old charm. "Professor Ramesh Bhatt was the only professional mime actor in the city," he said, adding that some school students have tried to promote the art in their own way.

"At present, there is just one professional mime actor in Vadodara, R Chawla, who was trained by Prof Bhatt in the eighties," he added.

Heading: Students highlight poor civic amenities in slum areas - Indian Express
Content:
A violent scene was witnessed at Ranavaas in the Fatehgunj area of the city when some Jordanian students of the M S University (MSU) had a fight with the residents of the society on Saturday.

The incident sparked off when the landlord of a Jordanian student, Ibrahim Mohammad, asked him not to allow his friends in the rented flat. The matter turned ugly due to miscommunication between the two, Sayajigunj police officers said.

Inspector D L Jhala said: "The incident took place on Saturday night when the landlord Vikas Rana asked Ibrahim not to invite his friends at the flat which was rented out to him."

A cross complaint was lodged by Rana's brother Hiren as well as Ibrahim on Saturday at the Sayajigunj police station.

One Pankaj Gana, who was injured when a mob from Ranavas pelted stones around 9.30 pm, said: "I sustained an injury on the head when the mob chased around 15 Jordanians who allegedly first hit the landlord. The Jordanians are creating nuisance in the area."

A family member of the landlord said: "It has been observed that Jordanians consume liquor and create nuisance. So we asked them not to allow their friends. They did not understand the language in which we communicated and hit Vivek Rana."

The Jordanian students, refused to comment on this issue.

This is the second such incident in two months where a tiff between the locals and Jordanian students has taken place.

In September, a group of MSU students allegedly beat up some Jordanian students, who later approached the varsity authorities and the police.

Heading: Civic bodies get ready to flex own cop muscle - Indian Express
Content:
Shedding light on the awful state of civic amenities in six slums of Vadodara city, students of Social Work Forum (SWF), released a report of their survey on 'Identifying the Gaps in the Services Provided to the Slum Dwellers' on Sunday. SWF is a students' body of MS University's Faculty of Social Work

The report was released following a panel discussion at Surya Hotel. City Mayor Balkrishna Shukla and varsity authorities were present on the occasion.

The report comes after 80 students from SWF conducted a two-day cycle rally in September, surveying six slum areas: Munjmahuda, Kishanwadi, Tusliwadi, Kalyannagar, Pensiopura and Jagnathnagar.

A student from SWF said: "Around 61 per cent of the total sample size, i.e. 349, do not have drainage facilities, 75.62 per cent do not have community bathroom facilities and 88.29 per cent live in two or less than two rooms. Most of the slum dwellers had cough and cold problems. There was a wide prevalence of malaria as well."

The mayor received the first copy of the report, which will be shared with the public later on, said SWF representatives.

Heading: CYG over, city Cong game for polls - Indian Express
Content:
We have given staff requirement, say PMC, PCMC chiefs; city police dept clueless

The state government is planning to arm civic bodies with a new police wing in its arsenal, which will function under various municipal corporations in the state.

To be called the urban police, they will enforce laws laid down in the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporation Act. They will penalise those those who flout the Act, like encroachers of government and civic land and those who illegally park vehicles on land belonging to civic bodies.

The urban police will have its own police stations. The chief of each municipal corporation will head its urban police department.

The step is being taken in view of rapid urbanisation and industrialisation leading to population concentration in cities, increase in encroachment upon government and civic land and mushrooming of illegal constructions.

The government view is that civic bodies would become a lot more efficient in implementing laws once urban police wings are set up.

In the past few years, mushrooming of slums, encroachments of land, land-grabbing and illegal parking of vehicles on civic land have been posing problems for the civic bodies in maintaining law and order. Besides, illegal constructions and encroachments have been coming in the way of development works.

At present, municipal corporations have to rope in city police to carry out anti-encroachment drives and prevent other civic offences. For this, they have to pay the police personnel. The proposed urban police will ease the civic bodies' dependence on them.

For setting up the civic police wing, local bodies will be able to recruit urban police as per requirement and the municipal corporation will have increased power to enforce laws once this agency is set up.

"The idea was floated by the state government's urban planning department. We have already given our requirement of urban police staff, to the state government. We are also ready to pay them salaries," said Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Commissioner Asheesh Sharma.

Additional Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane, however, said, "I do not know about the constitution or the purpose of urban police, so I cannot comment on it."

"The proposal has to be first passed by the cabinet. It will then be presented to the Home Ministry. Only then can the urban police wing turn into a reality. The setting up of an urban police force will also depend on how many municipal corporations give their positive response to the idea," he added.

The urban police would help the corporation in tackling the problem of encroachment by parked vehicles, Sharma said.

Pune Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi said, "We have given our requirement to the Urban Development Ministry. We have requested for 100 staff for the proposed urban police wing and a police station."

The urban police wing, once its is set up, will be the one to implement civic laws and penalise offenders. They would have special rights but their law-implementation rights will be limited to civic issues.

Heading: Rabi crop takes a hit, with key officers on strike - Indian Express
Content:
Party says CYG success will do wonders for it in the ensuing state and parliamentary elections

The success of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) — with MP Suresh Kalmadi as chairman of the organising committee — has put life back into the sulking city Congress as the party starts gearing up for the Lok Sabha and Assembly polls.

"CYG has been a success and will definitely benefit us in the polls," city Congress chief Abhay Chhajed said.

" The entire city unit was behind Kalmadi to make the Games a success. Our party cadres were involved in some way or the other in the CYG while the other political parties were working for the polls." The Games have put the city on the international map and the citizens are happy which, in turn, has shot up enthusiasm among party workers, said Chhajed.

Leader of the Congress in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), Ulhas Bagul, said citizens have gained while Kalmadi detractors have been silenced.

"There is no need of anyone to go and tell citizens about the Congress or Kalmadi. The public has enjoyed the Games and can themselves judge the contribution of party and its leaders to the growth of the city," he said.

The fresh wave of energy in the party, however, is likely to create problems as the list of aspirants for the Assembly polls is likely to increase. "There are definitely going to be many aspirants for the Assembly polls, but the ones with the best record will get the opportunity," Bagul, who is one of the aspirants, said.

According to political experts, Kalmadi has secured his position in city politics and would definitely make the most out of the successful hosting of the CYG. The praise for Kalmadi from various political leaders for the successful organisation of the CYG would go down well with the public.

Kalmadi has been the target of political parties in the city. The city NCP had kept the Congress out of power in the local civic body while going for an unconventional alliance with the Shiv Sena and the BJP. The ruling alliance had also rejected the civic administration's proposal to spend Rs 5 crore on the promotion of the Games. Hours before the Games, the NCP had not left any opportunity to criticise Kalmadi alleging him of hogging the limelight for the development of the city for CYG. "But the city MP has scored over all his opponents by strategically sharing the success of the Games with all political parties, especially the NCP," political experts observed.

Incidentally, Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, during the closing ceremony, was categorical in saying that Kalmadi had displayed his leadership qualities through the Games and managed to get "mileage" from it.

The city BJP has come down heavily on Kalmadi. "Kalmadi has misused the platform and it is evident from the political speech at the CYG.

If the Congress leaders are thinking that the CYG will help them, then let them remain in a fool's paradise," leader of Opposition in PMC, Vikas Mathkari, said.

"The citizens are intelligent enough to know that Kalmadi has done little for the development of the city as an MP and it was only due to the Pune pattern of NCP, Shiv Sena and BJP, that the city has taken the right path of development," he added.

Heading: Keep off anti-social elements: Muslim leaders tell youth - Indian Express
Content:
The rabi crop is set to take a beating in Pune and other parts of the state. The reason: assistant agriculture officers, who play a key role in ensuring quality crop production, are on strike and in no mood to give up till their demand of salary hike is met by the state government. Assistant agricultural officers are demanding that their basic salary be brought on a par with junior irrigation department engineers.

With the sit-in strike entering the eighth day on Monday, all operations, right from seed selection to seed sowing have been affected severely on 53.56 lakh hectare across the state.

"Everything has come to a standstill. Farmers are getting no tips on selecting the right kind of seed and technique to sow them in a scientific manner," said Sandeep Kevte, president of the Maharashtra Rajya Krishi Sahayak Sanghatana.

"We help farmers in practically every possible way to ensure quality and quantity of crop production," said Navin Borhade, secretary of the sanghatna, whose team concentrates on Maval area of Pune district. "Seed selection, seed treatment, land preparation, fertiliser selection, tillage operations and sowing are all monitored meticulously by assistant agricultural officers across the state. Since the strike began, these key activities have come to a stop," he said. The rabi season began in September. Pune is known for mass production of wheat and jowar while bajra, jowar, wheat and green pea are grown across the state. There are nearly 450 assistant agriculture officers in Pune and 11,569 in the whole state.

Not only has the strike cast a shadow on quality and quantity of rabi production, as many as 180 agriculture schemes sponsored by the state and central governments for farmers have also been adversely affected. The strike has also compounded the miseries of lakhs of labourers working under the Employment Guarantee Scheme.

Nearly 700 companies that supply seed to local and international markets are twiddling their thumbs as the seed testing laboratories have shut shop due to the strike. "The process of export worthiness certificates by labs in Pune and Nagpur has come to a stop. Without the certificates, export cannot take place," Borhade said.

Kevte said a delegation of assistant agriculture officers will meet Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh in Mumbai on Monday to press for a salary hike.

PM's Vidarbha package hurt
The strike has ground to a halt various government plans including disbursement of special Vidarbha package announced by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh last year. Because of the strike, farmers are not getting cows, bulls, fertilisers and seed.
The assessment work related to damage caused by the rain has also stopped in its tracks.

Heading: Delegates flood Asian Film Fest - Indian Express
Content:
Alleging that "a few people" were creating hindrance to the progress of the Muslim community, religious leaders from the community on Sunday appealed to Muslim youth to not get influenced by miscreants and instead concentrate on educating themselves.

"The Muslim community has been progressing, but there have been frequent efforts to pull it down. There are miscreants who want to stall development of the community and they should be kept away," said H M Shaikh, former principal of Wadia College.

Maulana Rajin Ashraf said the Muslim community was an integral part of the country and believed in its secular credential. "We have been contributing to the progress of the country despite being frequently ignored since Independence," he said.

Maulana Mohammad Ayub Ashrafi said the harassment of Muslim youth by the police merely on suspicion adds to the youth getting influenced by miscreants.

Shaikh said it has been noticed that the political parties take advantage of the opportunity and portray the entire Muslim community as a terrorist group for political gain.

The political parties instigate communal riots before the elections and spoil the secular structure of the country to create a rift between communities, he said, adding, "It should be understood that the Muslim community is not in favour of any particular party."

To stop the youth from being influenced by antisocial elements, Shaikh said they will try to bridge the communication gap through seminars.

The Muslim community is prepared to help the administration keep a check on the exploitation of the youth by miscreants. But it expects a proper treatment to others, he said.

Heading: Flamboyant Folk - Indian Express
Content:
Small to big
After countless appearances by big-screen stars on the small screen, it is now time for the small-screen stars to take the big screen by storm. The cast of Hats Off Production's popular show Jasubein Jayantilal Joshi Ki Joint Family will be setting a trend of sorts by appearing in a Gujarati film, Vanechand No Varghodo. The key cast of the show, including Swati Chitnis and Anang Desai, will shoot alongside Devang Patel, who is the lead actor in the movie. The team recently went to Ahmedabad to shoot the special sequence that will be seen in the movie. Maybe this pioneering effort will herald more big-screen-small-screen liaisons in the future.

Scarily predictable
TELEVISION's obsession with the supernatural is never-ending, it seems. The latest offering in the spine-chiller genre is SaharaOne's Kaisi Laagi Lagan. Mahi Vij plays the role of Pratha, who se family is cursed- that none of them will have a happy married life. But as fate will have it, Pratha does meet a man played by Asmit Kaushik with whom she falls in love. What happens next is anyone's guess, but it does involve Pratha overcoming the obstacles of age and time to bring the message of truth and love triumphing over evil. Did we hear somebody say 'same old'?

Heading: Small talk - Indian Express
Content:
With the grand finale of the grand games, CYG has marked another milestone in the history of the city. More than just the best athletes and the world-class infrastructure, CYG2008 showcased a vibrant cultural extravaganza too. While the opening and closing ceremony came along with mega celebrations, the other five days also witnessed grand festivities.

"This was the first ever international sport event held in the country. Having 71 participating nations, the idea was to bring forth the varied colours of our culture for everyone to witness and enjoy," says Shubhra Mehendirata, creative director of Rangpuhar, an event management company that organised the cultural programmes every evening.

"Being the hosts, we wanted the athletes to feel the family-like atmosphere when they win. Every evening we had a felicitation rally where the winning athletes saw the cheer and celebration for their victory. All athletes, foreign and Indian, whoever won medals that day sat in the carts among the bandwagon of dancers and performers representing diverse culture of our country," says Sanjay Mehendirata, director, Rangpuhar.

Apart from this rally the cultural centre at Balewadi stadium had different cultural programmes lined up everyday. "From jazzy DJ nights to cultural dance performances, there was a lot to keep the participants and guests entertain. Apart from this we also had handpicked handicraft artists from various regions of the country displaying their best," says Shubhra Mehendirata.

The main highlights were the Monestic Mass dance by the Lamas, from Sikkim and the Coolie Kali group from Tirchur, "We roped in the performers from their natives for which we also needed the support of their state administrations. Knowing it was for the CYG platform, we got good support from the ministry of culture too," said Shubra Mehendirata.

Every corner of the country has a fantastic act to offer, and that's what was showcased at the youth games. "Vibrant folk dance, artisans, handicrafts and more every part of India is blessed indeed. Our motto was to paint the city in the colour and spirit of games, and CYG, being such a grand affair, our goal was to put forth these glimpses of the rich heritage of the nation, before the world," she says. Although the celebrations are over, the essence of its success will stay for long.

Heading: Green Piece - Indian Express
Content:
Cheer and sports
Celebrating the sucess of Commonwealth Youth Games, that ended with a lot of cheer and enthusiasm, Stone Water Grill, at Koregoan Park . The restaurant called upon a party for the ones who were associated with the mega event. This was a night to unwind after a busy and eventful week at Balewadi. Curtains down
The closing ceremony of the Commonwealth Youth Games encompassed truimph and celebrations all over the city with a special laser show, art exhibition and fashion show at Ishanya The fashion show by Nivedita Saboo had models including Aditi Govitrikar and Anupama Verma captivate the audience with bridal and Indian wear. The show was choreographed by Aanchal Sachdev. Ther evening also saw dances and an enchanting Laser show. Heading: Tip of the iceberg - Indian Express
Content:
Paddy on the terrace seemed to be wishful thinking till Suresh Bapat made it happen at his home

Every morning as they sip their tea, the Bapats marvel at the paddy field in a place, which in normal discernment cannot be seen as an area of arable land. Right in the heart of the city and on the terrace of a bungalow are seen fully grown stocks of rice ready to be harvested, a sight that shatters all conventions of greater quantity of water and profound irrigable land required for paddy growth.

Despite having a full time career with Techno Serve, an engineering workshop, Suresh Bapat could not keep himself from trying farming on terrace, which was also well received and appreciated by the family.

Using 90 percent of vermicompost, six inch deep and over an area of 10 ft by 4 ft, with relatively modest water, 57-year-old Bapat claims to have encompassed several aspects associated to environment and garbage with this flourishing experiment.

Detailing about the technicalities of the venture and what inspired him to take up paddy cultivation, Bapat says, "I had been growing plants and vegetables for several years using the vermicompost generated from all the garden waste and wet garbage. This time during the rainy season I changed the old black fabric at the base of the beds. Mud and vermicompost was set again and the initial rains made the place marshy. That picture impelled me to think of a possibility of rice growth. We sowed around 1200 crops in July but were skeptic if rice would actually mature. Al the doubts were soon put to rest and you can see the crop standing now in front of you. My operators Sandip Jagade and Alpesh Betkar, who themselves own paddy fields in their village and were initially pessimistic about the advancement, were scandalised to see the progress."

"We will be harvesting in a few days but now we want to check whether rice can also be grown during the other season and hence we plan to sow our own grains again with hopes of a new crop," adds Sunita Bapat, wife of Suresh Bapat.

The green surprises continue as one wall of their bungalow is seen entirely covered with creepers that have been maintained for the last 25 years and have managed to elicit wonder from the passersby. Bapat feels such plantations are a necessity. "Garbage disposal is the biggest problem and the need of the hour is to undertake similar projects in everey premise. There also needs to be further research conducted on this. Basically rice growing does not demand much toil. Many friends and relatives have visited the place and even attempted to undertake similar plantings and vermiculture in their houses. In fact I do it for remaining physically fit, the rest of the good things come as side effects," smiles Bapat.

Heading: Court marshals - Indian Express
Content:
Sub zero temperatures and an ice bound existence notwithstanding scientist C G Deshpande, who recently led a team to the Indian research station in Arctic Circle, says he can never have enough of the Arctic

The degree of C G Deshpande's passion cannot be measured. Even if the man himself has measured all kinds of degrees, be it of temperatures or latitudes and longitudes. This Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) scientist is one of the few Indians who have visited both- the South as well as the North Pole. Deshpande recently returned from his research expedition at Ny Alesund- 8 degrees 55" N and 11 degrees 56" E, Arctic Circle working in temperatures as low as –3 degrees Celsius.

"We were a team of eight scientists who visited the Arctic Circle and I was the leader. This was our second research trip and was a part of the Indian Pole Year programme that started in 2007. My research was specifically limited to aerosol measurement in the Arctic region," explains Deshpande.

Arctic region is considered to be the biggest natural laboratory to conduct experiments and researches related to atmosphere. The credit however goes to the low pollution levels in the Arctic region. "Aerosols are the particles present in the air and they are present everywhere. The amount of aerosols in Arctic region is however going high due to continental pollution that settles down in the region," says Deshpande. He further adds, "The weather in Arctic region is very interesting. It is truly the land of the midnight sun. April to August is the time when the sun does not set which means there is light even during nights. Between august and October, the sun starts setting for five minutes and thus the duration of night that starts with five minutes, changes to 24 hours by October. October to February is again complete night. This characteristic weather has an impact on the aerosol concentration. For instance, during the summer, cool pure breeze flows from Arctic region to continents and in winters, the polluted air pours into the Arctic region from continents."

India is amongst 15 countries from across the globe and a part of four countries from Asia the other Asian countries being- Japan, China and Korea, to have been permitted to carry out researches in the Arctic region. Deshpande feels that it is too early to comment on the conclusion of the research, as it has just been two years since it started. "We are just recording the fluctuations in the aerosol levels. In fact India has also taken up a new task where scientists are recording the movements of the glaciers," adds he.

Deshpande has also been to Antarctica for carrying out similar researches and recalls some of the memorable moments of the expedition, one of them being the polar bear training. "The polar bear training is a must for these kind of expeditions. The polar bears are huge animals that weigh nearly 600 kgs. Their one leap measures 11 meters. They are not only dangerous, but also fatal to ignore because stories of polar bears attacking and devouring humans are quite regular in Polar Regions. We were trained to use a pistol and a gun to protect ourselves from the bears. In fact we were not allowed to leave the campus unless armed to threaten and in worst scenario kill the bears," he smiles.

The Indian station in Ny Alesund was recently named Himadri, and Deshpande also hoisted the Indian flag in the station. "Global warming is the much spoken about term these days and European and American countries are blaming us for the CFC (Chloro Fluoro Carbon) emissions. I am a scientist and not an authority to decide what actions need to be taken. But we all know that our emissions are much lesser than the ones by US and European countries. It is only researches like this that can prove our point to the world," he concludes.

Heading: Talk of the town - Indian Express
Content:
Judging is all about having a composed and unbiased mind, say the three Pune-based badminton judges of the recently concluded CYG

These judges belong to a different court. The fluctuating numbers on the scoreboards, other than the players' moves are a result of their decisions. Perfection is their domain for they cannot afford to make mistakes. Concentration, decision-making ability, unbiased judgements—it's a combination of these that makes an international judge and Sudeep Barve, Uday Sane and Vinod Badkundri the three international badminton judges from Pune, who are contributing their expertise at the Commonwealth Youth Games, know it only too well.

Badkundri was a badminton player during his college days and it was a wrong decision by one of the judges that made him lose a match as a player that decided his future career for him. "During one of the tournaments I realised that getting good judges was a very difficult task and decided to plunge into the field," he said. Barve was a badminton player as well and has an anecdote to support his career move. "During one of the tournaments, the judge did not turn up and I being a coach, was asked by the organisers to judge the match. From then on there was no looking back," he smiles.

What followed the decisions were countless certifications. While Badkundri is a Grade 1 Asian Badminton Confederation (ABC) certified judge, Sane completed his World Badminton Federation Certification in 2006. Barve says, "I completed my ABC accreditation in 2008 in Malaysia."

Amongst the 14 international judges in the country, the trio is extremely pleased with the kind of infrastructure that was made available to the players at CYG. "We have judged competitions across the worldand we truly believe that this infrastructure is world class," says Sane. Barve however points out, "The challenge is that we have good infrastructure for tournaments but the kind of courts that our players practice on are made of cement flooring. Coming to Balewadi for practice session is not always possible for everybody. It is thus important to create such facilities at various locations in the city."

The judges are optimistic about the future of badminton. Says Badkundri, "Saina is the first girl after Aparna Popat to bring about this change. And this is just the tip of the iceberg because there are a number of names like Aditi Bhutatkar and more ." Commenting on being able to create more world class players, Sane adds, "Badminton is a costly game and what is important for world ranking is collecting more and more points which in turn depends upon participating in more and more tournaments. Government support is extremely important."

Fourteen judges for a country like India might seem to be a small number but the judges are extremely satisfied with the count. "Only unfortunately we do not have any training institute in the country for judges except for the one by Government of Patiala where there is a six monthly course for judges."

Welcoming the shift of focus from cricket to other games, Barve says , "We all have been coaches and I believe that it is the responsibility of coaches as well as the students to make use of this trend. Coaches in India concentrate on skills but today's game is about pace and power. Other than the technicalities, fitness and spontaneity are important and if we concentrate on these aspects, glorious days are not far!"

Heading: COEP master expansion plan gets underway - Indian Express
Content:
Dental Care
To mark Oral Health Month (OHM) 2008 this October, Colgate-Palmolive (India) Ltd. and the Indian Dental Association (IDA) organised a free dental check-up for children from Pratham, the community based grass root organization that promotes education of underprivileged children. Model-Actress Sampada Vaze flagged-off the OHM Mobile Dental Vans in the city on October 16 and spent time with the children from the organisation, explaining to them the importance of good oral hygiene as they had their check-ups in one of the OHM Mobile Dental vans.

Food and fun
To mark the 'World Food Day' 25 children from Preet Mandir, a voluntary childcare and adoption organisation, wqere invited to the Royal Orchid Centre where the staff members welcomed them and ensured a memorable time for them. The kids were entertained with a series of shows. A Tom & Jerry cartoon movie was screened, followed by an entertaining magic show. And then after the entertainment package came the package apt for the on the occasion of World food Day. The kids were offered a sumptuous meal which they relished and are not likely to forget in ahurry. An admirable gesture indeed.

Diwali display
A mega NGO sale, at the Sharda Centre office on October 16 and 17 had 18 NGOs displaying their art and craft for diwali. The NGOs showcased a wide range decorative product. The exhibition had on display handmade items like lamps, candles, handicrafts, lampshades, stationary, handmade wall clocks, cushions, artificial jewellery, hand bags etc. The event was an initiative by Josh team which was organised and sponsored by Tech Mahindra for the welfare of the NGOs. Diyas, Sewa Sahyog, SAVALI, kite creations, Umang were some of the NGOs that participated in the two-day long fair.

The real visionaries
The White Cane Day was a day to not just reach out to the visually-impaired but also recognise the steel will that most of them have cultivated.A case in point being the members of the Poona Blind Men's Association (PBMA), who are a happy and a confident bunch, as amply evident on the White Cane Day function held last week. Lalita Pawar, 25, is from Thane and was born without sight. She has been staying at the institute for the past seven months. "I had not thought about education, but now that I am here I want to graduate so I can get a job as a telephone operator," she beams.Her best friend Parveen Pir Mohammed Sayed says, "I want to study the Naturopathy course that the Institute offers and work or start my own business on those lines."
These girls are vivacious, articulate and ambitious. With the aid of special equipment, computer software and their own Braille Press the Institute has instilled a sense of self-sufficiency in these people, which was evident as they enthusiastically participated in the festivities and felicitations.
Ask them of the most precious gift they feel thankful for and they chorus unanimously, " Our friends! Initially it is a little difficult for us to adjust but now we cannot imagine life without each other."

Heading: Former railway engineers support broad gauge for city’s metro rail - Indian Express
Content:
The College of Engineering Pune's (COEP) master expansion plan has finally seen the light with the girls' hostel expected to get ready within a month. The hostel will accommodate 400 girl students, said Dr Anil Sahasrabuddhe, director of COEP. This will be supplemented by a boys' hostel in the next couple of years. He was speaking at the first Global Meet of COEP Alumni Association on Sunday. "The phase one of this master plan to be completed in two years will also include developing the academic complex and library and knowledge centre and a guest house," said Christopher Beninger of Christopher Charles Beninger Architects Private Limited, who has designed and will implement the master plan.

Considering that the number of students studying in the college will go up from the present 3300 to 6500 in the next five years, the college has also planned a new boat club, auditorium, students' centre and additional housing for students and faculty. "All this keeping the college greenery intact, enhancing river connections and consolidating parking lots," Beninger said. "Our goal is to make the college 50 per cent self-sustainable in the next two years gradually moving to 100 self-sustainability," Sahasrabuddhe said. The architects have also planned a pedestrian plaza above the main road for students to easily go from one campus to another. "However, that shall become a reality only if the Pune Municipal Corporation and the state government supports it," said Beninger adding that the total master plan is worth Rs 250 core. "Of these, we are pursuing with the government to give us at least 25 crore, while the rest will be raised by the college," said Sahasrabuddhe. Meanwhile, the COEP Alumni Association has decided to send a memorandum to the Pune Municipal Corporation against the two proposed flyovers near Sancheti Hospital that shall disturb the college campus. Dr Pratap Raval, professor with Centre for Environment and Sustainable Infrastructure Development said that one of the flyovers would disturb the Electronics and Telecommunication Department of the College. Speaking about the future plans of the Alumni, Dr D J Doke said that the association shall come up with a classified list of COEPian Industrialists like the Yellow Pages, add a distinguished alumni chair for every department, increasing scholarship corpus so that about 3-4 lakh can be given every year.

Today, the alumni association has a total of 12,000 members including 6500 Indian members, 1500 from the USA and 3500 from the staff.

99-year old COEP alumnus
In 1928, term fee for civil engineering course was Rs 50 in COEP
. Perhaps, the only person to tell you this would be 99-year- old Keshav Shivram Joglekar, the oldest alive alumnus of the college, who graduated in the year 1931. Professor S Mandke introduced Joglekar in his absence during the first global meet of COEP Alumni Association, on Sunday. Joglekar couldn't make it to the meet due to personal reasons.
Joglekar, fondly called as Nanasaheb, had worked with V R Ranade and Sons for 18 years after passing out from COEP. "He had contributed in the construction of a couple of buildings during British period. He had also worked in Coimbatore, Rameshwaram and other parts of the country," said Professor S Mandke.
Later, he returned to Pune to become a licenced Pune Municipal Corporation surveyor and was instrumental in planning the bungalows on Prabhat Road. The government accredited him as a certified evaluation engineer. "He still writes the evaluation reports and has recently completed framing this year's report," Mandke said. Incidentally, the next two generations after Nanasaheb—Sadashiv Joglekar and Aniket Joglekar too are alumni of the College. Sadashiv is from the 1963 batch of mechanical engineering while Aniket is from the 1993 batch of Civil Engineering.

Heading: Post-CYG, PMPML to put CNG buses on BRTS track in Pimpri-Chinchwad - Indian Express
Content:
Around 25 former railway engineers gathered at the Indian Railway Institute of Civil Engineering (IRICEN) on Sunday morning to throw their weight behind the adoption of broad gauge (BG) for the Pune Metro Rail.

"We are happy that Vikas Matkari (BJP Corporator) has agreed to set up a meeting with the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC). We hope that all political parties from Pune will attend the meeting," said Vijay Rane, former managing director of Indian Railway Construction Company, who is pushing for the adoption of broad Gauge policy.
