Rane said that in 1853, when the Indian Railways was considering the gauge for the rail networks, it decided on broad gauge taking the country's population growth into consideration.

"It was Lord Dalhousie who fought for seven years for India to take up BG, when England itself was on Standard Gauge (SG). After all these years, we are thinking of going back to SG," Rane said.

Experts have been arguing that BG can carry more people at a more efficient cost than SG and is better suited for Indian conditions. Retired general manager of Indian Coach Factory B T Bhide said that it was wrong to suggest that metro coaches cannot be made in India. One of the reasons given for using SG coaches in India is that BG metro rail coaches are not made anywhere in the world. Only SG is available. "It is not a question of capacity, it is a question of priority. If they say that metro coaches are a priority then the capability exists in India. The ICF has manufactured metro coaches in the past. The Kolkata metro coaches were made in India. The impression that India does not have the capability to build metro coaches is false," Bhide said.

P V Gole, transport expert and former advisor to Metro Rail Urban Indian Metro Rail project, said, "It is the coach building companies that are pushing for standard gauge," he said.

Meanwhile, Matkari today reiterated that he will set up a meeting of experts with the DMRC. "Because of the accident in the Delhi Metro, it may be delayed. We will know in a day or two," he said.

Heading: Nagar Road Chamber is now Deccan Chamber of Commerce - Indian Express
Content:
As the Commonwealth Youth Games ended, at least eight Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses will ply on Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML)'s pilot BRTS route in Pimpri Chinchwad. The transport body will initiate a pilot run on a 13-km stretch between Nigdi and Dapodi. The PMPML will float tenders for the buses on BRTS route after studying the response of the pilot project.

The Maharashtra Natural Gas Limited (MNGL), which supplied fuel to the PMPML buses during the CYG, will continue the supply from its Chikhli pump at Chinchwad. "The pipeline work between Panvel and Chinchwad is complete and has been charged with CNG. For the first two-three days, CNG will continue to be supplied via caskets even at Chikhli as we are testing our compressors. From October 22, buses will be fueled using piped CNG," said Shama Sunder, managing director, MNGL.

The Warje pump, which fueled PMPML's CNG buses using caskets, was a stopgap arrangement for CYG. It will continue supplying the fuel to other vehicles, Sunde said. Pune is tapping the main pipeline between Dahej (Gujarat) and Dabhol (Ratnagiri) at Panvel. This 66-km long pipeline was completed before the CYG, except for a 3-km stretch on Dehu Road which is under defence land. With this pipeline work complete now, the Chikhli pump will supply piped fuel, a marked improvement from caskets which took 40 minutes to fuel one bus. "We need some basic information to float the tender. We will study the public response to the pilot project, the income, expenditure and profitability of the project. We are starting with eight buses, but will increase the number subsequently," said A Y Karche, joint managing director, PMPML. The company, which now has 19 CNG buses at its disposal, had initially expected 50 buses to arrive for the games. Now, the PMPML is expecting that the rest of the buses will arrive by month-end.

Heading: The Holy mood - Indian Express
Content:
The Nagar Road Industries Chamber of Commerce & Agriculture (NRICCA) has acquired a new identity and will now be referred as the Deccan Chamber of Commerce Industry and Agriculture. This was jointly announced by Yogesh Waghani and H. P. Srivastava, chairman and vice chairman of NRICCA in the 15 th Annual General Meeting yesterday.

The name change is being done to expand the scope of activities of NRICCA beyond Nagar road industrial belt, as more and more industries from various other industrial belts are keen on joining the Chamber, a release said. In fact few industrial houses from the Chakan industrial belt have already become members of NRICCA. Today NRICCA has over 186 companies as their members.

Noted law expert and member of parliament Ram Jethmalai was the chief guest for the function. Rathin Sinha, Surinder Agarwal, secretary and treasurer of NRICCA presented the financial report and summary of various initiatives undertaken by the chamber last year.

The annual awards given by NRICCA to individuals for their outstanding contribution in various fields were also presented on the occasion. Farhad Forbes, director, Forbes Marshall and Dinesh Munot, director, ZF Steering Gear received the Best Industrialist and Life Time Achievement award respectively . Ramanath Zha, principal secretary (Transport and State Excise) was awarded with NRICCA Award for Excellence – Public Service. In their speeches the awardees expressed confidence to deal with the current economic slow-down. Farhad Forbes stressed on the need to train the younger generation to deal with the tough times as many of them have not seen such a situation before.

Dinesh Munot expressed full confidence in Indian industry's capabilities to deal with such a situation as they have already done it in the past successfully.

In his address, Jethmalani appealed everyone to have courage to speak truth, which can bring about the change in today's condition which has poverty and misery in a large section of a society. Rajiv Kolhe and V. L. Malu, executive committee member proposed the vote of thanks and Yogini Gandhi anchored the show.

Heading: Toll collection: Villagers near Chandan Nagar border up in arms - Indian Express
Content:
Sikhs take out festive procession on the ocassion of Guru Granth Sahib tercentenary

MG Road wore a festive look on Sunday evening, Chants of Waheguru, Waheguru were buzzing all over the road as more than twenty thousand Sikhs participated in a two and a half kilometre long " Nagar Keertan" procession from Gurudwara Guru Singh Sabha in Ganesh Peth to Hollywood Gurudwara in Pune camp on the occasion of tercentenary of the holy Guru Granth Sahib, who the 10th and the last guru of the Sikhs, Guru Gobind Singh named as his successor. PC Pasricha former Director General of Police inaugurated the procession.

Keertans were played and crackers bursted. Lassi, cold drinks and sweets were distributed to people all along the way. Crowds gathered to watch Sikhs displaying traditional martial arts introduced by Sikh Gurus for self-defence. Kids dressed in traditional Sikh outfits could be seen riding on 40 horse buggies that participated in the procession.

Volunteers were seen cleaning the streets through which the procession passed. " We did not want other people to be affected. So, more than 150 volunteers picked up waste wrappers of eatables and other garbage from all the streets through which the procession passed. A water tanker also followed the procession to clean the streets," said Kabir Singh Sayal, Working Committee member of the procession committee.

Keertans and Langar will be organised at Gurudwara Guru Singh Sabha on October 23, 24 and 25 as a part of the celebrations.

Heading: Zensar Technologies launches new SL platform - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune-Nagar road constructed at the Chandan Nagar border has led to a blockade of a different kind. The villagers along the road and Ashoka Infrastructure Limited, the company that built the road, have entered into a dispute over the issue of toll tax. The villagers have been agitating against the company for collecting toll tax from them, even if they have to cross over to the other side within a one kilometre distance on the 54 km long road. Now, the company has pinned its hope on the proposal pending with the state government to resolve this long standing issue with local villagers. "According to the proposal, a monthly pass at discounted rate will be given to the villagers who have to travel frequently. They will have to pay Rs 31 for 50 trips. If this proposal is accepted, there is chance that this issue will be solved," said Sunil Raisomi of Ashoka Infrastructure Limited.

Since 2005, when the company was allowed to collect toll amount of Rs 31 for one side, the villagers have refused to pay. Last Monday, the villagers staged a rasta roko agitation when the company tried to enforce the toll for all. "Agitations have been going on, but lately the company has taken to filing court cases against individuals," said Anil Chonde, sarpanch of Wadu village. Chonde said that even if the villagers have to cross over to go to the nearby market they have to pay a toll tax of Rs 62 for both ways. "We have been telling them to issue monthly passes or return tickets for locals on a more economical scale, but they have not agreed," he said.

Over the last two months, the company has filed over 20,000 cases in the court against local villagers for not paying toll tax. "In the last three years we have filed 54,000 police complaints, but that didn't help. So now, we have started filing court cases," Raisomi said. According to the company, every day it has to let go of nearly 7,000 vehicles that refuse to pay the toll tax. "Some of them are local transporters who ferry commuters and goods along the road. They collect reimbursement but refuse to pay the toll," Raisomi said.

Heading: ‘Indian companies reevaluating disaster recovery strategy’ - Indian Express
Content:
The new 'Second Life' (SL) platform of Zensar Technologies Limited that allows users to enjoy various possibilities in the virtual world was inaugurated by Kiran Karnik, former NASSCOM president the other day. The new version allows users to create 'Innovation Park' on SL with features like recruitment, innovation, business promotion, induction, education and green Zensar.

Second life is an internet-based programme launched in 2003 and developed by Linden Research Inc. It is a downloadable client program, which enables its users to interact with each other through avatars thus providing a creative social networking service.

For instance, a 'Sandbox' has been created for passers-by, for those who want to innovate in the Zensar Innovation Park. The Sandbox essentially gives the avatar a chance to experiment and build assets to learn the art of creation on SL.

Ganesh Natarajan, Deputy Chairman and Managing Director, Zensar Technologies Ltd and Chairman NASSCOM said, "Zensar has a diverse workforce and global customers from across 14 nationalities in 18 countries, and the Zensar Innovation Park on SL forms an effective platform for the coming together of global teams. The platform serves a lot of our communication, training and learning needs".

Heading: Poacher arrested for killing tiger, aide absconding - Indian Express
Content:
Symantec Corp. the other day launched the India findings of its Disaster Recovery (DR) survey, a global research initiative that surveyed 1,000 executives worldwide. The results revealed key influencers driving Indian enterprises to reevaluate their DR strategy.

While a whopping 74 percent of the respondents claimed the rampant increase in virus attacks prompted them to revisit their DR plan, 68 percent are going in for a reevaluation to avoid data loss incidents and 54 percent to prevent accidental or malicious employee behavior.

Furthermore, continuous technological advancements such as virtualization and enterprise mobility have independently led 60 percent to re-examine their DR strategy on an ongoing basis.

"Disaster Recovery planning is not limited to virus attacks or natural calamities but various supplementary factors that hinder seamless business operations,''said Anand Naik, director, Systems Engineering, Symantec Corporation.

"Enterprises should identify, classify and prioritize critical assets for disaster prevention, detection, response, recovery and mitigation," he added.

Heading: Great injustice, says transferred officer - Indian Express
Content:
The CID West Bengal arrested a poacher on Saturday night in connection with the recent killing of a Royal Bengal tiger in Sunderbans. Another accused is still absconding.

A CID team led by DSP (Headquarters) Niladri Chakrabarty, SDPO Canning Debashish Sardar and Assistant Field Director of Sunderbans Tiger Reserve Anjan Guha on Saturday night rounded up one of the poachers Paritosh Mondal, who later confessed to his crime during interrogation.

The investigating agency had learnt that the suspects — Paritosh Mondal and another Panchanan Giri — were residents of Kumirmari island in Sunderbans. Accordingly, a huge contingent of police and forest department officials encircled the island and raided the houses of the two poachers located in Sharodpara village of the Sunderbans.

The officials recovered a firearm with one bullet and a suspected tiger thigh bone from the house of Mondal. An old tiger thighbone was found in his possession. "We will hand over the tiger thighbone to the forest department to ascertain if our suspicion is right. If they confirm that it is indeed a tiger bone then a fresh case will be lodged against Mondal," said Sanjay Mukherjee, Special IG, CID.

On reaching the house of Panachanan Giri, they found Giri to be missing. A musket with six bullets was found from Giri's house.

Mondal later led the team to the spot where the incident had taken place. Two fired cartridges were found from the spot - compartment five of the Jila forest in the core area of the Sunderbans tiger reserve. The CID believes at least one of the bullets has been fired from the musket recovered from the house of Panchanan Giri. The other weapon, which Mondal had used, is still untraceable.

During interrogations, Mondal confessed that both he and Giri had colluded in such poaching expeditions in the past. In fact, tiger claw marks on Mondal's body further indicate that this was definitely not his first encounter with big cats. Giri too, had been arrested in 2003 for possessing tiger skin. "It is not even 24 hours since the arrest. The interrogation is still on. Only at the end of the interrogation we will be able to know more details about the poaching nexus. A tiger carcass fetches upto Rs 22-25 lakh in the international black market and is exported to countries like Japan, Korea and China," said Mukherjee.

According to Mondal, they had shot the tiger around 5.30 pm on October 3, 2008. After firing two bullets, the tiger had leapt into darkness and disappeared. Sine they were scared of getting down the tree top from which they had shot the tiger, the duo waited until next morning. But when they alighted the next morning, they could not trace the tiger. They only learnt about the carcass from the newspapers. On tracing Mondal's antecedents the police found that he had been the prime accused in a case in the year 1999, which involved the murder of seven people, Mukherjee said.

On October 6, the body of a tiger was found floating on a river in Sunderbans. The CID was handed over the case on October 8. After visits by senior police officers on October 8 and October 10 in Sunderbans, two sub-inspectors of the CID set up camp in Sunderbans since October 15 in disguise and it was they who learnt about the location of the poachers. Three senior forest officials were transferred for failing to discharge their duties.

Heading: Mamata dares govt to stop Lalbazar ‘siege’ - Indian Express
Content:
A day after three senior forest officials were transferred in connection with the incidents of tiger poaching in the Sunderbans, S S Bist, who was shifted from the post of principal chief conservator of forests (wildlife) said it was a "great injustice" done to them.

"If transferring three officers could make our forests more secure, then so be it. We have been repeatedly asking the state government to fill up the vacancies of forest guards. Sunderban only has 49 forest guards out of 102 for manning 2,500 square kilometre area. Even the state armed police, which was deployed for forest protection in Sajnekhali (in Sunderbans) was taken away for Nandigram, and never brought back. The department's lethargy had led to a huge delay in releasing funds to the tune of Rs 70 lakhs provided by the Centre for tiger protection and we only got it on October 13," he said. "We co-ordinated with the CID so that they could track down the culprits," he added.

While former Sunderban Biosphere Reserve Director Pradip Shukla refused to comment on the transfer, former Field Director of Sunderban Tiger Reserve Niraj Singhal could not be reached.

Heading: BJP to go it alone in forthcoming polls - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee warned the state government on Sunday that the latter would be responsible for any untoward incident during her party's Lalbazar Abhiyan on Monday. The TMC will gherao the Kolkata police headquarters as a mark of protest against alleged police atrocities.

"We have planned a peaceful agitation tomorrow and will go ahead with it. The government will be responsible for any untoward incident on Monday. The state government should show restraint. How can the government decide upon the agitation of the opposition?" said Banerjee at a press conference at her Kalighat residence on Sunday.

Banerjee had announced her Lalbazar siege programme after a TMC leader's brother Swarup Biswas and other party supporters were arrested by police in connection with the attack on Charu Market police station by a mob. This was followed by a telephonic tiff between Leader of the Opposition Partho Chatterjee and Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti.

Mamata also accused the commissioner of Kolkata police, Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti, and state home secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti for siding with the ruling CPM. The Trinamool supremo said although she would not be present during her party's march to Lalbazar, she would join her party workers if things go wrong.

"I will stay at home and watch it over television. If something wrong happens I will join my party colleagues," she said.

Criticising the two Chakrabartis she said: "The commissioner and the home secretary are brothers and are siding with the CPM. They are behaving like card holders of the CPM. The police commissioner cannot use the language he used that day. He is a public servant and needs to be neutral. Why doesn't he drop his uniform and join politics?"

She challenged the CPM to dare stop her party's agitation. Referring to Saturday's DYFI rally, Mamata said: "The CPI-M should fight politically. They have lost their political ground and now after two years of rule they, along with the police, are terrorising Bengal. The CPM's youth and students' wing have planned to stop us tomorrow. Who are they to stop us?" said Banerjee.

The DYFI had held a rally in Esplanade on Saturday where it had announced that it will be organising street corner meetings throughout Kolkata and the suburbs against TMC's Lalbazar march on Monday.

Heading: To fight breast cancer, institute plans mobile check-up units - Indian Express
Content:
The state BJP on Sunday announced its decision to fight the forthcoming elections in the state alone. The announcement put an end to the chances of a pre-poll tie up with the Trinamool Congress in the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls.

"We were with Mamata Banerjee, but that was a long time ago. Everybody knows that she has severed ties with us. At this moment, there is no question of any alliance with any party in the state. If such a situation is created in future, we will see," said BJP state president Satyabrata Mukherjee.

In a press statement issued by BJP state vice-president Col (retd) Sabyasachi Bagchi, the BJP attacked all the major political parties in the state, including the Trinamool Congress, Congress and the CPM. The BJP also accused the three parties of minority appeasement.

It criticised the stand of the three parties on the police encounter in Jamia Nagar and stated that their stand may fetch them extra minority votes in the border areas of Bengal but will also "..give a fillip to an increase of infiltration of terrorists to this side of the border, endangering the Indian existence of West Bengal.." the statement read.

The statement also said minority-oriented votebank politics will be counter productive in Bengal as people would give a befitting reply.

The party expressed concern over the decrease in the water level in Haldia port due to insufficient dredging. "The demise of the Haldia port will be disastrous for the economy of West Bengal as well as entire north-eastern India. Hence we want the ruling Left Front and the UPA government headed by Congress to stop playing politics at the cost of economic development.." the statement read.

The BJP state unit also lauded the economic development during the NDA regime at the Centre, and at present in Gujarat under Narendra Modi.

Heading: Bali gangster arrested in raid - Indian Express
Content:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Cancer Research Institute with the help of the Central government will operate two breast cancer check-up vehicles to create awareness as well as to detect cases of breast cancer throughout the state.

"The vehicles will commence work soon after Diwali and will be equipped with facilities to detect breast cancer. We will work in the remote areas of the state," said Asish Mukherjee, medical director of the institute.

Every year, 12,000 to 14,000 new cases of breast cancer are detected in West Bengal. Despite this, very few people in the state are aware about the disease. "Initially, the institute will focus on West Midnapore district and Cooch Behar where there is very little awareness about the disease," Mukherjee said.

"Majority of the breast cancer cases are curable if detected in an early stage," the director said.

A free breast cancer check-up camp was also organised by the institute on Sunday, where more than 400 women were examined. Kolkata Police Commissioner Gautam Mohan Chakraborty, who was present on the occasion, said the police would team up with voluntary organisations to spread awareness about breast cancer throughout the city. "We will try to carry out the awareness campaign in other districts as well," Chakraborty added.

Heading: Couple escapes collision with Chief Minister’s convoy - Indian Express
Content:
The CID and the Howrah police have arrested Subhas Bhowmik, alias Buboon, a gangster from the Bali area, during a joint raid on his hideout on Delhi Road on late Saturday night.

The police said that two of his associates were also arrested during the raid and two-and-a-half kilogram of ganja was seized from their possession.

According to the police, Bhowmik and his associates had been eluding them for quite sometime. "Bhowmik is the most important member of the Bali-based Ramesh Mahato gang. He was wanted in several cases of murder and extortion," an officer of the Bali police station said.

Bhowmik is also the prime suspect in the murder of Bijoy Dutta, brother of a local Trinamool leader. Dutta was shot from a close range about a year ago. The police suspect the murder was done for political gains and Bhowmik was hired to eliminate Dutta. Bhowmik's associates Gourab Bhattacharya and Shiba Das were also allegedly involved in the murder.

"Bhowmik heads the extortion racket of the Mahato gang," said a police officer. "His main targets are builders, promoters and small-time businessmen of the Bali area," he added. The arrested were produced in court on Sunday. While Bhowmik was remanded in police custody, his associates were sent to jail.

Heading: Leopard carcass found on railway tracks - Indian Express
Content:
Love, they say, is blind. A young couple proved the idiom true, much to the distress and discomfort of the Kolkata police.

The youth, aged around 20 years, and his girlfriend, aged around 19 years were riding a bike on Nasiruddin Road at around 4:30 pm on Sunday.

According to police sources, the couple, oblivious to their surroundings, was crossing through Syed Amir Ali Avenue, when they almost collided with the convoy of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, en route to Nandan from his Palm Avenue residence. "They were probably very engrossed with themselves and did not realise that the Chief Minister's convoy was approaching," said a police officer of the Traffic Police.

The motorbike stopped barely inches short of the Chief Minister's convoy. Astonished policemen immediately intercepted the bike and took the couple to the Karaya police station.

"The couple was interrogated at length and their parents were contacted to establish their identities," said a police officer of the Karaya police station.

The police sources said the youth is from the Baghbazar area in north Kolkata and the girl is a resident of Barasat.

The police, however, do not see any malicious intention of the couple. "It seems to be sheer carelessness on their part that they intercepted into the CM's convoy route," said another officer of the Karaya police station.

Traffic is stopped on the road through which the CM's convoy passes.

Besides, traffic on all lanes leading to the road is also stopped until the convoy passes through.

"The traffic police in-charge for manning the crossing will be pulled up for questioning," said a source.

A senior police officer of Lalbazar, however, dismissed the allegations that the security of the Bhattacharjee's convoy was compromised.

Heading: Police gear up to control protest - Indian Express
Content:
The carcass of an adult male leopard was found near the railway tracks between Binnaguri and Banarhat railway stations in north Bengal on Sunday.

The mutilated body of the leopard was first spotted by a group of locals, who informed the nearby forest range office at 11.30 am.

The carcass bore several injury marks that indicated the animal was probably mowed down by a speeding train. "The tail and legs were severed and it appeared as if the animal was dragged along for quite a distance after it was caught under the wheels of a train," Divisional Forest Officer Tapas Das said. The carcass has been sent for postmortem and the forest officials expect to get the report on Monday. The Department has also lodged a complaint with the Railway authorities.

North Bengal has witnessed several frequent incidents of wild animals — elephants, leopards and bisons — being mowed down by trains. On August 11, the Alipurduar-Jhajha Express ran over a leopard in the Shongachi tea estate area of Malbazaar.

"This issue has been repeatedly taken up with the Railway authorities, but so far there has been no headway in this regard," said Das. According to forest officials, leopards often stray into tea estates in search of food.

Heading: Administration to deal strongly with Gorkhaland issue: Biman Bose - Indian Express
Content:
The Kolkata Police have made elaborate arrangements for the Trinamool Congress's plan to gherao Lalbazar at 11 am on Monday.

The police said more than 10,000 policemen will be deployed across the city to ensure that the Trinamool's Lalbazar siege programme does not go out of control. Deputy Commissioner (headquarters) Vineet Goyel said the police will take no chances and will be ready with full force to stop the Trinamool supporters from reaching Lalbazar.

All the entry points to the Kolkata police headquarters will be manned since morning. Forces will be deployed on all important roads leading to Lalbazar — Rabindra Sarani, Fairly Place, RN Mukherjee Street, Rani Rashmoni Avenue, Bentick Street, Tea Board and the South East gate of Raj Bhawan. "All these areas are entry points to Lalbazar and we will try to stop the agitators at these points," Goyel said.

After the Charu Market incident, several Trinamool supporters, including the brother of a Trinamool MLA, were arrested on charges of attacking the police station. Two days later, Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee had given a call to gherao Lalbazar to protest the arrest of her party supporters and the biased attitude of the police. Leader of the Opposition, Partha Chatterjee, also had an argument over telephone with the commissioner of police the same night.

"Apart from the usual weapons that the police use to stop such agitations, we are also keeping all other options on standby," the DC added.

Heading: Kolkata confidential - Indian Express
Content:
The administration will deal strongly with the present Gorkhaland situation and the party will also hold talks to resolve the issue, said Left Front chairman Biman Bose on Sunday.

"The state administration will deal strongly as far as the present Gorkhaland impasse is concerned,"

Bose said on the sidelines of the inaugural function of a new eye hospital on Tarak Pramanik Road on Sunday.

He was answering questions about the name of the state government being washed off on several boards of government offices by pro-Gorkhaland agitators. "There need to be talks on the issue and if necessary our party will also hold talks to resolve the situation," Bose said.

Referring to Monday's proposed Lalbazar march by the Trinamool Congress, the Left Front chairman refused to attach any importance to the program.

"This is a free country; one can go to Lalbazar, Keoratala or Nimtala. What can be done about that," he said.

He, however, made it clear that the administration would take stern action if the agitators tried to break law. Asked whether party cadres would be deployed to try stop the rally, Bose chose to remain mum.

Heading: Unable to fund treatment, man commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
On Diwali, Chini dia

Designer lamps for Kalipuja and Diwali came into vogue some years ago, replacing the traditional earthen lamps filled with oil. This year, however, cheap but effective electronic lamps are in demand. People are thronging shops to buy the "Made in China" lamps. A shopkeeper said the demand has been on the rise since last year. "This year, it seems even higher," he said. But why have people shifted from the traditional lamps? "It is less costly and less cumbersome. We save on oil and the lamps do not burn out or are put off by strong winds. What's more, this is a one-time buy and can be used in all occasions to decorate the home," said a customer.

Phone break

Though it dealt with some serious issues including the party's national poll programme, the recently held CPM Central Committee meeting failed to get the undivided attention of the party members. The bigwigs who attended the morning to evening sessions at Alimuddin Street were often seen on their cellphones ¿ even when the party's Delhi-based leaders were speaking. On two occasions, the conversations stretched for nothing less than 15 minutes. "We have a whole lot of important things to do and the meetings go on and on till late evening everyday," remonstrated a senior party member, "we just have to take an unauthorised break".

Overdrive

The recent arrest of a Bangladeshi criminal in the city has put the police on the alert — so much so that ordinary Bangladeshi tourists are facing a tough time. The problem came to the fore at one of the Central Kolkata police stations, where a Bangladeshi citizen had come for help. The man, who had his pocket picked near New Market, only wanted to lodge a complaint. But he found himself facing a battery of questions. After an hour of grilling, the man decided to give up and call it a day. "Your never know who's who. He may be a Bangladeshi criminal hiding here, you know," said a policeman at the station by way of explanation.

Collecting dues

Money has always been the one factor that united people with varying ideologies. This came to the forefront again in Singur, where cutting across party lines, people demanded that the Tatas come back. The pro-Nano lobby includes the so-called syndicate engaged in supplying materials to the Tata plant and some Trinamool and Congress supporters who were seen in Save Farmland rallies. Now, all are to be found at the temporary dharna manch set up by the Save Nano Committee. All have bills that the Tatas or the ancillary industries are yet to pay. "There is no other way to get our money back," said a contractor reportedly close to the local Trinamool leadership. The suppliers hope that even if the Tatas do not set up a factory in Singur, the agitation should at least help them get their dues.

Sweet and sour

It is well documented that the sacked Jet Airways employees had led the CITU procession at the Dum Dum airport to demand reinduction. What is not so well known is the arrangement CITU leaders had made to coax them to join CITU victory rally after the reinstatement. An array of sweets had been laid out to help Jet employees celebrate. For the record, the employees did gather at the CITU office, had the sweets, but implored CITU leader Dipankar Ghosh to let them go as the management had asked them to give the party a miss.

Heading: Super strikes light up mundane draw - Indian Express
Content:
Unable to bear expenses of his treatment, a man committed suicide at Shibnath Bhaduri Street in Shyampukur on Sunday by setting himself on fire. The police said that 58-year-old Kamal Das was bed-ridden due to a hip injury.

According to the police, around 6 am on Sunday, his family saw smoke coming out of his room. When they broke open the door, Das' charred body was found inside. He was rushed to a local hospital where he was declared dead on arrival.

Although no suicide note was found inside the room, locals said that Das had been depressed for quite sometime. Locals believe the man killed himself, as he did not have the money for his treatment. A case of unnatural death has been registered.

Heading: Whatmore, Amre coaches for Challenger Trophy - Indian Express
Content:
I-LEAGUE:Mohun Bagan, Mohammedan Sporting play out 1-1 draw in a match which both sides desperately needed to win to crawl up the points table

In Indian football, one often comes across matches that could put you to sleep, but for a few brilliant moments that stand out as silver linings against the otherwise mundane run of play.

Desperately hungry for full points, Mohun Bagan and Mohammedan Sporting played out a typically unimpressive draw in their I-League Premier Division encounter today. But in the course of the 1-1 scoreline under lights at the Yuba Bharati Krirangan, two lip-smacking goals were scored — both in the first half of the match — that stood out as the highlights of the day's action and will be remembered for a while.

With their key players like Baichung Bhutia and PC Lalawmpuia sidelined with injuries, Mohun Bagan were up against the odds in their pursuit for their opening victory in the I-League. Of late, Mohammedan Sporting have been their bogey team. Anyway, Bagan haven't opened the scoring in key matches in recent times, and coach Shabbir Ali's boys cashed in on the odds stacked up against Mohun Bagan.

The black-and-white brigade opened the scoring very early into the match, as Theodore Sunday expertly set up Goutam Thakur who found the back of the Bagan net just 3 minutes into the action. And Bagan, no stranger these days to trailing for most part of the match, fought back through their trusted lietenant Jose Ramirez Barreto. The Brazilian slammed his critics shut with a stunning 24th minute volley strike to bring Bagan back into the match.

But for these two goals, the match saw the usual slump from a lively start to a whimper of a finish, with plenty of opportunities being wasted.

In the end, both the teams were left dissatisfied with split points, having gone into the match with just one point from three outings each.

The opening goal showed how heavily Md Sporting rely on their foreigners. The goal went to Thakur, but the credit for setting it up goes to the duo of Mike Okoro and Sunday. Barely had the Mohun Bagan defence settled down when the crafty Okoro sent out a pass to Sunday in the goal box. Sunday, instead of taking a shot, didn't let go of the ball, drawing the Bagan defence and goalie Shilton Paul out of position. That's when he pushed the ball from the right to an unmarked Thakur on top of the goal box, who simply placed the ball in. A lazy Deepak Mondal limply attempted a goalline save, and in vain.

Down by a goal in the 3rd minute, Mohun Bagan reacted with alarm, pounding the Md Sporting goal area with booming centres, only to be frustrated by the black-and-white defence and an enterprising goalie in Tharangachan.

Finally, 24 minutes into the first half, it was Bagan's old warhorse Barreto who drew parity and brought relief for a visibly distraught coach Karim Bencherifa. Yet again, the credit for assisting the goal goes to Malsawm Tluanga, who sent across a well-judged pass to Barreto from the far right. Barreto, instead of taking his time with the ball, simply chose to get rid of it on the volley. He trapped in, tossed it up a little, and fired a measured right-footer.

It was a delectable goal, and it could only have come from someone of the class of Barreto, who finally justified the faith that rests on him, particularly after messing up two identical headers shortly after Md Sporting opened the scoring.

Barring the two memorable goals, there was nothing else too savoury about the match. There were two clear chances that came Md Sporting's way in the second half, but an unusually lazy Okoro couldn't make them count, letting Mohun Bagan off the hook in what could have been a lost cause any other day.

Heading: Double crowns for Nagaraj, Settu - Indian Express
Content:
It's not just about Yuvraj Singh versus Mohammad Kaif, or S Badrinath against Cheteshwar Pujara. The upcoming NKP Salve Challenger Trophy is also a battle for supremacy among India's high-profile coaching aspirants-Dave Whatmore, Praveen Amre, and the lesser-known Bharati Arun.

All three veterans are seasoned campaigners associated with the National Cricket Academy (NCA) in Bangalore. And they will now be spearheading the three teams in the Challenger Trophy to be played in Cuttack next week.

Whatmore has been picked coach of the India Blue team, which will be led by Yuvraj Singh. Praveen Amre will be the coach of the India Reds, whose captain is Badrinath. And the India Green side, with Kaif as their skipper, will have Arun as coach, sources in the BCCI told The Indian Express.

The three teams will take each other on in a round-robin basis in day-night 50-overs-a-side matches, and the tournament will be played at the Barabati Stadium in Cuttack from October 23 to 26.

Whatmore's induction into the high-profile tournament as coach of one of the teams has added colour to the event, which serves as an annual platform for the national selectors to get a hang of the fringe talent in the country. The former Sri Lanka coach, who revolutionised the island country's performance in modern-day cricket before taking up the Bangladesh job, is currently associated with the NCA as its coaching director.

Amre, the India Reds coach, too has been around as a popular coach for years now, having served as the Under-19 India coach at successful ventures.

Arun, meanwhile, has been coach of the Tamil Nadu and Bengal senior sides in the Ranji Trophy, and is currently the bowling coach of the NCA.

The Challenger Trophy will be played alongside the more intensively followed India-Australia Test series. But the Krisnamachari Srikkanth-led selection committee and the BCCI top brass will closely follow the action in Cuttack. The tournament is expected to help the selectors out in spotting talent ahead of the coming India-England home series in November-December.

Heading: ‘Launch campaigns in schools, colleges’ - Indian Express
Content:
R Nagaraj of Mysore and S Settu of Chennai won double crowns at the 2nd GVK-AISTA Senior National Ranking Tennis Tournament at the Calcutta South Club. Fourth seed Nagaraj won the Senior Singles 45+ years finals defeating second seed Yogesh Shah from Ahmedabad 6-2, 6-0. Partnering RV Rama Raju from Hyderabad, Nagaraj beat the top seed Andhra pair of V Srinivas Reddy and K Meher Prakash 6-2, 6-1 to lift the doubles trophy.

In the Senior Singles 55+ years fifth seed Settu too the title beating top seed V Rama Mohan Rao of Hyderabad in three sets 3-6, 6-3, 6-2. Settu then paired up with A Rambabu from Hyderbad to take the doubles crown beating TAPN Rao of Andhra and K Radha Krishnamurthy of Vijaywada 6-4, 6-2.

The Senior Singles 65+ years was won by fourth seed VR Kulkarni of Karnataka at the expense of sixth seed Kesava Perumal 6-1, 6-1.

Senior Doubles 65+ years crown went to the top seed pair of CB Raju from Hyderabad and Akhtar Ali of Kolkata. They defeated the fourth seeded pair of S Muthu Kumaraswamy and Kesava Perumal 6-2, 6-3.

Final results:

Senior Singles 45+ Finals : R. Nagaraj (Kar)(4) beat Yogesh Shah (2)(Guj) 6-2,6-0.

Senior Singles 55+ Finals : S. Settu (5)(TN) beat Dr. V. Rama Mohan Rao (1)(AP) 3-6,6-3,6-2.

Senior Singles 65+ Finals : V.R. Kulkarni (4)(Kar) beat Kesava Perumal (6)(TN) 6-1,6-1.

Senior Doubles 45+ Finals : R.V. Rama Raju (AP) & R. Nagaraj (Kar)(2) beat V. Srinivas Reddy (AP) & K. Meher Prakash (AP)(1) 6-2,6-1.

Senior Doubles 55+ Finals : A. Rambabu (AP) & S. Settu (TN)(1) beat T.A.P.N. Rao (AP) & K. Radha Krishnamurthy (AP)(2) 6-4,6-2.

Senior Doubles 65+ Finals : C.B. Raju (AP) & Akhtar Ali (WB)(1) beat S. Muthu Kumaraswamy (TN) & Kesava Perumal (TN)(4) 6-2,6-3.

Heading: Make presumed consent a law for organ donation, say experts - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Baldev Singh Aulakh heads the Renal Transplant and Urology Department at the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital. A pioneer for the promotion of cadaver donation, he shares his thoughts regarding organ transplantation with Sameer Kumar Sharma

Ques* You are spearheading the organ donation awareness campaign in the state. What is your strategy?

We need to send this message to the people of the state and sensitise them. We have already started a campaign in schools and colleges of the state.

Ques* But political will is necessary to get substantial results.

That is right. And that is why conferences like the one we organised in association with Indian Society of Organ Transplant (ISOT) can go a long way in arriving at some conclusion so that laws can be made and process simplified. The CM has also agreed to work towards this cause and we will submit a report to the government over what can be done by the state government. Leaders who participated in the conference will also spread this message around. Religious leaders can also play an important role.

Ques* What is the organ donation scenario in the state as regards cadaver donation?

It is nil. There has been no cadaver donation in the state insofar as my knowledge is concerned. In fact, it has been almost non-existent in the country, let alone the state. I have done over 1,000 transplants so far in my career spanning 14 years but all these were carried out from living donors.

Ques* How can the gap between demand and supply be bridged?

There is a demand of about 1.5 lakh kidneys every year but due to scarcity of donors, only a very few of them (3000-5000) get kidney transplants. This can be dealt with only when there is sufficient number of cadaver donors.

Heading: Police pull up banks, call for more security - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing his opinion on organ transplantation in the country, Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda said it was wrong that while Amritsar-based Dr P K Sarin was prosecuted in the kidney racket case, the recipients were not.

"I think Dr Sarin was wronged, as even some bureaucrats had received organs," he said. Dhanda was speaking at a panel discussion during the 19th Annual Conference of Indian Society of Organ Transplantation (ISOT) on Sunday. The discussion focused on legal, ethical and social issues in organ transplantation.

Dhanda said, "Organ donation needs to be clearly defined and presumed consent of a deceased should be made a law since we cannot let human organs go waste after death."

N P S Aulakh, DGP, Punjab said: "Several people lose their lives in road accidents across the state. Instead of letting them go waste, their organs can be used for transplantation purposes. "

He added: "In the last year, over 3,000 people died on roads in accidents. If there is a presumed consent in such cases, organs can be used for the mankind."

"We can also mention a declaration of such consent on driving licences to facilitate cadaver donation," he said, admitting that police personnel should be made aware of Transplant of Human Organ Act. "There were only 13 cases registered under Transplant of Human Organ (THO) Act in the state in the last year," said the DGP.

Most of the speakers from judiciary, legislature and executive, who participated in the conference held in the state for the first time, agreed to make presumed consent of the clinically dead person into a law so that their organs can be used to save lives of others.

Dr S S Sandhu, Chief Principal Secretary to Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, sought to alleviate apprehensions against the organ transplantation. "Since transplantation takes a religious overtone in our country, people are against it. They should know that why it is important and it is not against the religion," he said. "Once masses become aware, we can go in for legislation of presumed consent," Sandhu added.

Representing media in the conference, Rajat Sharma, chairman and editor-in-chief of India TV, said there is a need for enhanced communication between media and doctors to spread awareness about the transplantation. "Doctors should inform the media so that we can also highlight the donors and their families," he added.

KS Grewal, justice Punjab and Haryana High Court, MS Grewal, ex-minister medical education, Dr BS Aulakh, organising secretary of the conference, were also present at the conference.

India should learn from Spain, says UK doctor

Sir Peter Morris, renowned Surgeon and Director of Oxford Radcliffe Hospital of UK, said,"I have been visiting India for the past 15 years and nothing concrete has happened in the country for cadaver donation." He added:" India can benefit a lot through cadaver donation. We have been holding discussions and the transplant community has been meeting regularly, but this has not not gone any further. The government should devise a plan to persuade the public to accept this." Indian can take inspiration from Spain where more than 95 per cent of the organ donations are through cadaver donors, Morris added.

Heading: Hospitals full, dengue surges on - Indian Express
Content:
Following the last week's unsuccessful attempt of robbery at a local bank, the Ludhiana police have issued fresh directives to all the banks in the city for taking safety measures in their premises.

While the police have been criticised for not being able to check the repeated incidents of thefts at various banks, it has also been found that a few banks had not taken safety measures issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

Senior Superintendent of Police R K Jaiswal said he had recently held a meeting with representatives of various banks after the unsuccessful robbery attempt at Tagore Nagar branch of the Oriental Bank of Commerce. Last year, two unidentified youths had snatched Rs seven lakh from the employees of same bank on gunpoint.

Jaiswal said all the banks had been asked to install the sirens, as at many of the banks sirens did not work, when miscreants barged into the premises. Banks had also been asked to inform the police in advance when their security guards were going on leave so that alternative security may be provided to them. In March 2006, a survey was conducted on local banks of Ludhiana, which had found many banks were not following the police directives to ensure safety. For example, at a bank, a security guard was found counting the cash instead of standing at the entry point, while another guard had gone to get some papers xeroxed.

Cases of bank robbery

October 10, 2008: Unsuccessful attempt to theft at Oriental Bank of Commerce (OBC), Tagore Nagar branch.

September 2007: From the same bank, two unidentified armed youths snatched nearly Rs seven lakh from employees.

February 16, 2005: Unsuccessful attempt at Salem Tabri branch of OBC. Miscreants tried to cut the vault by a gas cutter.

January 30, 2005: Unknown thieves enter Madhopuri branch of Central Bank. Use gas cutter to open the locker, could not succeed.

January 12, 2005: PCR team foiled a robbery at the Ferozepur Road branch of Bank of Allahabad.

Heading: Consumer body fines college - Indian Express
Content:
Dengue cases have increased further as the influx of patients shows no slowdown in hospitals even a month after the disease began to spread in the district.

City hospitals are facing problems in serving the patients, who are pouring in large numbers every day. Hospitals are fast running out of beds and blood availability has hit all-time low. The Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) has been admitting nearly 50 to 60 patients every day. The hospital has already registered about 1,300 patients so far. A few hospitals have already reportedly stopped admitting symptomatic patients.

Residents are also complaining about the lax attitude of the municipal corporation in undertaking the fogging operations in various parts of the city. Worse, the temperature has been hovering around 30 degree Celsius for quite some time now. Experts say this temperature is best for the mosquito's survival and there may not be any relief soon.

Of over 2,000 patients of dengue reported in the state, over 14,00 cases are claimed to be from the district. The Health department, however, has confirmed 1144 cases till Saturday. Three deaths reported in the last couple of days are suspected to be due to the dengue.

Jang Bahadur of Shimlapuri reportedly died on October 18 at the DMCH. Saraswati (10) of Jeevan Nagar died on October 17 evening. While the third death has not been reported at the hospital, it is suspected that Mahinder Singh (24) of Giaspura also died of the disease. The health department has confirmed four dengue deaths in the district so far, while another death, that of Sunny (24), who reportedly died on October 16 evening has not been confirmed by the department so far.

Heading: Sexagenarian feeds 250 stray dogs a day, shelters parrots, gets US award - Indian Express
Content:
A full bench of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Punjab at Chandigarh recently pronounced a verdict against Punjab medical Institute and Hospital of Electropathy and its affiliating body called NEHM of India, New Delhi.

The commission imposed a fine of Rs 50,000 on the institute for misleading people by falsely inserting the authority of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt of India, while the affiliating body (NEHM of India) is imposed a fine of Rs 1,00,000. Out of this amount, Rs One Lakh will go to the complainant as compensation and also to meet his litigation cost. The Commission also ordered to send the copy of this judgment to the Delhi High Court for initiating contempt proceeding against the respondents for violating an earlier order of the court.

Heading: Lucknownama - Indian Express
Content:
Kukku Bakhshi, an animal lover, would never have imagined that his concern for stray dogs would fetch him an award. Supreme Master Ching Hai International Association, a USA-based Non Government Organisation, conferred him with Shining World Compassion Award, recognising his love for lesser beings, even as the 62-year-old feeds over 250 stray dogs a day.

Bipin Jayantilal Thosani, who represents the NGO in Bombay, said," Our association decided to award him after reading a report in online edition of Ludhiana Newsline on March 25." The report mentioned Bakhshi's love for dogs.

Thosani added, "Ching Hai, the NGO's founder and a renowned humanitarian, a spiritual teacher and accomplished artist), also appreciated Bakhshi's efforts. Later, I and my colleague came from Bomaby to confer him with this award. Bakshi is the first person in the state to get this award."

Bakhshi was awarded with a plaque and $1000.

His day begins at 4 am, as he packs his bags with biscuits, buns and milk packets and leaves for his destination on a rickshaw to feed stray dogs. "I carry 60 bowls with me to give them milk, biscuits and buns. I buy 30 litres of milk and several packets of edibles a day," Bakhshi said. "I spend nearly Rs 1000 daily to feed these dogs. While sometimes people donate some eatables, mostly I arrange these on my own largely through the pension of my father," he added.

His love is reflected in the fact that he has assigned a local bakery to prepare special biscuits for dogs, that contains sulphur. Only son of his parents, Bakhshi is unmarried. "A few years ago, I lost my mother and now I stay with my father and take care of him," he said.

His love for animals is all too evident as you make your way to his house through a street in Kareempura Bazar. You come across bowls of milk and biscuits which he has kept for dogs. He has given shelter to seven cats, five parrots and a dog in his home. And clean beddings for all of them. As he reaches near the parrots, they start shouting, "Kukku... kukku...." He gives big bowl of milk with "desi ghee ki choori" and eggs to his cats. "All of them recognise me and have become my friends," he said.

Thosani has suggested him to think beyond mere feeding the animals. "We advised him to spend some part of the award money on giving anti-rabbies injections to stray dogs and tie a tag around their neck that these dogs have been vaccinated."

Expressing gratitude for Poonam Kalra, founder of another NGO Hope, and the USA NGO, Bakhshi said, "I am pleased that someone recognised my service to lesser mortals."

Heading: No smooth sailing for rail factory at Rae Bareli yet - Indian Express
Content:
Wearing party on the sleeve

It is a democratic convention the world over that a person ceases to belong to any particular political party after he is elected to the constitutional office of the speaker. A few months ago, Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee refused to bow to CPM diktat. In Uttar Pradesh however, there is little respect for such high conventions. Assembly Speaker Sukhdeo Rajbhar is often seen at BSP programmes. In fact, last week, he attended three events organised by the BSP to woo the Muslims, the OBCs and economically backward sections of the upper castes.

No trickledown effect

Union Water Resources Minister Saifuddin Soz has sent a letter to all chief ministers requesting them to prevent the wastage of packaged drinking water. He has pointed out that usually one litre water bottles are served in official meetings, seminars and public functions and most of it goes waste because the participants drink very little. Soz has, therefore, suggested that bottles of 200 ml be served. But despite his initiative, the letter is yet to be circulated among the secretaries and principal secretaries in UP. Obviously, even simple things don't get done easily in government.

The other option

On Sunday morning, Information Department officials were mortified to find that reporters of television news channels were missing at the BSP convention on "The problems of upper castes, causes and solution," which Chief Minister Mayawati was to address. It turned out that Samajwadi Party president Mulayam Singh Yadav had called a media conference at the same time, and most of the reporters had gone there. The reasons were obvious. This was the BSP's third such convention in a week and nobody expected it to make great news. But Mulayam Singh was meeting the media after quite some time. Besides, unlike Mayawati, Singh is easily accessible and answers media queries which can make a good copy. For the babus, however, it came as a revelation that reporters would prefer an opposition leader to the chief minister.

SOS heard?

A senior minister in the BSP government, waiting for his flight in the VIP lounge of the Delhi airport, had an interesting encounter with a bureaucrat who was recently chargesheeted by the CBI in a corruption case. To his great surprise, the babu began with falling at his feet. Then getting up, he began his tale of woe, which continued through the bus ride to the aircraft. What is yet to be known is whether for all his pains, he received any assurance of help.

Once bitten

It was a piquant situation for Higher Education Minister Rakesh Dhar Tripathi outside CMS auditorium last Saturday. The honourable minister wanted to cross a barricade to reach the gate through which Chief Minister Mayawati was to emerge after the BSP convention on problems of SCs/STs and OBCs. But a policeman stopped him, saying, "The CM is coming out shortly, you can't go there". The minister argued but to no avail. Looking upset, he walked away, muttering, "because of people like you, others get a bad name". The policeman was not one to back down. "I once got a scolding for allowing someone like him. I won't make the same mistake again," was his loud riposte.

Paper trail

The Lucknow jail authorities recently learnt that Sabaudin, a terror accused in their custody, is well informed about the developments in the world outside. The jail officers were on tenterhooks for days regarding his source of information. Did it indicate a breach in the jail's security system? Finally, one of them accosted the accused with a direct question. And the answer left him flummoxed. "Sir, you give me two newspapers daily," said Sabaudin, "since I have nothing else to do, I read everything printed there."

Password

In the BSP regime, the very mention of "Behenji" can work miracles. An official at Kanshi Ram Memorial, which is coming up on Jail Road, felt that a contractor was taking too long to polish the stones at the entrance. He asked him to speed up the work ¿ in vain. So one morning, he spread the word that the "Behenji" would be inspecting the project that evening. Lo and behold, the work was finished on time. Of course, the "Behenji's" visit is still awaited.

Heading: Police had faked Delhi encounter: Mulayam - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh government's decision on Saturday to give back 189.25 hectare land for the proposed rail coach factory at Rae Bareli may not be the end of the controversy.

Officials said since the land has now been given on a lease for 90 years, the paperwork done after the initial "allotment on resumption" from the gram sabha has become irrelevant. Officials in the state government and the Railways said the land allotment on a lease and land allotment on resumption were two different things. Therefore, the terms and conditions of the lease and other details will have to be worked out by mutual agreement by the two sides. After that, fresh paperwork will have to be done.

Ambrish Srivastava, Sub-District Magistrate of Lalganj where the factory site is located, said: "The land was earlier given on resumption basis and we had calculated the amount accordingly. But, giving it out on a lease would require new paperwork and a new set of calculations and guidelines. Then, we have to seek the approval of the state government after which it would be sent to the Railways.

This process may take six months."

Sources in the Railways said the Mayawati Cabinet's decision on Saturday, in effect, reopened the land issue, but in a different way. Negotiations to work out the details of the lease agreement could drag on, delaying the project. "A new set of guidelines and formalities mean that even if there is no hitch, the project could be easily delayed by one year. Thus, in an indirect way, it would ensure that the project does not take off as scheduled. This is yet another hindrance," a railway official said.

Sources said the Railways were consulting legal experts and the matter might be raised before the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court, which is scheduled to hold a hearing on October 22 on the petitions filed by the Railways and some farmers against the cancellation of land allotment. At the last hearing on October 13, the court had directed the state government not to change the Railways' possession of the land, nor to give the land to anyone else.

Heading: ‘Victim’ alive, but 4 men to be tried for murder - Indian Express
Content:
Not giving up his party's demand for a judicial probe into the encounter at Delhi's Batla House area in which two suspected Indian Mujahideen operatives were killed, Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav on Sunday warned the Congress-led UPA government that delay in taking a decision could turn the public opinion against the ruling alliance and alienate the minorities.

"Confusion prevails over the police encounter among the common people, particularly the Muslims. An inquiry will clear the confusion and help the UPA government to remove the suspicion," Yadav told reporters.

"According to my information, the Delhi police had organised a fake encounter at Batla house," he added.

As for the death of a Delhi police inspector in the incident, Yadav said, "There is also some controversy over his killing in the same encounter. Only a judicial probe could find out the facts."

Asked whether his party would withdraw support to the UPA government if its demand for judicial probe was rejected, Yadav said," If the demand is not accepted, then it would add to the prevailing confusion. It is up to the Centre to decide whether to clear the confusion or take a political bashing in the next elections."

Yadav, however, said a favourable result was expected to come out of the ongoing talks with the Congress for an electoral alliance. "Discussions are going on over whether the SP-Congress alliance would be for UP only, or in the assembly elections in other states too," he said.

He said the SP will contest most of the seats in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh assembly elections slated for next month. "In Delhi, the party will contest on a few seats only," he added.

Yadav said the list of candidates for these states would be announced after a meeting of the party's parliamentary board. He said his party would launch an aggressive protest from October 21 to 23 against the Mayawati government's misrule and corruption. Party workers would violate prohibitory orders and court arrest during the agitation, he added.

Heading: Now, Maya turns her attention to upper castes - Indian Express
Content:
Almost a decade ago, four youths — Ram Kumar, Ram Pratap, Ram Kripal and Santosh Kumar — were booked for murder. Within months, the "victim", Ram Sajivan, was found to be alive and well.

But the youths are still facing trial. No action has been taken against the policemen who had conducted the investigation. The complainant who had filed the case has been acquitted.

Still, despite issuing summons to the cops in the case, on September 19, 2008, the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate SK Tiwari had committed the case for trial in the sessions court. Vipin Tiwari, advocate of the accused, said: "In spite of being aware that Ram Sajivan is alive, the CJM's court transferred the case to the sessions court." The first hearing is on October 24.

On January 16, 1999, Chandrakala, a resident of Bajauli village, lodged a complaint with Patranga police station, stating that her son Ram Sajivan (33) was missing. In the complaint, she accused the four brothers residing in the village of murdering Sajivan and disposing of his body.

Ten days later, police recovered an unidentified body from near Mawai police station. The then station officer of Patranga, Ahamad Jalaal Zaidi declared that the body was of Sajivan and the brothers were arrested.

A few months later, Sajivan returned to the village. "When the villagers asked where he had been, he said he had gone to Ahmedabad in search of employment," said Tiwari.

The return of Sajivan should have ended the ordeal of the brothers but it did not. Neither Sajivan nor Zaidi informed the court about the development "as it could have landed them in trouble," said Tiwari.

He alleged that Sajivan and Zaidi had framed the brothers in a false case so that they could capture their house and land.

The accused approached the High Court with the new facts and sought bail, which was granted in 2001. They even approached the Governor.

In May 2002, the government ordered that a case be filed against Zaidi, Chandrakala, Sajivan and others who were produced by the prosecution as witnesses. Only Chandrakala was booked, Tiwari said. But she was acquitted for want of evidence. Tiwari alleged that the police left enough loopholes so she could be acquitted.

Public prosecutor Asha Ram Chaudhry of the CJM court said: "We have issued summons to the station officer and other persons. The recording of their statements will be sent to the sessions court."

Tiwari said neither the station officer, nor others have appeared in the court despite several summons.

Zaidi, who is now posted as Civil Lines police outpost in-charge in Barabanki district, however, said he had not received any summon or notice. The case, he said, "was finished after Chandrakala was released by the court."

Faizabad SSP R K S Rathore refused to comment, saying he had not gone through the case.

An exasperated Ram Kripal said: "We have been suffering for years over this false case. We can't understand this system of law."

His brother Santosh Kumar, however, is patient. "We know we can't be punished," he said. "Once the case is over, we will seek damages from the government, the police, Ram Sajivan and the witnesses who said we were killers," he added.

The story so far

* January 1999: Chandrakala files complaint saying her son Ram Sajivan missing

* Ten days later, police recover unidentified body. Arrest four brothers

* A few months later Sajivan returns.

* 2001: Accused approach High Court, get bail

* May 2002: Government orders case against accuser, cops. Chandrakala acquitted

* September 19, 2008: CJM's court sends murder case for hearing in the sessions court

* October 24: Trial to begin in sessions court

Heading: I don't regret Kidnap: Minissha Lamba - Indian Express
Content:
After holding conventions on Muslims and OBCs, Chief Minister Mayawati has said if she forms the government at the Centre, she would provide reservation to the poor among the upper castes in government jobs.

On Sunday, while addressing her party's convention on "The problems of upper castes: its causes and solutions" in Lucknow, she urged them to join hands with the Dalits and OBCs to improve their economic condition. Mayawati said earlier her party was under the impression that there were no poor people among the upper castes, but the association of upper caste people with the BSP enabled her to know about the growing demand for reservation.

"This demand is a pointer to the prevailing unemployment and poverty among the upper castes," Mayawati told the gathering. "My party makes any promise only after giving a serious thought to the issue. Whatever the BSP promises, it delivers," she added.

She said problems of upper castes can be eliminated only by changing the current economic policies. "The upper caste people should get associated with a party that can formulate better economic policies," she said.

She said unlike other parties, including the Congress and the BJP, her party would not form any government with the help of industrialists. "The BSP wants to form its government with the help of people's support," she added.

The BSP chief said during the last Assembly elections, Brahmins got elected in such a large number because they associated themselves with her party.

Mayawati said she could not do much for the upper castes in her previous regimes because she had formed the government not on her own, but with the help of the BJP. The BJP never wanted her to reach out to upper castes, she added.

Heading: Salman Khan, father win over the Shiv Sena! - Indian Express
Content:
Setting the stage on fire, the cute Minissha Lamba walked the ramp for the designer duo Shane and Falguni Peacock on the second day at the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week (WIFW) in New Delhi. Championing the anti-breast cancer campaign on the fashion platform, the petite actress gets candid in a talk with Ashok Kumar of IndianExpress.com.

How does it feel to walk the ramp for the cause of anti-breast cancer campaign?

It feels great because it can (breast cancer) happen to anyone. We always think that it will happen to someone else and does not give much attention to it.

My walking on the ramp for the cause of the anti-breast cancer campaign just goes on to show that the biggest priority for us is ourselves. A woman's essence in her physical form are her breasts, which are her distinguishing feature. And, what better place to do such a campaign, to make people aware of the hazards of this disease (breast cancer).

How in your opinion could events like fashion shows help fight breast cancer?

Fashion events like Wills India Fashion Week are very popular among the people. So, if such platforms are used to highlight the cause of the breast cancer, no doubt more people will become aware of it. We should not forget that such shows reach out to everyone.

What do you like more, acting or modelling? Which one of the two is easier?

Of course I like acting more than modelling. Acting is dearer to my heart. Both the trades need different types of orientation but acting before the camera is a difficult task compared to walking on the ramp.

It is not difficult to walk down the ramp.

Kidnap did not do well at the box office. Do you regret being part of it now? Have you learnt any lessons from it?

No, I don't regret being part of Kidnap at all. As an actor you give your best to the character you play for the movie. There is no point giving a second thought to the decision taken earlier and regretting over it in retrospect.

Coming to your query, if I have learned anything from the movie, I would say anything and everything that happens in life to you is a learning experience. I personally feel Kidnap was not a bad film.

Heading: Star terminates ‘Kyunki’: Balaji - Indian Express
Content:
Bollywood actor Salman Khan and his father Salim have found favour with the Shiv Sena for their self-professed Hindu values which the saffron group feels will "help the country remain undivided".

Referring to a reported statement of script writer Salim that he was a Muslim by birth but a Hindu by 'samskara' (indoctrination), an editorial in the Sena mouthpiece 'Saamna' on Monday said it reflected progressive thinking of the father-son duo and should be welcomed.

"Salman is different from the other Khans in Bollywood. He installs Ganesh idol at home and follows in the footsteps of his liberal father," it said.

'Saamna' said the Muslim clergy have issued fatwa against Salman ostracizing him for his actions but both the son and father appear to be least bothered.

"If Indian Muslims imbibe these values as demonstrated by Salman-Salim, the country will remain undivided by religion and they will lead happy lives here.

"Muslims in India need Salim Khan and not Amar Singh or Abu Azmi of Samajwadi Party who can be sent to Pakistan where Islam is in danger," the editorial said.

Heading: One has to understand the censors' opinions: Madhur - Indian Express
Content:
Content maker Balaji Telefilms Ltd said on Monday SGL Entertainment Ltd, part of broadcaster Star group, has terminated sourcing and telecasting TV serial 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi' from November 10.

The serial is produced by Balaji and the termination is in breach of contractual obligation owed by the Star group to Balaji, it said in a statement to the stock exchange.

Balaji is pursuing all legal remedies available to it, it said.

Star is owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.

Heading: 'Rock On' concert for Bihar flood victims - Indian Express
Content:
Corporate and Page 3 were movies that provided a realistic view into the trials and tribulations of the rich and famous. Madhur Bhandarkar says people in society, their lives and issues have always fascinated him, so, naturally, it was imperative that a film on fashion would soon follow. "All society parties have models and designers as guests. I wanted to highlight this fraternity through a film," says Bhandarkar in a telephonic interview. Fashion is ready for release on October 29 but much to Bhandarkar's dismay has been given an A certificate, though he says he removed all possible objectionable content. "The censor board have their own opinions and one has to understand that," he states philosophically.

Bhandarkar's last film Traffic Signal, that narrates a depressing story of beggars and hawkers at red lights, didn't really work. "Though the idea had been on my mind, I did not immediately start working on Fashion. Otherwise the audience would have labelled me as someone who only makes films on high society," he continues.

There's a lot of hype about Fashion, about how it exposes the dark side of the glamour industry but Bhandarkar rubbishes the trivia. "It views the fashion world from the perspective of the middle-class man who comes home after a nine-to-five job and turns on the TV set to see models walking on the ramp. His idea of the fashion industry ends there. I take that audience behind the ramp into the professional and personal lives of the models and designers," he explains. Bhandarkar's style of cinema has coined a new phrase in Bollywood, 'middle cinema'. The film stars Priyanka Chopra (who plays Meghna Mathur) in the lead along with a host of real life models. It's Bhandarkar's most expensive venture yet, with budgets exceeding Rs 40 crore. "I visited many fashion weeks in Delhi and Mumbai, spoke with choreographers, model coordinators, designers and buyers to give the film authenticity," says Bhandarkar. His next film, Jail, explores lives of inmates.

Heading: No settlement finalized: Madonna's publicist - Indian Express
Content:
Filmmaker Farhan Akhtar and actor Arjun Rampal are joining hands with some of India's best known rock bands at a concert to raise funds for flood victims in Bihar.

The 'Rock On for Humanity' concert, to be held in Mumbai on Oct. 31, is an initiative by Akhtar and Rampal, both of whom starred in the Bollywood hit "Rock On" – about four friends who form a rock band.

Rampal said the idea for the concert came about while he, Akhtar and "Rock On" producer Ritesh Sidhwani were reading about the film's success in newspapers.

"At the same time, the papers were also full of all these terrible things that the floods were doing in Bihar," Rampal told reporters.

"That's when we thought we should do something about this."

Funds raised at the concert will help set up rehabilitation camps for women and children in some of the worst affected areas in Bihar, where nearly 300 flood-related deaths were reported.

"Rehabilitation will take a lot of time and effort. We hope this concert will go a small way towards that end," said lawmaker Priya Dutt, whose Nargis Dutt Memorial Charitable Trust is also associated with the initiative.

Bollywood actors Shah Rukh Khan and Hrithik Roshan are slated to make an appearance at the concert, organisers said.

Heading: I am more relaxed acting with Ranbir: Deepika - Indian Express
Content:
Madonna's divorce settlement with her estranged husband Guy Ritchie has yet to be finalised, the singer's publicist said on Sunday.

The Sun and The Mail on Sunday reported that the two had struck a deal over their finances and how to split their property. The Mail also reported that they had agreed to a custody arrangement for the couple's children.

In a brief e-mail message sent to The Associated Press, Liz Rosenberg said she would not be commenting on media reports that the pop star and her film director husband had reached or were about to agree on how to share the couple's multi-million dollar fortune and custody of their children.

"I will not be commenting on the various reports regarding the divorce or of the settlement which has not been finalized," Rosenberg said. A statement from Guy Ritchie's representatives in London also declined comment.

Madonna and Ritchie announced their separation Wednesday after nearly eight years of marriage and Britain's tabloid press has speculated wildly on the outcome of the high-profile split.

Madonna and Ritchie married in December 2000 at a castle in Scotland. The couple are reportedly worth around USD 525 million, the bulk of that belonging to Madonna. Ritchie has an estimated USD 35 million fortune. They own homes in London, Los Angeles and New York, and a 1,200-acre (485-hectare) retreat in Wiltshire, England.

The couple has two children: Rocco, 8, and David Banda, 3, who was adopted in Malawi in 2006. Madonna also has a 12-year-old daughter, Lourdes, from her relationship with personal trainer Carlos Leon.

Heading: Small-budget films beat biggies at Box Office - Indian Express
Content:
Success sits easy on Deepika Padukone. Relaxing in her make up van outside the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week venue, the lissome model-turned-actor talks animatedly about her smashing debut and her relationship with actor Ranbir Kapoor. "I am only two films old in Bollywood, so I find it a little premature when people call me successful. When I approach a shot, I give it my best. It's great if the film clicks. If it doesn't, I don't brood over it," she grins, in between getting ready for a turn on the ramp for designers Shantanu and Nikhil's Fiama di Wills show.

Padukone is still basking in the success of her second release, Sidharth Anand's Bachna Ae Haseeno. The conversation veers towards Kapoor as her co-star and Padukone acknowledges, "I am more relaxed when I am acting with him and it shows on screen," she smiles. In fact, ever since their romance became public, there have been many offers for them as a lead pair. But the actor is quick to point out in the same breath that they are not looking to cash in on their romance. "We don't approach offers thinking it will give us more time with each other. We have been signing projects only if they are appropriate for our careers. With that kind of money involved, nobody takes a risk unless they are confident it will pay off," she says.

Soon, we'll see the 22-year-old in Nikhil Advani's Chandni Chowk to China opposite Akshay Kumar, where she again has a double role after Om Shanti Om. "I am very fond of the movie because it's the first time I have attempted action in a film. I had been training in jujitsu most of last year that involves hanging from cables and wires," says Padukone, with some bruises from her action sequences clearly visible.

"There's this particular fight sequence that I have with Akshay in the movie which I was quite nervous about. He taught me action should be like a dance, smooth and graceful," she recalls. Even as she waits for the release of the film during Diwali, the actor is busy shooting for director

Imtiaz Ali's yet to be titled film, opposite Saif Ali Khan. "It's a simple romance, quite contemporary, something which Imtiaz is so good at creating," she says.

Heading: We monitored and beat the examinees: Shiv Sena - Indian Express
Content:
Much-hyped big releases with superstars have failed to impress cinegoers this year but small-budget films made by newer and lesser-known filmmakers have managed to draw in the crowds and also rake in big money at the marquee.
