He added that the Centre had failed on all fronts particularly on providing relief to the common man who was suffering from high prices of commodities. He said, "This government has not taken any step to lower the fuel prices in the country, which can help to reduce the price rise.

Singh added that 80 per cent of the total requirement of key fertiliser DAP, is imported in India. He said that the Centre has failed to announce the subsidies, which led to the delay in placing of orders by big companies.

"For this reason, there is a shortage in the open market whereas members of the cooperative societies in the state were getting DAP as per requirement."

He called upon the farmers to join these societies on a large scale so that they could avail the facilities provided by them. He said that till date 1.55 lakh million tonnes of DAP has been supplied of the total 3.10 lakh million tonnes indent. He said that remaining will be provided up to November 15.

Heading: Residents see hope as MC to take charge of green belts in southern sectors - Indian Express
Content:
Following an indefinite strike by workers against the expulsion of some of their fellow workers and alleged violations of labour laws, the production remained suspended for the fourth consecutive day at the GMP Technical Solutions factory at Mandhala village near the Industrial estate in Barotiwala.

The workers today staged a dharna outside the factory gate and held a rally to register their protest. The workers were demanding immediate revocation of the suspended workers and intervention of officials of the Labour department to solve the issue amicably.

The workers had gone on an indefinite strike on Friday after the factory management had allegedly terminated 11 workers on various charges.

After this, the workers had pleaded the case of their fellow workers before the management. However, after getting no response, the workers decided to go on a strike. Besides, the workers are also demanding the abolition of the contract labour system in the factory.

The agitating workers alleged that despite orders of the state government, the management is still employing the workers on contract basis. Even, the ESI facility was not being provided to the workers and the Provident Fund scheme had also not been introduced by the management despite repeated assurances.

Indian National Trade Union Congress leader Shayam Thakur said that exploitation of workers would not be tolerated at any cost and the agitation would be intensified if the legitimate demands are not conceded.

Heading: Demands met, docs call off strike - Indian Express
Content:
The green belts in the southern sectors of the city seem to be a neglected lot. The lack of maintenance is reflected by the overgrown trees, presence of weeds and wild growth.

Recently, a decision was taken for handing over the maintenance of the green belts to the Municipal Corporation from the UT Administration. The residents are hopeful that with the MC taking charge, the situation would improve.

Manav, a resident of Sector 49, says, "While the green belts and parks in the northern sectors are well maintained, the southern sectors seem to be getting "step-motherly" treatment. No efforts are being made for preserving the green belts. We are waiting to see the difference, once the MC takes charge."

Satish Chandra Sharma, general secretary of Chandigarh Social Welfare Council, on the other hand says, "Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal has given MPLAD funds for the development of parks. In Sector 51, while a green belt was developed, no provision was made for pathways or lights. The mayor had sanctioned an amount of Rs 2 lakh for the park. We are hoping that the green belts will be developed in the coming days."

The officials of the MC Horticulture department, meanwhile, state that they are awaiting a formal nod for taking up work. They claim that with additional areas coming under them, more staff would be required. "Some staff should be transferred from the Administration to the MC or new staff should be recruited," said an official.

Heading: Hoax call keeps police on toes, Mohali man held - Indian Express
Content:
Assault on senior resident: Strong view taken of the strike, says PGI deputy director; services of ad hoc resident doctors who participated in the protest will be terminated

The Association of Resident Doctors (ARD) called off its strike on Monday after the PGI authorities accepted all demands of the resident doctors.

In a late evening decision, the association said the resident doctors had decided to report on duty immediately and the functioning in the OPDs and other departments would be normal from Tuesday.

Earlier in the day, the ARD had refused to call off its strike, seeking a public apology from Dr Santhosh Kumar, an assistant professor who had allegedly assaulted a senior resident of the urology department a few days ago.

Dr Santhosh had already submitted his apology to the PGI Director, but the resident doctors were demanding a separate apology to the ARD.

The two other demands of the ARD included disciplinary action against Dr Santhosh and formulation of clear rules so that a similar incident is not repeated in future.

Taking to Newsline, ARD president Dr Prabhu said: "We had raised three specific demands with the authorities, which have been met. We have decided to resume work from today. Dr Santhosh has apologised to the ARD as was demanded."

On Saturday, the association had said it would resume work, but in a late-night meeting on Sunday decided that resident doctors should press for a written apology to the ARD. The association had gone on a mass casual leave on Saturday.

Even as the ARD remained adamant on its stand till 8 pm on Monday, despite a series of meetings with the PGI authorities and Director K K Talwar, the hospital claimed that 60 per cent resident doctors reported to work on Monday. Intensive case units and emergency services were not affected as resident doctors had already decided not to boycott work in these units.

Monday being a holiday, the impact of the strike was less as laboratory services were shut. All planned surgeries were, however, postponed and only emergency cases were taken up.

The controversy sparked off after senior resident Dr Sanand Kumar was allegedly assaulted and abused by Dr Santhosh, assistant professor of the same department, last Wednesday, in front of operation theatre staff and technicians. The tiff began after Dr Santhosh found his patient listed on the second number on the OT list for the day by the resident doctor even though as he had wanted the number 1 slot for him. The professor reportedly lost his cool and abused Dr Sanand. The matter was then reported to the head of the department and the director, PGI.

A three-member committee comprising Dean Prof V Sakhuja, Sub-Dean Prof Amod Gupta and Prof Savita Malhotra of the Department of Psychiatry was appointed to inquire into the matter. The panel found Dr Santhosh guilty of using unparliamentary language. Dr Santhosh has, meanwhile, proceeded on leave.

Earlier in the day, Dr Prabhu had told Newsline: "We have charted out three demands that we expect the PGI to accept. In case they don't, we will not withdraw the strike."

Deputy Director, PGI Administration, A K Gupta said: "The PGI has acted swiftly to settle the case. The committee found the faculty member guilty and he has tendered his apology. He also apologised to the senior doctor today by meeting him personally. We have forwarded the matter to the ministry already. We have already taken a strong view of the strike by the resident doctors and have issued them letters. The services of ad hoc resident doctors who took part in the strike would be terminated."

Heading: PU to finally free vacant OBC seats for general category - Indian Express
Content:
A Telephone call on Monday morning, warning of bombs planted somewhere in Chandigarh or Mohali, sent the police into a tizzy. With the India-Australia cricket Test being played in Mohali, the police swung into action and thoroughly combed the PCA Stadium and other places in the township, though they did not find anything suspicious.

One person has been arrested on charges of making the hoax call.

The call was received around 8.45 am at the Chandigarh Police Control Room at its telephone number 100. The caller said: "Aaj shehar mein 11 bajkar 5 minute par bomb fatega. Bacha sakte ho to bacha lo (Bombs will explode at 11.05 am today. Save the city if you can)."

Since no specific place was mentioned in the call made from a Mohali telephone number, the Chandigarh Police alerted its Mohali counterparts. The police launched a massive combing operation in their respective jurisdictions with the help of bomb disposal squads. Heavily crowded public places and other vulnerable points were evacuated, but nothing suspicious was found.

"The Punjab Cricket Association (PCA) Stadium in Mohali, which is hosting the second cricket Test match of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy-2008 between India and Australia, was thoroughly combed," said Mohali Superintendent of Police (City) Varinder Paul Singh.

After the "explosion" time 11.05 am elapsed, the police tracked down the landline telephone number from where the call was made.

"During investigations that lasted for almost an hour, the number was traced to a unit in Industrial Area, Phase III, Mohali," said Singh.

A worker at the unit, Manki Kumar, a resident of Bhagwanpur village in Siwan district of Bihar, was arrested after his voice matched with that in the call recorded at the Police Control Room.

The Mohali police handed over the man, in his early 30s, to the Chandigarh Police, which booked him under Sections 506 and 507 of the IPC.

"During preliminary interrogation, the caller confessed to making the call and said it was just a mischief to get a leave from the factory as he presumed the hoax call would make the police evacuate all industrial units as well," said a senior investigating officer, adding that further interrogation was in progress to ascertain any other motive behind making the call and to find out the previous track record of the caller.

Heading: School buses banned on V6 roads from next week - Indian Express
Content:
It took more than a fortnight and a contempt case in the High Court for the Panjab University (PU) to comply with the directions issued by the Supreme Court to de-reserve seats lying vacant under the OBC quota. On October 4, the Punjab and Haryana High Court had directed the university to free the seats for general category students, but PU did not do so. As a result, a contempt case was filed, which comes up for hearing on Tuesday.

Jungshed Singh, who was seeking admission for his son in the University Institute of Legal Studies (UILS), had filed a writ petition in the HC after PU refused to de-reserve the vacant seats. Talking to Newsline, he said: "We had moved the court seeking relief. But even after the court gave directions to the university to de-reserve the seats, the latter did not comply with the orders. Hence, we filed a contempt case."

Sources in PU said it was in the absence of any written directions that the authorities did not de-reserve the seats.

PU officials said they had now decided to comply with the order.

When asked what took the university so long to decide on de-reserving the seats even after the court's orders, Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti initially refused to answer, saying: "You are not my boss to ask me such questions."

He later said: "There is a set procedure and we are following it."

Legal Retainer for PU Advocate Anupam Gupta said: "I was approached by PU for legal opinion. I have advised them to de-reserve the vacant seats under OBC quota in all departments. I told them to place an advertisement, declaring de-reserving of all seats lying vacant under the OBC quota. This decision will be extended to all departments, including the UILS."

Heading: Accessorise - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Police have decided to impose a ban on the plying of school buses on V6 (inner roads in sectors) roads from next week. It said stern action would be initiated against those found violating the orders.

Superintendent of Police (Traffic) H S Doon said they had received many complaints from the residents against the school buses plying on the V6 roads. "We received complaints of reckless driving by the drivers of these buses. There are several unreported incidents of minor accidents involving school buses. As a safety measure, we decided not to let these buses enter the V-6 roads," he added.

Officers said they would keep a close watch on the school buses in the sectors. The buses would be allowed to run only up to the V5 roads. "Beat officers have been instructed to make sure that no bus violates the norm. They will inform the station house officer immediately after spotting a violation so that the matter can be taken up with the school authorities. The buses will be impounded and heavy fine will be imposed," said DSP (Traffic) J S Cheema.

There are several school buses which pick and drop children from V6 roads. "We have decided to convene a meeting with all the schools to tell them not to pick and drop students from V6 roads. The roads are congested and often lead to accidents. The V5 roads are wide enough to cater to the buses," he added.

The Administration has also asked the school authorities to install speed governors in their school buses. Doon said the upper limit of the speed governor will be 50 kilometres per hour. "We have given the schools a month's time to comply with the orders. After that, we will start issuing challans to the vehicles found without speed governors," said Cheema.

Heading: Romantic Notes - Indian Express
Content:
Pret apart, this season designers have their eyes set on jewellery, bags, stoles, scarves, belts...

For the first time since the inception of Indian fashion, accessories, crucial elements in fashion are high on every designer's list and were one of the highlights at the recently-concluded fashion weeks. Bags, scarves, shawls, wrap dresses, jewellery...accessories are simply indispensable.

Nods city-based designer Jas Lakhmana, who customizes accessories as per the outfit she designs and her client's profile. "I never let a great outfit be ruined by poor accessories and so besides helping them choose the right stuff, I even tell them how to sport these,'' the 'it' accessories of the festive and fall-winter season are belts, scarves, hankies, embroidered bags in fabrics, clutch bags, poly-blend formal shoes and antique jewellery, especially earrings. Add some bling for the festive look, especially traditional embroidery like dabka and gota-patti and go in for metallic colours. "Belts are a must-have and I 'm doing them in all sizes, styles and materials. Braided and satin belts are dressy and chic,'' adds Jas. Babi recommends waist belts with sarees, armlets, brocade and swaroski embellished bags and big cocktail rings and earrings.

Jewellery designer Deepti Sudhindra has found her niche by etching Henry David Thoreau's poetry on to silver, transforming ubiquitous coconut shells into delicate beads, pendants and necklaces. "I take a coconut shells and embellish it with silver," explains Sudhindra, 32, whose design element is essentially Indian. At Trenz, Fun Republic, its an overdose of long pearl chains that rule. "Those in pink are high on the trend-o-meter," Suraj, proprietor of Trenz tell us, as he showcases big, bold belts and a variety of traditional earrings, which he feels go perfect with the western wear. Agrees Anjul, a jewellery designer, who put up a stall at Whispering Willows. "With the festive season on, Kundan is flaunted in a big way," she says.

Turning scarves, shawls and wraps into a heritage label is Bappaditya Biswas, 36, who founded Bai Lou in 2002. Closely working with weavers of Bengal, Biswas uses Jamdani and double cloth weaving techniques. "We don't believe in embellishments on top of the fabric. Everything is woven in and comes out as a finished product," says Biswas. "Wearing scarves is a recent trend in India," says Biswas. And the scarf has reinvented itself and is an affordable way to liven up the look of any outfit, adding both colour and pattern to an ensemble. Your bag, hair, belt loop, neck, sport it anywhere and casually, but choose a fabric that flows and is not stiff. As for bags, patent leather ones in bold colours, formal clutches, big bags with gold details are what you must bag.

Heading: Picture Perfect! - Indian Express
Content:
A Debut with love, of love and for love...Mera Ranjha marks Canadian Meera's entry into the Punjabi music. Born into a family of engineers Meera has given voice to her love for profound music and poetry. And the album is a dream come true for the young singer who learnt to follow her heart after a sad incident in her life. "Both Western and Indian music appeals to me, that's where the inspiration to do this album came from," she tells us. As for her style she says it's a combination of pure "raw appeal, soul, reggae, pop, rap" et al.

"Today's Punjab is a unique mixture of traditional valour and success throughout the world, so in a sense the album tries to capture that essence with a very international feel. Gurmeet Singh has composed the music for the lyrics by Kala Nizampuri, Manjeet and Sudhakar Sharma. "Listeners can look forward to a mix of pacy, foot tapping and sensual numbers," smiles Meera as we discover that singing is not her only talent. Back in Canada she is a TV host, a jewellery and fashion designer a business woman. Some versatility!

Heading: Southern Platter - Indian Express
Content:
A photo exhibition brings glimpses of beautiful Hungarian landscapes, architecture, history and culture

This one's a sure shot delight for architecture and history lovers, for the Hungarian photographic exhibition is just about that. As part of the Hungarian cultural festival an exhibition of world heritage photographs are on display at Government Art Gallery- Sector 10. The focus is on eight Hungarian cities, each with a history, speciality and pull of its own. You can also read interesting facts and specifics on each view.

The first cluster takes you through Budapest with shots of the Opera, the Danube twinkling in the reflection of the bridge lights. There are also images of the splendid building of the Matthias Church, The Parliament and the Hero's Square. You can also get a tour of the village of Holloko and its surroundings. While in one capture women dressed in colourful traditional costumes greet you, another one with a woman and child by the side of crucifix is touching. However its the caves of Aggtelek that take the breath away. Fascinating natural formations of Baradla and a concert being held inside them!

The architecture of the Millenary Benedictine Abbey of Pannonhalma, of the monastery, the church and the library gives you an insight into Hungarian traditions. Catch the flora and fauna of the Hortobagy National Park. If ancient is what you dig then the the cemetery of Roman era Pecsi will take you there. Various images of Peter and PAul burial chamber, early Christian mausoleum is rare view. There are also images of portrait of a young man, David, Adam and Eve. The town of Ferto gives you both stone and sea. A taste of Hungarian wine may yet be a far off option but you can at least see how its all done. Wine cellars, grapes and vineyards and several hundred year old bottles of wine. Visit the exhibition and plan your next holiday in advance, you have at least eight options!

On till October 22.

Heading: Hopefully, better things lie ahead for me this year: Pujara - Indian Express
Content:
Splash It!

Hanung Retail Ltd, the retail arm of Hanung Toys & Textiles Ltd, opens its fifth exclusive store Splash at Phase V, Mohali. Nestled in in a carpet area of 800 square feet, it showcases the complete range of Splash Home furnishings like bed sheets, bed covers, comforters, curtains, towels, bath mats and premium export range of furnishings. With a target of having 20 stores by the end of this financial year. "We aim to have over 150 outlets by the end of 2010," says Varun Sachar, Head of Hanung Retail Ltd. The store also houses soft toys, electronic toys, and virtual gaming along with Play-n-Pets products.

Cause & concern

To celebrate the joy of the festive season, children of Theatre Age presented a cultural programme which was aimed at creating awareness about various social issues like national integration, communal harmony, perils of polythene and horrors of drug addiction. The evening opened up on a note of national integration by an impressive musical ballad, Vande Matram and was followed by a short play highlighting the message of communal harmony. A foot-thumping medley of popular film songs had the audience join the children, while Raj Machal had the audience in splits with his mimicry of film actors. Two other short musical plays conveyed the message of keeping away from polythene and drugs.

Heading: Sushil felicitated at akhara - Indian Express
Content:
With two back to back centuries in Buchi Babu cricket tournament, Cheteshwar Pujara has reinstated that he is hungry for more in the coming Ranji season. Currently in Chandigarh to participate in the J P Atray tournament which he describes as 'decision of his team-mates and the company', he says he is looking forward to repeat his last year's performance in the Ranji Trophy. "It is always hard to score consistently but I am hoping for the best. My batting has improved a lot nut like I said earlier I still need to work out on my weakness. It's good to know that I was the top scorer in last year's Ranji trophy. There's still one month left for the Ranji Trophy to commence. I will definitely try to carry my form in Buchi Babu ahead," says the prolific scorer who has been praised my veterans like Dravid and Kiran More.

Always a future prospect, Cheteshwar came into the limelight with a mammoth unbeaten 306 (540m, 516b, 36x4) in a West Zone Under-14 match against Baroda in 2000-01. Runs followed from his willow and soon he was the mainstay of the Saurashtra team which had an impressive run last year; all due to Cheteshwar who emerged as the highest scorer in the Ranji Trophy. "People think that I am more suited to Test than ODIs but let me clear one thing that I was the highest run scorer in Under-19 World Cup in Sri Lanka (he was the player of the tournament) and last year also I scored in excess of 450 odd runs. I have also talked to many coaches to improve my batting in ODIs. Besides that Ihave also done well in Twenty20 cricket," says Pujara.

His team mates from the World Cup team, Piyush Chawla and Rohit Sharma has already made it into the Indian team. Even Virat Kohli has donned the Indian colour. So doesn't he feel left out or dejected? "It's the selectors' decision. They did well and got the reward. It's not late for me. I am performing well and if I continue this way then I have got enough chance to play for the Indian team. I am waiting for that opportunity," says the right handed batsman and a part time bowler.

Apart from Ranji Trophy, it is the New Zealand series that he is looking forward to. 'Apart from the Ranji Trophy and New Zealand series in 2009 I haven't thought about anything," adds Pujara. The IPL enigma is something which he still hasn't been able to figure out. "I don't know what went wrong last year. I didn't get a chance to play any game. Hopefully this year will be different," says Pujara who signed three year contract with Kolkata Knight Riders last year.

Heading: Punjab Gold Cup 4-nation hockey approved by FIH - Indian Express
Content:
Olympian Sushil Kumar was felicitated by 'Gulzar Akhara' near Zirakpur on Saturday. "Sushil has not only brought laurels to the country but inspired the younger generation to take up wrestling and make a name for them in this sport." said Ranbir Singh Kundu, organiser and coach of Gulzar Akhara.

Sushil was accompanied by two coaches Ram Chander and Yashbir Singh of Satpal Akhara. As many as 40 wrestlers from the akhara welcomed their hero on an open jeep. The function was attended by many persons from adjoining villages. Apart from the akhara, State Bank of India also honoured the star grappler with a memento and a bouqet. Sushil also interacted with the wrestlers shared tips with them. The akhara has been a nursery for the budding wrestlers and have produced wrestlers who have done well in various junior international tournaments.

Heading: Carmel Convent, GHMS paddlers clinch TT titles - Indian Express
Content:
The International Hockey Federation (FIH) has accorded approval to the Punjab Gold Cup Men Four-Nation Invitational Double Leg Hockey Tournament to be hosted by the Punjab Sports Department from February 5 to 14 next year.

According to Punjab Sports Director Pargat Singh, FIH General Manager Christophe Troendle has conveyed the sanction to ad hoc committee of the Indian Hockey Confederation. Besides hosts India, Pakistan, Holland and German teams would be seen in action in the double leg to be played at the Sector 42 Hockey Stadium in Chandigarh and the second leg, classification match and final will be staged at the Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar.

The Punjab Sports Department will provide to and fro air fare for 22 members, including one umpire of each team, free board and lodging and local transport.

Pargat Singh said that the double-leg series would be professionally managed. Expert agencies will be associated for the smooth and professional conduct of the tournament. Expert agencies would be associated and the matches would be telecast live.

Meanwhile, the Punjab Sports Department has also requested the International Hockey Federation through Mrs Amrit Bose of Indian Hockey Confederation, for sanction to organise an invitational Four-National Women hockey tournament in the last week of April, next year.

Besides hosts India, three national teams from Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, Australia, Holland and Germany will compete in the double-leg tournament in Jalandhar.

Heading: Wong to meet Tushar in boys’ u-10 final - Indian Express
Content:
Guru Harkishan Model School, Sector 38 and Carmel Convent School, Sector 9 claimed the boys' under-19 and girls' under-19 team championships, respectively, in the North Zone Central Board of Secondary Education (Cluster XIII) Table Tennis Tournament organised by The Banyan Tree School, Sector 48-B at the Sector 23 Badminton Hall here today.

Carmel Convent defeated KC Public School of Jammu by 3-1 in the girls' under-19 final. GHMS-38 also recorded an identical 3-1 verdict against DAV Public School, Sector in the boys' under-19 team championship final.

Rajeshwari stole the show in the girls' Under-19 team championship final against KC Public School as she won both her matches. She prevailed over Tanvi by 11-4, 10-12, 11-4, 11-6 to give her team the lead. Harjasleen then defeated Lavanya by 11-9, 11-4, 11-9 in the second singles. However, Ishita lost to Sandeep 3-11, 6-11, 5-11. That was the only game the Jammu and Kashmir school won in the final. Rajeshwari then wrapped up the final with a fluent 11-6, 11-9, 11-3 against Lavanya as Carmel Convent registered a 3-1 win. SD Public School of Ambala Cantonment blanked Bhavan Vidayalaya of Panchkula by 3-0 to finish third in the girls under-19 team championship.

Dev Saini performed well as he won both his matches to enable GHMS-38 defeat DAV Public School, Sector 8 by 3-1 in the boys under-19 team championship final. Sameer Singla put GHMS in the lead by beating Rajan Mahindra by 11-8, 8-11, 11-9, 11-6 in the opening singles match.

Heading: JP Atray tournament likely to get underway today - Indian Express
Content:
Top seed Kevin Wong and second seed Tushar Khanna moved into the boys' under-10 singles final of the 20th Yonex Chandigarh State Badminton Championship being conducted by Chandigarh Badminton Club under the patronage of Chandigarh Badminton Association here on Saturday. As the Sector 42 Badminton Hall was left unplayable due to leakage in roof, today the matches were conducted at Government Model Senior Secondary School in Sector 23 here. Kevin won ousted Ahil 21-9, 21-12 in the semi-final of boys' under-10 while Tushar defeated Aryan Singh 24-22, 19-21, 23-21.

Kevin Wong also advanced to the boys Under-13 semi-final after defeating Shaurya Rattan by 21-13, 21-12 in the quarter-final match.

Top seed Rajjan Singh gave a walkover to Vishal. Robin Saini and Chetnaya also entered semi-finals. Robin beat Lovepreet Singh by 21-15, 21-15 and Chetanya beat Gauravdeep Singh by 21-18, 21-14.

Giant-killer Mehak Sood will meet Sherya in the girls' Under-16 singles final. In semi-final matches, Mehak eliminated the challenge of Navika by 21-17, 22-20.

Earlier in a quarter-final match, Mehak Sood pulled off the biggest surprise as she ended the challenge of topseed Rushmi by 21-14, 21-15.

Top seed Oscar Bansal and second seed Pankaj Nathani entered the men's quarter-finals with victories. International Oscar Bansal easily prevailed over Aman Sethi by 21-16, 21-8.

Heading: On Gurta Gaddi Diwas, Rodrigues flags off mobile clinic bus - Indian Express
Content: The 15th All India J P Atray Memorial Cricket Tournament is likely to get underway on Sunday with LIC Cricket Club taking on Rajasthan Cricket Association at PCA Stadium, Mohali, Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association locking horns with BPCL at Sector-16 Cricket Stadium, and Moody ICL taking on MRF at DAV Sector-8. With the cloud cover receding in the evening the organisers were hopeful of getting the matches through at the three venues may be with a little delayed start if the weather holds on during the night. All eyes will be on Sourav Ganguly who will be playing for LIC.

Heading: To expose easy availability of drugs, activist produces hashish in court - Indian Express
Content:
As part of the Gurta Gaddi Diwas celebrations, Punjab Governor and UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (Retd) inaugurated a medical camp and flagged off a fully-equipped AC mobile clinic bus today. The bus was launched by the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Sewa Society at IMA Bhawan in Sector 35.

Accompanied by Jean Rodrigues, the Administrator went around different wards in the city, interacted with the members of the medical team and took stock of the facilities being provided in the hospital.

Rodrigues said they were in the process of synchronising healthcare services by pooling the existing resources and integrating the medical network available at PGIMER, General Hospital and the Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32, to ensure access to quality healthcare in the region. The Medicity is in an advanced stage of planning which will be equipped with super-speciality services with research facilities and 100 beds for chemotherapy and dialysis patients to help our goal of providing free treatment to the poor patients, he said.

General Rodrigues asked the Home Secretary to constitute a team of officers and management of the Guru Granth Sahib Sewa Society to coordinate endeavour to boost medical services in the region and reach out to people who cannot come to hospitals for treatment.

H S Sabbharwal, General Secretary of the Sri Guru Granth Sahib Sewa Society, highlighted its goals and said that the fully-equipped AC mobile clinic bus with latest eye and dental equipment will conduct five camps in a week in rural areas within a 40-km radius of Chandigarh. He said the society has given 12 stretchers each to PGI and General Hospital, Sector 16.

There is a plan to start angiography and angioplasty facilities and the poor patients will be given free services, he added.

Heading: Mayor visits Ward 13, gets first-hand account of people’s problems - Indian Express
Content:
Goswami says he has 'no confidence' in the police to discuss the issue, alleges police-drug mafia nexus

"If the court permits, my volunteers and I can produce such packets in tonnes before the court," said Hemant Goswami before producing a packet of hashish in the court of Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur to drive home his point on the easy availability of drugs in the city.

Surprised by the act, Chief Thakur asked Goswami as to where he got the packet from. The social activist said his volunteer had purchased the packet from outside a school located in Dadumajra three days ago.

Goswami claimed that drugs are easily available outside almost every school and at various joints in the city.

On being asked by the Chief Justice as to why the packet was not brought to the notice of the Chandigarh Police, Goswami submitted that not only the Chandigarh Police but even the Punjab Police officers were involved with drug peddlers and thus he had no confidence in reporting the issue to them.

Confirming Goswami's claim, senior standing counsel for UT Administration, Advocate Anupam Gupta alleged a nexus between the Chandigarh Police officers and drug peddlers in the city, which, he added, is being investigated.

Terming the easy availability of drugs in the city as highly unfortunate, the Chief Justice asked the senior standing counsel not to protect the Chandigarh Police officers and ensure that it is stopped immediately.

"This is highly unfortunate, it is being done so blatantly," remarked the Chief Justice.

Referring to the recent suspension of two Station House Officers (SHOs) and eight other Chandigarh Police officers for the alleged nexus with drug peddlers, Goswami questioned as to why an FIR has not been registered by the Chandigarh Police against the erring police officers.

"As per the NDPS Act, the offence is non-cognisable and an FIR should be registered. Nine months have passed but no FIR has been registered. My life is also under threat because of the revelations made by me against the Chandigarh Police," said Goswami.

Anupam Gupta requested the court to ask Goswami to share the details with him and he (Gupta) will ensure that strict action is taken against the guilty. "I will meet the UT Administrator in this regard and will ensure that this nexus between the police and drug mafia is brought to an end," assured Gupta.

Heading: Health plan finds no takers in govt schools - Indian Express
Content:
To get a first-hand account of problems being faced by area residents, Mayor Pardeep Chhabra visited Ward Number 13 comprising Sectors 49, 50 and 51. He was accompanied by area councillor Ram Sumer Maurya.

Both were received by S S Bhardwaj and Satish Chandra Sharma, co-chairman and general secretary of the Chandigarh Social Welfare Council.

S K Bajaj, president of the SBI Society, Sector 49, apprised the mayor of the need of a green belt for which land has already been earmarked. He also requested for axing some trees near PGI/PEC societies that obstruct traffic. Deep pits in the sector were shown to the mayor with a request to declare them as official malba ground. Non-functional streetlights were also brought to the notice of the mayor.

Sharma requested the mayor to make provision of traffic lights on the crossroad of Sector 49-50, as it was highly accident-prone. He was also requested to ensure full functioning of the streetlights on V-3 and V-4 roads.

Menace of stray cattle roaming in the ward area, especially near New Light Society Sector 51, was brought to the mayor's notice. Bhardwaj apprised the mayor that the green belt in Sector 51 needs pathways and lights. The mayor sanctioned a sum of Rs 2 lakh for the project.

The concerned officers were directed to take necessary action on grievances of the residents.

Heading: PU faces faculty crunch, blames it on lack of funds - Indian Express
Content:
The Comprehensive School Health Programme started by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has drawn a mixed response. While private schools have incorporated the scheme in their curriculum, the government schools are lagging behind.

As per the scheme, the Board has asked all the schools affiliated to it to set up health clubs.

In a circular issued to the schools, the Board had pointed out the necessity to build on the components of knowledge related to health and nutrition, developing healthy attitudes and enhancing life skills to overcome the multiple health concerns affecting school going children both in the urban and remote areas of the country.

To implement the same, the schools were to fulfill certain objectives like creating health cards for each student, carrying out surveys on health-related concerns and organising health walks as part of social campaigns.

"We have appointed a doctor who does a regular check-up of students.

The progress is sent to parents on a quarterly basis.

We also hold talks on various health issues to create awareness among students," says Sanjay Sardana of Manav Mangal Smart School.

"The school monitors the physical as well as the emotional growth of students and the parents are also regularly informed. We also hold debates and discussions on various health related topics for the benefit of students," says Punita Singh, counsellor, Carmel Convent School.

As per the objectives, the schools have to celebrate days like World Health Day and create awareness about World No Tobacco Day and World AIDS Day among others.

The schools have also been instructed to provide nutritious snacks in the canteen under the programme.

"We have not received any such instructions. Though we do have first-aid available in the school in case of emergency, but there is no full-time doctor. We are not aware that students' medical report has to be sent to their parents on a regular basis," says a principal of a government school requesting anonymity stating that they have been asked by the department to not give any statement to the media.

Expressing concern on the programme not being implemented properly in government schools, Vinod Sharma, president, Government Teachers' Union said,

"The scheme is for the benefit of the students and it must be implemented in full spirit. Teachers as well as principals should make sure that there is a holistic development of students."

Heading: UT Engineering dept urged - Indian Express
Content:
With almost a quarter of the academic session coming to an end, students at the UIET department of Panjab University are yet to be beneficiaries of basic facilities including faculty and infrastructure.

Around 165 seats were increased last year, but the department seems to be ailing owing to inadequate resources. Though the authorities maintain that the hiring process of faculty is on, there is still a long way to go for the department. Talking to Newsline, Prof B S Sohi, chairperson of the department said, "There is a shortage of faculty and other infrastructure facilities, however, the same is being taken care of. In all, the department is short of 35 readers and 15 lecturers. The hiring process of faculty is going on."

The department has also been in the news a number of times after students complained of the lack of facilities. Two issues demanding immediate attention of the authorities is the hiring of adequate faculty and the construction of lecture halls, according to students.

Meanwhile, it is not only the UIET department that is facing a faculty crunch. Other departments too seem to be struggling with having to make do with guest faculty in order to comply with the required work force. Be it the University Business School, the Economics department or the Mass Communication department, the absence of faculty in all these departments is being compensated by the guest faculty. Sources maintain that at present the university is short of around 250 lecturers and readers.

The authorities at the university, meanwhile, owe the faculty shortage to the lack of funds and claim that the university is in urgent need of finances. According to a university official, "The first and foremost reason for the lack of faculty is due to the shortage of funds. For hiring a faculty member, we need to take into consideration the opinion of the Finance Board and most of the times, the board insists that we hire only in dire need."

Further explaining and clarifying the university's stand, PU Registrar S S Bari said, "We have begun with the hiring process and faculty is being appointed in all departments wherever required."

Heading: ‘Rote system of learning still rules the roost’ - Indian Express
Content:
UT Engineering dept urged to expedite road, streetlight repairs in Sector 43

With the number of accidents in the city witnessing a steep rise over the last one year, the traffic police department has asked the UT Engineering department to recarpet the potholed roads and repair the defunct streetlights immediately.

Officials said there have been over 1000 accidents, both minor and major, reported in the city due to the poor condition of roads and streetlights. Speaking to Newsline, Superintendent of Police (Traffic) H S Doon said they had taken up the matter with the Engineering department in the presence of the Home Secretary in a meeting held last week.

"The condition of roads is getting from bad to worse and there are several roads without streetlights. It leads to accidents more often," added Doon. Sources said the Home Secretary has also instructed the Engineering department to expedite the work.

Officials with the Engineering department, meanwhile, assured that work would start soon. "There are many roads where the recarpetting work is on. Other damaged roads will be recarpetted soon. Also, we have initiated work of repairing the defunct streetlights," added an official.

Sector 43 residents, meanwhile, have lodged several complaints with the Engineering department regarding the issue. "We met several officers but they gave mere assurances. There have been several accidents reported during night, courtesy the poor condition of roads and defunct streetlights," said Daleep Sahai, a resident of Sector 43.

Heading: ADC Kirpal dies waiting for kidney - Indian Express
Content:
While we are fast progressing in almost every possible field and also bringing in changes for the betterment of education, there still remains an area of neglect. No doubt, we have excellent universities like the Delhi University and equally good professional institutes like the IITs and IIMs, yet a lot remains to be desired.

Unfortunately, we are stuck with the age-old examination system to assess the students' capabilities. Those scoring 80 to 90 per cent are considered geniuses, no matter how bad their understanding of the subject is. Schools and colleges judge a students' knowledge of the topic through a three-hour examination. Students cram to memory and then jettison out all they had studied the previous night.

This is detrimental to both — the student as well as the institution. The student is not completely in sync with the subject. As the students are aware of the topics relevant from the examination point of view, they only do selective study. In their bid to prepare for the test, they overlook several topics which may hold practical significance.

The rote system of learning still rules the roost. Instead of monitoring a students' progress at regular intervals, he is judged only in the annual examinations.

For a long time, educationists and academicians have debated whether the education system needs a revamp.

Indeed, we need to move with the changing times. Topics that are redundant should be done away with.

There has always been over-emphasis on the theory part of the subject. Students should be made more adept with the practical aspect of the subjects. More time should be spent in the laboratories than merely cramming formulae.

Heading: Education set in cement in this Bathinda slum - Indian Express
Content:
The 1986-batch PCS officer, Kirpal Singh (51), posted as ADC Tarn Taran, who was suffering from severe kidney ailment and hospitalised for the last two months, breathed his last at a private hospital at Mohali late last evening.

His last remains were brought here today, and civil and police officers, apart from other prominent persons, attended the cremation. Kirpal, who is survived by his wife and two young children, was born on May 20, 1957, and worked as a lecturer before joining the civil service in 1986.

His first posting as executive magistrate was at Tarn Taran and ironically his last duty too was in the same district. He had also served as ADC at Amritsar and Muktsar.

His condition worsened when a kidney donor, Sunny, took a U-turn earlier this month, despite the fact he had consented to donate his organ to the officer and the transplantation was cleared by the authorisation committee.

The controversy snowballed and finally the authorisation committee rejected the donation. Sunny's parents had raised a hue and cry over the issue.

Sources said officer's family might initiate a legal action against Sunny, as he had taken money and then refused to donate kidney. The family members at his official residence at Taylor Road here said legal hassles came in the way, and they failed to save him.

Kirpal's friends remember him as a great friend and a soft-spoken professional.

Heading: Majha ex-servicemen on hunger strike - Indian Express
Content:
Cement plant sets up school for wards of labourers

A corporate house's endeavour has added wings to the dreams of children of daily-wagers .

A school set up near the Ambuja Cement plant for the children of labourers has helped them not only get acquainted with the three R's of reading, writing and arithmetic, but also soared the self-esteem of their parents.

"I am proud of my daughter and will make all-out efforts to make her a professional and not a daily-wager like me," says Jaiwanti, whose daughter Deepa is the only one from Bathinda district to clear the entrance exam for Jawaharlal Navodaya Vidyalaya for Class VIII and wants to become an engineer.

Jaiwanti lives with her family in a basti near the plant, where 60 other migrant families from Orissa stay. The school, set up under two sheds, provides education up to Class V, and the officials from the cement plant have taken services of volunteers to teach. In 2006-07, 14 students from the basti passed Class V examination and are now in Class VI in a nearby government school.

Mamta, a student, said, "Before joining this school, we used to roam around the whole day. But now, we all nurture a dream to do well in life." The basti has formed an 11- member committee, headed by one of their senior residents, Champa, who coordinates between the settlement and the cement plant officials and the volunteers. The committee holds a meeting twice a month. Demanding that the school be extended to Class X, Champa said, "The school has made a big difference to the lives of children as well as their families."

Wherewithal for studying, ranging from books to uniforms, are provided by the corporate house, which collects token money of Rs 10 from each student and deposits it with the committee. The committee uses the money on children's extra-curricular activities.

Talking with The Indian Express, Pearl Tiwari, Assistant vice-president, Ambuja Cement Foundation, CSR Arm, said, "Every private company should be aware of its social responsibility."

Heading: Farmers block rail traffic - Indian Express
Content:
Charging the government with ignoring the interests of the armed forces and the ex-servicemen, the Majha Ex-servicemen Human Rights Front today went on a hunger strike in protest against the recommendations of the Sixth Pay Commission. The protesters demanded assured employment for Army officers till the age of 60 by an Act of Parliament, besides pension benefits for jawans retiring at the age 37 years.

G S Sandhu, president of the front, said the hunger strike was being observed in over 600 districts across the country. "The government has forced us to take this step and we will not call off our stir till our demands are met," he said.

Heading: Nod for dedicated power supply to IT units - Indian Express
Content:
Peeved over the "measly" bonus for paddy, increasing input costs, high cost of diesel and non-renumerative minimum support price, seven farmers' unions today blocked rail traffic all over the state today, resulting in major inconvenience to the commuters.

Farmers blocked traffic for three hours in Rajpura, Ludhiana, Amritsar, Moga, Ferozepur, Tarn Taran, Abohar, and many other places. The seven protesting unions included Kirti Kisan Union, Jamooheri Kisan Sabha, Bharatiya Kisan Union (Ekta), Bharti Kisan Union (Krantikari), Bharti Kisan Union (Ekta) Punjab, Kisan Sangharsh Committee and Punjab Kisan Union.

Addressing the gathering of farmers here at Ladhowal, Hardev Singh Sandhu, president of the Kirti Kisan Union, said, "It is sad that the government does not act according to the recommendation of its commission. The Swaminathan Commission has very clearly stated that the farmers should get an MSP of Rs 1,050 for paddy, but the government announced Rs 880. To rub salts on our wounds, we have been given a bonus of Rs 50 per quintal. Why did the government set up a commission when it was not ready to accept the recommendations?"

Farmer union leader Mahinder Singh Seelo, president, Jamhoori Kisan Sabha, said, "The input costs in agriculture have gone up, but farmers still are not getting enough to recover the costs. This huge gap in input costs and MSP has left them broken."

They complained that farmers in the cotton belt were getting less than the MSP. They said the state government had failed to provide required facilties in the mandis. Union leaders, Nirbhay Singh Dhudike, Balkar Singh Dakaunda, Raghbir Singh, Satbir Singh and Pichhora Singh Sidhpur, said that the government was not concerned about their problems.

AMRITSAR:Farmers today blocked Flying Mail and another train for over three hours at railway stations in Amritsar, Tarn Taran and Rayya. Shouting anti-government slogans, the farmers , led by various unions, including Kisan Sangharsh Committee, charged the government with withholding the bonus on paddy. They claimed that their demand for loan waiver must be considered and the Punjab State Electricity Board should not be privatised.

Satnam Singh Pannu, a farmer leader, said the agitation would continue till the government accepted their demands.

Heading: When music melts borders - Indian Express
Content:
In a bid to woo investments in the state, the Punjab government has decided to provide dedicated power supply to IT companies setting up projects here. An in-principle decision to this effect was taken on Friday at a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, and the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) has been asked to undertake a feasibility survey to set the concept rolling.

New industry and IT companies had been shying away from investing in the state for want of uninterrupted power supply. Government sources said even the existing companies were not expanding their operations due to this reason.

Managing Director of Punjab Infotech R K Verma, confirming the development, said the decision would apply to both existing and upcoming IT units in Punjab. He said a committed infrastructure, which could include new sub-stations and transformers, would ensure uninterrupted electricity to IT corridors. "The concept development strategy is being worked out, and the PSEB will undertake an exhaustive survey," the MD said.

Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh could not attend the meeting, in which Secretary, Power, Suresh Kumar and officials of the PSEB participated. Industries Minister Manoranjan Kalia is scheduled to meet the management of reputed IT companies in New Delhi on October 24.

The decision is being viewed as crucial ahead of the meeting, where the government plans to flaunt the decision. The state government has proposed setting up of new IT corridors at Kapurthala (a 50-acre IT SEZ) and Ropar. Punjab Infotech has initiated the process of identifying land banks in the state which could be used for commissioning new IT corridors.

Kalia said, "Uninterrupted power supply is central to the industry. The CM has issued necessary instructions to the PSEB, and we are hoping investments in the months to come. The government now has concrete plans to offer companies."

Government efforts are also on to ensure synergies with other related departments to boost IT prospects. Presently, there is dearth of concerted effort with departments, largely operating in isolation when it comes to IT. A recent report by the FICCI has downgraded the prospects of investment in Punjab. FICCI's findings had said that majority of the respondents (nearly 62 per cent) took a pessimistic view of Punjab as investment destination.

* PSEB asked to undertake a feasibility survey

* Armed with this decision, Industries Minister Manoranjan Kalia is scheduled to meet the management of reputed IT companies in New Delhi on October 24

Heading: Many Congressmen oppose Preneet’s candidature - Indian Express
Content:
Soulful rendition of Sufi 'Kalaam' by Pakistani artistes mingled with Indian classical, Punjabi and Rajasthani folk music to create a feeling of 'saanjh' (unity) between India and Pakistan at 'Saanjh-2008 Fifth Amritsar-Lahore Festival' that concluded here late last evening.

The rhythmic performance by 'Punjtani' (25 dholis) from Pakistan at the onset of the festival left the audience spellbound. Creating a fusion of various kinds of music, Lakhwinder Wadali and Ashraf Ali shared the stage with musical legends from Pakistan, Sain Zahoor, Hamid Ali and Salman Amjad Amanat, son of legendary Amjad Amanat Ali Khan.

While Lakhwinder belted out an array of Punjabi folk songs, Ashraf Ali wove the magic of Rajasthani music with his presentation, 'Padharo Maro Des' and 'Jab Dekhun Banne Ki Lal Peeli Akhiyan'.

Subtleties of music were unraveled when Hamid Ali sang 'thumri', and after he left the stage, Salman Amjad Amanat Ali Khan created a musical aura. The performances were interspersed with interactions of audience with the visiting Pakistani artistes. They mainly discussed Indo-Pak relations and the need for enhancing cordiality.

Cabinet Minister Bikramjit Singh Majithia extended "hand of sincerest friendship" to the East Punjab.

Usman Peerzada of Rafi Peer Theatre Group said medium of music and theatre could help in strengthening the bond of friendship between India and Pakistan. Faizan Peerzada, one of the directors of Rafi Peer Theatre Group, echoed Usman's views.

A segment of the programme would be held in Lahore next month.

Heading: Leaders demand more bonus on paddy - Indian Express
Content:
A few Congress workers from Patiala had registered their opposition against Member of Parliament Preneet Kaur before AICC observer Jagannath Shetty, when he had recently held a meeting with various party groups in the constituency.

Sources said the dissidents said their MP did not steer them during the recent civic and panchayat polls in the state, where the Congress suffered a drubbing. Sources, however, said Shetty was also given a resolution passed by the District Congress Committee for giving the ticket to Preneet. Congress leaders said this was done primarily by some close associates of Preneet, which did not have the assent of various senior leaders and MLAs.

Shetty faced some tough moments in the interiors of Patiala, where some MLAs opposed to Preneet's candidature. However, Shetty refused to comment on the controversy. "I am yet to submit the report to the AICC, so I cannot share its contents," he said. Sources said Shetty also met many sitting and former MLAs, who opposed Preneet. He also had a dinner at the residence of Samana MLA Brahm Mohindra, who does not share a good rapport with former CM Capt Amarinder Singh or his wife.

Sources said those against MP's candidature were of the view that "she has represented the area for 10 years now and the baton should now be handed over to a young candidate". Some even supported the candidature of her son Raninder Singh.

Youth Cong polls

CHANDIGARH: Buoyed by the response to its membership drive, the Punjab Youth Congress, which registered over three lakh members in September, says this would help the party in the ensuing LS elections. The drive will now lead to the election of office-bearers of the state Youth Congress at block and district levels. Punjab Youth Congress president Vijay Inder Singla said the record number of registrations in just one month was a good indicator. He said the three-day visit of Rahul Gandhi to Punjab has charged up the youths.

Heading: Post-debt waiver, agriculture credit growth takes a hit - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Congress has urged AICC president Sonia Gandhi for an additional Rs 50 bonus on per quintal on paddy. A few days ago, the Center had announced Rs 50 bonus, which has been ridiculed by the Akali government in Punjab.

A state unit delegation, led by Punjab president Mohinder Singh Kaypee, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal, Preneet Kaur, Rana Gurjit, Avtar Singh Brar, Tej Prakash, Lal Singh, Parminder Singh Pinky met the Congress president in New Delhi on Monday. In a memorandum, the delegation sought concessions for the lower sections of the society. "The small and medium loans running in thousands of rupees in each case also deserve a waiver, which will cost the state exchequer only a few crore in each state," it said.

The memorandum said more than 25,000 lives were lost and equal number of families faced the wrath of terrorism. The UPA government has sanctioned a package for the 1984 riot victims of Delhi, but gave nothing to terrorist victims of Punjab, the delegation said. Pinky and Raj Kumar Verka urged the UPA chairperson to convene a special session of the AICC in Punjab which was last held in 1975.

Heading: Planning, statistical depts to be separated - Indian Express
Content:
The Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme 2008 has hit agricultural credit in Haryana, which has declined substantially in the first quarter of this year. Debt waiver and relief to about seven lakh Haryana farmers to the tune of Rs 2,000 crore has led to credit growth not meeting targets for the first quarter of 2008-09, Haryana Special Secretary, Finance,

Vijay Vardhan said at the state-level bankers' conference (SLBC) held in Chandigarh today.

"Advances for the first quarter are Rs 3,625 crore against the targeted Rs 6,000 crore and banks need to enhance credit through self-help groups (SHGs)," he added. Punjab National Bank (PNB), convenor bank for the SLBC, said the first phase of financial inclusion has been completed in Haryana and no block of the state is now unbanked with opening of at least one account in every rural household of the 21 districts of the state.

Haryana is growing at 11.2 per cent, higher than the national average, said PNB CMD Dr K.C. Chakraborty, adding that the achievement of banks in respect of national goals was satisfactory. Banks need to help small borrowers availing credit up to Rs 50,000 by dispensing with the practice of calling for no-due certificate, but obtaining self-declaration instead, he added.

On the impact of the economic crisis on the country's second largest public sector lender, he said they are not facing any liquidity crunch and have adequate funds to lend money to borrowers. "We have thousands of crores of rupees as reserves for lending purposes," Chakraborty said, while commending on the timely steps taken by regulators and policy makers to insulate the Indian financial market from the adverse impact of global turmoil.

"The present situation is also ideal for expanding to other countries. Anything in the overseas markets is available at cheaper rates. Banks who have the strength to expand overseas must go for it," he said.

Heading: ‘India has potential to be the world’s food factory’ - Indian Express
Content:
The state government is reportedly planning to segregate the Planning and Statistical Department for better administrative purposes.

The idea is to strengthen the State Planning Board at the state as well as at the district level so that planning could emerge from the grassroots level and people's participation could also be ensured.

Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda recently held a meeting in this regard and after hearing the discussion, he agreed in principle to strengthen the State Planning Board by separation of planning wing from the economic and statistical organisation. In the coming months, the government will take necessary steps in this regard, say sources.

A senior government official said that for long it had been felt that there was a need to separate the economic and statistical organisation from that of planning for effective working of both the departments.

Most of the other states in the country have already segregated the two departments keeping in view the vision document of the Planning Commission. At the Centre, too, the Ministry of Statistics and the Planning

Commission have been working independently.

The official said the State Planning Board must function as a counterpart of the Planning Commission of the Central government and must have advisers/experts in various fields on its panel similar to that of the Planning Commission with the support of the Planning Department.

The Planning Commission is reportedly in the process of formulating a new scheme for strengthening of Planning Process in the state/districts under which funds will be provided to the states by the Central government for strengthening its planning machinery.

In view of this, the planning and the statistics departments need to be segregated to be able to take full advantage of the Central government's initiative.

The District Planning Unit functioning in each district will work under the Department of Planning.

It was also decided that the modalities for strengthening of Department of Planning in support of State Planning Board, including requirement of additional manpower at each level along with additional financial liabilities, will be worked out and put up at the earliest to the government for approval.

According to the vision document of the Planning Commission, the formulation of the Annual/Five Year Plans should start at the village level, block level,and then gradually to the district level and not vice-versa. It, therefore, requires strengthening of infrastructure at the district-level planning.

Also, monitoring and evaluation of any development scheme/project is as important as the project itself.

Separate monitoring cells need to be created at the district level.

The proposed change will benefit the public as the government would be able to chalk out planning for the people at the grassroots level, according to sources. This way the government would be able to incorporate the views and demands of the people in a better way.

Heading: Kufri residents on a revival mission - Indian Express
Content:
India has the potential to become a food factory not only for the country, but for the entire world. Accordingly, the size of the food processing industry would triple with investment going up from Rs 4,60,000 crore to Rs 13,80,000 crore by 2015.

This was a common view of food experts during a two-day national seminar on "Food Safety and Quality", organised on the premises of the Guru Jambheshwar University here today.

The seminar was inaugurated by Dr Kuldip Dhindsa, Director General of JCD Vidyapeeth, Sirsa. Vice-Chancellor of the University, Lt Gen Dr D.D.S. Sandhu (retd), Dr Dhindsa and Registrar Prof R.S. Jaglan released a book titled "Food Safety and Quality" on the occasion.

Shivrein, general manager of Parle Products Ltd,

Bahadurgarh, was the guest of honour. An alumni meet was also organised at the Department.

Expressing concern over the food safety and quality of the food available on rehris, Dr Kuldip Dhindsa said the food is unhygienic for consumption and the main reason for deadly diseases like diarrhoea and cholera, besides other water-borne diseases.

Dr Dhindsa further said safety of food was a matter of perpetual concern. In the anxiety of feeding millions of people, Dr Dhindsa said the safety standards of the food chain were neglected.

Prof R.S. Jaglan, Registrar of the University, said safety of food implies absence or the presence of acceptable and safe levels of contamination, adulteration and naturally occurring toxicants that may be injurious to health.

Heading: More BJP leaders to join Cong: Kaul Singh - Indian Express
Content:
Gear up to convert Kufri into community-based tourism spot

Where the government fails, the community shows the way to change. That's exactly what the 130-odd families of Kufri propose to do in their drive to showcase Kufri as the state's first community-based tourism destination.

For years, Kufri has attracted millions of tourists, popular film units and skiing enthusiasts. But it's pitiable condition, environmental pollution, vanishing snow trails, drying natural water sources and abrupt decline in arrival of quality tourists have left the locals, who earn their livelihood from tourism, worried about Kufri's future.

Investments to the tune of crores seem to have already gone downhill. What's left at Kufri is a toxic cesspool of horse dung, broken tracks and haphazardly built shopping counters, often covered with shabby polysheets.

"That's not the Kufri of our dreams. It's no longer a tourist spot that can attract visitors and support families in its vicinity," rues Amar Singh, a villager.

The villagers are not alone in the drive to turn Kufri into a model of community-based tourism. The Rotary Club (mid-town), Shimla, backed by leading hotelier Dhian Chand and academicians, including Aparna Negi, have helped villagers prepare a blueprint for Kufri.

This month, the Club engaged the services of a Netherlands-based organisation, Pum, which sent its member, Joseph, an environmentalist who camped at Kufri and came up with an integrated plan for Kufri's revival. "If the community takes up two new alternatives — reinventing Kufri as a clean and hygienic spot and remodeling their occupation, including pony business — I can guarantee you a place matching Amsterdam," says Joseph.

Joseph has already held meetings with Dr Nagin Nanda, Director, Environment and Scientific Technologies, and told him about his observations on Kufri's deteriorating environment. The villagers also propose to meet Secretary-cum-Commissioner, Tourism, Manisha Nanda.

What has been helpful for the villagers is the state government's new scheme of home-stay tourism. They propose to improve their existing houses, take up floriculture and grow organic vegetables as an alternative venture. "The tourists staying in houses under home-stay will have a choice to pluck green organic vegetables and get them cooked on demand," says Amar Singh.

Significantly, all local families are ready to sacrifice their pony business since it has become an environmental hazard. The horse dug and mud at Kufri, a dirty side of the pony business, has already ruined Kufri. "We will not contribute to Kufri's unnatural death; rather we want it to become a world-famous destination," declares Sohan Singh, a member of the Kufri panchayat.

Dhian Chand says the Rotary Club will act as a catalyst in bringing villagers, government agencies and experts on a common platform for the revival of Kufri.

Heading: Shimla airport to have aviation observatory - Indian Express
Content:
Pradesh Congress Committee chief Kaul Singh Thakur today claimed that the campaign to strengthen the Congress was riding a high wave and many more BJP leaders were in contact with the party. Though senior BJP leader Maheshwar Singh has ruled out joining the Congress, there were other big BJP leaders who were ready to switchover in the coming days, claimed Kaul. Addressing mediapersons in Shimla today, Kaul Singh said the party has succeeded in dwarfing the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in the state by winning over Karan Singh and later, with the exit of Vijai Singh Mankotia from active politics.

He demanded that the government should implement the retention policy for regularisation of unauthorised structures. He condemned the latest decision of the government as per which the electricity and IPH department have been directed by the town and country planning (TCP) department to cut off all power, water and sewerage connection to the buildings within Shimla Municipal Corporation for which no-objection certificates have not been obtained from the TCP.

"The government is harassing people this way. Despite there being a provision to give relief to people through implementation of retention policy, the government is going for an action that would harm at least 30 per cent buildings in the town," said Kaul Singh. A formal announcement of appointment of former minister Kuldeep Kumar as head of the Schedule Cast cell of the party was also made by Kaul Singh today.

Heading: HFCL staff denied entry on factory premises - Indian Express
Content:
Shimla Airport at Jubarhatti would now get an aviation observatory that is expected to make the landing of in-bound flights easier during bad weather conditions. The Indian Metrological Department (IMD) has already completed the initial formalities for the observatory and the equipment would soon be installed, confirmed Director General of IMD, Ajeet Tyagi.

At present, there is no apparatus at the airport that can automatically convey the sudden change in weather in Shimla due to which flights coming to Shimla from Delhi or Chandigarh could be informed in time. There have also been many instances where the flights took off from another station but could not get landing permission due to bad weather.

The Himachal Pradesh government has been insisting on expansion of Shimla and Kullu airports and has informed the Central government about the requirement. Installation of an aviation observatory is a prelude to the future expansion. A team of the Civil Aviation Ministry has already visited Shimla airport thrice to assess it for expansion. The only expansion in recent times has been that of introduction of an additional terminal at Bhuntar airport in Kullu.

Tyagi, who was in Shimla to attend a workshop on the user requirements of weather and climate in western Himalayan region, said that besides the aviation observatory which would establish a direct link with other airports, Himachal would get more advanced technology to predict disasters such as a cloud burst. A doppler radar has already been sanctioned by the IMD for Himachal that can help in forecasting cloudbursts, but allotment of land is still awaited for it.

State Horticulture Minister Narender Bragta was present at the opening ceremony and assured that requisite land for the radar in Shimla would be allotted. It would benefit areas within 30 kilometres of its radius. Bragta also asked the IMD to consider another doppler radar for tribal areas of Lahaul and Spiti, Kinnaur and Pangi. Bragta said the state government is drawing an extensive policy in collaboration with the Met department to help the state tackle natural disasters, which wreak havoc on agriculture and horticulture economy.

Heading: Ahluwalia sent in 14-days judicial remand - Indian Express
Content:
Following alleged imposition of a ban on the entry of workers by the management, work at Himachal Futuristic Company Limited at Chambaghat came to a halt today. Irked over the alleged unilateral decision of the management of the factory, the workers assembled outside the factory's main gate and raised slogans.

Trouble started when the employees of the unit formed an independent union after withdrawing their association with the Bhartiya Mazdoor Sangathan (BMS). They alleged that some leaders of BMS were siding with the management. The workers were demanding a hike in their basic salary, beside various other benefits under the provision of existing labour laws and directions from the state government.

They said the management of the factory had ordered transfer of one of their colleagues to Delhi without any valid reason. They said the issue was taken up with the management, but when the employees went for work today, they were asked to sign on certain documents. After their refusal, their entry was banned on the factory premises.

Heading: Bridge on Jalal river awaiting inauguration for yr - Indian Express
Content:
Subash Ahluwalia was given 14 days of judicial remand by a Shimla court today. Ahluwalia's bail application came up for hearing in the court of Special Judge J.L. Gupta, who, after hearing both sides, remanded him in judicial custody and directed that the accused be lodged in Kaithu jail in Shimla till November 3.

Meanwhile, Ahluwalia also moved a bail application in the High Court, that would come up for hearing on October 22.

Ahluwalia's counsel M.S. Chandel resisted the judicial remand of the accused, while the prosecution replied that there was enough material on record to detain the accused in judicial custody. The Special Public Prosecutor argued that though it is not mentioned in the remand application that the accused be remanded in judicial lock-up, he made an oral request for it.

His counsel also submitted an application to the special court, requesting for shifting Ahluwalia's medical treatment to PGI, Chandigarh. In his application, Ahluwalia had submitted that he was being over-medicated by the doctors in hospitals of Shimla and needed immediate medical treatment at a better place.

The hearing on the application would come up on November 3.

Throughout the 13 days of his police remand, the Vigilance Bureau was unable to interrogate Ahluwalia as he remained admitted to the hospital and was not available for interrogation. The prosecution stated before the court that his police remand will not serve any purpose.

The court directed the Vigilance DSP investigating the case to make arrangements for transfer of custody and send the judicial custody warrant of the accused to superintendent of Kaithu sub-jail.

Meanwhile, Subhash Ahluwalia remained admitted to Indus Hospital. By evening, the Vigilance submitted custody warrants to officials at Kaithu jail, but there was no move so far to remove him from the hospital to jail.

Heading: Seminar on non-violence - Indian Express
Content:
The bridge constructed on Jalal river at a cost of Rs 5.5 crore has been awaiting inauguration for the last one year. The bridge, measuring 280 meters, was completed last year. But the previous chief minister Virbhadra Singh could not find time to inaugurate it, giving the opportunity BJP Chief Minister PK Dhumal.

The bridge connects Dadahu, near Renuka, to Trimli and Dhaula Kuan on the Nahan-Paonta Road national highway 72, reducing the distance by 35 kilometers. The bridge is already in use, and its inauguration is only a formality now. Dhumal will preside over the inaugural function on November 8, to be held during the Renuka Fair.

Heading: Boyfriend hits girl at a Noida nightclub, fractures her arm - Indian Express
Content:
A three-day seminar on "Non-violence" began at Indian Institute of Advance Studies (IIAS) here today, with leading scholars, academicians and intellectuals deliberating on the issue.

In his welcome address, Prof Peter Ronald deSouza, IIAS Director, reflected on the need for exploring the concept of non-violence in the present context. He referred to the growing tendency of violence and asked the

participants to closely focus

their deliberations.

Dr Gangeya Mukherji, a fellow at the Institute, said the scholars were meeting in disturbed times when people across the globe have come to feel that honest negotiation and fair agreement is no longer possible.

In the first session, chaired by Syed Shahabuddin, Prof S.C. Bhattacharya presented a paper on "Himsa-Ahimsa debate in early India: Two Mahabharata Episodes", in which he examined some of the stands of the

complex "Brahmanical attitude to Ahimsa".

Heading: DU launches IT course for disabled students - Indian Express
Content:
A call centre employee has alleged that she was allegedly abused and pushed from the stairs by her boyfriend, due to which she fractured her arm, inside Elevate, a pub located at the Centrestage Mall in Noida.

According to the girl, Palka Malik, a resident of Sector 19, she had gone to Elevate on Sunday night with one Abhinav Chugh, her ex-fiance and his neighbour Vishal. While Abhinav and Palka were dancing, Abhinav allegedly asked her to join another couple so that he could dance with the other girl. "We had a heated argument when I refused to disturb the other couple," said Malik, who has lodged an FIR at the Sector 20 police station. There were around 15 people in the pub at the time of the incident.

Malik alleged that Abhinav, a resident of Ghaziabad, abused and pushed her from the stairs of the first floor around 3.45 am.

"I fractured my right arm as a result. There were no security officers in the pub to take note of the situation. However, one Ashish Agarwal, also present in the club, came to my aid and took me to Max Hospital," the girl said. Meanwhile, the PRO of Elevate, Tarina, has refuted allegations that any such incident took place inside the pub. "We usually remain open till 4 am and there are security men and bouncers inside the pub to take action in any such situation. According to the pub's security officer, the couple had a fight outside the pub," she added.

Heading: Court dismisses bail plea of advocate charged with extortion - Indian Express
Content: Disabled students at Delhi University can now learn IT skills at the new Information and Communication Technology Centre set up jointly by the NTPC Foundation and Delhi University. The centre was inaugurated Monday by NTPC's Chief Managing Director R S Sharma and DU's Pro Vice-Chancellor S K Tandon. There are about 1,000 physically-challenged students currently enrolled at the DU. Students will be awarded a diploma and a certificate under the short term course scheme of DU. The centre has cost the NTPC about Rs 30 lakh. The centre is equipped with software with screen magnification software for students suffering from low vision, officials said. The university will be responsible for designing the courses for the students while NTPC Foundation will fund the infrastructure and recurring costs, including teachers' expenses and maintenance.

Heading: Annual installment to Indian football - Indian Express
Content:
Advocate Ravindra Chaddha's second appearance in court as an accused failed to bring any respite to him after his bail plea was dismissed on the ground that his role was instrumental as tainted money changed hands.

Chaddha, Crime Branch Inspector K G Tyagi, Sub-Inspector Mukesh and Assistant Sub-Inspector Rajvir, were arrested on Friday by Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) sleuths on charges of falsely implicating a businessman and attempts to extort money from his son in a murder that took place last September. As the police custody remand of the other three accused got over on Monday, they were produced before Special Judge A S Yadav when, Chaddha, who was a counsel for Delhi Police before the Delhi High Court as an additional public prosecutor till 2006, moved his bail plea.

The advocate's advocate averred during the hearing that no specific role could be attributed to Chaddha and that there was no requirement to keep him in further custody.

ASJ Yadav, however, differed, considering that initial investigation and the sting tape had showed that Chaddha was acting as a conduit for illegal transaction of bribe on behalf of Inspector Tyagi.
