"The entire transcription shows Chaddha was acting as a conduit on behalf of Tyagi —most of the talks (between the complainant and the accused) took place in his chamber," noted the judge while dismissing his bail application.

Meanwhile, the prosecution sought extension of police remand of Tyagi, contending his further custodial interrogation was imperative to get to the root of the case. The prosecutor argued that they had information regarding his properties in Meerut and Shahdara in Delhi, which were disproportionate to his sources of income, and he was to be taken to these places.

Accepting the demand, ASJ Yadav extended Tyagi's police custody by another three days, till October 23. However, Tyagi's junior colleagues were sent to judicial custody till November 3. The accused were picked up by the ACB on a complaint by Gopal Krishan Aggarwal and his son Abhinav after the latter filmed a sting on them. Gopal Krishan was arrested last December in connection with the murder of Vijay Singh Yadav, a proclaimed 'bad character' of Hauz Qazi in Delhi, near his office in Sitaram Bazar. According to Abhinav, Inspector Tyagi, the investigating officer, had then, with the help of Chaddha, started taking bribes from them and extorted over Rs 26 lakh, of which the advocate took his share of Rs 4 lakh. After the complainant failed to fulfill the demand of another Rs 25 lakh, on August 1, Tyagi used his influence to get a case registered against Gopal Krishan under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), he alleged.

Heading: ‘Laxman dismissal made my career’ - Indian Express
Content:
Wung United play only one tournament a year but the Manipur club has provided ample players to big teams

For Wung United, change is the only constant. The defending champions of the RN Tamchon Trophy have only one thing in common, year after year — their impeccable performance in this tournament, the only one the club plays in every year. The team composition keeps changing and team officials move on to other things apart from football, allowing another set of faces to take centrestage — all this, for some exposure and in search of greener pastures.

On Monday, they entered the semi-finals of the 2008 edition, thrashing DMZP 3-1 at the Ambedkar Stadium. And this when they are not officially registered as a club, something they do not seem too concerned about. "I have heard people call our club and the tournament a 'local' one. The basic idea behind the tournament is to highlight the talent of the North-East,"says this year's team manager Apan Shimray, who earns a living teaching English Literature at Jamia Milia Islamia University. "Apart from the infrastructural and financial shortcomings, what we really miss is the media coverage back home. Now, we have seventeen Delhi-based players out of the 22," he adds.

The team has scored six goals in four matches compared to 25 goals in six matches last year and is without six of their main players from last year, but Shimray is not upset. On the contrary, he is proud of the six who are absent — since they are all playing for bigger clubs.

"Duidong was picked by Mohammedan Sporting of Kolkata while Ninglei and N Shimrah joined Churchill Brothers. Achan Keising is now playing for a Mumbai club after a few coaches and officials from these clubs spotted them. That's the purpose of this tournament," adds Shimray.

One of the six was Sochungmi Raleng, the highest scorer for Services in Santosh Trophy 2008 and currently on a one-year contract with I-League debutants Chirag United. "He (Raleng) was playing for Army XI and then we arranged for his participation in the RM Tamchon Trophy last year. He scored thirteen of the twenty-five goals that we scored.

Three months later, he went to become the highest scorer at the Santosh Trophy and now he is in the main striker for Chirag United," Shimray adds.

Coach Edmund Hungshi says co-ordination is not an issue. "We prepare in advance through the thirteen units that monitor students from the North-East in various colleges of Delhi University. Then, the sports union of various institutions gives us the best opportunity to finalise," he says.

Hungshi's own identity gives an idea what Wung United's identity is all about. After introducing himself as a former u-14 representative for Manipur, he reveals that he is also a Zakir Hussain College pass-out and has been a coach for two years at Apex School.

And after October 25th (the final day of the tournament), he will go back to studies — reading a few preparatory books on Civil Services. In the other quarter-final on Monday, Sinlung HSA FC beat Chandel United 2-1.

Heading: Sowjanya dumps Dipti - Indian Express
Content:
For the past one week, Chetanya Nanda had been putting in extra hours at the Delhi Ranji nets, to camouflage his disappointment at missing out on a spot in the Challenger and setting himself up to the extra grind. When he did make the mark — on Monday, Nanda was named replacement for Amit Mishra in the India Blue side led by Yuvraj Singh — the leg-spinner had little time to savour the moment.

"This is my first big call and I don't even have time to react. Only this morning at the nets, Virat and others were talking of taking the early flight to Cuttack and discussing their travel schedules while I ignored them. On hindsight, I shoudl have taken more interest," he says jokingly. "When a friend called up to inform me of my selection, I dismissed it as a prank. It was only much later, when I started getting calls from everywhere, did I realise it was true. All this while I was preparing for the longer format, suddenly in two days' time, I have to play limited overs cricket, probably one of the most important matches of my career," he says.

The 29-year old, though, feels he's up to the task. "It's all about rhythm — if you are getting a good feel, then minor variations like bowling a bit flatter for one-day cricket isn't a problem. Right now I am feeling very good and confident about my bowling," he says.

Nanda believes that his dismissals of Misbah-ul-Haq and VVS Laxman changed his career. "Those two high-profile wickets in the Nissar Trophy and Irani Cup respectively brought me a lot of attention, as much as my five-wicket hauls. I have had a good season and to get big names in your kitty, especially those who play spin very well, only boosts your confidence," he says.

Heading: Bond with the best - Indian Express
Content:
Qualifier Sowjanya Bavishetty of Andhra Pradesh defeated sixth seed Dipti Srivastava of West Bengal 6-4, 7-5 in the first round. Top seed Shalini Sahoo of Delhi had no such problems in cruising past wild card Soniya Dayal — she defeated her 6-3, 6-2. Heading: The Joker In the Pack - Indian Express
Content:
Want to dress like James Bond? Master tailor Angelo Petrucci reveals the secrets behind 007's sharp suits

When Italian tailor Angelo Petrucci, 36, was asked to design suits for Pierce Brosnan for the Bond film, GoldenEye in 1995 he worked on creating illusions for Brosnan's lean frame. "He's great as Bond but we were used to the more strapping Sean Connery," says Petrucci, who was in Delhi recently to custom make suits for select customers here. Petrucci represents Brioni, the menswear label from Italy. He's been designing for Bond films till the last release starring Daniel Craig, Casino Royale.

Dressed in a crisp blue suit at Brioni's store at The Oberoi, Petrucci talks fondly of his first Bond experience. "The character James Bond has immaculate style. We selected the best fabrics, Prince of Galles-Glencheck, Grisaglia-Sharkskin and pinstripes which were in vogue that time," he says. Petrucci designed 70 suits for GoldenEye, each costing 3,000 euros. "All suits for James Bond were designed as per the scene. So I would study each Bond film, scene by scene and design a suit accordingly," he explains. He met Brosnan just thrice, off the set. "Once at a London nightclub, then with his costume designer Lindy Hemming and once he invited me to his palatial bungalow in Ireland," says Petrucci.

The prolific tailor has also designed clothes for 24 heads of state like Gerhard Schroeder, Nelson Mandela and Azlan Shah, the former Sultan of Malaysia. "The thought process involved in designing suits for presidents is very different from Bond. They're not jumping off buildings and they know what they want," he smiles. This is Petrucci's first experience designing for Indian men. More than 24 prominent Delhiites, from politicians to businessmen, visited Brioni to check out Petrucci's suits, each of which retails for over Rs 2 lakh. The scion of the JK Tyre group, Hemant Singhania, popped in for a look, as did city lawyer Ankur Chawla and a prominent city advertising head honcho.

Petrucci is all excited about the upcoming Bond flick, Quantum of Solace, though he has nothing to do with Bond's attire in this flick. "I'm not sure who's done the clothes," he says and adds a tad forlornly, "But I hope they ask me again." Petrucci has his favourites when it comes to Bond, and Brosnan clearly stands out. "Brosnan was more elegant and charming. Daniel Craig is 8 cms shorter, more athletic, but not as charming as Brosnan," he sighs. Although Petrucci is no longer designing suits for Bond films, he is sure he will, soon.

Heading: Wired World - Indian Express
Content: When Manish Arora takes up the crowning act of a fashion week, somehow, you don't mind terribly that the show started over an hour late. For the Grand Finale of Wills India Fashion Week, Arora interpreted the circus, a theme he says that has fascinated him for a while. The ramp was converted into a mini-ring, the models had their faces painted like clowns and the show area was jam packed with people. His ensembles ranged from clown pants to built in bras to mini skirts and voluminous jackets. Spunky and outrageous, with ostrich feather embellishments and leather sequins, the king of colour once again created a madly vivid palette, the way only he can.

Heading: Haute Face - Indian Express
Content: When Dutch jazz musician Yuri Honing and his trio visited Delhi for a performance at Select Citywalk on Saturday, the man had plans other than just the concert. "Wired Paradise is my quintet, which is largely inspired by Hollywood. It mixes electronica with rock and jazz. And I plan to take it to Mumbai since that's where the real work is happening," says Honing, who plays the saxophone and is on his third visit to the country. "Since the blend of Carnatic music with western jazz has been done for many decades, I'm looking to add another layer to the musicians in India who are working with newer sounds of jazz," he says. Although Honing's trio is progressive jazz that has combined the classical Arab music in their repertoire, his quintet is edgy and different with electronica incorporated regularly. "Jazz music is alive and it's not the same that our grandfathers used to hear. It's has been improvised a lot more than people realise," he says. Honing already has three more visits chalked out and has his eyes fixed on tinsel town.

Heading: Domestic help gets death penalty for killing employer's son - Indian Express
Content:
The fashion week threw up two new stunners

When newbie Malavika Rane walked down the runway for the Delhi Fashion Week, most designers took her to be a seasoned model. The 21-year-old was adjudged the "New Face" by Tikka Shatrujit Singh, adviser, Louis Vuitton and bagged a gift voucher for Rs 2.5 lakh. "I had been doing fashion shows off and on through college but took it up seriously only after my graduation," she said. The Mumbai-based model walked the ramp for seven designers including Malini Ramani, James Ferriera, Gaurav Gupta and Rahul Reddy. "She is different and has an interesting face. In fact, I did not know that she was walking the ramp for the first time," says designer Gaurav Gupta.

Another big find was Tanzanian model Millen Megsi who was judged the "Face of the Week" among 22 models in the finale and took home a gift voucher from LV.

The contest was floated on the second day of the fashion week and Megsi was every designer's choice. "Black models are gorgeous and you will see more of them in the next fashion week," said designer Tarun Tahiliani in whose show Megsi cut a decadent figure in a sterile white jersey gown. So, are black models an inclusive gesture in the multi cultural city? "As far as I know, it's not the first time black models are walking the ramp in India. In fact, they add more diversity and reflect the global world we live in," said Gupta.

Heading: Cabbies held for NRI’s kidnap, murder - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi Court on Tuesday awarded death sentence to a domestic help for killing his employer's four-year-old son when he resisted his attempt to rape his sister in 2006.

Additional Sessions Judge Babu Lal awarded the capital punishment to Sanjay Das, a resident of Bihar, after holding him guilty under section 302 of Indian Penal Code.

"I award you death sentence for murdering a four-year child. You can file an appeal in 30 days before the High Court," the court said.

The Court also held Das, in his early twenties, guilty for raping one of his employer's daughter and imposed a fine of Rs 3,500 on him.

In this case, Das killed the four year old boy when he had resisted the servant's attempt to rape his sister on the fateful day of October 19, 2006.

Das, who was hired by his employer just three days before the incident, had brutally killed the boy and fled from the employer's residence in Roop Nagar in North Delhi.

He was arrested from Haridwar a day after the incident.

Heading: Metro wields the axe on engineers, fines contractor - Indian Express
Content:
Saudi-based businessman had taken private taxi from IGI; was robbed, murdered, body dumped on NH-8

Nine days after Gurgaon police found an unidentified body on National Highway-8 and later learnt it was that of an NRI businessman, Delhi Police today arrested two persons for the kidnap, robbery and murder of K T Shameer.

The 39-year-old cloth merchant from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, was abducted from outside IGI Airport by private cabbies late October 10 evening. He was robbed and the body thrown in the bushes on Delhi-Jaipur highway, near Manesar. Shameer, whose business trip to India began on October 7, had arrived that evening (October 10) from Ahmedabad on a Spice Jet flight (SG-218).

Palam police today arrested Manish, 24, and Monu, 25, from Sanjay Gandhi T-point when the duo was returning from Haridwar. A third accused, one Anil, is still absconding, Joint Commissioner of Police (Operations) Amulya Patnaik said. "They were interrogated and were found involved," Patnaik said.

The police have learnt from their interrogation that Shameer had stepped out of IGI Airport sometime after 9.30 pm on October 10. But instead of taking a prepaid taxi, he went to the trio's private taxi: a white Ambassador; registration number DL1T-6001. The taxi belongs to Manish's elder brother and he was behind the wheels, as Monu and Anil pinned Shameer down in the rear seat.

The car sped off towards Jaipur on NH-8. As they hit the highway, police said, the two in the backseat held a countrymade pistol to Shameer's head and tied his hands. They then calmly took away his two bags, two cellphones, cash, ATM cards and other belongings. Thereafter, they shot Shameer and threw the body on the highway.

Body found in the bushes
The police in Bilaspur (Gurgaon) recovered the body on October 11 and registered an FIR under IPC Section 302 (murder) against unknown persons. But since they could not identify the body for the next three days, the police buried him on October 14 — the day Shameer's cousin Afzal, based in Chennai, filed a missing complaint with Palam police (see box).

"The accused dumped the body on the highway, between Manesar and Bilaspur (in Gurgaon), and sped off," JCP (Operations) Amulya Patnaik said. "We checked all prepaid taxi records at IGI after receiving the (missing) complaint on October 14, and then asked many private cabbies and security staff.

"We also checked CCTV footage."

The elaborate searches bore result: police found the trio, who operated as cabbies at the airport, were not seen since October 10, Patnaik said.

Sources said the first clue, that Shameer took a private taxi, came from CCTV footage.

The police then found from the trio's families, based in East Mehram Nagar, that they had gone to Haridwar. All three had switched off their cellphones and used another car to flee — the white Ambassador car was traced in Haridwar. Officials said that they had also withdrawn money from Shameer's account in Riyadh's Al-Razi Bank.

The police upped their watch, and the duo's luck ran out this morning when police intercepted their car at Sanjay Gandhi T-point.

Victim had called home but did not connect
Shameer had rung up his wife in Riyadh at 5 pm and 9 pm on October 7, after landing in Mumbai. But, police said, the calls did not connect; his wife found the cellphone unreachable thereafter. Shameer's Chennai-based cousin, Afzal, was in touch with the victim till October 10 and filed a missing report at Palam police station on October 14.

Shameer's brother Dr Shaheer Kaithal also arrived from Australia on October 14. Shameer comes from Mahe in Kerala and was settled in Riyadh for the past 12 years.

He was booked on a return flight to Riyadh on October 12 after meeting a friend in Delhi on October 10.

Security system at IGI
* Delhi Police mans security and traffic outside the terminals
* CCTV cameras installed at airport and departure halls, but not in the range of prepaid taxi booths and taxi parking
* Two or three officers can usually be found outside the airport, and one traffic official at the prepaid taxi booth
* Taxi owners registered with prepaid booth can be traced easily but many private taxi cabs also operate in and around IGI; authorities do not possess any records of these

Heading: Teen boy falls off rooftop, pierced by rod, in hospital - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) on Monday imposed a penalty of Rs 10 lakh on Afcons, the contractor building the Vikas Marg stretch of the elevated Metro line and dismissed its assistant engineer in charge of the site. The action comes a day after two persons were killed and a dozen injured when an under-construction bridge of the elevated Metro line collapsed at Laxmi Nagar.

The DMRC also suspended a junior engineer at the site and removed the Afcons project manager and deputy project manager from all DMRC works in future.

Delhi Metro officials said further action against the contractor would be decided after the panel, formed after Sunday morning's mishap, completes its inquiry. The technical committee comprises S N Sinha (professor, IIT-Delhi), Des Charnock (international safety expert, general consultants to DMRC), and Rajan Kataria (chief engineer-design, DMRC).

Delhi Metro spokesperson Anuj Dayal said the panel would take about 10 days to complete the inquiry.

Dayal also said every launcher on Metro lines under construction would now work under the supervision of a DMRC assistant engineer to ensure safety. 

Meanwhile, the accident site was teeming with labourers, engineers and DMRC officials, as well as curious onlookers who came to Laxmi Nagar to get a first-hand view of the "action site". "It's not the same as seeing it on the television — the gravity has only just struck me," Raju Saniwal, who works with a courier delivery company in North Delhi, said.

The DMRC, meanwhile, has assigned almost 400 labourers and assorted officials to clear the debris, even as area residents tried to come to terms with the crash. In the narrow alleys that flank each side of Vikas Marg, the main connector to Trans-Yamuna areas of East Delhi, residents stood fixed on balconies watching recovery work. "I cannot help but feel fortunate that the slabs fell one by one, not all at the same time. Had that happened, our clinic would have suffered extensive damage," said Vikas Kakkar, an administrator at Walia Medical Clinic, a dispensary overlooking the mishap site.

"Many labourers, including the operator of the crane crushed, were saved because it was their tea time early in the morning — they were assembled in one corner," Kakkar said.

Metro officials at the site, some specially flown in from Mumbai, were still in shock. "DMRC has a great reputation when it comes to reliability and safety," said a senior engineering supervisor (name withheld on request), summoned from Mumbai right after the incident early Sunday. "What happened here feels so much like a natural calamity — something that occurs despite all procedures and regulations."

Meanwhile, many residents claimed that one more body was recovered from the rubble this morning. Kakkar said, "There was another crane at the site and its operator was inside when the accident took place. I saw them remove the body; they sent it off during the early hours today."

Metro officials, though, confirmed that no more casualty was reported.

(Spot reporting by MANDAKINI GAHLOT)

Heading: Days after Jamia Nagar ‘excursion’, 4 UP cops transferred - Indian Express
Content:
In a freak accident, a 14-year-old boy was pierced by a rod after falling from the terrace of his school in West Delhi on Monday morning. The boy miraculously survived and is recovering at Deen Dayal Upadhyay (DDU) Hospital.

Doctors said the rod had got in from one side of Shivdutt Mahato's neck and exited from the other side. "But, thankfully, none of the vital organs had been injured," hospital Medical Superintendent Dr AK Prasad said. "Mahato was very lucky that his oesophagal tube had not been damaged in the accident — we just removed the rod and stitched him up."

What also helped Mahato was the fact that he did not lose much blood by the time he was rushed to the hospital.

According to an official of Thomas Public School, in West Delhi, Mahato was playing on the school terrace when he accidentally lost his footing and fell. He fell on construction material lying on the ground floor and got impaled by one of the rods, the school official said.

The school authorities called a PCR van that took him to the hospital. "The police had cut the rod before they brought him," Dr Prasad said. "He underwent operation in the morning and is now out of danger."

On July 12, Supratim Dutta, 22, an executive with HCL, was impaled by a five-foot-long iron rod on his torso after an accident in his office cab while on way to work. He has recovered following surgery at AIIMS.

Heading: In L-18 area, locals want to change all house numbers for good, ‘not due to notoriety’ though - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida policemen who had crossed the Uttar Pradesh border and entered Delhi to arrest an alleged chain-snatcher at Jamia Nagar on Thursday were transferred on Monday.

According to sources, the four policemen have been transferred after the Uttar Pradesh government took note of the alleged use of a black Verna car to chase the alleged chain-snatchers and the violence that erupted in Jamia Nagar on October 16.

According to sources, Station House Officer Ramsen Singh has been transferred to the Police Lines. Sub-Inspector Ajay Pal and Constables Kulwinder singh and Vijayveer have been transferred to the Economics Offence Wing of Varanasi, sources said. "All four policemen were beaten up in Jamia Nagar after they tried to pick up two young boys, who they claim to have been chasing," a police source said.

The Noida policemen had managed to escape.

Noida police, meanwhile, claim one of the men the police team was chasing has five cases registered against him in Sahibabad (Ghaziabad) and Delhi. "Aamir Rehman, who was allegedly chased by the UP Police team, has been booked in cases under IPC Sections pertaining to attempt to murder and assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property," the police source said.

Delhi Police officials had said after the incident that the row erupted because the UP policemen were not in uniforms and their car did not bear a registration number.

The Delhi Police had also said they were not informed about the case.

Heading: From MCD office to hall of fame - Indian Express
Content:
Just when the address L-18, Batla House was making its presence on the national map, residents of Jamia Nagar in South Delhi have mooted an idea to change numbering of houses in the area to make it more "systematic".

A month since the September 19 encounter that killed Inspector M C Sharma and two suspects of last month's serial blasts, residents say the plan has nothing to do with the encounter and the subsequent notoriety achieved by 'L-18'. The main reason they want the change is to deal with everyday problems in the way buildings are numbered in the colony at present.

Being an unauthorised colony with no definite construction plan, Jamia Nagar residents number their houses they way they wish: sometimes in sequence with the adjacent house number and, at times, randomly. The problem, thus, is locating the right address in the maze of houses in the area's narrow lanes and bylanes. For instance, anyone stepping into the colony would find houses numbered A-6, A-7 and A-8 followed by an A-161/1 popping out of nowhere.

"The postman's job is the toughest as the numbering has been extremely haphazard for years now," says Syed Asad Moin, a member of the RWA federation of Jamia Nagar. "Often, failing to find the right address, the postman drops off the mail at a house with the closest matching address."

Many a times, he says, residents do not receive electricity bills sent by the BSES. Result: dues pile up. "A huge bill is then slapped on the resident, errant by default, along with a penalty and a notice of misuse."

Now, some members of the Federation of Okhla RWA for Reforms and Development (FORWARD) are trying to work out a way to renumber the plots and organise their lives. Though the RWA members are divided on the plan's feasibility, most agree that the locality needs a more organised allotment of addresses.

M L Khan, an MCD engineer and resident of the area, is among those working on the project. Khan admits that the idea, when enacted, might initially create confusion, and some residents have already shown concerns. "But it will bring in long-term relief," he says. "We are planning it for Joga Bai Extension soon — that locality has addresses in utter disarray."

Working feverishly on new sketches and maps of the locality, Asad says the plan is to allot new addresses, in a sequence, to around 500 houses in each block. "Each floor of each house will be part of the proposed numbering plan," he says.

But the plan is on hold for now since it needs sanction of the local municipal councillor and the MLA — a task difficult to achieve with elections just round the curb. "Once the polls are over, we will get all certificates of the change of address attested by the local representatives," Asad says.

Heading: Limbs lost to Metro mishap, life changes course for the victims - Indian Express
Content:
Civic body would move out of the Town Hall soon. Here's how it plans the upkeep of its old headquarters

Constructed in 1860, the Town Hall is one of the Capital's oldest buildings. The municipality cannot do much structural alteration since it is a heritage site but there are plans to make convert Town Hall into a five-star inn with a museum, theme parks, food courts, amphitheatre, library, and a bazaar on the lines of Dilli Haat.

The civic body expects to generate revenue for the project. "The project would be created on Build, Own, Operate, Transfer (BOOT) basis," an MCD official says. "It will start soon after MCD moves to the Civic Centre next year."

The building at present has nine fragments: the main building, press building, dispensary, barracks, Dangal Maidan, Mahatma Gandhi Maidan, children's park, women's park, pension building and a godown.

Main Building
At present housing all MCD departments, the building is slated to pave way to a five-star inn. According to MCD's survey, the first floor, with its huge rooms and open verandahs, is ideal for a hotel. The meeting hall, which can hold up to 300 people, would most likely give way to a theatre or a convention hall.

Press Building
The high ceilings and long halls of the building is ideal to provide uninterrupted space for a museum, says the MCD study.

As per plans, an experiential and interactive museum would be built, with galleries and the walls providing creative and meaningful content. The museum walls would depict the city's history: from pre-Mughal to post-Independent Delhi.

Mahatma Gandhi Maidan, children's park, women's park

At GANDHI MAIDAN, MCD proposes a light-and-sound park, much like the one that has been drawing crowds for years at the Red Fort. The light-and-sound show would focus on Delhi's history and enact scenes from the freedom struggle, with emphasis on the British-era Town Hall.

CHILDREN'S PARK would be redeveloped to attract family gatherings. Proposed essentially as a hub of cultural activities, the park would host and organise kathputli (puppet) shows, folk dances, music events, open-air cinema and laser shows.

WOMEN'S PARK would be dedicated to India's women achievers.

Dispensary
Proposed to be converted into an art gallery-cum-library. The library, the municipality says, would stock titles on Delhi's history, culture, literary treasure, scientific contribution, music, and art.

Barracks and Dangal Maidan
Close to the Old Delhi Railway Station, MCD plans a bazaar, ala Dilli Haat, with a commercial centre along with food courts here. A multi-level underground parking is also proposed at the site.

Pension dept and Godown
This, as per plans, would be developed as an exclusive food court. Plans are afoot to get a taste from across the city: fares right from the paranthe-wali gali to the new food chains.

Heading: Congress withdraws criminal cases against BJP leaders - Indian Express
Content:
Dhanu Mahato
Happy to have gained the opportunity to earn Rs 3,600 for his new bride, Dhanu Mahato — a 22-year-old from Bihar, came to Delhi early this year. Dhanu was on a night duty on Saturday at the Laxmi Nagar Delhi Metro construction site. On Sunday, he lost his right leg in the accident, which got crushed when the bridge collapsed.

His brothers are yet to break the news to his wife.

"I do not know how to inform my family back home. His wife will be shattered. He came to Delhi soon after his marriage last year. We were planning to go home in December," said Nitesh Kumar, Dhanu's brother.

Dhanu was rushed to the Lok Nayak Hospital with a metal beam lodged in his foot. "His foot had a deep cut. Some one got him to the hospital and called the numbers saved in his cell. We got here an hour after the accident, and the doctors informed us that his leg would have to be amputated," Nitesh added.

Hari Singh Meena
Another 22 year-old victim working in the night shift on Saturday, Hari Singh Meena lost his right leg and is still battling for life at the Lok Nayak Hospital. "He had lost a lot of blood and is still in a serious condition. The rest of the victims are out of danger. We are constantly monitoring his condition," said Dr Ajay Bahl, Chief Casualty Medical Officer, Emergency, Lok Nayak Hospital.

Meena is a resident of Geeta Colony. His family got to know about the accident late in the evening. "He occasionally goes out with his friends, so we assumed he would be back by afternoon. When he did not return, we started looking for him and later got to know about the accident. His friend finally called us late in the evening and informed us of the mishap," said Ghanshyam Meena, Hari's uncle.

Vinod kumar
In the same ward, Vinod, a 35-year-old from Bihar is also recovering from injuries from the freak accident. Vinod is a labourer who doubled as an electrician when required at the construction site.

Kumar suffered multiple fractures and injuries in the head, arms, feet and chest. Vikram, who shares a room with Vinod in Gurgaon said, "Since we live in Gurgaon, we were not worried when he did not reach home till afternoon. Later we got a call about the accident and rushed to the spot."

Shivesh
Nineteen-year-old Shivesh is the youngest victim of the accident. He was returning from his computer classes and was on the Blueline bus on which a portion of the bridge fell, trapping him under the debris. The injury left him temporarily paralysed, from which he has recovered.

Shivesh is a resident of Paharganj area in Central Delhi.

"He was planning for an outing later in the day but ended up in the hospital," said Sonu, his brother.

Heading: 14 days to JNU polls: candidates at ease with both local, global issues - Indian Express
Content:
Election sops are not always aimed at the general public. The BJP found that to its advantage as the Delhi government decided to withdraw criminal cases against two of its Opposition leaders — Delhi BJP chief Harsh Vardhan and the leader of Opposition Jagdish Mukhi.

The application in this regard was moved before the court of the Metropolitan Magistrate Siddharth Sharma, who has allowed the plea and discharged both leaders.

The request for withdrawal of the cases against the BJP leaders was moved in the court through the additional public prosecutor, wherein the Deputy Home Secretary wrote that the Lieutenant Governor had provided his sanction for withdrawing the cases against the BJP leaders.

The application was moved under Section 321 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and mentioned it was in the interest of the public to withdraw the cases, which had been filed when the BJP leaders had protested against the government despite prohibitory orders. Both leaders had been booked under Section 188 of the IPC for alleged disobedience to the order of a public servant and faced a maximum jail term of a month.

While Harsh Vardhan had courted arrest on March 1, 2006, Mukhi was taken into custody on November 2 the same year for raising slogans along with protestors against the policies of the ruling Congress party near the Vidhan Sabha. Both politicians were later released on bail.

After going through the application, MM Sharma observed that the cases could be withdrawn if a trial court found justifiable grounds, which showed that the object of administration of justice was better served by the withdrawal of the cases.

"Considering the nature of the offence and the reasons given in the application - that the accused persons were acting/protesting against the ruling party and the same party has put forth a proposal for the withdrawal of prosecution, and also to maintain harmony in the state machinery, I grant permission to withdraw the case," held the Magistrate on Friday.

Heading: Call centre employee murder: killer known to victim, say police - Indian Express
Content:
From the sinking US economy to the recent encounter at Jamia Nagar — with students' elections due in November, national and international issues held fort at the Jawaharlal Nehru University today, in line with long-held traditions. The list of issues were put up as the JNU Election Committee announced the final list of candidates and allowed the presidential as well as the Gender Sensitisation Committee Against Sexual Harassment (GSCASH) candidates to lay out their manifestoes before mediapersons.

Vikram Singh, presidential candidate from the Youth for Equality (YFE) spoke against OBC reservations in the country. "In JNU, students of reserved categories have been able to avail hostel facilities, while most general category students have been left deprived," he said.

Virma Ram, spokesperson of the National Student Union of India (NSUI) praised the Congress government for implementing the RTI Act, the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act and the OBC reservations while the Student Federation of India (SFI) focussed on the UPA government's failure in terms of increased poverty and inflation. Smaller parties and independent candidates also discussed issues of communalism and reservation in educational institutes. Citing the recent Jamia Nagar incident, Mohd Hafeezur Rehman, presidential candidate for the Student Voice, said, "In India, being a Muslim makes one a terrorist but those involved in the massacre of Christians in Orissa and those involved in the Babri Masjid demolition are free."

Apart from national issues, the NSUI, SFI and the ruling All India Students' Association (AISA) spoke of the immediate needs of the university, especially on proper implementation of OBC reservation. Sandeep Singh, the outgoing president from AISA who is contesting again for the same post chalked out his party's agenda, "We will like to work more towards the expansion of hostels, classrooms and health centres."

The JNUSU elections will be held on November 3 and will not follow the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines.
